knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz geometry of an extended-real-valued function
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. Write \(\partial f(x)\) for its limiting subdifferential, \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f=\{x:\partial f(x)\neq\varnothing\}\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))=\inf_{v\in\partial f(x)}\|v\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, possibly nonsmooth and nonconvex local geometry, formulated with the limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz geometry if, for every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\), there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), a number \(\eta\in(0,+\infty]\), and a continuous concave function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to[0,+\infty)\), continuously differentiable on \((0,\eta)\), such that \(\varphi(0)=0\), \(\varphi'(s)>0\), and \[\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge 1\] for every \(x\in U\) satisfying \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper lower-semicontinuous function has KL geometry when every point \(\bar x\) with a nonempty limiting subdifferential admits a neighborhood, an objective-value window, and an increasing concave desingularizing function \(\varphi\) whose derivative multiplied by the subgradient slope is at least one throughout the corresponding upper level strip.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\;\exists(U,\eta,\varphi)\;\forall x\in U\cap\{f(\bar x)<f<f(\bar x)+\eta\}:\ \varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(s=f(x)-f(\bar x)\), the inequality is equivalent to \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge 1/\varphi'(s)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), then \(\partial f(x)=\{\nabla f(x)\}\), so the slope term becomes \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\).
For \(\varphi(s)=c s^{1-\theta}\), where \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1)\), the condition becomes a power-type gradient or subgradient inequality.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every point in the active strip has \(0\notin\partial f(x)\), because the defining product is at least one.
The definition is local in both the decision variable and the objective-value gap.
boundary_notes: The condition is not imposed at points with \(f(x)=f(\bar x)\).
No convexity, analyticity, definability, or uniformity over a set is included in this definition.
Using a strong slope or another subdifferential requires a separately specified variant.

notation.meaning: Local spatial neighborhood and objective-gap radius.

review_flags: No supplied locator identifies an inspected source supporting this exact nonsmooth KL definition; a precise authoritative locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth, nonsmooth, and uniform levels of KL geometry
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(\bar x\) be a reference point, and let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact with \(f\equiv f_\Omega\) on \(\Omega\). The smooth level is considered only when \(f\) is differentiable; the variational levels use \(\partial f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A dependency-order definition distinguishing three increasingly general or uniform formulations; it does not assert that every function satisfies them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Łojasiewicz-to-KL lineage of \(f\) is the ordered triple \((\mathsf{LG}_{\bar x},\mathsf{KL}_{\bar x},\mathsf{UKL}_{\Omega})\), where \(\mathsf{LG}_{\bar x}\) denotes a local inequality \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge C|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^\theta\) for differentiable \(f\); \(\mathsf{KL}_{\bar x}\) denotes \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\) on a local upper level strip; and \(\mathsf{UKL}_{\Omega}\) denotes the latter inequality with one common triple \((U,\eta,\varphi)\) valid for all base points in \(\Omega\), equivalently on a tubular neighborhood of \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lineage is the ordered collection of the classical smooth gradient inequality at a point, its nonsmooth KL reformulation using a limiting-subgradient slope, and the uniform KL formulation using common parameters near a compact constant-level set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Lineage}(f;\bar x,\Omega):=(\mathsf{LG}_{\bar x},\mathsf{KL}_{\bar x},\mathsf{UKL}_{\Omega})\), with the three components defined by their respective gradient, subgradient-slope, and set-uniform inequalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: At a smooth point, \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))=\|\nabla f(x)\|\), so a power-type \(\mathsf{KL}_{\bar x}\) has the classical gradient form after matching constants and exponents.
special_cases_latex: For \(\Omega=\{\bar x\}\), the uniform formulation reduces to a pointwise formulation after restricting the neighborhood.
For analytic differentiable \(f\), the classical gradient inequality is the smooth origin of the lineage.
immediate_consequences_latex: The notation separates passage from smooth gradients to generalized slopes from the separate operation of compact-set uniformization.
A claim at one level does not, by definition alone, establish a claim at another level.
boundary_notes: The ordered triple records formulations, not an unconditional implication theorem.
Uniformization requires constant objective value on the compact reference set in the standard form.
Infinite-dimensional variants and alternative slopes are excluded.

notation.meaning: Uniform KL formulation on a compact set.

review_flags: The lineage packaging and exact dependency order require a source explicitly presenting all three formulations.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth, nonsmooth, and uniform levels of KL geometry

children.title: Classical Gradient Łojasiewicz Geometry
children.top_down_role: The analytic smooth-function origin of the convergence geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Gradient Łojasiewicz Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a critical point of a real-analytic function, the gradient controls a fixed power of the objective-value gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be real analytic, and let \(\bar x\in U\) satisfy \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\). Then there exist a neighborhood \(V\subset U\) of \(\bar x\), constants \(c>0\), and \(\theta\in[1/2,1)\) such that
\[
|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^{\theta}\le c\|\nabla f(x)\|\qquad\text{for every }x\in V.
\]
Equivalently, with \(\varphi(s)=c(1-\theta)^{-1}s^{1-\theta}\), one has \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge1\) whenever \(x\in V\) and \(f(\bar x)<f(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is real analytic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists V,c>0,\theta\in[1/2,1): |f(x)-f(\bar x)|^\theta\le c\|\nabla f(x)\|\) for all \(x\in V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional gradient inequality for a real-analytic function near a critical point.

source_witnesses.locator: Theorem 2.3 (Łojasiewicz gradient inequality)

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U_0\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(f:U_0\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(\bar x\in U_0\) satisfy \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth local geometry at a critical point; analyticity is a recognition hypothesis rather than part of the defining inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has classical gradient Łojasiewicz geometry at \(\bar x\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\subset U_0\) of \(\bar x\), constants \(C>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), and an exponent \(\theta\in[0,1)\) such that \[\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge C|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^\theta\] whenever \(x\in U\) and \(|f(x)-f(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuously differentiable function has classical gradient Łojasiewicz geometry at a critical point when, locally and for sufficiently small objective gaps, its gradient norm is bounded below by a positive constant times a fixed power of the absolute objective gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists U,C>0,\varepsilon>0,\theta\in[0,1)\;\forall x\in U:\ |f(x)-f(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\Rightarrow\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge C|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^\theta.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: On the upper level strip \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\varepsilon\), setting \(\varphi(s)=[C(1-\theta)]^{-1}s^{1-\theta}\) gives \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge1\).
special_cases_latex: When \(\theta=0\), the gradient norm is bounded away from zero at every nearby point having nonzero objective gap.
For a nondegenerate smooth critical point, the frequently occurring exponent is \(\theta=1/2\), although that value is not imposed by the definition.
immediate_consequences_latex: No distinct critical point with a different nearby objective value can lie in the region where the inequality holds.
The exponent and constants are local data attached to \((f,\bar x)\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not assert that every continuously differentiable function satisfies the inequality.
Some conventions write the exponent as \(1-\alpha\); exponents must be translated before comparison.
The absolute-gap formulation is stronger in domain coverage than an upper-strip-only KL formulation.
review_flags: A precise source locator for the stated exponent convention and two-sided objective-gap formulation is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Local gradient Łojasiewicz inequality

children.title: Nonsmooth KL Slope Geometry
children.top_down_role: The extension to generalized slopes and nonsmooth criticality.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth KL Slope Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonsmooth KL property requires a desingularized value gap whose derivative times the limiting-subgradient slope is at least one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). The function \(f\) has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property at \(\bar x\) if there exist \(\eta>0\), a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), and a continuous concave function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb{R}_+\), continuously differentiable on \((0,\eta)\), such that \(\varphi(0)=0\), \(\varphi'(s)>0\), and
\[
\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\,\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1
\]
for every \(x\in U\) satisfying \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\) throughout a punctured upper level neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-subdifferential formulation of the KL property for proper lower-semicontinuous functions.

notation.meaning: nonsmooth slope used in the KL inequality

source_witnesses.locator: Section 3, nonsmooth Łojasiewicz inequality and Theorem 3.1

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsmooth KL inequality at a subdifferentiable point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). Define the limiting-subgradient slope by \(m_f(x):=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\), with \(m_f(x)=+\infty\) when \(\partial f(x)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonsmooth and nonconvex local geometry expressed through the limiting-subgradient slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has the nonsmooth KL property at \(\bar x\) if there exist \(\eta\in(0,+\infty]\), a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), and a continuous concave function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to[0,+\infty)\), continuously differentiable on \((0,\eta)\), satisfying \(\varphi(0)=0\) and \(\varphi'(s)>0\), such that \[\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))m_f(x)\ge1\] for all \(x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) with \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonsmooth KL property holds at \(\bar x\) when a local concave change of objective scale converts the limiting-subgradient slope into a quantity uniformly bounded below by one throughout a sufficiently small upper objective strip.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists(U,\eta,\varphi)\;\forall x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}\partial f:\ 0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\Rightarrow\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))m_f(x)\ge1.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Defining \(\psi(s)=1/\varphi'(s)\), the inequality reads \(m_f(x)\ge\psi(f(x)-f(\bar x))\), where \(\psi(s)>0\) on \((0,\eta)\).
special_cases_latex: For differentiable \(f\), \(m_f(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|\).
For convex \(f\), the limiting subdifferential agrees with the convex subdifferential.
A power desingularizer produces \(m_f(x)\ge c[f(x)-f(\bar x)]^\theta\) after renaming the positive constant.
immediate_consequences_latex: There are no critical points with strictly larger objective value inside the active strip.
The defining inequality depends on objective values and slope, not on a particular algorithm.
boundary_notes: Lower-level points with \(f(x)<f(\bar x)\) are outside this formulation.
Replacing the limiting subdifferential by a proximal, Clarke, or convex subdifferential changes the statement unless equality is known.
The definition is pointwise and supplies no common parameters over a set.

notation.meaning: Distance from zero to the limiting subdifferential.
Points having a nonempty limiting subdifferential.

review_flags: No precise inspected source was supplied for this limiting-subdifferential formulation.

children.title: Uniformized KL Geometry
children.top_down_role: Uniformization near compact critical sets and cluster sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniformized KL Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise KL inequalities on a compact constant-level set admit one common neighborhood, value range, and desingularizing function with the standard KL regularity properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(\Omega\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) be compact. Suppose that \(f\) is constant on \(\Omega\), with value \(f_\Omega\), and has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property at every point of \(\Omega\). Then there exist \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\eta>0\), and a continuous concave function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb{R}_+\), continuously differentiable on \((0,\eta)\), such that \(\varphi(0)=0\), \(\varphi'(s)>0\) for every \(s\in(0,\eta)\), and
\[
\varphi'(f(x)-f_\Omega)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge 1
\]
for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)<\varepsilon\) and \(f_\Omega<f(x)<f_\Omega+\eta\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) is compact, \(f\) is constant on \(\Omega\), and \(f\) has the KL property at every point of \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\eta>0\), and one KL desingularizer \(\varphi\) enforcing the slope inequality near every point of \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform KL inequality on a compact constant-level set, suitable for cluster-set arguments.

notation.meaning: common value of the function on the compact set

source_witnesses.locator: Lemma 6 (Uniformized KL property)

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform KL property on a compact constant-level set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. Let \(\Omega\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) be nonempty and compact, and suppose \(f(x)=f_\Omega\) for every \(x\in\Omega\). Write \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)=\inf_{z\in\Omega}\|x-z\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional uniformization near a compact set lying in one objective level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has uniformized KL geometry on \(\Omega\) if there exist \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\eta>0\), and a continuous concave function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to[0,+\infty)\), continuously differentiable on \((0,\eta)\), with \(\varphi(0)=0\) and \(\varphi'(s)>0\), such that \[\varphi'(f(x)-f_\Omega)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\] whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)<\varepsilon\) and \(f_\Omega<f(x)<f_\Omega+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformized KL geometry means that one spatial radius, one objective-gap radius, and one desingularizing function work simultaneously near every point of a compact reference set on which the objective is constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\varepsilon,\eta>0,\varphi\;\forall x:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)<\varepsilon,\ 0<f(x)-f_\Omega<\eta\Rightarrow\varphi'(f(x)-f_\Omega)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tubular-neighborhood statement is equivalent to requiring the same \((\eta,\varphi)\) and a common neighborhood containing \(\Omega\), after possibly shrinking its distance from the compact set.
special_cases_latex: For \(\Omega=\{\bar x\}\), this is a pointwise KL property with explicitly chosen metric and value radii.
A compact cluster set of a bounded descent sequence is a typical reference set when the objective is known to be constant on it.
immediate_consequences_latex: All points in the active tube share the same slope lower-bound function \(s\mapsto1/\varphi'(s)\).
Uniform parameters avoid selecting different KL data along different subsequences approaching \(\Omega\).
boundary_notes: Compactness and constancy of \(f\) on \(\Omega\) are part of this standard uniform formulation.
Pointwise KL properties on a noncompact set do not automatically provide uniform parameters.
This definition does not itself establish that pointwise KL geometry can be uniformized.
review_flags: A source locator for the compact-set uniformization statement and its exact hypotheses is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform KL property on a compact constant-level set

children.title: KL Recognition Classes
children.top_down_role: Function classes for which KL behavior follows from established analytic or tame-geometric recognition routes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal{F}\) be a class of proper lower-semicontinuous functions \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), possibly with varying finite dimension \(n\). The KL property is understood relative to the limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A meta-level definition for classes whose structural description supplies a KL recognition route; individual analytic, semialgebraic, globally subanalytic, and definable classes require separate recognition results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The class \(\mathcal{F}\) is a KL recognition class if every \(f\in\mathcal{F}\) has the KL property at each \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\); explicitly, for every such pair \((f,\bar x)\), there exist local data \((U,\eta,\varphi)\) satisfying \[\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\] for all \(x\in U\) with \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\). A structural subclass is recognized only when a theorem establishes this universal implication from membership to the KL property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function class is KL-recognizable when membership in the class guarantees, through an applicable recognition theorem, the pointwise nonsmooth KL property for every proper lower-semicontinuous member at every point with a nonempty limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{F}\text{ is KL-recognizable}\iff\forall f\in\mathcal{F}\ \forall\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f:\ f\text{ has the KL property at }\bar x.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The universal quantification may be expressed as \(\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{KL}}\), where \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{KL}}\) is the class of proper lower-semicontinuous KL functions.
special_cases_latex: A recognized semialgebraic class is obtained by restricting \(\mathcal{F}\) to proper lower-semicontinuous functions with semialgebraic graphs.
A definable recognition class must fix the underlying o-minimal structure.
immediate_consequences_latex: Recognition is a property of a specified function class and theorem scope, not merely of an informal model label.
Closure constructions preserve recognition only when their outputs remain within a recognized class or a separate stability result applies.
boundary_notes: This definition does not itself prove that any named structural class is KL-recognizable.
Properness and lower semicontinuity cannot be silently omitted from a nonsmooth extended-valued recognition claim.
Infinite-dimensional recognition results lie outside the stated ambient domain.

notation.meaning: Class of proper lower-semicontinuous functions having the KL property at all subdifferentiable points.

review_flags: The meta-definition and any concrete recognition classes require authoritative locators; none of the supplied hints addresses KL recognition.

children.title: Analytic-Algebraic Model Classes
children.top_down_role: Analytic, polynomial, and algebraically generated models.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). A real-analytic function is locally represented by a convergent power series. A basic semianalytic set in an open neighborhood \(V\) is described by finitely many analytic equalities and strict inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local analytic-algebraic representation; the definition classifies models but does not by itself assert a KL theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is an analytic-algebraic model if its epigraph is locally semianalytic: for every \((\bar x,\bar t)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\), there is an open neighborhood \(V\) such that \(\operatorname{epi}f\cap V\) is a finite union of sets of the form \[\{z\in V:a_i(z)=0\ (i=1,\ldots,p),\ b_j(z)>0\ (j=1,\ldots,q)\},\] where all \(a_i\) and \(b_j\) are real analytic on \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-valued function belongs to the analytic-algebraic model class when, around every point, its epigraph can be expressed as a finite union of pieces cut out by finitely many real-analytic equations and strict inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{sa}}\iff\operatorname{epi}f\text{ is locally a finite union of basic semianalytic sets}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a finite-valued continuous function, one may instead require the graph \(\{(x,t):t=f(x)\}\) to be semianalytic, provided the chosen source establishes equivalence with the epigraph formulation in that setting.
special_cases_latex: Every polynomial is real analytic, so polynomial equality and inequality models are included.
A real-analytic objective restricted by finitely many analytic constraints yields an extended-valued model \(g+\delta_C\) when the resulting epigraph has the stated representation.
Nash functions give an analytic-algebraic subclass whose analytic components also satisfy polynomial relations.
immediate_consequences_latex: The class is local and permits different finite analytic descriptions in different neighborhoods.
Finite algebraic models arise by restricting the defining analytic functions to polynomials.
boundary_notes: Local semianalyticity is not identical to global subanalyticity or definability in an arbitrary o-minimal structure.
Projection of a semianalytic set need not remain semianalytic; subanalytic language is needed for such projections.
A KL recognition conclusion is not part of this definition.

notation.meaning: Indicator taking value zero on \(C\) and \(+\infty\) outside it.

review_flags: The node title admits several analytic-algebraic class conventions; a source is needed to confirm the intended epigraph-based semianalytic definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Locally semianalytic extended-valued model
Real-Analytic Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite-dimensional real-analytic objective has a local power-type KL inequality at each critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be real analytic. At every critical point \(\bar x\in U\), the classical gradient Łojasiewicz inequality holds locally. Consequently, \(f\) satisfies the smooth KL property at \(\bar x\): there exist \(\eta>0\), a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\), and a power desingularizer \(\varphi(s)=a s^{1-\theta}\), where \(a>0\) and \(\theta\in[1/2,1)\), such that
\[
\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge1
\]
for \(x\in V\) with \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\).
assumptions_latex: \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) is real analytic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) has the smooth KL property at \(\bar x\) with a power desingularizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local KL recognition for finite-valued real-analytic objectives.

source_witnesses.locator: Theorem 2.3 (Łojasiewicz gradient inequality)

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial objectives, and regular functions on smooth real algebraic manifolds, possess local power-type gradient and KL inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Every polynomial \(p:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is real analytic and therefore satisfies a local gradient Łojasiewicz, hence smooth KL, inequality at each critical point. More generally, if \(M\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a smooth real algebraic manifold and \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) is regular, then around every critical point \(\bar x\in M\) there exist \(c>0\), \(\theta\in[1/2,1)\), and a relative neighborhood \(V\) such that
\[
|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^\theta\le c\|\operatorname{grad}_M f(x)\|\qquad(x\in V).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(p:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is polynomial; alternatively, \(M\) is a smooth real algebraic manifold and \(f\) is regular on \(M\).
\(\bar x\) is a critical point in the applicable ambient space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A local power-type Łojasiewicz gradient inequality, and thus the KL property, holds at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial and regular algebraic objectives as power-type KL models.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial case is standard, but the record additionally asserts a Riemannian gradient inequality for regular functions on smooth real algebraic manifolds. The cited Euclidean analytic-cost theorem does not inspectably support that manifold extension; a dedicated analytic-manifold or algebraic-manifold source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraic extended-valued function
Semialgebraic Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proper lower-semicontinuous semialgebraic function has the KL property at every point of its limiting-subdifferential domain and locally admits a power-type desingularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and suppose that \(\operatorname{epi}f\) is semialgebraic. Then \(f\) has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property at every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). More precisely, for each such \(\bar x\), there exist \(a>0\), \(\theta\in[0,1)\), \(\eta>0\), and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that, with \(\varphi(s)=a s^{1-\theta}\),
\[
\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge 1
\]
for every \(x\in U\) satisfying \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(a>0\), \(\theta\in[0,1)\), \(\eta>0\), and a neighborhood \(U\) on which the power-type KL inequality holds above \(f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL recognition theorem for proper lower-semicontinuous semialgebraic functions.

notation.meaning: KL exponent in the power desingularizer

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Algebraic Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely piecewise-polynomial function on semialgebraic regions is semialgebraic; if proper and lower semicontinuous, it is KL.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_1,\ldots,D_m\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be semialgebraic sets whose union is \(\operatorname{dom}f\). Suppose that for each \(i\), a polynomial \(p_i\) satisfies \(f(x)=p_i(x)\) on \(D_i\), and that the pieces agree wherever their domains overlap. Then
\[
\operatorname{gph}f=\bigcup_{i=1}^m\{(x,t):x\in D_i,\ t=p_i(x)\}
\]
is semialgebraic. If the resulting extended-real-valued function is proper and lower semicontinuous, it is a KL function on \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f\).
assumptions_latex: \(f|_{D_i}=p_i|_{D_i}\) for polynomials \(p_i\), with compatible overlap values.
The assembled extended-real-valued \(f\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{gph}f\) is semialgebraic and \(f\) has the KL property on \(\operatorname{dom}\partial f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite semialgebraic piece descriptions provide a direct KL recognition certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Gluing Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite semialgebraic gluing preserves semialgebraicity but does not guarantee lower semicontinuity, while countable gluing need not preserve definability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Finite gluing preserves semialgebraicity when every piece domain and every piece graph is semialgebraic. Compatibility on overlaps makes the gluing single-valued, but it does not ensure lower semicontinuity. For example,
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}1,&x=0,\\0,&x\ne 0,
\end{cases}
\]
has a finite semialgebraic graph but is not lower semicontinuous at \(0\); hence the standard proper lower-semicontinuous KL recognition theorem cannot be invoked at that point. Moreover, countable gluing need not preserve semialgebraicity or definability, so no semialgebraic KL conclusion follows from countably piecewise algebraic descriptions alone.
assumptions_latex: Each member of the finite gluing has a semialgebraic domain and semialgebraic graph.
The nonsmooth KL recognition theorem being invoked requires a proper lower-semicontinuous function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite semialgebraic gluing alone does not guarantee lower semicontinuity, and countable gluing need not preserve definability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: What finite semialgebraic gluing does—and does not—guarantee for KL recognition.

knowledge_statements.title: Globally Subanalytic Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proper lower-semicontinuous globally subanalytic function satisfies the nonsmooth KL property at each subdifferential-domain point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and suppose that \(\operatorname{epi}f\) is globally subanalytic. Then \(f\) is definable in the o-minimal structure of globally subanalytic sets and has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property at every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). Thus, for each such \(\bar x\), there are a neighborhood \(U\), \(\eta>0\), and a concave definable desingularizer \(\varphi\) satisfying
\[
\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1
\]
throughout the corresponding punctured upper level neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) has the KL property at every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL recognition for lower-semicontinuous functions definable in the globally subanalytic structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An o-minimal tame model is an extended-valued function whose finite-valued graph is definable in a fixed o-minimal expansion of the ordered real field; fixing the structure specifies which operations and transcendental functions are allowed.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: O-minimal stratification supplies the geometric regularity behind a nonsmooth KL inequality for proper lower-semicontinuous definable objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and definable in a fixed o-minimal structure. \[
\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1
\]
locally above the level \(f(\bar x)\). Thus tame finite-dimensional geometry supplies a verifiable recognition route to KL convergence analysis.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and fix \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). Let \(\Phi_\eta\) denote the admissible concave desingularizing functions on \([0,\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A parameter-space definition separating spatial, value-gap, and desingularization data for a local nonsmooth KL inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The KL desingularization parameter set of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) is \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\bar x):=\left\{(U,\eta,\varphi):\begin{array}{l}U\text{ is a neighborhood of }\bar x,\ \eta\in(0,+\infty],\ \varphi\in\Phi_\eta,\\ \varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\\ \text{for all }x\in U\text{ with }0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\end{array}\right\}.\] The function has the KL property at \(\bar x\) exactly when this set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local KL parameter set collects every neighborhood, objective-gap radius, and admissible desingularizing function for which the KL slope inequality holds at the chosen reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\bar x)\neq\varnothing\iff f\text{ has the KL property at }\bar x.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: One may replace \(U\) by a radius \(r>0\) and use \(B(\bar x,r)\) because every neighborhood contains an open ball.
The reciprocal slope profile \(\psi=1/\varphi'\) parameterizes the same inequality when \(\varphi\) can be recovered within the selected admissible family.
special_cases_latex: Power-type parameter data take \(\varphi(s)=c s^{1-\theta}\).
Uniform set-valued parameter data replace \(\bar x\) by a compact constant-level set and require one common triple.
immediate_consequences_latex: Shrinking \(U\) or decreasing \(\eta\) preserves admissibility of a fixed \(\varphi\) restricted to the smaller interval.
Different admissible triples may describe the same local KL germ.
boundary_notes: The parameter set may be empty.
No uniqueness or optimality of \(\eta\), \(U\), or \(\varphi\) is implied.
Comparing parameters across exponent conventions requires normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: General Desingularizing-Function Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general KL parameter uses an increasing concave desingularizer whose derivative rescales the stationarity residual to a uniform positive lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\eta\in(0,+\infty]\), the admissible desingularizing family \(\Phi_\eta\) consists of functions \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb{R}_+\) that are continuous on \([0,\eta)\), satisfy \(\varphi(0)=0\), are concave, and are continuously differentiable on \((0,\eta)\) with \(\varphi'(s)>0\). A function \(f\) has the KL property at \(\bar x\) with parameter \((U,\eta,\varphi)\) if \[\varphi'\!\left(f(x)-f(\bar x)\right)\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)\ge 1\] for every \(x\in U\) satisfying \(0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((U,\eta,\varphi)\) is a valid local KL parameter exactly when the displayed inequality holds on its prescribed value slice.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible nonlinear reparameterizations for the general KL inequality.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix \(\eta\in(0,+\infty]\). Functions are defined on the objective-gap interval \([0,\eta)\), and derivatives are required only on its interior \((0,\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General nonlinear reparameterizations used in the standard differentiable-desingularizer version of the KL property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The admissible desingularizing-function family is \[\Phi_\eta:=\{\varphi:[0,\eta)\to[0,+\infty):\ \varphi\text{ is continuous and concave on }[0,\eta),\ \varphi(0)=0,\ \varphi\in C^1(0,\eta),\ \varphi'(s)>0\ \forall s\in(0,\eta)\}.\] A member \(\varphi\in\Phi_\eta\) desingularizes \(f\) at \(\bar x\) on \(U\) when \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\) throughout the associated upper level strip.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An admissible general desingularizer is a continuous concave function starting at zero, continuously differentiable with strictly positive derivative for positive gaps, and capable—when paired with a function and neighborhood—of satisfying the KL slope inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi\in\Phi_\eta\iff\varphi\in C([0,\eta))\cap C^1((0,\eta)),\ \varphi(0)=0,\ \varphi\text{ concave},\ \varphi'>0.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Concavity and differentiability imply that \(\varphi'\) is nonincreasing on \((0,\eta)\).
The associated reciprocal profile \(s\mapsto1/\varphi'(s)\) is positive and nondecreasing.

The linear case \(\varphi(s)=cs\) corresponds to \(\theta=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every \(\varphi\in\Phi_\eta\) is strictly increasing on \([0,\eta)\).
Restricting \(\varphi\in\Phi_\eta\) to \([0,\eta')\) with \(0<\eta'\le\eta\) yields a member of \(\Phi_{\eta'}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Power-Type KL Exponent Families
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power desingularizers convert the KL inequality into a stationarity-residual lower bound proportional to the objective gap raised to exponent θ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\theta\in[0,1)\) and \(c>0\). The power-type desingularizer is \(\varphi(s)=c s^{1-\theta}\) for \(s\ge 0\), with \(\varphi'(s)=c(1-\theta)s^{-\theta}\) for \(s>0\). Thus the KL inequality with this \(\varphi\) is equivalent to \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)\ge \frac{1}{c(1-\theta)}\left(f(x)-f(\bar x)\right)^\theta\] on the selected neighborhood and positive value slice. The parameter \(\theta\) is called a KL exponent of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) when such a local inequality holds.
assumptions_latex: \(0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\) on the local KL slice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The power-form KL inequality is equivalent to a residual bound of order \(\left(f(x)-f(\bar x)\right)^\theta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power desingularizers parameterized by the KL exponent.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly differentiates the power desingularizer and obtains the corresponding residual inequality. It fits the exponent-family leaf, but the exponent convention and parameterization have no inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). Exponents use the slope form \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge\kappa[f(x)-f(\bar x)]^\theta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise finite-dimensional power-type KL geometry under the exponent convention \(\theta\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The power-type KL exponent set of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) is \[\Theta_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\bar x):=\left\{\theta\in[0,1):\begin{array}{l}\exists\kappa,\eta,r>0\text{ such that}\\ \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge\kappa[f(x)-f(\bar x)]^\theta\\ \forall x\in B(\bar x,r)\text{ with }0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\end{array}\right\}.\] Any \(\theta\) in this set is a KL exponent at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A number \(\theta\in[0,1)\) is a power-type KL exponent when the limiting-subgradient slope locally dominates a positive multiple of the objective gap raised to \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\bar x)\iff\exists\kappa,\eta,r>0\ \forall x\in B(\bar x,r):\ 0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge\kappa[f(x)-f(\bar x)]^\theta.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inequality is the KL inequality generated by \(\varphi(s)=[\kappa(1-\theta)]^{-1}s^{1-\theta}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\theta=0\), the slope is locally bounded below by \(\kappa>0\) off the reference level.
For \(\theta=1/2\), the squared slope dominates the objective gap after adjusting the constant.
Values \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) describe weaker power lower bounds near zero than \(\theta=1/2\) on a sufficiently small gap interval.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\theta\) is admissible, then every larger \(\theta'<1\) is locally admissible after shrinking the objective-gap radius and modifying the constant.
Thus the smallest admissible exponent, when attained, gives the sharpest member of this convention's local power family.
boundary_notes: Some literature calls \(1-\theta\), rather than \(\theta\), the KL exponent.
The definition does not assert existence or attainment of a minimal exponent.
Rate conclusions are not part of this definition and require algorithmic descent hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Set of admissible power-type KL exponents.

review_flags: A precise source is required to validate the exponent convention, admissible range, and parameter normalization.

children.top_down_role: Local parameters at individual critical points versus uniform parameters on critical sets.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise and set-uniform KL exponent hierarchy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. Let \(\Omega\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) be nonempty and satisfy \(f\equiv f_\Omega\) on \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A hierarchy comparing local power parameters at individual points with parameters required to hold uniformly near a constant-level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\bar x\in\Omega\), let \(\Theta_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\bar x)\) be the pointwise exponent set. Define the uniform exponent set by \[\Theta_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\Omega):=\left\{\theta\in[0,1):\exists\kappa,\varepsilon,\eta>0\ \forall x,\ \begin{array}{l}\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)<\varepsilon,\\0<f(x)-f_\Omega<\eta\end{array}\Rightarrow\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge\kappa[f(x)-f_\Omega]^\theta\right\}.\] The point-to-set hierarchy is the inclusion \(\Theta_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\Omega)\subseteq\bigcap_{\bar x\in\Omega}\Theta_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise exponent sets allow constants and neighborhoods to vary with each reference point, whereas the set-uniform exponent set requires one exponent, slope constant, spatial radius, and objective-gap radius to work near the whole constant-level set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Theta_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\Omega)\subseteq\bigcap_{\bar x\in\Omega}\Theta_{\mathrm{KL}}(f,\bar x)\), with uniform membership defined by common \((\kappa,\varepsilon,\eta)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a singleton \(\Omega=\{\bar x\}\), the uniform exponent definition agrees with the pointwise definition after translating between ball and distance neighborhoods.
special_cases_latex: When \(\Omega\) is finite, a common exponent already admissible at every point can often be paired with minimum radii and adjusted constants, subject to matching value levels.
For compact \(\Omega\), a separate uniformization result may produce common data from pointwise KL information.
immediate_consequences_latex: Uniform exponent membership implies pointwise membership at every point of \(\Omega\).
The reverse inclusion is not contained in the definition and requires uniformity hypotheses.
boundary_notes: Constancy of \(f\) on \(\Omega\) is required by this formulation.
No equality between the uniform set and the intersection of pointwise sets is asserted.
Non-power desingularizers require a parallel hierarchy formulated with function families rather than scalar exponents.

notation.meaning: Exponent set admitting common parameters near \(\Omega\).
Exponent set with parameters local to \(\bar x\).

review_flags: The hierarchy and its exact set-uniform parameter convention require an explicit authoritative source.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise and set-uniform KL exponent hierarchy
Pointwise KL Parameters
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise KL parameter supplies a neighborhood, value radius, and desingularizer valid around one specified reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and fix \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). A pointwise KL parameter at \(\bar x\) is a triple \((U_{\bar x},\eta_{\bar x},\varphi_{\bar x})\), where \(U_{\bar x}\) is a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), \(\eta_{\bar x}>0\), and \(\varphi_{\bar x}\in\Phi_{\eta_{\bar x}}\), such that \[\varphi_{\bar x}'\!\left(f(x)-f(\bar x)\right)\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)\ge1\] for all \(x\in U_{\bar x}\) with \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta_{\bar x}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((U_{\bar x},\eta_{\bar x},\varphi_{\bar x})\) is pointwise KL data at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL data attached to one reference point.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The record is a suitable definition of point-dependent KL data and matches its terminal container. No source supports the exact parameter convention or displayed definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Setwise KL Parameters
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A setwise KL parameter is one neighborhood, value radius, and desingularizer that works uniformly around a constant-value reference set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) be nonempty and suppose that \(f\) is constant on \(\Omega\), with common value \(f_\Omega\). A setwise KL parameter for \(f\) on \(\Omega\) is a triple \((U,\eta,\varphi)\), where \(U\) is a neighborhood of \(\Omega\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\varphi\in\Phi_\eta\), such that \[\varphi'\!\left(f(x)-f_\Omega\right)\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)\ge1\] for every \(x\in U\) satisfying \(f_\Omega<f(x)<f_\Omega+\eta\). The same data must work simultaneously near every point of \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((U,\eta,\varphi)\) supplies a uniform KL inequality on the prescribed neighborhood of \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common KL data valid around an entire constant-value set.

notation.meaning: common value of f on Ω

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes common setwise data from pointwise data and requires a constant reference value. It lacks a citation with a specific locator for this uniform setwise formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Point-to-Set Uniformization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise KL inequalities on a compact constant-value set admit one common desingularizer and common neighborhood and value radii.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(\Omega\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) be compact. Assume that \(f\) is constant on \(\Omega\), with value \(f_\Omega\), and that \(f\) has the KL property at every point of \(\Omega\). Then there exist \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\varphi\in\Phi_\eta\) such that \[\varphi'\!\left(f(x)-f_\Omega\right)\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)\ge1\] whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\Omega)<\varepsilon\) and \(f_\Omega<f(x)<f_\Omega+\eta\).
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) is compact and \(f\) is constant on \(\Omega\).
\(f\) has the KL property at every \(\bar x\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist common \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\eta>0\), and \(\varphi\in\Phi_\eta\) giving the displayed setwise KL inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformization of pointwise KL inequalities over a compact constant-value set.

notation.meaning: common value of f on Ω

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the point-to-set uniformization leaf and states the standard compact constant-value uniformization pattern. Because it is a nontrivial theorem and no evidence is cited, its exact hypotheses and conclusion require an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local growth, error-bound, residual, and gradient-dominance profile
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(S\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a reference solution or critical set, and let \(f_*\in\mathbb{R}\) be the common reference value. Let \(R:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,+\infty]\) be a chosen residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A definitional catalogue of neighboring regularity inequalities; it deliberately makes no unconditional equivalence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local regularity-language profile for \((f,S,R)\) on a neighborhood \(U\) consists of any specified subset of: growth \(f(x)-f_*\ge a\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p\); objective error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le b[f(x)-f_*]^q\); residual error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le cR(x)^r\); slope domination \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge d[f(x)-f_*]^\theta\); and gradient dominance \(f(x)-f_*\le e\|\nabla f(x)\|^\gamma\) in the smooth case, where all constants and exponents are positive except \(\theta\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neighboring regularity languages describe the same local model through separately named inequalities involving objective growth, distance to a reference set, a criticality residual, a subgradient slope, or a smooth gradient norm; which implications or equivalences hold depends on additional hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{R}(f,S,R;U)\subseteq\{\mathsf{Growth}_{p},\mathsf{ObjEB}_{q},\mathsf{ResEB}_{r},\mathsf{Slope}_{\theta},\mathsf{GD}_{\gamma}\}\), with each member defined by its displayed local inequality.
special_cases_latex: Quadratic growth corresponds to \(p=2\).
A Lipschitz residual error bound corresponds to \(r=1\).
The Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality is a smooth gradient-dominance condition with \(\gamma=2\), up to normalization.
immediate_consequences_latex: The profile records precisely which regularity statement is assumed rather than treating nearby languages as synonyms.
Constants, exponents, neighborhoods, and reference sets must be retained when translating between formulations.
boundary_notes: No equivalence among the listed inequalities follows from their definitions alone.
Convexity, prox-regularity, subdifferential continuity, isolation of solutions, and metric subregularity assumptions may change available correspondences.
The residual \(R\) must be specified; different algorithms generally induce different residuals.

notation.meaning: Common objective value on the reference set.

review_flags: The node is an umbrella over several model-dependent languages; sources are needed for the intended catalogue and any supported correspondences.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Locally equivalent slope and algorithmic residual
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(S\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\), and define \(m_f(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\). Let \(R:D\to[0,+\infty]\) be a residual on \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local comparison between an intrinsic limiting-subgradient slope and a specified method-dependent residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((m_f,R)\) is a slope-residual representation pair around \(S\) on \(D\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\) and constants \(0<c_-\le c_+<+\infty\) such that \[c_-m_f(x)\le R(x)\le c_+m_f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U\cap D.\] A one-sided slope-dominating residual requires only \(m_f(x)\le cR(x)\), while a one-sided residual-dominating slope requires only \(R(x)\le c m_f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slope and a residual form a local representation pair when they are bounded above and below by fixed positive multiples of one another near the reference set. One-sided variants retain only the comparison needed in a particular analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((m_f,R)\text{ is a representation pair near }S\iff\exists U,c_-,c_+>0\ \forall x\in U\cap D:\ c_-m_f(x)\le R(x)\le c_+m_f(x).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Two-sided comparison is equivalent to \(c_-\le R(x)/m_f(x)\le c_+\) wherever \(m_f(x)>0\), together with matching zero sets in the comparison neighborhood.
special_cases_latex: For smooth unconstrained optimization, \(m_f(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|\), and the gradient norm itself is an exact residual with \(c_-=c_+=1\).
For composite problems, a proximal-gradient mapping can serve as \(R\) only under hypotheses establishing the stated comparisons.
immediate_consequences_latex: Within the comparison neighborhood, \(R(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\partial f(x)\).
A KL slope lower bound transfers to a residual lower bound through the inequality \(R\ge c_-m_f\).
A residual convergence estimate transfers to the intrinsic slope through \(m_f\le R/c_-\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not claim that an arbitrary algorithmic residual is comparable to the limiting-subgradient slope.
Constants may depend on the model, metric, step size, and neighborhood.
One-sided comparison is insufficient for conclusions requiring equivalence of criticality measures.
review_flags: The abstract two-sided comparison definition requires a source, and concrete residual instances require model-specific evidence.

abla f|(x)\) measures the greatest first-order rate of local decrease available from \(x\), without selecting a derivative or subgradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\nabla f|(x)\) is the local descent-slope quantity defined by the displayed formula.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-slope description of local objective descent.

notation.meaning: strong slope of f at x

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent, uses properly delimited mathematics, and fits the slope-geometry leaf. A specific source is required for the strong-slope convention used here.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity-Residual Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stationarity residual is the distance from zero to the limiting subdifferential; it vanishes exactly at stationary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. Its limiting-subdifferential stationarity residual is \[r_f(x):=\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)=\inf\{\|v\|:v\in\partial f(x)\},\] with \(r_f(x)=+\infty\) when \(\partial f(x)=\varnothing\). Consequently, \(r_f(x)=0\) exactly when \(0\in\partial f(x)\), so vanishing residual is equivalent to limiting-subdifferential stationarity. Residual sublevel sets \(\{x:r_f(x)\le\epsilon\}\) describe approximate stationary geometry at tolerance \(\epsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_f(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential residual measuring first-order nonstationarity.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The limiting-subdifferential residual definition and its stationarity interpretation fit the container. No inspectable source is supplied for the subdifferential convention, empty-set distance convention, or closedness-dependent zero-residual equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Slope–Residual Comparability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided local bounds make strong slope and subdifferential residual interchangeable in KL inequalities, up to constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(D\subset\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). The strong slope and stationarity residual are locally comparable on \(D\) if there exist constants \(0<c\le C<+\infty\) such that \[c\,\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)\le |\nabla f|(x)\le C\,\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)\qquad(x\in D).\] Under this condition, a KL inequality written with either quantity transfers to the other after rescaling its constant or desingularizing function; the KL exponent is unchanged in the power-type case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Slope-form and residual-form KL inequalities on \(D\) are equivalent up to multiplicative constants.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local two-sided equivalence between descent slope and subdifferential residual.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The content kind is correctly a condition, and the stated two-sided comparison does permit transfer of slope-form and residual-form KL inequalities after rescaling. The transfer and exponent-preservation claims are nontrivial and have no cited source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Error Bound and Metric Subregularity
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^n\), let \(F:X\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) be set-valued, fix \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\), and put \(S:=F^{-1}(\bar y)\). Distances are Euclidean, with \(\operatorname{dist}(z,\varnothing)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, local, Lipschitzian error bounds are used. Hölder error bounds require a separate exponent and are not included in the defining equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mapping \(F\) is metrically subregular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar y\) with modulus \(\kappa\geq0\) if there exists \(\delta>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq \kappa\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\qquad\forall x\in B(\bar x,\delta).\] Equivalently, the residual \(r_F(x):=\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\) provides a local error bound for the solution set \(S\) at \(\bar x\). For a proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), the stationarity mapping \(F=\partial f\) and \(\bar y=0\) give \[\operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,(\partial f)^{-1}(0)\bigr)\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\] locally around a critical point \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity of a mapping at a solution means that, locally, distance to the solution set is bounded by a constant times the equation residual. Thus a local error bound and metric subregularity are the same inequality after taking the residual to be the distance from the target value to the mapping. Applied to the limiting subdifferential, this bounds distance to the critical set by the stationarity residual.
assumptions_latex: For the subdifferential specialization, \(f\) is proper and lower semicontinuous and \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) with \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is metrically subregular at }(\bar x,\bar y)\iff r_F(x)=\operatorname{dist}(\bar y,F(x))\text{ is a local error-bound residual for }F^{-1}(\bar y).\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(F^{-1}(\bar y)\cap B(\bar x,\delta)\neq\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F^{-1}(\bar y))\leq\kappa r_F(x)\) on \(B(\bar x,\delta)\).
For a single-valued residual map \(R\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,R^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|\) locally.
special_cases_latex: For \(F=\partial f\), the target set is the limiting-critical set \(\operatorname{crit}f=(\partial f)^{-1}(0)\).
Replacing the right side by \(\kappa r_F(x)^q\), \(q\in(0,1]\), gives a Hölder error bound rather than the Lipschitzian definition.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(r_F(x_k)\to0\) and \(x_k\) eventually remains in the defining neighborhood, then \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\to0\).
boundary_notes: Subregularity fixes the target value and is weaker than metric regularity, which quantifies uniformly over nearby target values.
No isolatedness of the reference solution is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error bound controls distance to a closed target set by a nondecreasing function of a residual; linear and Hölder moduli are standard cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let \(S\subset X\) be a nonempty closed set, and let \(r:X\to\mathbb{R}_+\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(r(x)=0\) for every \(x\in S\). Let \(\psi:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+\) be nondecreasing with \(\psi(0)=0\), and let \(U\subset X\) be a neighborhood of \(S\). A local error bound with modulus \(\psi\) holds on \(U\) when \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\psi\!\left(r(x)\right)\qquad(x\in U).\] The linear case has \(\psi(t)=\kappa t\) with \(\kappa>0\), while a Hölder case has \(\psi(t)=\kappa t^q\) with \(\kappa>0\) and \(q\in(0,1]\).
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and \(S\subset X\) is nonempty and closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\psi(r(x))\) holds for every \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual control of distance to a target solution or stationary set.

notation.meaning: closed target solution or stationary set

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Subregularity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity bounds distance to an inverse image by the residual distance from a fixed target value to the mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) be a set-valued mapping between finite-dimensional normed spaces, and let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). The mapping \(F\) is metrically subregular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar y\) if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(x,F^{-1}(\bar y)\right)\le\kappa\,\operatorname{dist}\!\left(\bar y,F(x)\right)\qquad(x\in U).\] The least admissible \(\kappa\), interpreted as an infimum, is the local subregularity modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) is set-valued between finite-dimensional normed spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inverse-image error bound holds locally at \(\bar x\) for the fixed value \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local inverse-image error bound for a set-valued mapping.

notation.meaning: solution set for the inclusion ȳ∈F(x)

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the metric-subregularity leaf. Its finite-dimensional specialization and local-modulus convention require an inspectable source locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Transfer to KL Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex objective, a local subdifferential error bound yields a power-type KL residual inequality for which one-half is an admissible exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\), and write \(f_*=\min f\). Suppose that for some neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\) and some \(\kappa>0\), \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)\] for every \(x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). Then every \(x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) satisfies \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x)\right)\ge\kappa^{-1/2}\left(f(x)-f_*\right)^{1/2}.\] Consequently, on every sufficiently small positive-value slice contained in \(U\), \(f\) admits a power-type KL inequality with exponent \(1/2\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
There are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\) and \(\kappa>0\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\) for every \(x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}\partial f\).

children.title: Objective Growth Condition Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Objective growth around points or solution sets.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(S\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}f\) be nonempty, and let \(f_*=f|_S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is local around a point or compact subset of minimizers. It describes value growth and does not assume convexity, differentiability, or uniqueness of a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an exponent \(p>0\), the function \(f\) has local \(p\)-growth relative to \(S\) at \(\bar x\in S\) if there exist \(c>0\) and \(\delta>0\) such that \[f(x)-f_*\geq c\,\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p\qquad\forall x\in B(\bar x,\delta).\] It has uniform local \(p\)-growth along a compact set \(S_0\subseteq S\) if the same constants work whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S_0)<\delta\). The case \(p=1\) is sharp or linear growth; \(p=2\) is quadratic growth. More generally, a growth modulus \(\omega:[0,\delta)\to\mathbb R_+\) defines \(\omega\)-growth through \(f(x)-f_*\geq\omega(\operatorname{dist}(x,S))\), where \(\omega(0)=0\) and \(\omega(t)>0\) for \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective has local order-p growth around its minimizer set when its value gap is at least a positive constant times the pth power of the distance to that set. Linear growth is the sharpest named power case, while quadratic growth is the standard second-order case. A general growth hierarchy is obtained by replacing the power with any positive modulus vanishing only at zero.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\operatorname{argmin}f\) is nonempty and \(f\) is constant with finite value \(f_*\) on \(S\).
\(\bar x\in S\) for the pointwise-local definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f_*\geq c\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p\) for every sufficiently nearby \(x\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The power-growth inequality is equivalent to \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq c^{-1/p}(f(x)-f_*)^{1/p}\) on the same neighborhood.
For \(\omega(t)=ct^p\), the associated value-gap error-bound exponent is \(1/p\).
special_cases_latex: \(p=1\): \(f(x)-f_*\geq c\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\), called sharp or weak-sharp growth.
\(p=2\): \(f(x)-f_*\geq c\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\), called quadratic growth.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any sequence in the defining neighborhood with \(f(x_k)\downarrow f_*\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\to0\).
boundary_notes: Growth relative to the complete minimizer set is weaker than growth relative to one selected minimizer when minimizers are nonisolated.
The order comparison between different exponents is local and depends on restricting distances below one.

notation.meaning: Common objective value on the selected minimizer set.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Growth Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local order-p growth means that objective excess dominates a positive multiple of the pth power of distance to the designated minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, let \(S\subset\operatorname{argmin}f\) be nonempty and closed, and suppose \(f\) is constant on \(S\) with value \(f_*\). The function \(f\) has local growth of order \(p>0\) relative to \(S\) if there exist \(c>0\) and an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\) such that
\[
f(x)\ge f_*+c\,\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p
\]
for every \(x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}f\). When \(S=\{\bar x\}\), this is pointwise local growth at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f_*\ge c\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p\) locally for some \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local order-p growth relative to a local-minimizer set.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from x to S

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but the cited section on local optimality does not inspectably support the extended-real, order-p, setwise formulation. An authoritative variational-analysis locator for growth relative to a closed minimizer set is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Growth Conditions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth requires objective excess to dominate squared distance to the relevant minimizer set in a neighborhood of that set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and let \(S\subset\operatorname{argmin}f\) be nonempty and closed, with \(f|_S=f_*\). The quadratic-growth condition relative to \(S\) holds if there exist \(c>0\) and an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\) such that
\[
f(x)-f_*\ge \frac{c}{2}\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2
\]
for all \(x\in U\cap\operatorname{dom}f\). For \(S=\{\bar x\}\), the condition becomes \(f(x)-f(\bar x)\ge (c/2)\|x-\bar x\|^2\) locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f_*\ge \frac{c}{2}\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\) locally for some \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Setwise quadratic growth near a closed set of minimizers.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The stated setwise quadratic-growth condition is precise and appropriately classified as a condition. The cited strong-local-minimum section appears directed to pointwise smooth growth and does not confirm the distance-to-set extension.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Versus Setwise Growth
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise growth forces an isolated minimizer; setwise growth permits a continuum of minimizers, as shown by the function x1 squared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f(x)-f(\bar x)\ge c\|x-\bar x\|^p\) locally for some \(c>0\), then \(\bar x\) is an isolated local minimizer. Setwise growth \(f(x)-f_*\ge c\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^p\) need not isolate points of \(S\). Indeed, for \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2\) and \(S=\{0\}\times\mathbb{R}\), one has
\[
f(x_1,x_2)=\operatorname{dist}((x_1,x_2),S)^2,
\]
so setwise quadratic growth holds globally, while pointwise quadratic growth fails at every \(\bar x\in S\) because other minimizers occur arbitrarily near \(\bar x\).
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a set on which \(f\) has the constant value \(f_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise growth implies local isolation, whereas setwise growth does not.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of isolated-minimizer growth with growth relative to a minimizer set.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise-isolation implication and the setwise counterexample are mathematically consistent and fit the comparison leaf, but no inspectable source supports the general comparison claim.

children.title: PL Gradient-Dominance Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Smooth value-gap regularity and its relationship to special KL regimes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, let \(f:U\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and bounded below, and assume \(S=\operatorname{argmin}_U f\neq\varnothing\) with value \(f_*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the smooth finite-dimensional PL condition. It need not imply convexity, strong convexity, or uniqueness of minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) satisfies the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition with constant \(\mu>0\) on \(V\subseteq U\) if \[\frac12\|\nabla f(x)\|^2\geq\mu\bigl(f(x)-f_*\bigr)\qquad\forall x\in V.\] If \(V=U\), the condition is global; if \(V=B(\bar x,\delta)\cap\{f_*<f<f_*+\eta\}\), it is local at \(\bar x\in S\). On points with positive value gap this is exactly the smooth KL inequality with power desingularizer \(\varphi(s)=\sqrt{2s/\mu}\), because \(\varphi'(s)=1/\sqrt{2\mu s}\) and hence \(\varphi'(f(x)-f_*)\|\nabla f(x)\|\geq1\). Thus PL gradient dominance is the smooth KL power regime with KL exponent \(1/2\), under the convention \(\varphi(s)=cs^{1-\theta}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The PL condition bounds the objective gap by the squared gradient norm. It may hold for nonconvex functions and for functions with nonunique minimizers. In the smooth setting it is precisely the KL inequality with a square-root desingularizing function, equivalently KL exponent one half under the usual power convention.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu>0\) and the inequality is required on the declared set \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac12\|\nabla f(x)\|^2\geq\mu(f(x)-f_*)\) on \(V\), equivalently \(\varphi'(f(x)-f_*)\|\nabla f(x)\|\geq1\) with \(\varphi(s)=\sqrt{2s/\mu}\).
special_cases_latex: A positive-semidefinite quadratic \(f(x)=\frac12x^\top Ax\) satisfies PL with \(\mu\) equal to the smallest positive eigenvalue of \(A\), even when \(A\) is singular.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every stationary point in \(V\) is globally minimizing relative to the reference value \(f_*\).
boundary_notes: PL does not by itself provide a distance-to-solution error bound without additional structure.
The correspondence stated here uses the smooth gradient; nonsmooth KL conditions use a subdifferential slope.

notation.meaning: KL exponent in the power desingularizer convention.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.8, equation (3.45) and the paragraph identifying PL as a special KL condition
