knowledge_statements.title: Escape-to-Infinity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decreasing objective sequence may still diverge spatially: for the exponential objective, iterates moving to positive infinity have no cluster point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Descent alone does not prevent escape to infinity. For \(F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) defined by \(F(x)=e^{-x}\), the sequence \(x_k=k\) satisfies \[F(x_{k+1})<F(x_k),\qquad F(x_k)\downarrow0,\qquad |x_k|\to\infty.\] Its initial sublevel set \(\{x:F(x)\le F(x_0)\}=[0,\infty)\) is unbounded, and the sequence has no cluster point in \(\mathbb{R}\). Thus monotone objective decrease and convergence of objective values cannot replace a boundedness or compactness hypothesis in the abstract KL architecture.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)\downarrow0\) while \(|x_k|\to\infty\), so \((x_k)\) has no finite cluster point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of compactness when descent does not confine iterates to a bounded sublevel set.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The explicit exponential counterexample is mathematically correct and the failure_boundary kind fits the container, but the evidence contract requires a source or an explicit standard-field rationale; neither is supplied.

children.title: KL Convergence Consequences
children.top_down_role: The qualitative conclusions supplied by the abstract architecture.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \((x^k)_{k\ge0}\subset\operatorname{dom}F\) be a bounded descent trajectory to which a local Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz inequality and compatible descent and relative-error conditions apply.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a definition of the qualitative conclusion package targeted by an abstract discrete KL analysis, not a theorem asserting that unspecified algorithms satisfy it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The trajectory has the qualitative KL convergence-consequence package at \(x^\star\) if: its total length is finite, \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|<\infty\); the entire sequence converges, \(x^k\to x^\star\); the limit is limiting-critical, \(0\in\partial F(x^\star)\); the objective values converge compatibly, \(F(x^k)\to F(x^\star)\); and the cluster set collapses, \(\omega(x^0)=\{x^\star\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The qualitative KL consequence package consists of finite trajectory length, convergence of every iterate to one point, limiting criticality of that point, convergence of objective values to its objective value, and collapse of the cluster set to the singleton containing that limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|<\infty,\quad x^k\to x^\star,\quad 0\in\partial F(x^\star),\quad F(x^k)\to F(x^\star),\quad \omega(x^0)=\{x^\star\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In a complete normed space, finite length makes the trajectory Cauchy and therefore supplies whole-sequence convergence.
For a relatively compact sequence, whole-sequence convergence to \(x^\star\) is equivalent to the assertion that its cluster set is the singleton \(\{x^\star\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(F\in C^1\), the criticality component is \(\nabla F(x^\star)=0\).
For a composite objective \(F=f+g\), the criticality component is \(0\in\nabla f(x^\star)+\partial g(x^\star)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Persistent wandering among distinct cluster points is excluded.
The tail displacement satisfies \(\|x^k-x^\star\|\le\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}\|x^{j+1}-x^j\|\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not itself supply rate estimates.
Finite length is stronger than mere convergence.
Criticality need not mean local or global optimality in a nonconvex problem.

notation.meaning: cluster set of the iterate sequence

review_flags: No inspected source was available for the exact abstract KL consequence package.
The hypotheses under which a theorem yields this package must be sourced independently.

children.title: Finite-Length Trajectories
children.top_down_role: Summable motion and exclusion of persistent wandering.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Length Trajectories
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the abstract KL descent hypotheses, total inter-iterate motion is summable, so trajectory tails cannot keep wandering by a positive distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_k)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy the sufficient-decrease, relative-error, compactness, and limit-compatibility hypotheses of an abstract KL convergence theorem for a proper lower-semicontinuous objective \(F\). If \(F\) has the KL property at every point of the trajectory cluster set, then the trajectory has finite length: \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|<\infty.\] In particular, the tail displacement satisfies \(\|x_m-x_k\|\le\sum_{i=k}^{m-1}\|x_{i+1}-x_i\|\to0\) uniformly over \(m>k\), excluding persistent wandering.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and KL on the trajectory cluster set.
The sequence satisfies sufficient decrease and a relative-error bound.
The trajectory is precompact and limit-compatible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summability consequence produced by the abstract KL descent argument.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Finite length is the correct kind of consequence for this container, but the statement refers collectively to an unspecified abstract KL theorem. A source is needed to fix and verify the exact sufficient-decrease, relative-error, compactness, limit-compatibility, and KL-uniformization hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space and let \((x^k)_{k\ge0}\subset X\). In a normed space, take \(d(x,y)=\|x-y\|\). For \(k\ge0\), define the remaining path length \(L_k=\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}d(x^{j+1},x^j)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is metric and applies independently of smoothness, convexity, or the particular optimization algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The discrete trajectory \((x^k)\) has finite length if \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}d(x^{k+1},x^k)<\infty\). Equivalently, \(L_0<\infty\), or the partial polygonal lengths \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}d(x^{k+1},x^k)\) are uniformly bounded in \(N\). Under this condition, \(L_k\downarrow0\) and \(d(x^m,x^k)\le L_k\) for all \(m>k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete trajectory has finite length when the sum of all distances between successive iterates is finite. This is absolute summability of motion, not merely convergence of the individual step sizes to zero. Its tail length tends to zero and uniformly controls every later displacement from the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{len}(x):=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}d(x^{k+1},x^k)<\infty.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The nonnegative tail series \(L_k\) is finite for every \(k\) and satisfies \(L_k\to0\).
special_cases_latex: In \(\mathbb R^n\), finite length implies that \((x^k)\) is a Cauchy sequence and hence converges.
If the sequence becomes constant after some index, it automatically has finite length.
immediate_consequences_latex: Successive steps satisfy \(d(x^{k+1},x^k)\to0\).
In any complete metric space, the trajectory converges to some \(x^\star\).
For its limit \(x^\star\), one has \(d(x^k,x^\star)\le L_k\).
boundary_notes: The converse is false: a convergent sequence can have infinite total length.
The condition \(d(x^{k+1},x^k)\to0\) does not imply finite length.
Finite length alone does not identify the limit as critical for an objective.

notation.meaning: remaining path length from iterate k onward

review_flags: The mathematical definition is standard, but no supplied locator was inspected and verified for this exact metric formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-length discrete trajectory

children.title: Whole-Sequence Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence beyond accumulation-point or subsequence guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Whole-Sequence Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite length makes the full trajectory Cauchy and therefore convergent; compatibility additionally identifies its limit as critical.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_k)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a trajectory satisfying the hypotheses of the abstract KL finite-length result. Then there exists \(x_\star\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \[x_k\to x_\star.\] Indeed, finite length makes \((x_k)\) a Cauchy sequence, while completeness of \(\mathbb{R}^n\) supplies its limit. If limit-criticality compatibility also holds, then \(0\in\partial F(x_\star)\). Thus the conclusion concerns the entire sequence and is stronger than the existence of a convergent subsequence.
assumptions_latex: Limit-criticality compatibility holds when the criticality conclusion is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x_\star\) with \(x_k\to x_\star\); under compatibility, \(0\in\partial F(x_\star)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convergence of the entire KL trajectory, not merely selected subsequences.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The finite-length-to-whole-sequence-convergence implication is mathematically coherent in Euclidean space and theorem is an appropriate content kind. The record nevertheless depends on an uncited abstract KL finite-length result and an uncited compatibility mechanism for the criticality addendum.

children.title: Limiting Criticality
children.top_down_role: Identification of the limit through the chosen stationarity notion.

knowledge_statements.title: Limiting Criticality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Attentive convergence and vanishing limiting subgradients imply that the trajectory limit is a limiting critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and suppose \(x_k\to x_\star\) with \(F(x_k)\to F(x_\star)\). If there exist \(w_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) such that \(w_k\to0\), then \[0\in\partial F(x_\star).\] In particular, a relative-error estimate \(\|w_{k+1}\|\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\), together with finite length, supplies \(w_k\to0\) and therefore identifies the whole-sequence limit as a limiting critical point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial F(x_\star)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity of the trajectory limit in the limiting-subdifferential sense.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem matches limiting criticality and states the necessary attentive convergence and vanishing-subgradient hypotheses. An authoritative source with a precise locator is still required for sequential closedness of the limiting subdifferential and for the KL-trajectory specialization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting-critical point of an extended-real objective
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(\widehat\partial F\) denote the Fréchet subdifferential, and let \(\partial F\) denote the limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional variational-analysis definition for nonsmooth, nonconvex extended-real objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\), the limiting subdifferential is \(\partial F(x)=\{v:\exists x^j\to x,\ F(x^j)\to F(x),\ v^j\to v,\ v^j\in\widehat\partial F(x^j)\}\). The point \(x^\star\) is limiting-critical for \(F\) if \(0\in\partial F(x^\star)\), equivalently \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^\star))=0\). A convergent trajectory has a limiting-critical limit when \(x^k\to x^\star\) and this inclusion holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is limiting-critical when the zero vector belongs to its limiting subdifferential. The limiting subdifferential consists of limits of Fréchet subgradients taken at nearby points whose positions and objective values converge compatibly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x^\star\in\operatorname{crit}F\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial F(x^\star).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(\partial F(x^\star)\) is closed, \(0\in\partial F(x^\star)\) is equivalent to \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^\star))=0\).
For differentiable \(F\), limiting criticality is equivalent to \(\nabla F(x^\star)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For convex proper lower-semicontinuous \(F\), \(0\in\partial F(x^\star)\) is equivalent to global minimality.
For \(F=f+\delta_C\), with smooth \(f\) and closed \(C\) under an applicable sum rule, criticality is \(0\in\nabla f(x^\star)+N_C(x^\star)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A limiting-critical point is first-order stationary in the selected nonsmooth sense.
For nonconvex \(F\), limiting criticality alone does not distinguish minimizers, maximizers, and saddle-type points.
boundary_notes: The limiting and Clarke subdifferentials need not coincide.
Membership in \(\operatorname{dom}F\) is required.
Criticality is necessary for many local minima but is not sufficient for local optimality.

notation.meaning: indicator function of a set C

review_flags: A precise variational-analysis source locator for the limiting-subdifferential definition was not supplied or inspected.

children.title: Cluster-Set Collapse
children.top_down_role: Exclusion of nontrivial connected sets of distinct trajectory limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Set Collapse
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once a precompact trajectory has finite length, all convergent subsequences share one limit and the cluster set is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_k)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) have finite length, and assume it has at least one cluster point \(x_\star\). Then \((x_k)\) converges to \(x_\star\), and its cluster set collapses to the singleton \[\omega(x_0)=\{x_\star\}.\] Hence no two distinct points can be subsequential limits. In the abstract KL setting, precompactness supplies a cluster point and the KL finite-length conclusion supplies uniqueness, thereby excluding convergence toward a nontrivial connected continuum of critical points.
assumptions_latex: The sequence \((x_k)\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) has a cluster point \(x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to x_\star\) and \(\omega(x_0)=\{x_\star\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite length reduces the trajectory cluster set to its unique whole-sequence limit.

notation.meaning: cluster set of the trajectory starting from x_0

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The finite-length argument correctly forces convergence and singleton cluster-set collapse, and property fits the container. No source or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied for this nontrivial recorded claim or its abstract KL specialization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Collapse of a trajectory cluster set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space and let \((x^k)_{k\ge0}\subset X\). Define \(\omega(x^0)=\{\bar x\in X:\exists k_j\uparrow\infty,\ x^{k_j}\to\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological trajectory property. Relative compactness is separated from collapse because a sequence may have an empty cluster set in a noncompact setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cluster set of \((x^k)\) collapses at \(x^\star\) if it is nonempty and \(\omega(x^0)=\{x^\star\}\). Equivalently, every convergent subsequence has the same limit \(x^\star\), and at least one such subsequence exists. If the trajectory is relatively compact, cluster-set collapse is equivalent to whole-sequence convergence \(x^k\to x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cluster-set collapse means that the trajectory has at least one accumulation point and that every convergent subsequence converges to the same point. With relative compactness, this rules out persistent wandering and forces the entire sequence to converge.
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exists a subsequence converging to \(x^\star\), and every convergent subsequence of \((x^k)\) has limit \(x^\star\).
For a relatively compact metric sequence, \(\omega(x^0)=\{x^\star\}\) if and only if \(x^k\to x^\star\).
special_cases_latex: Every convergent sequence has a collapsed cluster set.
A finite-length trajectory in a complete metric space has a singleton cluster set at its limit.
immediate_consequences_latex: Distinct trajectory limits are excluded.
A nontrivial connected continuum of cluster points is excluded.
Under continuity of \(F\), all subsequential objective limits equal \(F(x^\star)\).
boundary_notes: A set with at most one cluster point is not necessarily a collapsed cluster set because it may be empty.
Uniqueness of critical points in an objective sublevel set is stronger than cluster-set collapse.
Without relative compactness, a singleton cluster set does not by itself control subsequences escaping every compact set.

notation.meaning: cluster or omega-limit set of the discrete trajectory

review_flags: The hinted limit-point geometry source was not inspected, so it is not cited.
A locator supporting the exact singleton-cluster-set formulation is required.

children.title: KL Rate Architecture
children.top_down_role: Rate regimes and observables organized by local desingularization geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(x^k\to x^\star\), and put \(r_k=F(x^k)-F(x^\star)\ge0\). Suppose a local power-type KL inequality is expressed by \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\ge c(F(x)-F(x^\star))^\theta\), with \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local discrete KL analysis after entry into a neighborhood where the power-type inequality and algorithmic descent estimates are valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KL rate architecture is the organized association of a local exponent \(\theta\), a desingularizing function \(\varphi(s)=a s^{1-\theta}\) with \(a>0\), and separately named observables: objective gap \(r_k\), iterate error \(e_k=\|x^k-x^\star\|\), step size \(s_k=\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\), tail length \(L_k=\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}s_j\), and stationarity residual \(g_k=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^k))\). A rate statement belongs to the architecture only when it specifies the observable, exponent or contraction factor, constants, and the index from which the estimate holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KL rate architecture pairs the local desingularization geometry, usually summarized by a power exponent, with explicit rate observables. Objective gaps, distances to the limit, step lengths, remaining path lengths, and stationarity residuals are kept distinct because their exponents and required assumptions need not coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal R_{\mathrm{KL}}=(\theta,\varphi;\ r_k,e_k,s_k,L_k,g_k),\qquad \varphi(s)=a s^{1-\theta}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the stated power function, \(\varphi'(s)=a(1-\theta)s^{-\theta}\), so the KL inequality \(\varphi'(F(x)-F(x^\star))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\ge1\) is equivalent to a lower bound proportional to \((F(x)-F(x^\star))^\theta\).
special_cases_latex: The regime \(\theta=0\) is associated with finite termination under standard discrete KL descent hypotheses.
The range \(0<\theta\le\tfrac12\) is associated with geometric behavior, while \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\) is associated with polynomial behavior, subject to the chosen KL convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: Rate claims for different observables can be compared without treating them as identical.
The tail-length estimate directly controls iterate distance through \(e_k\le L_k\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x^k\to x^\star\) be a discrete descent trajectory for \(F\), and suppose the local KL inequality uses \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\ge c(F(x)-F(x^\star))^\theta\) with \(\theta\in[0,1)\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local qualitative classification under the stated exponent convention; individual observable exponents are not identified by this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard KL rate regime associated with \(\theta\) is classified as follows: \(\theta=0\) is the finite-termination regime; \(0<\theta\le\tfrac12\) is the linear-geometric regime; and \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\) is the sublinear-polynomial regime. The classification records the qualitative asymptotic form after the trajectory enters the KL neighborhood, while every quantitative statement must separately identify whether it concerns objective gap, iterate distance, path length, step size, or stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated power-type KL convention and standard descent framework, exponent zero corresponds to finite termination, exponents up to one half correspond to geometric convergence, and exponents above one half correspond to polynomial convergence. This classification is qualitative and does not make the rates of different observables interchangeable.

special_cases_latex: The boundary value \(\theta=\tfrac12\) belongs to the geometric regime in this convention.

children.title: Finite-Termination Regime
children.top_down_role: The sharpest KL rate class.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Termination Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With KL exponent zero, sufficient decrease and relative error force the convergent trajectory to reach its limit after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(x_k\to x_\star\) with \(F(x_k)\downarrow F(x_\star)\). Assume that, for all sufficiently large \(k\), \(F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\), \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x_{k+1}))\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\), and the KL inequality holds with exponent \(\theta=0\). Then there exists \(K<\infty\) such that \[x_k=x_\star\quad\text{and}\quad F(x_k)=F(x_\star)\qquad\text{for every }k\ge K.\]
assumptions_latex: The KL inequality near \(x_\star\) has exponent \(\theta=0\), and \(x_k\to x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(K\in\mathbb{N}\) such that \(x_k=x_\star\) for all \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL exponent-zero regime under quadratic sufficient decrease and relative error.

notation.meaning: KL exponent in the power-type desingularizing function

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is plausible under the stated descent, relative-error, convergence, and exponent-zero assumptions, and its kind matches the rate-regime container. A source is essential because the exponent convention and the exact local KL inequality determine whether the finite-termination conclusion follows as stated.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite termination of a discrete KL trajectory
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x^k)_{k\ge0}\subset X\) be a discrete trajectory in a metric space, let \(x^\star\in X\), and, when an objective is present, let \(r_k=F(x^k)-F(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact discrete termination, distinguished from convergence within a tolerance and from finite identification followed by continued motion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The trajectory is in the finite-termination regime at \(x^\star\) if there exists \(K\in\mathbb N\) such that \(x^k=x^\star\) for every \(k\ge K\). Consequently, all later steps and tail lengths vanish. If the objective gap uniquely identifies \(x^\star\) on the trajectory tail, the condition is equivalently \(r_k=0\) for every \(k\ge K\). In the power-type KL classification using exponent \(\theta\), this is the regime conventionally associated with \(\theta=0\) under standard sufficient-decrease and relative-error hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite termination means that an exact iterate reaches the limiting point after finitely many updates and every subsequent iterate remains there. It is stronger than geometric convergence and stronger than satisfying a numerical stopping tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists K\in\mathbb N\quad\forall k\ge K:\quad x^k=x^\star.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\exists K\) such that \(d(x^{k+1},x^k)=0\) for every \(k\ge K\) and \(x^K=x^\star\).
The remaining path length satisfies \(L_K=0\).
special_cases_latex: An algorithm whose update map fixes every critical point remains at \(x^\star\) after first reaching it.
For a uniquely identifying nonnegative gap, eventual equality \(r_k=0\) is equivalent to eventual equality \(x^k=x^\star\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The trajectory has finite length.
Every standard nonnegative error observable is eventually zero.
Whole-sequence convergence to \(x^\star\) is immediate.
boundary_notes: Finite identification of an active manifold does not imply finite termination of the iterates.
Floating-point stopping based on a tolerance is not exact finite termination.
The association with \(\theta=0\) requires the surrounding discrete KL hypotheses.

notation.meaning: first or any valid terminal index
remaining path length from the terminal index

children.title: Linear-Geometric Rate Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Locally geometric convergence behavior.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((a_k)_{k\ge0}\) be a nonnegative error sequence associated with a trajectory, such as an objective gap, iterate distance, or remaining path length, and suppose \(a_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local asymptotic rate terminology for a specified scalar observable; no claim is made that all KL observables share the same contraction factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The observable \((a_k)\) converges Q-linearly if there exist \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(K\) such that \(a_{k+1}\le q a_k\) for every \(k\ge K\). It converges R-linearly, or geometrically, if there exist \(C>0\), \(q\in(0,1)\), and \(K\) such that \(a_k\le Cq^{k-K}\) for every \(k\ge K\). Eventual Q-linear convergence implies geometric convergence. In the standard power-type KL convention, the range \(0<\theta\le\tfrac12\) is associated with geometric decay under the full discrete KL hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Q-linear convergence means that the chosen error contracts by a uniform factor below one at every sufficiently late iteration. Geometric or R-linear convergence means that the error is bounded by a constant times a geometric sequence. The observable and the distinction between these two notions must be stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[a_{k+1}\le q a_k\quad(k\ge K),\quad 0<q<1,\qquad\text{or more generally}\qquad a_k\le Cq^{k-K}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The geometric bound is equivalent to \(a_k=O(q^k)\) for some \(q\in(0,1)\).
A Q-linear bound yields \(a_k\le a_Kq^{k-K}\) for all \(k\ge K\).
special_cases_latex: For iterates, R-linear convergence means \(\|x^k-x^\star\|\le Cq^{k-K}\).
For objective values, it means \(0\le F(x^k)-F(x^\star)\le Cq^{k-K}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every geometric rate is faster than every fixed inverse-polynomial bound asymptotically.
A geometric tail-length bound gives the same type of bound for iterate distance.
boundary_notes: R-linear convergence need not imply a one-step Q-linear contraction.
The word linear describes the convergence order, not affine motion of the iterates.
KL geometry alone is insufficient without descent and relative-error estimates.

notation.meaning: the explicitly selected nonnegative rate observable

review_flags: General rate terminology is standard, but no supplied locator was verified for the KL-specific correspondence.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear–geometric convergence correspondence
Linear Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Q-linear convergence means that the iterate error eventually contracts by a fixed factor. R-linear convergence means that the iterate error has a geometric upper bound, and every Q-linearly convergent sequence is R-linearly convergent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\|\cdot\|)\) be a normed space and let \(x_k\to x_\star\). The sequence converges Q-linearly if there exist \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(k_0\in\mathbb N\) such that \(\|x_{k+1}-x_\star\|\le q\|x_k-x_\star\|\) for every \(k\ge k_0\). It converges R-linearly if there exist \(C>0\), \(q\in(0,1)\), and \(k_0\in\mathbb N\) such that \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le Cq^{k-k_0}\) for every \(k\ge k_0\). Q-linear convergence implies R-linear convergence.
assumptions_latex: \((X,\|\cdot\|)\) is a normed space and \(x_k\to x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_{k+1}-x_\star\|\le q\|x_k-x_\star\|\Longrightarrow \|x_k-x_\star\|\le \|x_{k_0}-x_\star\|q^{k-k_0}\) for every \(k\ge k_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Q-linear and R-linear convergence of iterates in the KL linear-rate regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Decay Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative convergence measure decays geometrically when, from some iteration onward, it is bounded by a constant times a fixed ratio raised to the elapsed iteration count. An eventual one-step contraction yields such a bound from the iteration where that contraction begins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((u_k)_{k\ge0}\) be a nonnegative sequence. It lies in the geometric-decay regime if there exist \(C>0\), \(q\in(0,1)\), and \(k_0\in\mathbb N\) such that \(u_k\le Cq^{k-k_0}\) for every \(k\ge k_0\). Equivalently, \(u_k=O(q^k)\) for some \(q\in(0,1)\). If there exist \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(k_1\in\mathbb N\) such that \(u_{k+1}\le q u_k\) for every \(k\ge k_1\), then \(u_k\le u_{k_1}q^{k-k_1}\) for every \(k\ge k_1\), so the sequence has geometric decay.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_{k+1}\le q u_k\) for every \(k\ge k_1\Longrightarrow u_k\le u_{k_1}q^{k-k_1}\) for every \(k\ge k_1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric decay of a nonnegative KL convergence observable.

knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Measure Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two eventually comparable error measures have the same geometric decay factor, so either both exhibit a linear-geometric rate or neither does.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((u_k)\) and \((v_k)\) be nonnegative sequences. Suppose there exist \(c_1,c_2>0\) and \(k_0\in\mathbb N\) such that \(c_1u_k\le v_k\le c_2u_k\) for every \(k\ge k_0\). Then, for every \(q\in(0,1)\), \(u_k=O(q^k)\) if and only if \(v_k=O(q^k)\). Hence linear-geometric classification is invariant under eventual two-sided multiplicative equivalence, although the bounding constants may differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_k=O(q^k)\Longleftrightarrow v_k=O(q^k)\) for each \(q\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers geometric rates between comparable nonnegative convergence measures.

children.title: Sublinear Regime
children.top_down_role: Polynomially decaying convergence behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Sublinear Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For KL exponent above one half, standard descent and relative-error hypotheses yield polynomial decay of objective gaps and iterate distances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(x_k\to x_\star\) satisfy sufficient decrease and relative error. Set \(s_k=f(x_k)-f(x_\star)\). If near \(x_\star\) the KL desingularizer is \(\varphi(s)=cs^{1-\theta}\) with \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), then there exist \(C_1,C_2>0\) and \(k_0\) such that, for \(k\ge k_0\), \(s_k\le C_1k^{-1/(2\theta-1)}\) and \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le C_2k^{-(1-\theta)/(2\theta-1)}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard KL-exponent rate for sufficient-descent sequences with relative error.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial exponents are plausible under a standard KL convention, but this theorem requires a KL-specific source to verify the exponent convention and all convergence hypotheses. Proper lower semicontinuity, iterate convergence, sufficient decrease, and relative error alone may omit the value-continuity or attentive-convergence condition used by the intended abstract theorem.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((a_k)_{k\ge0}\) be a nonnegative error observable satisfying \(a_k\to0\). In a power-type KL setting, use the exponent convention \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\ge c(F(x)-F(x^\star))^\theta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local asymptotic classification of a specified observable. The definition separates generic polynomial decay from observable-specific exponents derived under additional hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The observable is in a polynomial sublinear regime if there exist \(C>0\), \(p>0\), and \(K\) such that \(a_k\le C(k-K+1)^{-p}\) for every \(k\ge K\), while no geometric bound is asserted. In the standard power-type KL classification, \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\) corresponds to polynomial decay under the complete discrete KL assumptions. For the commonly obtained objective-gap recurrence, the characteristic gap exponent is \(p=1/(2\theta-1)\); rates for iterate distance, motion, and residuals must be stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rate observable is polynomially sublinear when it is eventually bounded by a negative power of the iteration count. In the standard KL exponent convention, exponents above one half lead to this qualitative regime under suitable descent and relative-error conditions. The polynomial power depends on which quantity is measured.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists C>0,\ p>0,\ K:\quad a_k\le C(k-K+1)^{-p}\quad\forall k\ge K.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The bound can be written \(a_k=O(k^{-p})\).
For a positive sequence, polynomial decay implies \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}a_k^{1/k}\le1\), but does not supply a contraction factor below one.
special_cases_latex: For the standard KL objective-gap recurrence and \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\), one commonly obtains \(F(x^k)-F(x^\star)=O(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)})\).
An iterate-distance rate may have a different exponent even when derived from the same KL parameter.
immediate_consequences_latex: The observable converges to zero.
The rate is slower than a geometric bound of fixed ratio when the polynomial order is sharp.
boundary_notes: The displayed objective-gap exponent is not automatically the exponent for stationarity residuals or iterate distances.
A big-O polynomial upper bound alone does not exclude the possibility of a faster actual rate.
Exponent conventions and recurrence hypotheses must be checked before applying the KL correspondence.

children.title: KL Rate Observables

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical observables for KL trajectory rates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(x^k\to x^\star\), assume \(F(x^k)\ge F(x^\star)\), and suppose the trajectory has finite length when a tail-length observable is used.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete finite-dimensional KL analysis; the definition catalogs observables and does not assert a universal rate relation among them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The canonical KL rate observables are the objective gap \(r_k=F(x^k)-F(x^\star)\), iterate distance \(e_k=\|x^k-x^\star\|\), step or motion size \(s_k=\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\), remaining path length \(L_k=\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}s_j\), and stationarity residual \(g_k=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^k))\). A KL rate statement is observable-specific when it gives an eventual bound for at least one named sequence, with its constants and exponent or contraction factor, without silently transferring that bound to the other observables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KL rate observables are the distinct measurable quantities whose decay may be estimated: objective error, distance to the limit, individual step size, remaining trajectory length, and a first-order stationarity residual. A valid rate statement names the quantity being bounded because these sequences are related but generally have different rate formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal O_k=(r_k,e_k,s_k,L_k,g_k)=\bigl(F(x^k)-F(x^\star),\ \|x^k-x^\star\|,\ \|x^{k+1}-x^k\|,\ \sum_{j=k}^{\infty}\|x^{j+1}-x^j\|,\ \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^k))\bigr).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The motion observables satisfy \(s_k=L_k-L_{k+1}\) whenever \(L_k<\infty\).
The iterate error is controlled by tail length: \(e_k\le L_k\).
special_cases_latex: For smooth \(F\), \(g_k=\|\nabla F(x^k)\|\).
For composite \(F=f+g\), a proximal-gradient mapping may replace or bound the limiting-subgradient residual when the appropriate comparison is established.
immediate_consequences_latex: A rate for \(L_k\) immediately bounds \(e_k\).
Objective convergence and stationarity-residual convergence remain logically distinct without an error bound.
boundary_notes: The observables may be undefined or infinite without their stated domain and finite-length assumptions.
A rate for objective values does not automatically give the same rate for iterates.
Algorithm-specific residuals require an explicit comparison with \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^k))\).
review_flags: No inspected locator was available for this complete KL-observable catalog.
Algorithm-specific residual equivalences require separate evidence.

children.title: Iterate-Distance Rates

knowledge_statements.title: Iterate-Distance Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterate convergence is measured by distance to a chosen limit or to the solution set, bounded by a prescribed sequence tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\|\cdot\|)\) be a normed space, let \(S\subset X\) be nonempty, and define \(d_k=\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)=\inf_{z\in S}\|x_k-z\|\). An iterate-distance rate is a bound \(d_k\le \rho_k\) with \(\rho_k\downarrow0\). For a specified limit \(x_\star\in S\), the pointwise form is \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le\rho_k\). If \(S=\{x_\star\}\), the setwise and pointwise measures coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a nonempty subset of a normed space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,S)\le\rho_k\to0\), or \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le\rho_k\to0\) for a specified limit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterate rates expressed relative to a limit point or solution set.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Value Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective convergence is quantified by bounding the nonnegative gap between the current value and the limiting or optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(x_k\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(f_\star\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(f(x_k)\ge f_\star\). Define \(s_k=f(x_k)-f_\star\). An objective-value rate is a bound \(0\le s_k\le\rho_k\), where \(\rho_k\to0\). Geometric rates use \(\rho_k=Cq^k\) with \(q\in(0,1)\); polynomial rates use \(\rho_k=Ck^{-p}\) with \(p>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f(x_k)-f_\star\le\rho_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence rates expressed through nonnegative objective-value gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Trajectory-Motion Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Motion rates bound either each step or the untraveled tail length; a vanishing finite tail also bounds distance to the eventual limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_k)\) lie in a normed space and define the step \(\Delta_k=\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\) and tail length \(L_k=\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}\Delta_j\), whenever the series is finite. A trajectory-motion rate consists of bounds \(\Delta_k\le\alpha_k\) or \(L_k\le\rho_k\), with the relevant envelope tending to zero. If \(L_k<\infty\), then \((x_k)\) is Cauchy and, in a complete space, converges to some \(x_\star\) with \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le L_k\).
assumptions_latex: The iterates lie in a normed space.
The tail series defining \(L_k\) is finite when a tail-length rate is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_k\le\alpha_k\) or \(L_k\le\rho_k\); if the space is complete, then \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le L_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rates for individual steps and the remaining trajectory length.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x^k)_{k\ge0}\) be a finite-length trajectory in a normed space. Define \(s_k=\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\) and \(L_k=\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}s_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete motion-based rates, distinct from objective-gap, iterate-distance, and stationarity-residual rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trajectory-motion rate is an eventual quantitative bound on either the one-step motion \(s_k\) or the remaining motion \(L_k\). A geometric motion rate has \(s_k\le C_s q^{k-K}\) or \(L_k\le C_Lq^{k-K}\) for some \(q\in(0,1)\). A polynomial motion rate has \(s_k\le C_s(k-K+1)^{-p_s}\) or \(L_k\le C_L(k-K+1)^{-p_L}\) for positive exponents. Because \(s_k=L_k-L_{k+1}\) and \(\|x^k-x^\star\|\le L_k\), the tail-length observable is the direct motion certificate for convergence to the limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trajectory-motion rates measure either how far one update moves or how much total path remains after an iterate. The remaining-path observable is stronger for locating the limit because it bounds the distance from the current iterate to that limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_k:=\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|,\qquad L_k:=\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}s_j,\qquad s_k=L_k-L_{k+1},\qquad \|x^k-x^\star\|\le L_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A geometric tail-motion rate is \(L_k=O(q^k)\) for some \(q\in(0,1)\).
A polynomial tail-motion rate is \(L_k=O(k^{-p_L})\) for some \(p_L>0\).
special_cases_latex: Finite termination is characterized by \(L_K=0\) for some finite \(K\).
For a convergent finite-length trajectory, a bound on \(L_k\) is automatically an iterate-distance bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(L_k\to0\), persistent motion of positive total tail length is excluded.
A geometric tail-length rate yields geometric convergence of the iterates.
Summability of \((s_k)\) is precisely finite trajectory length.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity-Residual Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity convergence is quantified by bounding a subgradient distance, gradient norm, or specified first-order residual by a vanishing envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(x_k\in\operatorname{dom}f\). Define \(r_k=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_k))\). A stationarity-residual rate is a bound \(r_k\le\rho_k\) with \(\rho_k\to0\). For smooth unconstrained \(f\), this becomes \(r_k=\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\); for a specified residual mapping \(R\), the analogous measure is \(r_k=\|R(x_k)\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_k))\le\rho_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rates expressed through subgradient slope or another first-order residual.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation is plausible and internally consistent, but it lacks an inspectable source for the limiting-subdifferential residual and its smooth and residual-mapping specializations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \((x^k)\subset\operatorname{dom}F\), and define \(g_k=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^k))\). An algorithm may instead produce a residual \(R_k\ge0\) comparable with \(g_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonsmooth first-order residuals; an algorithm-specific mapping is included only after an explicit comparison with the limiting-subgradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stationarity-residual rate is an eventual bound on \(g_k\) or on a specified residual \(R_k\) satisfying constants \(0<c_1\le c_2<\infty\) and \(c_1g_k\le R_k\le c_2g_k\) on the relevant tail. It is geometric if \(g_k\le Cq^{k-K}\) with \(q\in(0,1)\), and polynomial if \(g_k\le C(k-K+1)^{-p}\) with \(p>0\). Such a rate measures approach to first-order stationarity and is distinct from rates for objective gap or distance to a particular critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationarity-residual rate quantifies how quickly the distance from zero to the limiting subdifferential vanishes. An algorithmic residual can be used in its place only when a stated comparison makes it a valid stationarity measure. Geometric and polynomial rates are defined by the corresponding eventual upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[g_k:=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^k)),\qquad g_k\le Cq^{k-K}\ \text{or}\ g_k\le C(k-K+1)^{-p}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If a minimum-norm limiting subgradient \(v^k\in\partial F(x^k)\) exists, then \(g_k=\|v^k\|\).
For \(F\in C^1\), \(g_k=\|\nabla F(x^k)\|\).
special_cases_latex: For constrained smooth optimization modeled by \(F=f+\delta_C\), the residual is \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\nabla f(x^k)+N_C(x^k))\).
A proximal-gradient mapping may serve as \(R_k\) when established comparison inequalities hold.
immediate_consequences_latex: Either displayed rate implies \(g_k\to0\).
Under compatible subsequential closedness and objective-value convergence, cluster points are limiting-critical.
boundary_notes: A small stationarity residual need not imply proximity to a minimizer without an error bound.
Residual rates do not automatically equal objective-gap rates.
The limiting subdifferential can be empty at some domain points, making the distance infinite under the usual convention.

notation.meaning: distance from zero to the limiting subdifferential at the kth iterate
algorithm-specific residual explicitly comparable with g_k

children.title: Abstract KL Framework Variants
children.top_down_role: Major extensions that replace monotone single-step descent by auxiliary or perturbed energies.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Qian and Pan, Convergence of a Class of Nonmonotone Descent Methods for KL Optimization Problems

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lyapunov and perturbed variants of the abstract KL framework
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z^k\in\mathbb R^m\) be an augmented state built from current and past algorithmic variables, let \(\mathcal E:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous Lyapunov function, and let \((\varepsilon_k)\), \((\eta_k)\) be nonnegative error sequences.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic discrete variants replacing monotone descent of the original objective by descent of an auxiliary energy or by summably perturbed inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An abstract KL framework variant is a lifted or perturbed descent system for which there exist \(a,b>0\) such that \(\mathcal E(z^{k+1})+a\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|^2\le\mathcal E(z^k)+\varepsilon_k\), \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\mathcal E(z^{k+1}))\le b\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|+\eta_k\), and \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\), \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\). A compatibility condition relates convergence of \(z^k\) to convergence of the primary iterate and the limiting value of \(\mathcal E\). The KL property is imposed on \(\mathcal E\) near its relevant cluster set rather than necessarily on the original objective alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An abstract KL variant replaces exact monotone descent of the original objective by a Lyapunov energy on an augmented state, possibly with summable perturbations. The energy has a sufficient-decrease inequality, its stationarity residual is controlled by state motion and error, and convergence of the lifted state must project consistently to the original iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal E(z^{k+1})+a\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|^2\le\mathcal E(z^k)+\varepsilon_k,\quad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\mathcal E(z^{k+1}))\le b\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|+\eta_k,\quad \varepsilon,\eta\in\ell^1_+.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The unperturbed lifted framework is obtained by setting \(\varepsilon_k=\eta_k=0\).
A finite-memory method can use \(z^k=(x^k,x^{k-1},\ldots,x^{k-r})\) and an energy combining the objective with inter-iterate terms.
special_cases_latex: Inertial methods commonly use an energy of the form \(\mathcal E(x,y)=F(x)+c\|x-y\|^2\).
Inexact methods fit the perturbed form when their descent and residual errors are summable.
immediate_consequences_latex: Summable descent errors permit a corrected energy \(\mathcal E(z^k)+\sum_{j=k}^{\infty}\varepsilon_j\) to serve as a monotone quantity when finite.
Projection compatibility allows conclusions for \((z^k)\) to be transferred to the primary iterates.
boundary_notes: Arbitrary nonsummable noise is not covered by this definition.
The KL property of the original objective does not automatically imply the KL property of every augmented energy.
Stochastic variants require probabilistic hypotheses and are outside this deterministic formulation.
The constants and residual indices may differ among established frameworks.
review_flags: No supplied locator was verified for this lifted, perturbed KL framework.
The precise error summability and relative-error form vary by framework and require authoritative sourcing.

children.title: Controlled-Error Descent Family
children.top_down_role: Frameworks with controlled computational, stochastic, or modeling errors.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \((x^k)_{k\ge0}\subset\operatorname{dom}F\), and write \(s^{k+1}=x^{k+1}-x^k\). Distances are Euclidean and \(\partial F\) is the limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic abstract descent with additive computational or modeling errors. The definition supplies an interface for later KL arguments but does not itself assert convergence or the KL property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \((x^k)\) is a controlled-error descent sequence for \(F\) if there exist constants \(a>0\), \(b>0\), nonnegative sequences \((\varepsilon_k)\), \((\eta_k)\), and vectors \(w^{k+1}\in\partial F(x^{k+1})\) such that, for every \(k\ge0\), \[F(x^{k+1})+a\|s^{k+1}\|^2\le F(x^k)+\varepsilon_k,\qquad \|w^{k+1}\|\le b\|s^{k+1}\|+\eta_k.\] The errors are controlled when \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.\] A relative-error version replaces the second summability requirement by \(\eta_k\le c\|s^k\|\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), with \(c\ge0\), while retaining summable descent errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence is in the controlled-error descent family when each step gives quadratic sufficient decrease up to a nonnegative summable error, and a limiting subgradient at the new point is bounded by the step length plus a controlled residual. The control can be absolute summability of both error sequences or, in the relative-error variant, a residual bounded by the preceding step. This definition concerns only the descent and stationarity interface; applying a KL convergence theorem additionally requires boundedness or a cluster point, continuity of objective values along the relevant subsequence, and a KL property near the limiting set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^k)\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{err}}(F;a,b,\varepsilon,\eta)\iff \forall k\ge0:\ F(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le F(x^k)+\varepsilon_k,\ \exists w^{k+1}\in\partial F(x^{k+1}),\ \|w^{k+1}\|\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|+\eta_k,\ \varepsilon,\eta\in\ell^1_+.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The stationarity condition is equivalently \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|+\eta_k.\]
special_cases_latex: Exact abstract descent is obtained with \(\varepsilon_k=\eta_k=0\) for every \(k\).
A stochastic error model is not included unless the displayed inequalities and summability conditions hold pathwise on a specified probability-one event.
immediate_consequences_latex: Summing the descent inequalities gives \[a\sum_{k=0}^{N}\|s^{k+1}\|^2\le F(x^0)-F(x^{N+1})+\sum_{k=0}^{N}\varepsilon_k.\] Thus square-summability follows whenever \(F(x^k)\) is bounded below.
boundary_notes: Summability cannot be replaced merely by \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) without changing the family.
The definition alone neither implies finite length nor identifies a unique limit.

notation.meaning: Limiting subdifferential of the proper lower-semicontinuous objective.

review_flags: The supplied locator hints do not support this exact controlled-error KL interface; a source establishing the displayed sufficient-decrease, relative-error, and error-control conditions is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Controlled-Error KL Descent Sequence
Inexact Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact descent permits additive errors in decrease and stationarity estimates, provided both error sequences are controlled summably.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. A sequence \((x_k)\) satisfies inexact descent if there are \(a,b>0\) and nonnegative error sequences \((\varepsilon_k)\), \((\eta_k)\) such that \(f(x_{k+1})+a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\le f(x_k)+\varepsilon_k\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|+\eta_k\) for all \(k\), with \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\) and \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The descent and relative-error inequalities hold with finite total error accumulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract sufficient descent and relative error with summable inaccuracies.
review_flags: summability hypotheses vary across abstract frameworks

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: This is a suitable condition for the leaf, but summability requirements and the indexing of descent and relative-error terms vary across controlled-error KL frameworks. A specific source is required before selecting this formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbed Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturbed descent evaluates decrease and stationarity at displaced iterates, with perturbations vanishing and additive errors having finite accumulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. A sequence \((x_k)\) satisfies perturbed descent when there are perturbations \(e_k\in\mathbb R^n\), constants \(a,b>0\), and errors \(\varepsilon_k,\eta_k\ge0\) such that \(y_k=x_k+e_k\), \(f(y_{k+1})+a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\le f(y_k)+\varepsilon_k\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y_{k+1}))\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|+\eta_k\). A controlled perturbation regime requires \(e_k\to0\) and finite accumulated scalar errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The perturbed points \(y_k=x_k+e_k\) satisfy controlled descent and relative-stationarity inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent and relative-error conditions evaluated at perturbed iterates.
review_flags: compatibility between perturbation and KL neighborhood requires verification

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The proposed condition is framework-dependent. A perturbed-KL source is needed to verify evaluation at y_k, use of the unperturbed step length, scalar-error summability, and the conditions ensuring that perturbed points remain in the relevant KL neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Accumulation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Errors may vanish individually yet accumulate without bound; harmonic perturbations produce an infinite-length divergent trajectory, showing why summability cannot simply be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Vanishing errors alone do not preserve finite-length convergence. On \(\mathbb R\), take \(x_0=0\), \(e_k=1/(k+1)\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+e_k\). Then \(e_k\to0\), but \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|e_k|=\infty\), \(x_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}1/(j+1)\to+\infty\), and the trajectory has infinite length. Thus any abstract perturbed-descent theorem using error summability cannot generally replace it by the weaker condition \(e_k\to0\) without additional cancellation or stability assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation model permits additive updates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+e_k\).
Only pointwise decay \(e_k\to0\), not absolute summability, is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_k\to0\) does not imply \(\sum_k|e_k|<\infty\) or convergence of \((x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summability boundary for additive errors in finite-length convergence arguments.
review_flags: example is framework-level rather than a KL-specific algorithm
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The harmonic-update counterexample is correct and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf. However, the broader conclusion about hypotheses in abstract perturbed-descent theorems requires an inspectable framework source; the elementary example alone does not identify which theorem assumptions it invalidates.

children.title: Merit-Envelope Descent Family
children.top_down_role: Merit mechanisms allowing controlled temporary increases.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \((x^k)\subset\operatorname{dom}F\), and fix an integer memory length \(M\ge0\). Define the finite-window envelope \(E_k=\max\{F(x^j):\max(0,k-M)\le j\le k\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonmonotone descent controlled by a finite objective-value envelope. It permits temporary increases of the raw objective while requiring descent relative to the recent maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \((x^k)\) is a finite-window merit-envelope descent sequence for \(F\) with memory \(M\) if there exist constants \(a>0\), \(b>0\), a nonnegative summable sequence \((\varepsilon_k)\), and vectors \(w^{k+1}\in\partial F(x^{k+1})\) such that, for every \(k\ge0\), \[F(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le E_k+\varepsilon_k,\qquad \|w^{k+1}\|\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.\] The envelope is updated by \[E_{k+1}=\max\{F(x^j):\max(0,k+1-M)\le j\le k+1\}.\] Membership in this family requires the displayed inequalities for one fixed finite \(M\); it does not require \(F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k)\) at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit-envelope descent sequence measures sufficient decrease against the largest objective value in a fixed recent window. The current objective may therefore rise, but the accepted point must lie quadratically below the previous envelope up to a summable error. A subgradient at the accepted point must also be controlled by the step length. Memory length zero recovers ordinary monotone descent. The definition records the interface used by a nonmonotone KL analysis; convergence additionally needs conditions ensuring that the envelope and objective values have the same limiting level near the cluster set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^k)\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{env}}(F;M,a,b,\varepsilon)\iff \forall k\ge0:\ F(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le E_k+\varepsilon_k,\ \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|,\ \varepsilon\in\ell^1_+.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update can be written recursively as \[E_{k+1}=\max\bigl(F(x^{k+1}),F(x^k),\ldots,F(x^{\max(0,k+1-M)})\bigr).\]
special_cases_latex: For \(M=0\), \(E_k=F(x^k)\), so the definition reduces to monotone sufficient descent with summable error.
For \(\varepsilon_k=0\), every accepted value satisfies \(F(x^{k+1})\le E_k-a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The envelope dominates the raw value: \(F(x^k)\le E_k\) for every \(k\).
Any raw objective increase is bounded by \[F(x^{k+1})-F(x^k)\le E_k-F(x^k)+\varepsilon_k-a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2.\]
boundary_notes: An infinite or iteration-dependent memory window is outside this definition unless it admits a uniform finite bound.
Envelope descent is not the same as descent of a lifted energy depending on several iterates.

notation.meaning: Maximum objective value in the current window of at most \(M+1\) iterates.

review_flags: No inspected source precisely supports the stated finite-window envelope together with the KL relative-error interface.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Window Merit-Envelope Descent
Nonmonotone Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective values may rise between iterations, while a dominating merit envelope decreases sufficiently and controls the total squared motion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \((x_k)\subset\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \((M_k)\) be a merit envelope. The sequence satisfies nonmonotone descent if \(M_k\ge f(x_k)\), \(M_{k+1}\le M_k\), and, for some \(a>0\), \(M_{k+1}\le M_k-a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\) for every \(k\). Individual values \(f(x_{k+1})\) may exceed \(f(x_k)\), but the envelope decreases and \(\sum_k\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\le (M_0-\inf_k M_k)/a\) whenever the envelope is bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\le (M_0-\inf_k M_k)/a<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient decrease relative to a nonincreasing merit envelope.
review_flags: specific envelope constructions impose additional hypotheses

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping squared-motion bound follows from the stated envelope condition, and condition is an appropriate content kind. A source is nevertheless required because standard nonmonotone KL frameworks use different envelope constructions and may impose additional update, memory, or relative-error hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Windowed Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each new objective value may rise locally but must lie below the recent window maximum by a quadratic step penalty; consequently, the window maxima decrease monotonically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \((x^k)_{k\geq 0}\subset\operatorname{dom}\Phi\), and fix \(M\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(a>0\). Define \(E_k=\max\{\Phi(x^j):\max(0,k-M+1)\leq j\leq k\}\). Windowed descent holds when
\[
\Phi(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\leq E_k\qquad(k\geq0).
\]
Then \(E_{k+1}\leq E_k\); thus the window maximum is a monotone Lyapunov envelope even when \(\Phi(x^{k+1})>\Phi(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{k+1}\leq E_k\) for every \(k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window sufficient decrease condition for an abstract KL sequence.

notation.meaning: maximum merit value over the most recent window

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The finite-window descent condition and monotonicity of the window maximum are mathematically consistent and fit the condition container, but the record supplies neither a source nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Envelope Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The window merit is a maximum on a product space; its generalized slopes are convex combinations of slopes belonging to active window components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\geq1\), define the lifted window \(z^k=(x^k,x^{k-1},\ldots,x^{k-M+1})\), with unavailable initial entries repeated, and define
\[
\mathcal E(z^k)=\max_{0\leq i<M}\Phi(x^{k-i})=E_k.
\]
Its active set is \(I_k=\{i:\Phi(x^{k-i})=E_k\}\). If \(\Phi\) is locally Lipschitz at every active component, then
\[
\partial_C\mathcal E(z^k)\subseteq\operatorname{co}\{e_i\otimes v_i:i\in I_k,\ v_i\in\partial_C\Phi(x^{k-i})\},
\]
where \(\partial_C\) denotes the Clarke subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is locally Lipschitz at each component attaining the window maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_C\mathcal E(z^k)\) is contained in the stated convex hull of active component subgradients.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of the finite-window maximum used as a KL Lyapunov envelope.

notation.meaning: lifted vector of the current and recent iterates

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The product-space representation and stated Clarke maximum-rule inclusion are plausible and fit the representation container, but the exact nonsmooth calculus rule and its KL-envelope use require an authoritative source with a precise locator.

children.title: Non-Euclidean Descent Geometry
children.top_down_role: Changing local geometries and non-Euclidean residual measures.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \((x^k)\subset\operatorname{dom}F\). For each \(k\), let \(H_k\) be symmetric positive definite and set \(\|v\|_{H_k}=\sqrt{\langle H_kv,v\rangle}\) and \(\|z\|_{H_k^{-1}}=\sqrt{\langle H_k^{-1}z,z\rangle}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional changing quadratic geometry with uniform metric equivalence. General Bregman geometries require a separate formulation because their displacement measure need not be symmetric or norm-generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \((x^k)\) has a uniformly controlled non-Euclidean descent geometry for \(F\) if there exist constants \(a,b>0\), \(0<m\le M<\infty\), and matrices \((H_k)\) satisfying \[mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\qquad(k\ge0),\] such that, for every \(k\ge0\), \[F(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_{H_k}^2\le F(x^k),\] and there exists \(w^{k+1}\in\partial F(x^{k+1})\) with \[\|w^{k+1}\|_{H_k^{-1}}\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_{H_k}.\] The metric may change with \(k\), but its eigenvalues must remain uniformly separated from zero and infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A non-Euclidean descent geometry assigns a positive-definite local metric to each iteration. Sufficient decrease is measured by the squared primal metric norm of the step, while stationarity is measured in the corresponding dual metric. Uniform lower and upper spectral bounds ensure that these local residuals remain comparable with Euclidean step and subgradient norms. This makes the interface compatible with a standard finite-dimensional KL argument without forcing the algorithm to use one fixed geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^k,H_k)\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{vm}}(F;a,b,m,M)\iff \forall k:\ mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI,\ F(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_{H_k}^2\le F(x^k),\ \operatorname{dist}_{H_k^{-1}}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_{H_k}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Uniform metric control is equivalent to \[\sqrt m\|v\|\le\|v\|_{H_k}\le\sqrt M\|v\|\quad\text{for all }v\in\mathbb R^n\text{ and all }k.\]
special_cases_latex: Taking \(H_k=I\) for every \(k\) recovers Euclidean abstract descent.
A fixed preconditioner is obtained when \(H_k=H\succ0\) is independent of \(k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The decrease condition implies \[F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge am\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2.\]
The relative-error condition implies \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\le b\sqrt M\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_{H_k}.\]
boundary_notes: Degenerating metrics with \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\to0\) are excluded.
A Bregman divergence \(D_h(x^{k+1},x^k)\) is not automatically equivalent to this quadratic metric definition.

notation.meaning: Distance measured in the dual norm induced by \(H_k^{-1}\).

review_flags: A precise source for this variable-metric KL descent definition was not present among the supplied locator hints.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Non-Euclidean KL Descent Geometry
Variable-Metric Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive definite metrics allow the standard KL descent and residual inequalities to be measured in changing quadratic norms without losing Euclidean control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and satisfy \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) for constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\). A sequence \((x^k)\subset\operatorname{dom}\Phi\) satisfies variable-metric KL descent if, for constants \(a,b>0\),
\[
\Phi(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_{H_k}^2\leq\Phi(x^k),\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi(x^{k+1}))\leq b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_{H_k}.
\]
Uniform spectral bounds make these inequalities equivalent, up to constants, to Euclidean sufficient decrease and relative error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt m\|d\|\leq\|d\|_{H_k}\leq\sqrt M\|d\|\), so the abstract inequalities transfer to the Euclidean metric.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly coercive variable-metric form of abstract KL descent and relative error.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Uniform spectral equivalence and the transfer of the displayed inequalities to Euclidean norms are mathematically consistent, and condition is the correct knowledge kind. An authoritative source for this particular abstract variable-metric KL interface is absent.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective decrease and stationarity error are controlled by a Bregman divergence; strong convexity converts this control into ordinary Euclidean step control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h\) be differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex on a convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(D_h(y,x)=h(y)-h(x)-\langle\nabla h(x),y-x\rangle\). A sequence \((x^k)\subset C\cap\operatorname{dom}\Phi\) satisfies Bregman descent if constants \(a,b>0\) exist such that
\[
\Phi(x^{k+1})+aD_h(x^{k+1},x^k)\leq\Phi(x^k),\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi(x^{k+1}))\leq b\sqrt{D_h(x^{k+1},x^k)}.
\]
Strong convexity gives \(D_h(y,x)\geq\frac{\sigma}{2}\|y-x\|^2\), providing Euclidean step control.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex on convex \(C\).
\(\Phi\) is proper and lower semicontinuous on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract KL descent measured by a strongly convex Bregman divergence.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Strong convexity gives the displayed lower bound on the Bregman divergence, but that lower bound does not convert an upper residual bound by sqrt(D_h) into the usual Euclidean relative-error upper bound. An upper comparison for D_h, typically requiring Lipschitz continuity of the kernel gradient on the relevant region, would be needed for that transfer. The intended Bregman KL framework therefore requires a precise source before its correct hypotheses can be fixed.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Degeneracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing metric can make unit Euclidean steps appear summably small, so metric descent alone need not yield boundedness, Euclidean finite length, or iterate convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Uniform lower spectral control cannot generally be removed. Let \(C=\mathbb{N}_0\subset\mathbb{R}\), define \(\Phi(k)=2^{-k}\) on \(C\) and \(\Phi(x)=+\infty\) off \(C\), and take \(x^k=k\) and \(H_k=2^{-k}I\). Then \(\Phi\) is proper and lower semicontinuous and
\[
\Phi(x^{k+1})+\tfrac12\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_{H_k}^2=\Phi(x^k),
\]
yet \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|=1\) and \(x^k\to+\infty\). Thus metric finite length does not imply Euclidean finite length when \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\downarrow0\).
assumptions_latex: The lower eigenvalue bound \(H_k\succeq mI\) is absent.
The extended-real objective is defined on the closed discrete set \(\mathbb N_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|_{H_k}<\infty\) while \(\sum_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|=\infty\) and \((x^k)\) diverges.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of Euclidean convergence when variable metrics lose uniform coercivity.
