children.title: Memory-Based Descent Family
children.top_down_role: Lifted-energy frameworks for algorithms with memory.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), fix \(q\ge1\), and define lifted states \(z^k=(x^k,x^{k-1},\ldots,x^{k-q})\in(\mathbb R^n)^{q+1}\), with prescribed initial history. Let \(\Psi:(\mathbb R^n)^{q+1}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic algorithms with a fixed finite number of remembered iterates, analyzed through a lifted Lyapunov function rather than through monotonicity of the original objective alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal sequence \((x^k)\) belongs to a \(q\)-step memory-based descent family with lifted energy \(\Psi\) if there exist constants \(a,b>0\) and vectors \(v^{k+1}\in\partial\Psi(z^{k+1})\) such that, for every \(k\ge0\), \[\Psi(z^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le\Psi(z^k),\] \[\|v^{k+1}\|\le b\sum_{j=0}^{q}\|x^{k+1-j}-x^{k-j}\|.\] The lift must be objective-consistent on the diagonal: there is a constant \(c\in\mathbb R\) such that \[\Psi(x,x,\ldots,x)=F(x)+c\qquad\text{for every }x\in\operatorname{dom}F.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A memory-based descent sequence is analyzed after adjoining a fixed finite history to the current iterate. A proper lower-semicontinuous lifted energy decreases by at least a quadratic amount in the current step, and a lifted subgradient is bounded by the recent step lengths. On diagonal states, where every remembered iterate equals the same point, the lifted energy agrees with the original objective up to an irrelevant constant. Thus critical diagonal limits of the lifted system can be related to stationary points of the primal problem, subject to an additional projection condition when needed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^k)\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{mem}}(F,\Psi,q)\iff \forall k:\ \Psi(z^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le\Psi(z^k),\ \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Psi(z^{k+1}))\le b\sum_{j=0}^{q}\|x^{k+1-j}-x^{k-j}\|,\ \Psi(x,\ldots,x)=F(x)+c.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an inertial one-step memory, \(q=1\), the lifted state is \(z^k=(x^k,x^{k-1})\).
special_cases_latex: A common quadratic lift has \[\Psi(x,y)=F(x)+\frac{\gamma}{2}\|x-y\|^2\quad(\gamma\ge0),\] which is diagonal-consistent with \(c=0\).
When \(q=0\), the construction collapses to ordinary descent of \(F\), but this slot requires \(q\ge1\) to represent genuine memory.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\Psi\) is bounded below along the lifted sequence, then \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2<\infty.\]
Whenever all recent step lengths tend to zero, the lifted relative-error bound gives \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Psi(z^{k+1}))\to0\).
boundary_notes: Diagonal consistency alone does not guarantee that every lifted critical point projects to a critical point of \(F\).
Unbounded or dynamically increasing memory is excluded.

notation.meaning: Lifted state containing the current iterate and its preceding \(q\) iterates.

review_flags: No inspected source supports the exact lifted sufficient-decrease, subgradient, and diagonal-consistency definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Energy Descent with Finite Memory
Inertial Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inertial methods fit KL analysis by adding a kinetic term and bounding the lifted residual by the two most recent step lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z^k=(x^k,x^{k-1})\) and define \(\mathcal E(x,y)=\Phi(x)+\frac{c}{2}\|x-y\|^2\) with \(c>0\). An inertial sequence satisfies the lifted KL interface when constants \(a,b>0\) and vectors \(w^{k+1}\in\partial\mathcal E(z^{k+1})\) exist such that
\[
\mathcal E(z^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\leq\mathcal E(z^k),
\]
\[
\|w^{k+1}\|\leq b\bigl(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|+\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|\bigr).
\]
The kinetic term absorbs the one-step memory that may prevent monotonicity of \(\Phi(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E(z^k)\) is nonincreasing and the lifted subgradient is controlled by two consecutive increments.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-state lifted descent condition for KL analysis of inertial iterations.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The two-state kinetic-energy formulation is a coherent condition for the inertial-descent leaf, but no source supports the exact lifted energy, descent inequality, or two-increment residual bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistep Descent
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-memory method is represented on a product space, where weighted past increments produce descent and control the lifted stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(q\geq1\), set \(z^k=(x^k,x^{k-1},\ldots,x^{k-q})\), and let
\[
\mathcal E(z^k)=\Phi(x^k)+\sum_{i=1}^{q}\frac{c_i}{2}\|x^{k+1-i}-x^{k-i}\|^2,
\]
where \(c_i\geq0\). A multistep KL interface holds if constants \(a,b>0\) and \(w^{k+1}\in\partial\mathcal E(z^{k+1})\) satisfy
\[
\mathcal E(z^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\leq\mathcal E(z^k),\qquad
\|w^{k+1}\|\leq b\sum_{i=0}^{q}\|x^{k+1-i}-x^{k-i}\|.
\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted energy decreases, and its subgradient is bounded by the sum of the latest \(q+1\) increments.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory lifted descent interface with weighted recent increments.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The finite-memory product-state formulation is internally consistent and condition is the appropriate knowledge kind, but the exact energy weights and q+1-increment residual interface lack source support.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Energy Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Memory variables are added to the state so that a lifted energy obeys standard KL inequalities. If the memory energy vanishes and the lifted energy is value-continuous along the convergent sequence, limiting energy values transfer to the original objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z^k=(x^k,\tau^k)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^r\), where \(\tau^k\) stores finitely many memory variables, and let \(\mathcal E(x,\tau)=\Phi(x)+R(\tau)\) with \(R\geq0\). A lifted-energy interface consists of
\[
\mathcal E(z^{k+1})+a\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|^2\leq\mathcal E(z^k),\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\mathcal E(z^{k+1}))\leq b\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|.
\]
Suppose \(z^k\to(\bar x,\bar\tau)\), \(R(\tau^k)\to0\), \(R(\bar\tau)=0\), and \(\mathcal E(z^k)\to\mathcal E(\bar x,\bar\tau)\). Then
\[
\Phi(x^k)=\mathcal E(z^k)-R(\tau^k)\to\mathcal E(\bar x,\bar\tau)=\Phi(\bar x).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) and \(\mathcal E\) are proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi(x^k)\to\Phi(\bar x)=\mathcal E(\bar x,\bar\tau)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space representation connecting memory algorithms to abstract KL descent, with an explicit value-continuity condition for transfer to the original objective.

knowledge_statements.source_title: Algorithm Families Covered by KL Analysis
knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a family of algorithms for proper lower-semicontinuous objectives \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). An execution of \(A\in\mathcal A\) on \(F\) produces a state sequence \((z^k)\) in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and a proper lower-semicontinuous energy \(\Psi\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A classification interface, not a claim that every named method converges. Coverage is execution-specific and requires verification of the abstract descent conditions and the KL property of the selected energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An algorithm family \(\mathcal A\) is KL-admissible on a class \(\mathcal F\) if, for every \(F\in\mathcal F\), every bounded execution under the family's stated parameter safeguards admits a finite-dimensional state \(z^k\), an energy \(\Psi\), constants \(a,b>0\), and a nonnegative summable sequence \((\varepsilon_k)\) such that, for all \(k\), \[\Psi(z^{k+1})+a\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|^2\le\Psi(z^k)+\varepsilon_k,\] \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Psi(z^{k+1}))\le b\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|+\varepsilon_k,\] and every cluster point \(\bar z\) satisfies \(\Psi(z^k)\to\Psi(\bar z)\) along any subsequence \(z^k\to\bar z\). The energy must have the KL property at all cluster points, and its stationary diagonal or projected states must correspond to stationary solutions of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is covered by KL analysis when each bounded safeguarded execution can be represented by a finite-dimensional state and a proper lower-semicontinuous energy satisfying sufficient decrease, relative stationarity control, continuity of energy values at cluster points, and the KL property there. The representation must also connect stationary states of the energy back to stationary points of the original objective. Membership is therefore not determined by an algorithm name alone; it is established by an explicit realization of the common abstract interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal A\text{ is KL-admissible on }\mathcal F\iff \forall F\in\mathcal F\ \forall\text{ bounded safeguarded executions},\ \exists(z^k,\Psi,a,b,\varepsilon)\text{ satisfying the descent, relative-error, continuity, KL, and projection conditions}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: An individual execution is covered precisely when it admits such a certificate \((z^k,\Psi,a,b,\varepsilon)\); family-level coverage quantifies this certificate over the declared problem class and safeguards.
special_cases_latex: For a memoryless smooth method, one may take \(z^k=x^k\) and \(\Psi=F\).
For an inertial or splitting method, \(z^k\) may contain previous iterates or auxiliary variables and \(\Psi\) may differ from \(F\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition separates the method's procedural specification from its KL certificate.
If one admissible representation exists, alternative energies may provide additional certificates without changing the underlying algorithm.
boundary_notes: Boundedness of every execution is not built into admissibility; the quantifier applies to bounded executions.
The KL property of the original objective does not suffice when descent occurs only for a different lifted energy.

notation.meaning: Declared class of proper lower-semicontinuous objectives.

review_flags: The supplied sources do not state this family-level KL-admissibility classification with its full quantifier structure.

children.title: Smooth Descent Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Smooth methods whose generated sequences can satisfy KL descent mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable on an open set containing a sequence \((x^k)\), and put \(s^{k+1}=x^{k+1}-x^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth unconstrained descent. The interface abstracts away how directions and step lengths are computed and records only inequalities needed by a KL analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sequence \((x^k)\) realizes a smooth KL descent interface for \(f\) if there exist constants \(a,b>0\) such that, for every \(k\ge0\), \[f(x^{k+1})+a\|s^{k+1}\|^2\le f(x^k),\qquad \|
abla f(x^{k+1})\|\le b\|s^{k+1}\|.\] If the algorithm naturally controls the old gradient, the second condition may instead be certified by constants \(b_0,b_1\ge0\) satisfying \[\|
abla f(x^{k+1})\|\le b_0\|
abla f(x^k)\|+b_1\|s^{k+1}\|\] together with an independent step relation \(\|
abla f(x^k)\|\le c\|s^{k+1}\|\), yielding the displayed new-point bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth descent interface is a generated sequence for which objective reduction controls the squared step and the gradient at the accepted point is controlled by that step. It is deliberately weaker than a specification of gradient descent, Newton, or majorization-minimization: any smooth method that verifies the two inequalities enters the same KL architecture. A formulation using the old gradient is admissible only when a separate step relation converts it into the required new-point stationarity estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^k)\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{smooth}}(f)\iff \exists a,b>0\ \forall k:\ f(x^k)-f(x^{k+1})\ge a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2,\ \|\nabla f(x^{k+1})\|\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because \(f\) is smooth, \(\partial f(x)=\{\nabla f(x)\}\), so the relative-error condition is \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x^{k+1}))\le b\|s^{k+1}\|.\]
special_cases_latex: For gradient descent \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_k\nabla f(x^k)\), uniform bounds on \(\alpha_k\) and local Lipschitz continuity of \(\nabla f\) can be used to verify the interface.
A safeguarded Newton sequence belongs here only after its accepted steps satisfy both displayed inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(f(x^k)\) is bounded below, then \(\sum_k\|s^{k+1}\|^2<\infty\).
The relative-error condition then gives \(\|\nabla f(x^{k+1})\|\to0\).
boundary_notes: Smoothness alone does not imply either interface inequality.
Constrained smooth optimization requires a projected, normal-cone, or other constrained stationarity residual.
review_flags: The inspected gradient-method source supports smooth descent algorithms but not this exact two-condition KL interface.

children.title: Smooth Step-Control Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Fixed-step, backtracking, and related smooth descent families.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(d^k\) be a search direction, let \(\alpha_k>0\), and define \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_kd^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-step and backtracking smooth descent methods with quantitative angle, scaling, and accepted-step safeguards. The definition does not prescribe one particular line-search rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The iteration has a smooth step-control interface if there exist constants \(c_1,c_2,\underline\alpha,\overline\alpha,\sigma>0\) such that, for every nonstationary iterate, \[\langle
abla f(x^k),d^kangle\le-c_1\|
abla f(x^k)\|^2,\qquad \|d^k\|\le c_2\|
abla f(x^k)\|,\] \[0<\underline\alpha\le\alpha_k\le\overline\alpha,\qquad f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)+\sigma\alpha_k\langle
abla f(x^k),d^kangle,\] where \(0<\sigma<1\). A fixed-step realization chooses \(\alpha_k\equiv\alpha\) satisfying these conditions; a backtracking realization selects an accepted trial from a geometric grid while retaining the uniform lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth step-control interface consists of a gradient-related descent direction, a direction norm comparable with the gradient, uniformly nonvanishing accepted step lengths, and an Armijo-type decrease test. These conditions cover both a suitable fixed step and backtracking whose accepted steps remain uniformly bounded below. They make the accepted displacement quantitatively comparable with the gradient and convert the line-search decrease into the sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities used by a smooth KL interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[(d^k,\alpha_k)\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{step}}(f)\iff  orall k:\ \langle
abla f(x^k),d^kangle\le-c_1\|
abla f(x^k)\|^2,\ \|d^k\|\le c_2\|
abla f(x^k)\|,\ \underline\alpha\le\alpha_k\le\overline\alpha,\ f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)+\sigma\alpha_k\langle
abla f(x^k),d^kangle.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The angle and norm conditions imply \[-\langle\nabla f(x^k),d^k\rangle\ge(c_1/c_2^2)\|d^k\|^2.\]
special_cases_latex: Steepest descent has \(d^k=-\nabla f(x^k)\), hence \(c_1=c_2=1\).
Backtracking with trial lengths \(\alpha_0\beta^j\), \(0<\beta<1\), is included only when accepted lengths possess a uniform positive lower bound on the region visited.
immediate_consequences_latex: The Armijo inequality gives \[f(x^k)-f(x^{k+1})\ge \frac{\sigma c_1}{\overline\alpha c_2^2}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2.\]
The step relation gives \[\|\nabla f(x^k)\|\le(c_1\underline\alpha)^{-1}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\] after adjusting constants through the direction bounds.
boundary_notes: A line search whose accepted step lengths approach zero is not covered without a different residual argument.
The conditions exclude non-descent directions accepted by trust-region or filter mechanisms.
review_flags: The inspected source supports generalized gradient and Armijo methods, but not the exact uniform quantitative interface stated here.
knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Related Smooth Step-Control Interface
Gradient-Descent Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With steps uniformly inside the smoothness stability range, gradient descent satisfies quadratic decrease and bounds the next gradient by the latest step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and let \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha_k\nabla f(x^k)\), where \(0<\underline\alpha\leq\alpha_k\leq\overline\alpha<2/L\). Then
\[
f(x^{k+1})\leq f(x^k)-\left(\frac{1}{\alpha_k}-\frac{L}{2}\right)\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2,
\]
and
\[
\|\nabla f(x^{k+1})\|\leq\left(L+\frac{1}{\underline\alpha}\right)\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.
\]
Hence gradient descent supplies uniform sufficient-decrease and relative-error constants for the smooth KL framework.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Gradient descent satisfies uniform KL-compatible sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-step smooth gradient descent expressed through KL-compatible descent and residual bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Armijo backtracking repeatedly contracts a trial step until it gives quantified objective decrease along a descent direction, then advances and tests stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), parameters \(\beta,c\in(0,1)\), trial step \(\bar\alpha>0\), and descent directions \(p^k\) satisfying \(\nabla f(x^k)^{\mathsf T}p^k<0\), choose the least integer \(j_k\geq0\) such that
\[
f(x^k+\bar\alpha\beta^{j_k}p^k)\leq f(x^k)+c\bar\alpha\beta^{j_k}\nabla f(x^k)^{\mathsf T}p^k.
\]
Set \(\alpha_k=\bar\alpha\beta^{j_k}\) and \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_kp^k\). Stop when a prescribed stationarity tolerance \(\|\nabla f(x^k)\|\leq\varepsilon\) is met; otherwise repeat.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f(x^k)^{\mathsf T}p^k<0\) whenever the algorithm has not stopped.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted step satisfies the Armijo decrease inequality and returns an \(\varepsilon\)-stationary iterate upon termination.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking interface producing sufficient decrease for smooth KL analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Step-Control Compatibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient-related directions, bounded accepted steps, Armijo decrease, and smoothness convert a line search into the two uniform inequalities required by KL analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g^k=\nabla f(x^k)\), \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_kp^k\), and suppose constants \(c_1,c_2,\underline\alpha,\overline\alpha>0\) satisfy
\[
-(g^k)^{\mathsf T}p^k\geq c_1\|g^k\|^2,
\qquad \|p^k\|\leq c_2\|g^k\|,
\qquad \underline\alpha\leq\alpha_k\leq\overline\alpha.
\]
If the Armijo condition holds with parameter \(c\in(0,1)\) and \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz, then uniform constants \(a,b>0\) exist such that
\[
f(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\leq f(x^k),\qquad
\|\nabla f(x^{k+1})\|\leq b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.
\]
assumptions_latex: Directions satisfy the displayed gradient-related bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform \(a,b>0\) give sufficient decrease and relative error in the actual step norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient-related directions and nonvanishing accepted steps yield KL-compatible line-search bounds.

children.title: Safeguarded Newton Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Second-order families linked to KL analysis through safeguarded descent.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable on a region containing \((x^k)\). At iteration \(k\), let \(B_k=B_k^\top\), compute \(p^k\), and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_kp^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth second-order methods whose Newton or inexact-Newton proposals are modified or rejected until a globally descending accepted step is obtained. Local Newton rates are not part of this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The iteration realizes a safeguarded Newton interface if there exist constants \(m,M,c,\underline\alpha>0\) and forcing numbers \(0\le\eta_k\le ar\eta<1\) such that \[mI\preceq B_k\preceq MI,\qquad B_kp^k=-
abla f(x^k)+r^k,\qquad \|r^k\|\le\eta_k\|
abla f(x^k)\|,\] and the accepted step satisfies \[\alpha_k\ge\underline\alpha,\qquad f(x^k+\alpha_kp^k)\le f(x^k)+c\alpha_k\langle
abla f(x^k),p^kangle,\quad 0<c<1.\] If the raw Hessian fails the spectral safeguard, \(B_k\) may be a regularized Hessian or another symmetric positive-definite model matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguarded Newton interface uses an exact or residual-controlled solution of a positive-definite second-order model, but it accepts the proposal only through a global descent safeguard. Uniform spectral bounds prevent the model from becoming singular or arbitrarily ill-conditioned on the analyzed region. The forcing sequence controls linear-solve error, while a uniformly positive accepted step and an Armijo condition connect the second-order direction to the abstract smooth KL descent mechanism. The definition allows Hessian regularization and fallback model matrices; it does not require the unmodified Newton step at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(B_k,p^k,\alpha_k)\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sN}}(f)\iff \forall k:\ mI\preceq B_k\preceq MI,\ \|B_kp^k+\nabla f(x^k)\|\le\eta_k\|\nabla f(x^k)\|,\ \eta_k\le\bar\eta<1,\ \alpha_k\ge\underline\alpha,\ \text{and the accepted Armijo inequality holds}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The residual equation can be written \[r^k=B_kp^k+\nabla f(x^k),\qquad \|r^k\|/\|\nabla f(x^k)\|\le\eta_k\] at nonstationary iterates.
special_cases_latex: Exact damped Newton uses \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x^k)\) and \(r^k=0\) whenever the Hessian satisfies the spectral safeguard.
Levenberg-type regularization uses \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x^k)+\lambda_kI\) with \(\lambda_k\) chosen to enforce positive definiteness.

Once full steps are accepted and \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x^k)\), the interface coincides with the local inexact-Newton iteration.

Newton Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive definite Newton models and nonvanishing Armijo steps provide descent and residual bounds suitable for a smooth KL convergence argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and let \(B_k\) be symmetric with \(mI\preceq B_k\preceq MI\), where \(0<m\leq M\). Define \(p^k\) by \(B_kp^k=-\nabla f(x^k)\), choose an Armijo step \(\alpha_k\in[\underline\alpha,1]\), and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_kp^k\). Then \(p^k\) is a descent direction and uniform constants \(a,b>0\) exist such that
\[
f(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\leq f(x^k),
\qquad
\|\nabla f(x^{k+1})\|\leq b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on the relevant level set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The safeguarded Newton iteration satisfies uniform sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded Newton directions coupled to line search and KL-compatible step bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized-Newton Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a regularized Newton system, accept a damped step, and expose uniform sufficient-decrease and gradient-relative-error bounds required by KL convergence analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable and bounded below on the initial sublevel set. At iteration \(k\), choose a symmetric matrix \(B_k\), a regularization \(\lambda_k\geq 0\), and \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), solve \((B_k+\lambda_k I)d_k=-
abla f(x_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k\). The regularized-Newton interface to KL analysis requires constants \(a,b>0\) such that accepted steps satisfy \(f(x_{k+1})+a\lVert x_{k+1}-x_kVert^2\leq f(x_k)\) and \(\lVert
abla f(x_{k+1})Vert\leq b\lVert x_{k+1}-x_kVert\). The algorithm stops when \(
abla f(x_k)=0\); otherwise its output is the generated sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\) and \(f\) is bounded below on \(\{x:f(x)\leq f(x_0)\}\).
\(B_k+\lambda_k I\) is positive definite whenever a nonzero step is computed.
Accepted steps obey uniform descent and relative-error constants \(a,b>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_{k+1})+a\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2\leq f(x_k)\) and \(\lVert\nabla f(x_{k+1})\rVert\leq b\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\).

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Safeguard Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform positive curvature, quadratic accepted decrease, and a next-gradient bound define a KL-compatible safeguard; failed trials must be regularized, shortened, or restricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a smooth objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), a second-order safeguard regime holds on the iterates if constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\), \(\sigma>0\), and \(b>0\) exist such that every accepted matrix satisfies \(mI\preceq B_k+\lambda_k I\preceq MI\), every accepted step \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) satisfies \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq\sigma\lVert s_k\rVert^2\), and \(\lVert\nabla f(x_{k+1})\rVert\leq b\lVert s_k\rVert\). A trial violating curvature or decrease is rejected and recomputed by increasing regularization, shrinking the step, or entering a trust region. These conditions constitute the safeguard interface used by KL convergence arguments.
assumptions_latex: Each trial uses a symmetric matrix \(B_k\) and regularization \(\lambda_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(mI\preceq B_k+\lambda_k I\preceq MI\), \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq\sigma\lVert s_k\rVert^2\), and \(\lVert\nabla f(x_{k+1})\rVert\leq b\lVert s_k\rVert\) for every accepted step.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Majorization-Minimization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a tangent majorizing surrogate. Uniform surrogate curvature and controlled gradient mismatch yield the sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities used in KL analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable. Given \(x_k\), construct a differentiable surrogate \(Q_k:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(Q_k(x)\geq f(x)\) for all admissible \(x\), \(Q_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), and \(
abla Q_k(x_k)=
abla f(x_k)\). Choose \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x Q_k(x)\), stopping when \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). If \(Q_k\) is uniformly \(\mu\)-strongly convex and the gradient mismatch obeys \(\lVert
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla Q_k(x_{k+1})Vert\leq L_Q\lVert x_{k+1}-x_kVert\), then \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq(\mu/2)\lVert x_{k+1}-x_kVert^2\) and \(\lVert
abla f(x_{k+1})Vert\leq L_Q\lVert x_{k+1}-x_kVert\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq(\mu/2)\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2\) and \(\lVert\nabla f(x_{k+1})\rVert\leq L_Q\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact smooth surrogate minimization under uniform majorization, strong surrogate growth, and first-order consistency.

notation.meaning: smooth majorizing surrogate at iteration k
uniform strong-convexity modulus of the surrogates

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. For each base point \(y\), let \(Q(\cdot\mid y):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be a differentiable surrogate, and let \(x^{k+1}\) minimize or approximately minimize \(Q(\cdot\mid x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth unconstrained surrogate minimization with first-order consistency, global majorization on the relevant domain, and uniform strong convexity of each surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((x^k,Q)\) realizes a smooth majorization-minimization interface if there exists \(\mu>0\) such that, for every \(k\), \[Q(x\mid x^k)\ge f(x)\quad\text{for all }x,\qquad Q(x^k\mid x^k)=f(x^k),\] \[\nabla_xQ(x^k\mid x^k)=\nabla f(x^k),\] and \(Q(\cdot\mid x^k)\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. An exact update satisfies \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}Q(x\mid x^k).\] An inexact update is included only when a stated residual and surrogate-decrease condition preserves uniform sufficient decrease and relative stationarity for \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth majorization-minimization interface replaces the objective at each iterate by a differentiable upper model that touches the objective and matches its gradient at the base point. Uniform strong convexity makes the model minimizer well controlled and turns model improvement into quantitative objective decrease. Exact surrogate minimization is the canonical update. Approximate minimization belongs to the same interface only when its residual is controlled strongly enough to retain the abstract KL descent inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^k,Q)\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{MM}}(f)\iff \forall k:\ Q(\cdot\mid x^k)\ge f,\ Q(x^k\mid x^k)=f(x^k),\ \nabla_xQ(x^k\mid x^k)=\nabla f(x^k),\ Q(\cdot\mid x^k)\text{ is uniformly strongly convex},\ x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}Q(\cdot\mid x^k).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The majorization and touching conditions are equivalently \[Q(x\mid y)=f(x)+R(x,y),\qquad R(x,y)\ge0,\quad R(y,y)=0,\quad \nabla_xR(y,y)=0.\]
special_cases_latex: For an \(L\)-smooth function, \[Q(x\mid y)=f(y)+\langle\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle+\frac{L'}2\|x-y\|^2\] with \(L'\ge L\) yields a gradient step.
A quadratic positive-definite model with first-order consistency gives a variable-metric gradient update.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact minimization and strong convexity imply \[f(x^k)-f(x^{k+1})\ge Q(x^k\mid x^k)-Q(x^{k+1}\mid x^k)\ge\frac\mu2\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2.\]
boundary_notes: Tangential approximation without global or local accepted-step majorization is outside this definition.
Nonsmooth composite surrogates belong to the composite proximal interface rather than this smooth slot.

notation.meaning: Surrogate evaluated at candidate \(x\) and based at \(y\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous. The function \(g\) need not be convex unless stated by a concrete method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth-plus-nonsmooth methods represented through a proximal or model optimality residual and an objective or auxiliary-energy descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((x^k)\subset\operatorname{dom}g\) realizes a composite proximal interface for \(F=f+g\) if there exist constants \(a,b>0\), auxiliary points \(y^{k+1}\), and residuals \(r^{k+1}\) such that \[F(x^{k+1})+a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le F(x^k),\] \[r^{k+1}\in\nabla f(x^{k+1})+\partial g(x^{k+1})=\partial F(x^{k+1}),\qquad \|r^{k+1}\|\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.\] When stationarity is first obtained at \(y^{k+1}\ne x^{k+1}\), the interface additionally requires \(\|y^{k+1}-x^{k+1}\|\le c\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\) and a corresponding transfer bound for \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite proximal interface is defined by objective decrease and a proximal-model residual that becomes a limiting subgradient of the composite objective at the accepted point. The residual must be bounded by the accepted displacement. Auxiliary model points are permitted only when their distance from the accepted point and the transfer of stationarity are quantitatively controlled. The definition covers several proximal constructions while keeping their procedural details in their primary method theories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^k)\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{comp}}(f,g)\iff \exists a,b>0\ \forall k:\ F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2,\ \operatorname{dist}(0,\nabla f(x^{k+1})+\partial g(x^{k+1}))\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under the standard limiting-subdifferential sum rule, \[\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)=\partial(f+g)(x).\]
special_cases_latex: If \(f=0\), the interface reduces to a proximal-point-type interface for \(g\).
If \(g=0\), it reduces to the smooth descent interface.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(F(x^k)\) is bounded below, then \(\sum_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2<\infty\).
Consequently, the displayed residual bound gives \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\to0\).
boundary_notes: A residual evaluated only at an uncontrolled auxiliary point does not establish this interface.
Nonconvex \(g\) may make the proximal subproblem set-valued; an accepted selection must satisfy the displayed conditions.

notation.meaning: Composite stationarity residual at the accepted point.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Point Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iterate approximately minimizes the objective plus a quadratic proximity term, with residual proportional to the step and an explicit sufficient-decrease inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below. Given \(x_k\) and \(\lambda_k\in[\underline\lambda,\overline\lambda]\subset(0,\infty)\), choose \(x_{k+1}\) and an error \(e_{k+1}\) satisfying \(e_{k+1}\in\partial F(x_{k+1})+\lambda_k^{-1}(x_{k+1}-x_k)\) and \(\lVert e_{k+1}\rVert\leq\eta\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\). The exact step has \(e_{k+1}=0\) and minimizes \(F(x)+(2\lambda_k)^{-1}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\). If the inexact solve also guarantees \(F(x_{k+1})+(2\lambda_k)^{-1}\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2\leq F(x_k)\), stop when \(x_{k+1}=x_k\); otherwise continue and output the sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
The inexact residual and decrease conditions hold with a fixed \(\eta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_{k+1})+(2\lambda_k)^{-1}\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2\leq F(x_k)\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x_{k+1}))\leq(\eta+\underline\lambda^{-1})\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or controlled-inexact proximal-point steps for a proper lower-semicontinuous nonsmooth objective.

The displayed residual inclusion and decrease condition coherently imply the stated relative-error estimate, but the exact inexactness convention is not canonical and no authoritative source is provided.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}F\), and let \(0<\underline\lambda\le\lambda_k\le\overline\lambda<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional implicit regularization for possibly nonconvex lower-semicontinuous objectives, assuming the selected proximal subproblems possess solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact proximal-point sequence satisfies, for every \(k\), \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{F(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\}.\] An inexact proximal-point sequence with errors \((\delta_k)\) satisfies \[F(x^{k+1})+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le\inf_x\left\{F(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\}+\delta_k,\] and admits \(e^{k+1}\) with \(\|e^{k+1}\|\le\eta_k\) such that \[e^{k+1}\in\partial F(x^{k+1})+\lambda_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k).\] Controlled inexactness requires \(\sum_k\delta_k<\infty\), \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\), or a separately stated relative-error condition sufficient for the KL framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-point interface updates by minimizing the objective plus a quadratic penalty for moving from the current point. Exact updates solve this regularized problem globally. Inexact updates have both a controlled subproblem-value error and an approximate first-order condition. Uniform positive lower and upper bounds on the regularization parameter prevent the quadratic term from vanishing or becoming singular. For nonconvex objectives the proximal map may contain several points, and any selected global minimizer defines an exact update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_kF}(x^k):=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{F(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\}\] in the exact case, with the displayed value and residual inequalities defining the inexact case.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Every exact update satisfies the necessary inclusion \[0\in\partial F(x^{k+1})+\lambda_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k).\]
Equivalently, \[-\lambda_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k)\in\partial F(x^{k+1}).\]
special_cases_latex: For convex \(F\), the proximal subproblem is strongly convex and the exact update is unique.
For \(F=\iota_C\), where \(C\) is nonempty and closed, the exact update is a Euclidean projection onto \(C\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Comparison with \(x=x^k\) yields \[F(x^{k+1})+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2\le F(x^k)\] for exact updates.
The exact inclusion gives \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\le\underline\lambda^{-1}\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.\]
boundary_notes: For nonconvex \(F\), the first-order inclusion alone does not imply global solution of the proximal subproblem.
Local model minimizers define a different interface unless sufficient decrease is imposed separately.

notation.meaning: Possibly set-valued global proximal mapping of \(F\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), where \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(g\) is proper and lower semicontinuous. Let \(\lambda_k>0\), and assume the displayed proximal subproblem has an accepted global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional composite smooth-nonsmooth descent. Convexity of \(g\) is not required for the definition, but nonconvex proximal mappings may be set-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A forward-backward update is any selection \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\left\{g(x)+\langle
abla f(x^k),x-x^kangle+ rac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x-x^k\|^2ight\},\] equivalently \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_kg} igl(x^k-\lambda_k
abla f(x^k) igr).\] Its proximal-gradient residual is \[G_{\lambda_k}(x^k)=\lambda_k^{-1}(x^k-x^{k+1}).\] The step optimality inclusion is \[G_{\lambda_k}(x^k)-
abla f(x^k)\in\partial g(x^{k+1}),\] and the associated new-point composite subgradient is \[w^{k+1}=G_{\lambda_k}(x^k)+
abla f(x^{k+1})-
abla f(x^k)\in\partial F(x^{k+1}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward-backward step linearizes the smooth term at the current point and retains the nonsmooth term exactly, with a quadratic proximal regularizer. The same update is the proximal map of the nonsmooth term applied after a forward gradient step. Dividing the accepted displacement by the step size gives the proximal-gradient residual. Combining subproblem optimality with the change in the smooth gradient produces a genuine composite subgradient at the new point, which is the key correspondence to the KL relative-error condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_kg}(x^k-\lambda_k
abla f(x^k)),\qquad G_{\lambda_k}(x^k)= rac{x^k-x^{k+1}}{\lambda_k},\qquad G_{\lambda_k}(x^k)+
abla f(x^{k+1})-
abla f(x^k)\in\partial F(x^{k+1}).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update inclusion is \[0\in\partial g(x^{k+1})+\nabla f(x^k)+\lambda_k^{-1}(x^{k+1}-x^k).\]
special_cases_latex: If \(g=0\), then \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\lambda_k\nabla f(x^k)\) and \(G_{\lambda_k}(x^k)=\nabla f(x^k)\).
If \(f=0\), the update is a proximal-point step for \(g\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(\lambda_k\ge\underline\lambda>0\), then \[\|w^{k+1}\|\le(\underline\lambda^{-1}+L)\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.\]
A fixed point \(x^{k+1}=x^k\) satisfies \(0\in\nabla f(x^k)+\partial g(x^k)\).
boundary_notes: For nonconvex \(g\), the proximal mapping can be multivalued and the residual depends on the selected update.
The definition alone does not impose a step-size bound ensuring objective descent.

notation.meaning: Proximal-gradient residual associated with the selected forward-backward update.

knowledge_statements.title: Forward-Backward Step and Proximal-Gradient Residual
Forward-Backward Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a forward gradient move to the smooth term and a backward proximal move to the nonsmooth term; the step supplies descent and a stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous. For \(0<\gamma_k\leq\overline\gamma<1/L\), set \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma_k g}(x_k-\gamma_k\nabla f(x_k))\), equivalently minimizing \(g(x)+\langle\nabla f(x_k),x-x_k\rangle+(2\gamma_k)^{-1}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\). Stop when \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Then \(F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\geq(1/(2\gamma_k)-L/2)\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2\), while proximal optimality supplies a limiting subgradient of \(F\) controlled by the step.
assumptions_latex: \(F=f+g\), \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz, and \(g\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\geq(1/(2\gamma_k)-L/2)\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward gradient step on the smooth term followed by a backward proximal step on the nonsmooth term.

notation.meaning: possibly set-valued proximal mapping of g

The descent coefficient is mathematically consistent for a globally minimizing proximal selection with stepsizes below 1/L, but no source establishes the intended possibly nonconvex, set-valued proximal convention or the associated limiting-subgradient interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Gradient Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-gradient step equals minimization of a local composite model, and its scaled displacement produces a subgradient certificate at the new point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=f+g\), a stepsize \(\gamma>0\), and a point \(x\in\operatorname{dom}g\), define \(x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z\{g(z)+\langle
abla f(x),z-xangle+(2\gamma)^{-1}\lVert z-xVert^2\}\) and \(G_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}(x-x^+)\). Then \(x^+\in\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma
abla f(x))\), and model optimality is equivalent to \(G_\gamma(x)-
abla f(x)+
abla f(x^+)\in\partial F(x^+)\). If the proximal point is single-valued, \(G_\gamma(x)=0\) exactly when \(x=x^+\); in that case \(0\in\partial F(x)\). Thus the proximal-gradient mapping is a computable step-based interface to composite stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and the displayed proximal subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_\gamma(x)-\nabla f(x)+\nabla f(x^+)\in\partial F(x^+)\), and \(G_\gamma(x)=0\) implies \(0\in\partial F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between a proximal-gradient model minimizer, its update mapping, and a composite first-order condition.

notation.meaning: limiting subdifferential of the composite objective

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind correctly matches the equivalence and stationarity-mapping role of this leaf. The displayed optimality identity is coherent for a selected global proximal minimizer, but no authoritative source is supplied for this limiting-subdifferential formulation in the potentially nonconvex setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Residual Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computable correction of the scaled proximal displacement is a subgradient at the new point and bounds composite nonstationarity by the step length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\), let \(
abla f\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz, and let \(x^+\in\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma
abla f(x))\). Define \(r^+=\gamma^{-1}(x-x^+)+
abla f(x^+)-
abla f(x)\). Proximal optimality gives \(r^+\in\partial F(x^+)\), so \(r^+\) is a verifiable composite stationarity certificate. Moreover, \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^+))\leq\lVert r^+Vert\leq(\gamma^{-1}+L)\lVert x^+-xVert\). Consequently, a small accepted displacement or proximal-gradient mapping yields a quantitatively small limiting-subgradient residual at the new iterate, which is the relative-error interface used in KL analysis.
assumptions_latex: \(F=f+g\), with \(\nabla f\) \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(g\) proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^+\in\partial F(x^+)\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^+))\leq(\gamma^{-1}+L)\lVert x^+-x\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proximal-gradient displacement certifies limiting-subgradient stationarity for a smooth-plus-nonsmooth composite objective.

children.title: Higher-Order Composite Model Interface
children.top_down_role: Higher-order local models coupled to composite regularization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), let \(p\ge2\), assume \(f\) is \(p\)-times continuously differentiable on the relevant region, and let \(g\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. Denote the order-\(p\) Taylor polynomial of \(f\) at \(x\) by \(T_p^f(\cdot;x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional higher-order local models coupled with an exact nonsmooth term and a regularizer of order \(p+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regularized higher-order composite update with parameter \(\sigma_k>0\) is any selection \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{m_k(y):=T_p^f(y;x^k)+g(y)+\frac{\sigma_k}{p+1}\|y-x^k\|^{p+1}\right\}.\] It realizes a higher-order composite KL interface when there exist constants \(a,b>0\) such that, with \(s^{k+1}=x^{k+1}-x^k\), \[F(x^{k+1})+a\|s^{k+1}\|^{p+1}\le F(x^k),\] and there exists \(w^{k+1}\in\partial F(x^{k+1})\) satisfying \[\|w^{k+1}\|\le b\|s^{k+1}\|^p.\] The parameter and Taylor-remainder safeguards must hold uniformly on the region visited.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A higher-order composite model keeps the nonsmooth term intact, replaces the smooth term by its Taylor polynomial of order at least two, and stabilizes the model by a power regularizer one order higher. The interface requires accepted model solutions to produce objective decrease of order the step to the power p plus one and a composite stationarity residual of order the step to the power p. These are the higher-order analogues of quadratic sufficient decrease and linear relative error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^k)\in\mathcal I_{p\text{-}\mathrm{comp}}(f,g)\iff x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}m_k,\ F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge a\|s^{k+1}\|^{p+1},\ \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\le b\|s^{k+1}\|^p.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Model optimality is expressed by \[0\in\nabla_yT_p^f(x^{k+1};x^k)+\partial g(x^{k+1})+\sigma_k\|s^{k+1}\|^{p-1}s^{k+1}.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(p=2\), the regularizer is cubic and the stationarity residual is quadratic in the step.
For \(g=0\), the model reduces to a regularized higher-order smooth Taylor model.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(F(x^k)\) is bounded below, then \[\sum_k\|s^{k+1}\|^{p+1}<\infty.\]
Hence \(s^{k+1}\to0\), and the residual inequality yields \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\to0\).
boundary_notes: A bare Taylor model without regularization or an accepted-step safeguard is excluded.
Approximate model solutions require explicit value and optimality error conditions not supplied by this exact definition.

notation.meaning: Order-\(p\) Taylor polynomial of \(f\) at base point \(x\), evaluated at \(y\).

Proximal-Newton Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a proximal quadratic model, globalize its trial step, and require accepted decrease plus a subgradient residual proportional to the displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\), with \(f\) twice continuously differentiable and \(g\) proper and lower semicontinuous. At \(x_k\), choose a symmetric \(B_k\) with \(mI\preceq B_k\preceq MI\), and compute \(d_k\) by exactly or approximately minimizing \(g(x_k+d)+\langle\nabla f(x_k),d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle d,B_kd\rangle\). Choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and accept only if \(F(x_{k+1})\leq F(x_k)-\sigma\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2\). The subproblem residual must yield \(w_{k+1}\in\partial F(x_{k+1})\) with \(\lVert w_{k+1}\rVert\leq b\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\). Stop when \(d_k=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\) and \(g\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
Accepted inexact solves provide the displayed descent and residual bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_{k+1})\leq F(x_k)-\sigma\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2\) and some \(w_{k+1}\in\partial F(x_{k+1})\) satisfies \(\lVert w_{k+1}\rVert\leq b\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic smooth-term modeling combined with an exact or controlled-inexact proximal composite subproblem.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the Proximal-Newton Interface leaf. Accepted decrease and a subgradient relative-error bound are stated as requirements, but the mechanism by which an exact or inexact quadratic-model solve—especially after damping—produces the residual at the accepted point is version-dependent and unsupported by a source.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Model Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent higher-order composite model transfers approximate model stationarity into objective stationarity, while accepted model decrease supplies the KL descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\), and at \(x_k\) form \(M_k(x_k+s)=g(x_k+s)+m_k(s)\), where \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\) and \(
abla m_k(0)=
abla f(x_k)\). Compute a trial \(s_k\) satisfying \(M_k(x_k+s_k)\leq M_k(x_k)\) and a model stationarity residual bounded by \(\eta\lVert s_kVert^{p}\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) only when \(F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\geq a\lVert s_kVert^{p+1}\). If the gradient-model error satisfies \(\lVert
abla f(x_k+s_k)-
abla m_k(s_k)Vert\leq c\lVert s_kVert^{p}\), then some \(w_{k+1}\in\partial F(x_{k+1})\) obeys \(\lVert w_{k+1}Vert\leq(c+\eta)\lVert s_kVert^{p}\).
assumptions_latex: \(F=f+g\), with \(f\) differentiable and \(g\) proper and lower semicontinuous.
The model is first-order consistent and has order-\(p\) gradient error.
The trial satisfies model descent and an order-\(p\) model-stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\geq a\lVert s_k\rVert^{p+1}\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x_{k+1}))\leq(c+\eta)\lVert s_k\rVert^{p}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Higher-order or variable-metric local models whose approximation error transfers model optimality to objective stationarity.

notation.meaning: local composite model at iteration k

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind is reasonable for the Composite-Model Interface leaf. However, the model-stationarity residual is not explicitly defined as an element of a specified model subdifferential, and the order-p assumptions are convention-dependent. An authoritative source is needed to determine and support the precise formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Acceptance Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a model step only when actual reduction is a fixed fraction of positive predicted reduction; model growth then gives uniform objective descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current point \(x_k\), a model \(M_k\), and a trial step \(s_k\), define the predicted reduction \(\Delta_k=M_k(x_k)-M_k(x_k+s_k)\) and actual reduction \(A_k=F(x_k)-F(x_k+s_k)\). A ratio-based acceptance regime fixes \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\) and accepts the trial when \(\Delta_k>0\) and \(\rho_k=A_k/\Delta_k\geq\eta_1\). If accepted trials also satisfy \(\Delta_k\geq c\lVert s_k\rVert^q\) for constants \(c>0\) and \(q>1\), then \(F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\geq\eta_1c\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^q\). Rejected trials leave \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and trigger model regularization or radius contraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\geq\eta_1c\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^q\) for every accepted trial.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Actual-versus-predicted reduction tests ensuring accepted composite-model steps yield uniform objective decrease.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind correctly fits a model-acceptance regime. The reduction-ratio implication is algebraically sound once its assumptions hold, but no trust-region, regularization, or composite-model source is supplied for the acceptance convention and predicted-reduction growth hypothesis.

children.title: Multiblock Descent Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Multiblock families analyzed through a common objective or lifted energy.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) with finite-dimensional Euclidean blocks \(X_i\), let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and write \(x^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_m^k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic cyclic multiblock methods analyzed at completed sweeps through either the original objective or a finite-dimensional lifted energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A completed-sweep sequence \((x^k)\) realizes a multiblock descent interface if there exist intermediate states \(x^{k,0}=x^k,x^{k,1},\ldots,x^{k,m}=x^{k+1}\), where only block \(i\) changes from \(x^{k,i-1}\) to \(x^{k,i}\), and constants \(a_i>0\), \(b>0\) such that \[F(x^{k,i})+a_i\|x_i^{k,i}-x_i^{k,i-1}\|^2\le F(x^{k,i-1})\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\] and there exists \(w^{k+1}\in\partial F(x^{k+1})\) with \[\|w^{k+1}\|\le b\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i^{k,i}-x_i^{k,i-1}\|.\] A lifted-energy realization replaces \(F\) consistently in both conditions by a proper lower-semicontinuous energy on the completed-sweep state and its finite auxiliary data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiblock descent interface records a full cyclic sweep as one outer iteration. Each block update decreases the common objective by a quadratic amount in that block's displacement, and a subgradient at the completed sweep is controlled by the sum of all block displacements. Algorithms whose raw objective lacks this property may use a finite-dimensional lifted energy, provided the same descent and stationarity conditions hold for that energy and its stationary states project appropriately to the original problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^k)\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{block}}(F)\iff \exists(x^{k,i}),a_i,b:\ \forall k,i,\ F(x^{k,i-1})-F(x^{k,i})\ge a_i\|x_i^{k,i}-x_i^{k,i-1}\|^2,\ \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\le b\sum_i\|x_i^{k,i}-x_i^{k,i-1}\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(a=\min_i a_i\), a full sweep satisfies \[F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge a\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i^{k,i}-x_i^{k,i-1}\|^2.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(m=2\), the interface describes two-block alternating updates.
If every block is updated simultaneously, the intermediate-state requirement is replaced by a parallel-update certificate and is outside the cyclic definition.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(F(x^k)\) is bounded below, every block displacement is square-summable over completed sweeps.
The relative-error condition then yields asymptotic stationarity at completed sweeps.
boundary_notes: Essentially cyclic, randomized, or asynchronous schedules require different quantifiers.
Coordinatewise stationarity alone need not imply limiting-subdifferential stationarity of a nonregular objective.

notation.meaning: Intermediate state after updating the first \(i\) blocks of sweep \(k\).

children.title: Alternating-Minimization Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Alternating-Minimization Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update blocks cyclically by exact, inexact, or regularized minimization; a KL interface requires sweepwise decrease and a subgradient controlled by the sweep displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. From \(x^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_m^k)\), update blocks cyclically: for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), choose \(x_i^{k+1}\) as an exact or inexact minimizer of \(u\mapsto F(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},u,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_m^k)+(\tau_i^k/2)\lVert u-x_i^k\rVert^2\). Require constants \(a,b>0\) such that each completed sweep satisfies \(F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\geq a\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert^2\) and admits \(w^{k+1}\in\partial F(x^{k+1})\) with \(\lVert w^{k+1}\rVert\leq b\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert\). Stop when a sweep leaves all blocks unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below on the initial sublevel set.
There are finitely many Euclidean blocks \(X_i\).
Inexact block solves preserve the stated uniform sweepwise descent and residual bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\geq a\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert^2\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\leq b\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic exact, inexact, or proximally regularized minimization over finitely many variable blocks.

notation.meaning: value of block i at sweep k

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the Alternating-Minimization Interface leaf. The record explicitly imposes the sweepwise KL inequalities, but it blends exact, inexact, and proximally regularized block solves without sourcing the conditions under which each variant actually yields those inequalities.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous on finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, and let \((x^k,y^k)\in\operatorname{dom}F\). Let \(\alpha_k,\beta_k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block exact, inexact, or proximally regularized alternating minimization. KL coverage requires additional descent and subgradient controls beyond coordinatewise minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regularized alternating-minimization step is defined by \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\left\{F(x,y^k)+\frac{\alpha_k}{2}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\},\] \[y^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}\left\{F(x^{k+1},y)+\frac{\beta_k}{2}\|y-y^k\|^2\right\}.\] The unregularized exact method has \(\alpha_k=\beta_k=0\). An inexact realization replaces each global minimization by a value-error and block-optimality residual condition, with nonnegative error sequences explicitly controlled. It forms a KL interface only when there exist \(a,b>0\) and \(w^{k+1}\in\partial F(x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\) such that \[F(x^{k+1},y^{k+1})+a\|(x^{k+1}-x^k,y^{k+1}-y^k)\|^2\le F(x^k,y^k),\] \[\|w^{k+1}\|\le b\|(x^{k+1}-x^k,y^{k+1}-y^k)\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating minimization updates one block while holding the other fixed, then reverses the roles. Quadratic proximal terms may regularize either block subproblem; setting them to zero gives exact unregularized alternating minimization. Approximate block solutions require explicit errors. For placement in the KL architecture, the completed two-block sweep must additionally satisfy quantitative sufficient decrease and a full limiting-subgradient bound, since separate coordinatewise optimality conditions need not by themselves yield full stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\in\mathcal A_{\alpha_k,\beta_k}(x^k,y^k)\] exactly when the two displayed sequential regularized minimizations hold; KL-interface membership additionally requires the displayed full-sweep descent and relative-error inequalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The exact block optimality conditions are \[0\in\partial_xF(x^{k+1},y^k)+\alpha_k(x^{k+1}-x^k),\quad 0\in\partial_yF(x^{k+1},y^{k+1})+\beta_k(y^{k+1}-y^k),\] whenever the corresponding partial-subdifferential necessary conditions apply.
special_cases_latex: \(\alpha_k=\beta_k=0\) gives exact alternating minimization.
Uniformly positive \(\alpha_k,\beta_k\) gives proximal alternating minimization.
immediate_consequences_latex: Comparison with the previous block values yields monotonicity of \(F\) for exact regularized updates.
Uniformly positive regularization parameters give quadratic decrease in the two block displacements.
boundary_notes: Coordinatewise minimizers need not be limiting-critical points without regularity connecting partial and full subdifferentials.
Nonunique subproblem solutions require a specified selection but remain admissible if the interface inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: Partial limiting subdifferentials with respect to the indicated block.

children.title: Proximal Alternating Linearization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Proximal alternating linearized and related block-composite families.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F(x,y)=f(x)+g(y)+H(x,y)\) on finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, where \(f,g\) are proper and lower semicontinuous and \(H\) is continuously differentiable. Let \(c_k,d_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block proximal alternating linearization of a smooth coupling term with exact nonsmooth block penalties. The definition uses the newest available value in the second block update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method alternates between blocks, linearizing only the smooth coupling and treating each nonsmooth block term through its proximal map. The second update uses the newly computed first block. The subproblem and proximal-map expressions are equivalent descriptions of the same selected updates. To enter a KL descent analysis, the proximal curvatures must be sufficiently larger than the blockwise gradient Lipschitz constants, uniformly along the sequence, so that completed sweeps yield sufficient decrease and a controlled full subgradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\in\mathcal P_{c_k,d_k}(x^k,y^k)\] if and only if the two sequential proximal linearized subproblems, equivalently the two displayed proximal-map inclusions, hold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The block optimality inclusions are \[0\in\partial f(x^{k+1})+\nabla_xH(x^k,y^k)+c_k(x^{k+1}-x^k),\] \[0\in\partial g(y^{k+1})+\nabla_yH(x^{k+1},y^k)+d_k(y^{k+1}-y^k).\]
special_cases_latex: If \(H(x,y)=H_1(x)+H_2(y)\), the two updates decouple into blockwise proximal-gradient steps.
If \(f=g=0\), the updates become alternating block-gradient steps.
immediate_consequences_latex: Under uniform block-Lipschitz bounds and strictly larger proximal curvatures, there is \(a>0\) such that \[F(x^k,y^k)-F(x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\ge a\bigl(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2+\|y^{k+1}-y^k\|^2\bigr).\]
The optimality inclusions and block-Lipschitz continuity yield a full subgradient whose norm is bounded by current and immediately preceding block displacements.
boundary_notes: Parallel Jacobi linearization is not the sequential interface defined here.
Set-valued nonconvex proximal maps require an accepted selection satisfying the stated subproblems.

notation.meaning: Positive proximal curvatures for the first and second block models.

review_flags: No supplied authoritative locator supports this exact proximal alternating linearization definition and its KL-interface safeguards.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Block Proximal Alternating Linearized Interface
PALM Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PALM cyclically linearizes the smooth coupling and applies a block proximal step; uniform step margins yield descent and blockwise residual compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=H(x_1,\ldots,x_m)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x_i)\), where each \(g_i\) is proper and lower semicontinuous and \(H\) is continuously differentiable. During sweep \(k\), let \(z_i^k=(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},x_i^k,\ldots,x_m^k)\), choose \(c_i^k>L_i^k\), and set \(x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname{prox}_{g_i/c_i^k}(x_i^k-(c_i^k)^{-1}\nabla_iH(z_i^k))\), where \(L_i^k\) is a block-gradient Lipschitz bound. Stop when a full sweep is unchanged. Uniform bounds \(c_i^k-L_i^k\geq\delta>0\) and \(c_i^k\leq\overline c\) yield sweepwise sufficient decrease and a limiting-subgradient residual bounded by the sweep displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(F=H+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i\), with \(H\in C^1\) and each \(g_i\) proper and lower semicontinuous.
Each partial gradient \(\nabla_iH\) is Lipschitz along the updated block with bound \(L_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(a,b>0\) such that \(F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\geq a\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert^2\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\leq b\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic proximal linearization for block-separable nonsmooth terms coupled by a smooth function.

notation.meaning: mixed iterate used for block i during sweep k
local Lipschitz bound for the ith partial gradient

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind correctly matches the PALM Interfaces leaf. An authoritative PALM source is needed to fix the sufficient hypotheses and constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Alternating Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternately minimize each block with a proximal regularizer, using the newest available value of the other block, and stop when the full iterate displacement is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(F(x,y)=f(x)+g(y)+H(x,y)\), choose \((x^0,y^0)\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and parameters \(\alpha_k,\beta_k>0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), select
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\left\{f(x)+H(x,y^k)+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\},
\]
then select
\[
y^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}\left\{g(y)+H(x^{k+1},y)+\frac{1}{2\beta_k}\|y-y^k\|^2\right\}.
\]
Stop when \(\|(x^{k+1},y^{k+1})-(x^k,y^k)\|\leq\varepsilon\), and return \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\). Each displayed subproblem uses the current value of the other block without linearizing \(H\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper lower-semicontinuous functions.
\(H:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is continuous on the relevant level set.
Every displayed proximal subproblem admits a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^{k+1},y^{k+1})\) is the next proximal alternating iterate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact two-block proximal alternating minimization, distinguished from blockwise linearization.
review_flags: Exact proximal-alternating interface is standard, but no supplied locator directly supports this formulation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the terminal interface, and the exact two-block proximal alternating update is mathematically coherent. No citation or inspectable locator supports this particular formulation, including its parameterization and stopping rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Blockwise Residual Compatibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block residuals are compatible when they assemble into a full limiting-subgradient whose norm is bounded by the latest iterate displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z^k=(z_1^k,\ldots,z_p^k)\) be iterates for a proper lower-semicontinuous objective \(F\). Blockwise residual compatibility holds if there exist \(b>0\) and vectors \(r_i^{k+1}\) such that the assembled vector \(r^{k+1}=(r_1^{k+1},\ldots,r_p^{k+1})\) satisfies
\[
r^{k+1}\in\partial F(z^{k+1}),\qquad
\|r^{k+1}\|\leq b\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(z^{k+1}))\leq b\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|.
\]
Thus vanishing iterate displacements force the full stationarity residual to vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^N\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
The block residuals are evaluated at the common completed iterate \(z^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(z^{k+1}))\leq b\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-error condition connecting block optimality residuals to the full limiting subdifferential.
review_flags: A KL-compatible relative-error condition is stated, but no supplied source directly locates its multiblock derivation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the residual-compatibility leaf, and the distance inequality follows directly from the stated assembled-subgradient bound. An authoritative locator is still required for this multiblock relative-error condition and its interpretation as the intended KL interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Coordinate Descent Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly minimize selected coordinate blocks while fixing the others; cyclic and essentially cyclic schedules guarantee recurring selection of every block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\) and choose \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}F\). At iteration \(k\), select a nonempty block set \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\). For each \(i\in I_k\), using a fixed sequential order, set
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u_i}F(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},u_i,x_{i+1}^{k},\ldots,x_p^k),
\]
and set \(x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k\) for unselected blocks. A cyclic rule visits blocks in a fixed cycle; an essentially cyclic rule has an integer \(T\geq1\) such that every block is selected at least once among \(I_k,\ldots,I_{k+T-1}\). Stop when \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|\leq\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^{n_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb R^{n_p}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
Every selected block subproblem admits a minimizer.
The block-selection rule is cyclic, essentially cyclic, or otherwise explicitly specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\) is the completed selected-block coordinate-descent iterate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact selected-block descent covering cyclic and essentially cyclic schedules.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the selected-block and essentially cyclic formulation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the block-coordinate interface, but no source supports the combined selected-block, sequential-update, cyclic, and essentially cyclic formulation. The treatment of simultaneously selected blocks through a fixed sequential order also requires an explicit reference.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selected-block coordinate descent with cyclic and essentially cyclic rules
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), where each \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is nonempty, and let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). Write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), and let \(U_i(x)\subseteq X_i\) denote the nonempty set of admissible replacements of block \(i\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic block descent. Exact block minimization is used to define the interface; surrogate, proximal, inexact, and randomized updates are nearby variants rather than part of its formal core.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A selected-block coordinate-descent sequence is a pair \(\{(x^k,i_k)\}_{k\ge0}\) such that \(x^k\in X\), \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and, for every \(k\ge0\), \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in U_{i_k}(x^k)}F(x_1^k,\ldots,x_{i_k-1}^k,u,x_{i_k+1}^k,\ldots,x_m^k),\qquad x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\quad(j\ne i_k).\] The selection rule is cyclic when \(i_k=1+(k\bmod m)\). It is essentially cyclic when there exists an integer \(T\ge m\) such that \[\bigcup_{t=0}^{T-1}\{i_{k+t}\}=\{1,\ldots,m\}\qquad\text{for every }k\ge0.\] More generally, it is an admissible selected-block rule when every block is selected infinitely often. A full cyclic Gauss–Seidel sweep is the equivalent grouped update obtained by applying the displayed block minimization successively for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), using already updated blocks within the sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block coordinate-descent interface partitions the feasible set into blocks and, at each iteration, changes only a selected block by exactly minimizing the objective over that block's admissible replacement set. A cyclic rule visits blocks in the fixed order 1 through m. An essentially cyclic rule requires every block to occur in every window of some fixed finite length T. The weaker admissible selected-block condition requires each block to be selected infinitely often. A full Gauss–Seidel sweep groups m successive cyclic single-block updates and uses new values immediately.
assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) is a nonempty Cartesian-product domain.
For every iterate \(x^k\), the selected replacement set \(U_{i_k}(x^k)\) is nonempty and the displayed block argmin is nonempty.
The selection sequence \((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) is specified independently of the definition of the block minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(x^k,i_k)\}_{k\ge0}\) is a cyclic, essentially cyclic, or admissibly selected-block coordinate-descent process according to the corresponding quantified selection condition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For singleton selections, essential cyclicity is equivalent to the existence of \(T<\infty\) such that every block is updated at least once among iterations \(k,\ldots,k+T-1\), for every \(k\).
A cyclic full sweep can be represented either by \(m\) single-block iterates or by one outer iterate containing the successive Gauss–Seidel block minimizations.
special_cases_latex: If \(m=n\), \(n_i=1\), and \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R\), the interface is ordinary coordinate descent.
If \(U_i(x)=X_i\), each selected subproblem is unrestricted exact minimization over its block feasible set.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every exact selected-block update satisfies \(F(x^{k+1})\le F(x^k)\).
Cyclic selection is essentially cyclic with \(T=m\), and essential cyclicity implies that every block is selected infinitely often.
boundary_notes: Infinite visitation alone does not impose a uniform bound on the delay between two updates of a block and is strictly weaker than essential cyclicity.
The definition does not assert convergence, uniqueness of block minimizers, stationarity of cluster points, or a KL property.

notation.meaning: Admissible replacement set for block i at state x.
Uniform coverage-window length for an essentially cyclic rule.
