knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Landscape Regime Family Induced by Geometric Margins
Sample-Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When simultaneous derivative-deviation bounds decrease with sample size and eventually meet the prescribed tolerances, the sample-size regime starts at the smallest sample size meeting all three bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). Suppose that, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), the empirical objective satisfies the simultaneous bounds \[\Delta_k(n):=\sup_{x\in D}\|\nabla^kL_n(x)-\nabla^kL(x)\|_k\leq\varepsilon_k(n,\delta),\qquad k\in\{0,1,2\},\] where \(\Delta_0(n)=\sup_{x\in D}|L_n(x)-L(x)|\), the order-one norm is Euclidean, and the order-two norm is the operator norm. Let \(\tau_0,\tau_1,\tau_2>0\). Assume that each \(m\mapsto\varepsilon_k(m,\delta)\) is nonincreasing and that the set \(\{m\in\mathbb N:\varepsilon_k(m,\delta)\leq\tau_k\text{ for all }k\in\{0,1,2\}\}\) is nonempty. Define \[n_\star(\delta):=\min\{m\in\mathbb N:\varepsilon_k(m,\delta)\leq\tau_k\text{ for all }k\in\{0,1,2\}\}.\] Then every \(n\geq n_\star(\delta)\) satisfies all three prescribed transfer tolerances simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\delta\). The tolerances must be chosen below the margins required by the intended landscape certificate, with any feature-specific constants accounted for.
assumptions_latex: The value, gradient, and Hessian deviations admit simultaneous probability-\(1-\delta\) bounds \(\varepsilon_k(n,\delta)\).
For each \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\), the function \(n\mapsto\varepsilon_k(n,\delta)\) is nonincreasing.
Positive tolerances \(\tau_0,\tau_1,\tau_2\) are specified, and some \(m\in\mathbb N\) satisfies all three bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(n\geq n_\star(\delta)\), all three prescribed transfer tolerances hold simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample thresholds determined by uniform derivative concentration and landscape margins.

notation.meaning: smallest sample size meeting all prescribed tolerances

knowledge_statements.title: Noise Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise preserves a specified value gap, gradient exclusion margin, or negative-curvature margin when the corresponding uniform perturbation is smaller than that margin; a two-times perturbation allowance is needed for a gap between two objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), let \(L^{(0)}:D	o\mathbb R\) be a twice continuously differentiable noiseless population objective, and let \(L^{(\sigma)}:D	o\mathbb R\) be its twice continuously differentiable noise-perturbed counterpart. Suppose \[\sup_{x\in D}|L^{(\sigma)}(x)-L^{(0)}(x)|\leq eta_0(\sigma),\] \[\sup_{x\in D}\|
abla L^{(\sigma)}(x)-
abla L^{(0)}(x)\|\leq eta_1(\sigma),\] and \[\sup_{x\in D}\|
abla^2L^{(\sigma)}(x)-
abla^2L^{(0)}(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq eta_2(\sigma).\] A noiseless value gap \(L^{(0)}(y)-L^{(0)}(x)\geq m_0\) survives with gap at least \(m_0-2 eta_0(\sigma)\). A gradient exclusion bound \(\|
abla L^{(0)}(x)\|\geq m_1\) survives with residual at least \(m_1- eta_1(\sigma)\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2L^{(0)}(x))\leq-m_2\), then \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2L^{(\sigma)}(x))\leq-(m_2- eta_2(\sigma))\). Thus a stable noise regime for these features requires \(2 eta_0(\sigma)<m_0\), \( eta_1(\sigma)<m_1\), and \( eta_2(\sigma)<m_2\), retaining only the inequalities relevant to the intended certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(L^{(0)}\) and \(L^{(\sigma)}\) are twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(D\).
The displayed uniform value, gradient, and Hessian perturbation bounds hold.
The relevant noiseless feature has a positive margin \(m_0\), \(m_1\), or \(m_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Value gaps retain margin \(m_0-2\beta_0(\sigma)\), gradient exclusions retain margin \(m_1-\beta_1(\sigma)\), and negative curvature retains magnitude \(m_2-\beta_2(\sigma)\) whenever the respective residual is positive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative perturbation thresholds separating stable and unstable noisy landscapes.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally strongly convex population basin remains conditioned empirically when Hessian error is below its smallest curvature; an explicit perturbed condition-number bound results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq D\) be a basin on which the population Hessian satisfies \[\mu I\preceq\nabla^2L(x)\preceq M I\qquad(x\in B),\] for constants \(0<\mu\leq M\). Its population conditioning is \(\kappa=M/\mu\). If uniform curvature transfer holds on \(B\) with \(\varepsilon_2<\mu\), then \[(\mu-\varepsilon_2)I\preceq\nabla^2L_n(x)\preceq(M+\varepsilon_2)I\qquad(x\in B),\] and the empirical condition number is at most \((M+\varepsilon_2)/(\mu-\varepsilon_2)\). The well-conditioned regime requires this upper bound to remain below the application’s prescribed conditioning threshold.
assumptions_latex: Uniform Hessian error on \(B\) is at most \(\varepsilon_2<\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The empirical Hessian spectrum lies in \([\mu-\varepsilon_2,M+\varepsilon_2]\), giving condition number at most \((M+\varepsilon_2)/(\mu-\varepsilon_2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local spectral regimes controlling stability and empirical condition numbers.

knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Regime Interactions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise and sampling add in each uniform derivative-deviation budget. Gradient and curvature margins lose the combined deviation, while a value gap between two points can lose twice the combined value deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), and let \(L^{(0)}\), \(L^{(\sigma)}\), and \(L_n^{(\sigma)}\) denote the noiseless population, noisy population, and noisy empirical objectives. Suppose noise contributes uniform derivative-level deviations \(\beta_k(\sigma)\), and suppose that, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), sampling contributes deviations \(\varepsilon_k(n,\delta)\) between \(L_n^{(\sigma)}\) and \(L^{(\sigma)}\), for \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\), using absolute value at order zero, the Euclidean norm at order one, and the operator norm at order two. Then the triangle inequality gives \[r_k(n,\sigma,\delta):=\beta_k(\sigma)+\varepsilon_k(n,\delta)\] as a uniform order-\(k\) deviation bound between the noisy empirical and noiseless population objectives. Consequently, a noiseless value gap of size \(m_0\) survives with residual at least \(m_0-2r_0\), a gradient exclusion margin \(m_1\) survives with residual at least \(m_1-r_1\), and a negative-curvature magnitude \(m_2\) survives with residual at least \(m_2-r_2\). A joint certified regime therefore requires \(2r_0<m_0\), \(r_1<m_1\), and \(r_2<m_2\) for the respective features used by the certificate.
assumptions_latex: Uniform noise deviations \(\beta_k(\sigma)\) hold at each required order \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\).
With probability at least \(1-\delta\), uniform sampling deviations \(\varepsilon_k(n,\delta)\) hold simultaneously at each required order.
The noiseless landscape has the specified positive value-gap, gradient-exclusion, or negative-curvature margins.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With probability at least \(1-\delta\), the relevant features persist when \(2r_0<m_0\), \(r_1<m_1\), and \(r_2<m_2\), with residual margins \(m_0-2r_0\), \(m_1-r_1\), and \(m_2-r_2\), respectively.

children.title: Local-to-Global Certificate Routes
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms connecting local criticality to global optimality or recovery.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space or smooth manifold, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), let \(R\subseteq X\), and let \(X_\star\subseteq X\) be the designated globally valid solution set. Let \(C_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\) be a local certificate predicate defined using information available at \(x\), and let \(C_{\mathrm{glob}}(x)\) be a global optimality or recovery predicate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition formalizes an implication supplied by landscape structure. It covers exact and quantitative routes but does not assert that stationarity alone is sufficient for an arbitrary nonconvex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local-to-global certificate route on \(R\) is a tuple \((C_{\mathrm{loc}},C_{\mathrm{glob}},R,\eta)\) such that, for every \(x\in R\), \[C_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\ \Longrightarrow\ C_{\mathrm{glob}}(x).\] In the quantitative optimality form, \(C_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\) is a residual inequality \(r_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\leq\eta\), while \(C_{\mathrm{glob}}(x)\) is \[f(x)-\inf_X f\leq\omega(\eta)\quad\text{or}\quad \operatorname{dist}(x,X_\star)\leq\rho(\eta),\] for specified moduli \(\omega,rho:[0,infty)\to[0,infty]\). An exact route has \(\eta=0\), \(\omega(0)=\rho(0)=0\), and concludes \(x\in X_\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local-to-global certificate route is a uniform implication on a stated region: whenever a point satisfies a local predicate, it also satisfies a designated global-optimality or recovery predicate. Quantitative routes map a local residual tolerance to an objective-gap or distance-to-solution bound. Exact routes send a zero local residual to membership in the global solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in R,quad r_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\leq\eta\ \Longrightarrow\ \bigl(f(x)-\inf_Xf\leq\omega(\eta)\ \text{or}\ \operatorname{dist}(x,X_\star)\leq\rho(\eta)\bigr).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The route may be represented by the set inclusion \(\{x\in R:C_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\}\subseteq\{x\in R:C_{\mathrm{glob}}(x)\}\).
When \(C_{\mathrm{glob}}(x)\) is \(x\in X_\star\), the route says that the certified local-point set within \(R\) contains no spurious points.
special_cases_latex: A second-order route takes \(C_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\) to be \(\nabla f(x)=0\) and \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq0\).
A recovery route uses a representation map \(\pi:X\to Z\) and concludes \(d_Z(\pi(x),z_\star)\leq\rho(\eta)\).
A convex-dual route uses equality between a primal value and a dual lower bound as the local verifiable predicate.
immediate_consequences_latex: If an algorithm returns \(x\in R\) satisfying the local certificate, the same point automatically satisfies the route's declared global predicate.
Composing two valid implications \(C_1\Rightarrow C_2\) and \(C_2\Rightarrow C_3\) on a common region yields a route \(C_1\Rightarrow C_3\).
boundary_notes: A route is regional unless \(R=X\); behavior outside \(R\) is unspecified.
The definition separates the route from the theorem establishing it for a particular objective.
No inspected supplied source states this abstract certificate-route object.

notation.meaning: Moduli translating local residual accuracy into global quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero gradient and positive-semidefinite Hessian certify second-order stationarity; in a landscape where every nonglobal critical point is a strict saddle, they certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable. A point \( ar x\) has a second-order stationarity certificate when \(
abla f( ar x)=0\) and \(
abla^2 f( ar x)\succeq0\). These conditions certify that \( ar x\) is a second-order stationary point. If, additionally, every critical point of \(f\) is either a global minimizer or has a direction \(d\) satisfying \(d^{\mathsf T}
abla^2f( ar x)d<0\), then the certificate excludes the strict-saddle alternative and therefore certifies global optimality of \( ar x\).
assumptions_latex: Every critical point is globally minimizing or has a negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\) and \(\nabla^2f(\bar x)\succeq0\) imply \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\) under the benign-landscape hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth certificate under a benign strict-saddle landscape hypothesis.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Latent Recovery Certificate System Modulo Symmetry
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be a parameter space, \((Z,d_Z)\) a latent-object space, \(\pi:\Theta\to Z\) a representation map, and \(f_y:\Theta\to\mathbb R\) an objective constructed from data \(y\). Let \(z_\star\in Z\) be the intended latent object and let a group \(G\) act on \(Z\), representing unavoidable nonidentifiability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition separates optimization correctness from identifiability. Recovery is measured in the quotient geometry induced by a declared symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the symmetry-adjusted discrepancy \[d_G(z,z_\star):=\inf_{g\in G}d_Z(z,g\cdot z_\star).\] A latent recovery certificate system with accuracy \(\varepsilon\geq0\) is a predicate \(C_y:\Theta\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}\) satisfying \[\forall\theta\in\Theta,quad C_y(\theta)\Longrightarrow d_G(\pi(\theta),z_\star)\leq\varepsilon.\] It is a global-minimizer recovery system when \(C_y(\theta)\) is \(f_y(\theta)=\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}f_y(\vartheta)\). It is exact when \(\varepsilon=0\), so every certified parameter represents the orbit \(G\cdot z_\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latent recovery certificate system specifies a parameterization, a latent representation, an unavoidable symmetry group, and a predicate whose satisfaction guarantees closeness to the intended latent object modulo that symmetry. In the global-minimizer form, every global minimizer of the data objective must represent the target orbit. Exact recovery sets the quotient distance to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\{\pi(\theta):C_y(\theta)\}\subseteq\{z\in Z:d_G(z,z_\star)\leq\varepsilon\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the global-minimizer predicate, the defining implication is equivalent to \(\pi(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\Theta}f_y)\subseteq\{z:d_G(z,z_\star)\leq\varepsilon\}\).
When the group action is by isometries and orbit distance is a metric on \(Z/G\), the certificate states that the quotient class \([\pi(\theta)]\) lies within \(\varepsilon\) of \([z_\star]\).
special_cases_latex: With trivial \(G\), recovery is measured directly by \(d_Z(\pi(\theta),z_\star)\).
For real phase retrieval, \(G=\{+1,-1\}\); for orthogonal matrix factorization, \(G=O(r)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact global-minimizer recovery rules out globally optimal representations outside the target orbit.
A parameter-space error guarantee follows only if the representation map admits an inverse stability bound modulo its parameter symmetries.
boundary_notes: The certificate does not guarantee that an algorithm reaches a point satisfying \(C_y\).
Recovery of the latent object does not imply uniqueness of its parameterization.

knowledge_statements.title: Latent Recovery Certificate System Modulo Symmetry
Recovery Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measurement feasibility plus a positive restricted lower bound on every difference of two model elements certifies that the recovered latent object equals the truth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be finite-dimensional real normed spaces, let \(\mathcal M\subseteq E\), and let \(\mathcal A:E\to F\) be linear. Suppose \(b=\mathcal A(X_\star)\) for some \(X_\star\in\mathcal M\), and let \(\widehat X\in\mathcal M\) satisfy \(\mathcal A(\widehat X)=b\). If there exists \(\alpha>0\) such that \(\|\mathcal A(H)\|_F\geq\alpha\|H\|_E\) for every \(H\in\mathcal M-\mathcal M\), then \(\widehat X=X_\star\). Thus measurement feasibility together with the restricted lower bound is an exact-recovery certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(F\) are finite-dimensional real normed spaces.
\(\|\mathcal A(H)\|_F\geq\alpha\|H\|_E\) for every \(H\in\mathcal M-\mathcal M\) and some \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A(\widehat X)=b\Longrightarrow\widehat X=X_\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery from noiseless measurements using restricted injectivity on the model difference set.

notation.meaning: Set of all differences between two model elements.
The norms on E and F, respectively.

knowledge_statements.title: Identifiability Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is identifiable exactly when no nonzero difference of two model elements lies in the measurement nullspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\subseteq E\) and let \(\mathcal A:E\to F\) be linear. The measurements uniquely identify every element of \(\mathcal M\) if and only if \(\ker(\mathcal A)\cap(\mathcal M-\mathcal M)=\{0\}\). Indeed, for a fixed \(X_\star\in\mathcal M\), the localized condition \(\ker(\mathcal A)\cap(\mathcal M-X_\star)=\{0\}\) certifies that \(X_\star\) is the unique member of \(\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\mathcal A(X)=\mathcal A(X_\star)\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\subseteq E\) is the admissible model class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A|_{\mathcal M}\) is injective if and only if \(\ker(\mathcal A)\cap(\mathcal M-\mathcal M)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nullspace characterization of noiseless identifiability over a structured model class.

notation.meaning: Differences between model elements and the fixed truth.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The global and localized nullspace characterizations are mathematically precise, agree with the plain statement, and fit the certificate container, but no inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Latent-Object Transfer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence of factors to the reference symmetry orbit implies convergence of their represented latent objects when reconstruction obeys a Lipschitz bound throughout a fixed orbit-distance neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Theta,d_\Theta)\) be a metric space on which a group \(G\) acts, let \(E\) be a normed space, and let \(R:\Theta\to E\) satisfy \(R(g\cdot\theta)=R(\theta)\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(\theta\in\Theta\). Fix \(\theta_\star\in\Theta\), and define \(\operatorname{dist}(\theta,G\cdot\theta_\star)=\inf_{g\in G}d_\Theta(\theta,g\cdot\theta_\star)\). Suppose there exist \(L<\infty\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(\|R(\theta)-R(\theta_\star)\|_E\leq L\operatorname{dist}(\theta,G\cdot\theta_\star)\) whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(\theta,G\cdot\theta_\star)<\varepsilon\). Then every sequence \((\theta_k)\) satisfying \(\operatorname{dist}(\theta_k,G\cdot\theta_\star)\to0\) also satisfies \(R(\theta_k)\to R(\theta_\star)\). The same inequality transfers quantitative orbit-error bounds to latent-object error bounds.
assumptions_latex: \((\Theta,d_\Theta)\) is a metric space with a \(G\)-action, and \(E\) is a normed space.
There exist \(L<\infty\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) for which the displayed bound holds whenever \(\operatorname{dist}(\theta,G\cdot\theta_\star)<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(\theta_k,G\cdot\theta_\star)\to0\Longrightarrow\|R(\theta_k)-R(\theta_\star)\|_E\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from factor convergence modulo symmetry to convergence of the represented latent object.

notation.meaning: Symmetry orbit of the reference parameter.
Infimum of the metric distance from theta to points in the reference orbit.
Map from parameters to represented latent objects.

children.title: Convex-Dual Certificate System
children.top_down_role: External global certificates obtained from lifted, relaxed, or dual formulations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonconvex parameter set, let \(K\) be a convex set in a finite-dimensional vector space, let \(\Pi:X\to K\) be a lifting map, and let \(F:K\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be convex with \(f(x)=F(\Pi(x))\). Let \(Y\) be a dual-feasible set and \(d:Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) a dual objective satisfying weak duality \(d(y)\leq\inf_{Z\in K}F(Z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers exact and gap-based certificates obtained from convex liftings, relaxations, or dual problems. It does not assume that every lifted feasible point is representable by a nonconvex parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex-dual certificate for \(x\in X\) is a dual-feasible \(y\in Y\) such that \[F(\Pi(x))=d(y).\] An \(\varepsilon\)-certificate satisfies the nonnegative primal-dual gap bound \[0\leq F(\Pi(x))-d(y)\leq\varepsilon.\] The certificate system is the collection of tuples \((x,Pi(x),y)\) satisfying primal feasibility, dual feasibility, the lifting identity, and the stated gap relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-dual certificate pairs a nonconvex parameter with its convex lift and a dual-feasible object. Exact equality between the lifted primal value and the dual lower bound certifies global optimality. A quantitative certificate permits a primal-dual gap no larger than epsilon and therefore certifies the same objective-value accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal C_\varepsilon:=\{(x,y)\in X\times Y:0\leq f(x)-d(y)=F(\Pi(x))-d(y)\leq\varepsilon\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: An exact certificate is equivalently a zero primal-dual gap: \(f(x)-d(y)=0\).
If strong duality holds and both optima are attained, exact certification is equivalent to simultaneous primal and dual optimality together with equality of their objective values.
special_cases_latex: A semidefinite certificate uses a positive-semidefinite lifted matrix and a dual slack matrix satisfying feasibility and zero gap.
A convex relaxation certificate remains valid for the original nonconvex problem when the certified lifted optimum equals \(\Pi(x)\) for a feasible \(x\in X\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Weak duality gives \(0\leq f(x)-\inf_{z\in X}f(z)\leq\varepsilon\) for every \((x,y)\in\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), provided the convex lower bound is valid for all nonconvex feasible points.
An exact certificate establishes global optimality of \(x\) without requiring local derivative information.
boundary_notes: A relaxation optimum of lower value than every representable lift does not certify an original feasible parameter.
Zero gap alone is meaningful only after primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and the valid lower-bound relation have been established.
No supplied source was located for this exact abstract lifting-and-duality definition.

notation.meaning: Map lifting a nonconvex parameter to a convex feasible object.
Dual lower bound associated with a dual-feasible object y.
Set of parameter-certificate pairs with primal-dual gap at most epsilon.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Weak duality and zero primal-dual gap are standard global-optimality certificate mechanisms.
An inspected source is required for the node-specific combination with a nonconvex lifting map.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Convex-Dual Global-Optimality Certificate
Convex Lower-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex outer relaxation supplies a lower bound; an original-feasible point attaining that bound certifies global optimality and exact relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq C\subseteq E\), where \(C\) is convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be convex. Define \(p_S=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\) and \(p_C=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\). Set inclusion gives \(p_C\leq p_S\), so any certified value \(\ell\leq p_C\) is also a lower bound for the original problem. If some \(\widehat x\in S\) satisfies \(f(\widehat x)=p_C\), then \(p_S=p_C=f(\widehat x)\), certifying both global optimality and tightness of the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_C\leq p_S\), and \(\widehat x\in S\) with \(f(\widehat x)=p_C\) implies \(p_S=p_C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds obtained by minimizing the same objective over a convex outer relaxation.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the original problem.
Optimal value of the convex relaxation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound and tightness certificate is mathematically correct and appropriately classified, but no source with an inspectable locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a finite-dimensional convex equality-constrained problem, primal feasibility and convex stationarity with a multiplier certify matching primal and dual values and hence global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, let \(A:E\to F\) be linear, let \(C\subseteq E\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f:E\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. Consider \(\inf\{f(x):x\in C,\ Ax=b\}\), and define the dual function by \(q(y)=\inf_{x\in C}\{f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle_F\}\). If \(\widehat x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), \(A\widehat x=b\), and \(0\in\partial f(\widehat x)+A^*\widehat y+N_C(\widehat x)\), then \(\widehat x\) minimizes the Lagrangian over \(C\), so \(q(\widehat y)=f(\widehat x)\). Weak duality therefore certifies that \(\widehat x\) is globally optimal and \(\widehat y\) is dual optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(F\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, and \(A:E\to F\) is linear.
\(C\subseteq E\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\widehat y)=f(\widehat x)=\inf\{f(x):x\in C,\ Ax=b\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT-style primal-dual certificate for a convex equality-constrained problem.

notation.meaning: Dual function obtained by minimizing the equality-constraint Lagrangian over C.
Convex normal cone to C at x.
Convex subdifferential of f at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Tightness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation is tight exactly when it has an original-feasible minimizer; a positive value gap is the sharp obstruction to certificate transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq C\) be nonempty compact sets with \(C\) convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. The relaxation is tight precisely when \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)=\min_{x\in S}f(x)\), equivalently when \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\cap S\neq\varnothing\). Its failure boundary is crossed when every relaxed minimizer lies outside \(S\) and has value strictly below every point of \(S\); then the positive gap \(\Delta=\min_{x\in S}f(x)-\min_{x\in C}f(x)>0\) prevents any relaxed minimizer from certifying an original solution.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq C\) are nonempty and compact, with \(C\) convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_C f=\min_S f\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\cap S\neq\varnothing\); otherwise the value gap \(\Delta\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion separating tight convex relaxations from value-gap failure.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Compactness and continuity make both minima attainable, and the stated equivalence and positive-gap alternative are correct. The failure-boundary content kind also fits, but the record lacks an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Lambda\) be an instance index set. For each \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), let \(M_\lambda\) be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold, let \(f_\lambda:M_\lambda\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable, and let \(G_\lambda\) act smoothly on \(M_\lambda\) with \(f_\lambda(g\cdot x)=f_\lambda(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a taxonomy-level definition for smooth finite-dimensional model families studied through critical points, symmetries, and regional geometry. It is not a claim that every listed family has a benign landscape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A canonical smooth nonconvex landscape model is a datum \[\mathfrak L_\lambda=(M_\lambda,f_\lambda,G_\lambda,X_{\star,lambda},\{R_{\lambda,k}\}_{k\in K_\lambda}),\] where \(X_{\star,lambda}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in M_\lambda}f_\lambda(x)\), each \(R_{\lambda,k}\subseteq M_\lambda\) is a declared geometric region, and the landscape is analyzed using the critical set \(\operatorname{Crit}(f_\lambda)=\{x:\operatorname{grad}f_\lambda(x)=0\}\), Hessian inertia on tangent spaces, orbit structure under \(G_\lambda\), and the placement of \(X_{\star,lambda}\) within the regions. A model family is a collection \(\{\mathfrak L_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\) with these components specified uniformly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A canonical smooth nonconvex landscape model packages a smooth parameter manifold, a twice continuously differentiable objective, its symmetry action, its global minimizers, and a declared regional decomposition. Its landscape geometry consists of the critical set, tangent-space Hessian inertia, symmetry orbits, and the relationship between critical regions and global solutions. A family is indexed by problem instances with these objects specified consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak L_\lambda=(M_\lambda,f_\lambda,G_\lambda,\operatorname*{argmin}f_\lambda,\{R_{\lambda,k}\}_{k\in K_\lambda}),\qquad f_\lambda\in C^2(M_\lambda).\]

If the group action is free and proper, invariant landscape information may equivalently be described on the quotient manifold \(M_\lambda/G_\lambda\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m,n,q\geq1\), let \(\ell:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable, and parameterize matrices of rank at most \(q\) by \(X=UV^\top\) with \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\) and \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\). Let \(r\) be an optional smooth regularizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers smooth asymmetric factorization and its symmetric positive-semidefinite specialization. Measurement, sampling, corruption, and rank-misspecification assumptions define narrower descendant families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The asymmetric low-rank factorization landscape induced by \((\ell,r,q)\) is the smooth objective \[\Phi_q(U,V):=\ell(UV^\top)+r(U,V),\qquad (U,V)\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\times\mathbb R^{n\times q}.\] When \(r=0\), the represented matrix is invariant under \[(U,V)\mapsto(UQ,VQ^{-\top}),\qquad Q\in\operatorname{GL}(q).\] For a symmetric positive-semidefinite variable \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), the corresponding factorization landscape is \[\Psi_q(Y):=\ell(YY^\top)+r(Y),\qquad Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times q},\] with right-orthogonal symmetry \(Y\mapsto YQ\) for \(Q\in O(q)\) whenever the regularizer is invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank factorization landscape is the smooth objective obtained by composing a matrix loss with a rank-q factorization, optionally adding a smooth factor regularizer. The asymmetric form represents a matrix as U times V transpose and possesses a change-of-factor symmetry in the unregularized case. The positive-semidefinite form represents the matrix as Y times Y transpose and has right-orthogonal symmetry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Phi_q=\ell\circ\pi_q+r,quad \pi_q(U,V)=UV^\top,quad \operatorname{rank}(\pi_q(U,V))\leq q.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The factorized problem is \(\min\{\ell(X):\operatorname{rank}(X)\leq q\}\) expressed through the surjective parameterization \(X=UV^\top\), when \(r=0\).
For symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices, \(X=YY^\top\) parameterizes exactly the set \(\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{rank}(X)\leq q\}\).
special_cases_latex: The balancing regularizer \(r(U,V)=\frac\mu4\|U^\top U-V^\top V\|_F^2\) reduces scaling imbalance while preserving represented matrices at balanced factors.
Least-squares losses take \(\ell(X)=\frac12\|\mathcal A(X)-b\|_2^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The factorization removes an explicit rank constraint but generally makes the parameter objective nonconvex.
Equivalent factor pairs lie on symmetry orbits and cannot be distinguished solely from their represented matrix.
boundary_notes: A landscape guarantee depends on the loss, rank, regularizer, and data geometry; none is implied by factorization alone.
Nonsmooth penalties are outside the stated \(C^2\) regime.
No inspected supplied source directly supports this complete definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Matrix-Factorization Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exact-rank PSD factorization, all local minima reconstruct the target, exact factors differ only by an orthogonal transformation, and every other critical point is a strict saddle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be positive semidefinite with rank \(r\), and define \(f(U)=\tfrac14\|UU^{\mathsf T}-M\|_F^2\) for \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). Every local minimizer \(U\) satisfies \(UU^{\mathsf T}=M\) and is therefore global. Moreover, every critical point failing this equality has a direction \(D\) with \(\langle D,\nabla^2f(U)[D]\rangle<0\). Thus the only local minima are the exact factors \(U=M^{1/2}Q\), with the appropriate thin square root and \(Q\in O(r)\), while all other critical points are strict saddles.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is a local minimizer if and only if \(UU^{\mathsf T}=M\); every other critical point has negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-rank symmetric positive-semidefinite factorization with a squared Frobenius objective.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The exact-rank PSD factorization theorem is plausible and correctly scoped, but the strict-saddle assertion is a nontrivial landscape theorem and has no cited source. A specialist theorem locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Symmetric and Asymmetric Matrix-Factorization Objectives
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M_\star\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r\), and let \(q\geq r\). In the positive-semidefinite case assume \(m=n\) and \(M_\star\succeq0\). Norms are Frobenius norms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact means that the full target matrix is observed without measurement noise or missing entries. The definition supplies baseline objectives, not a classification of all their critical points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact asymmetric matrix-factorization landscape of width \(q\) is \[\Phi_q(U,V):=\frac12\|UV^\top-M_\star\|_F^2,quad (U,V)\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\times\mathbb R^{n\times q}.\] Its exact solution set is \[\mathcal S_q^{\mathrm{asym}}:=\{(U,V):UV^\top=M_\star\}.\] If \(M_\star\succeq0\), the exact symmetric landscape is \[\Psi_q(Y):=\frac14\|YY^\top-M_\star\|_F^2,quad Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times q},\] with solution set \(\mathcal S_q^{\mathrm{sym}}:=\{Y:YY^\top=M_\star\}\). The constants \(1/2\) and \(1/4\) are normalization conventions and do not alter minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact matrix-factorization landscape fits factor products directly to a fully known target matrix using squared Frobenius loss. The asymmetric model uses two rectangular factors, while the positive-semidefinite symmetric model uses one factor multiplied by its transpose. When the factor width is at least the target rank, the global minimum value is zero and the exact solution set consists of factors reproducing the target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname*{argmin}\Phi_q=\mathcal S_q^{\mathrm{asym}},quad \min\Phi_q=0;qquad \operatorname*{argmin}\Psi_q=\mathcal S_q^{\mathrm{sym}},quad \min\Psi_q=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing a compact singular-value decomposition \(M_\star=P\Sigma Q^\top\), one exact asymmetric factor pair is \(U=P\Sigma^{1/2}\) and \(V=Q\Sigma^{1/2}\), with zero columns appended if \(q>r\).
For \(M_\star=P\Sigma P^\top\succeq0\), one symmetric solution is \(Y=P\Sigma^{1/2}\), again with zero columns appended when needed.
special_cases_latex: For \(q=r\) and full-column-rank factors, asymmetric exact factorizations are related by invertible changes of basis.
For a rank-one positive-semidefinite target \(M_\star=xx^\top\), the symmetric objective is \(\frac14\|yy^\top-xx^\top\|_F^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every exact factorization is a global minimizer because the objectives are nonnegative.
The minimizer set is generally nonunique because factor symmetries preserve the matrix product.
boundary_notes: If \(q<r\), zero residual is impossible and the problem becomes best rank-constrained approximation rather than exact factorization.
No sampling operator, observation noise, or regularization is included.

children.title: Spectral Subspace Landscape Family
children.top_down_role: Spectral and subspace-estimation landscape models.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S^n\) be real symmetric and let \(1\leq qleq n\). The Stiefel manifold is \(\operatorname{St}(n,q)=\{U\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}:U^\top U=I_q\}\), and the Grassmannian identifies matrices having the same column space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers smooth eigen-subspace estimation through a trace objective. Statistical perturbation and eigengap-dependent recovery guarantees are not included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The rank-\(q\) spectral subspace landscape associated with \(A\) is \[f_A(U):=-\operatorname{tr}(U^\top AU),quad U\in\operatorname{St}(n,q).\] It is invariant under the right action \(U\mapsto UQ\) for \(Q\in O(q)\), and hence defines a function on \(\operatorname{Gr}(n,q)=\operatorname{St}(n,q)/O(q)\). Equivalently, using the projector \(P=UU^\top\), the landscape is \[-\operatorname{tr}(AP)\quad\text{over}\quad P=P^\top=P^2,quad \operatorname{tr}(P)=q.\] The minimizing subspaces are the invariant subspaces spanned by eigenvectors associated with the \(q\) largest eigenvalues of \(A\), with nonuniqueness when the selection boundary has an eigenvalue tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral subspace landscape optimizes the negative Rayleigh trace over orthonormal q-frames. Right multiplication by an orthogonal matrix changes the frame but not its subspace or objective value, so the intrinsic variable is a point on the Grassmannian. The same model can be written as linear optimization over rank-q orthogonal projectors. Its global minimizers are the leading q-dimensional eigenspaces, subject to ambiguity at tied eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal L_q(A):=\bigl(\operatorname{St}(n,q),U\mapsto-\operatorname{tr}(U^\top AU)bigr),\qquad f_A(UQ)=f_A(U).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The maximization form is \(\max_{U^\top U=I_q}\operatorname{tr}(U^\top AU)\).
The projector form replaces each frame orbit \([U]\) by \(P=UU^\top\).
special_cases_latex: For \(q=1\), the model is minimization of the negative Rayleigh quotient over the unit sphere.
Replacing \(A\) by a sample covariance matrix gives the standard principal-subspace estimation landscape.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\lambda_q(A)>\lambda_{q+1}(A)\), the leading subspace is unique as a Grassmannian point.
Individual minimizing frames remain nonunique because of right-orthogonal symmetry.
boundary_notes: Nonsymmetric matrices require singular-subspace or dilation formulations.
Without an eigengap, recovery of a unique q-dimensional subspace is not identifiable.
The supplied spectral-decomposition source hint does not by itself support the full Stiefel/Grassmann landscape definition, so no source is cited.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector representing the subspace spanned by U.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Rayleigh-trace optimization on the Stiefel manifold and its projector form are standard spectral-subspace formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Subspace Optimization Landscape
Principal-Subspace Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Stiefel trace objective has no spurious local maxima: maximizers span a dominant eigenspace, uniquely so under an eigengap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\), and maximize \(F(U)=\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}AU)\) subject to \(U^{\mathsf T}U=I_r\). A feasible point is stationary exactly when \(\operatorname{range}(U)\) is an invariant subspace of \(A\). Every local maximizer spans an \(r\)-dimensional dominant eigenspace and is globally maximizing. If \(\lambda_r>\lambda_{r+1}\), the maximizing subspace is unique, although its orthonormal basis is determined only up to right multiplication by an element of \(O(r)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{U^{\mathsf T}U=I_r}F(U)=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i\), attained precisely on dominant \(r\)-dimensional eigenspaces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace maximization on the Stiefel manifold for a symmetric matrix.

notation.meaning: Subspace spanned by the columns of U.
Orthogonal changes of basis within the subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: PCA Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PCA reconstruction error equals total variance minus captured variance, so its global solutions are the leading covariance eigenspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let centered samples form \(X=[x_1,\ldots,x_m]\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), and set \(S=m^{-1}XX^{\mathsf T}\). For every \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) with \(U^{\mathsf T}U=I_r\),
\[m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m\|x_j-UU^{\mathsf T}x_j\|_2^2=\operatorname{tr}(S)-\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}SU).\]
Consequently, minimizing PCA reconstruction error is equivalent to maximizing captured variance. The global solution subspaces are the dominant \(r\)-dimensional eigenspaces of \(S\); if \(\lambda_r(S)>\lambda_{r+1}(S)\), this subspace is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_U m^{-1}\sum_j\|x_j-UU^{\mathsf T}x_j\|_2^2=\operatorname*{argmax}_U\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}SU)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical PCA as equivalent reconstruction-error minimization and variance maximization.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the learned subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-to-Subspace Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthonormal frames modulo rotations correspond exactly to rank-r orthogonal projectors, and their spectral trace objectives agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The map \(U\mapsto P=UU^{\mathsf T}\) sends the Stiefel set \(\{U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}:U^{\mathsf T}U=I_r\}\) onto the rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors \(\{P:P=P^{\mathsf T}=P^2,\ \operatorname{tr}(P)=r\}\). Two frames give the same projector exactly when \(V=UQ\) for some \(Q\in O(r)\). For every symmetric \(A\), \(\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}AU)=\operatorname{tr}(AP)\); hence frame-based spectral optimization and projector-based subspace optimization have identical values and corresponding solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(UU^{\mathsf T}=VV^{\mathsf T}\Longleftrightarrow V=UQ\) for some \(Q\in O(r)\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}AU)=\operatorname{tr}(AUU^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between orthonormal frames, rank-constrained projectors, and spectral subspaces.

notation.meaning: Rank-r orthogonal projector representing a subspace.

children.title: Matrix-Sensing Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Factorized recovery under restricted measurement geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Sensing Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a sufficiently strong rank-restricted isometry, exact-rank factorized matrix sensing has only exact global minima and strict saddles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_\star\succeq0\) have rank \(r\), let \(b=\mathcal A(M_\star)\), and define \(f(U)=\tfrac14\|\mathcal A(UU^{\mathsf T})-b\|_2^2\) on \(\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). Suppose \(\mathcal A\) satisfies the rank-\(2r\) restricted isometry inequality \((1-\delta)\|H\|_F^2\leq\|\mathcal A(H)\|_2^2\leq(1+\delta)\|H\|_F^2\) for every matrix \(H\) of rank at most \(2r\), with \(\delta<1/5\). Then every local minimizer satisfies \(UU^{\mathsf T}=M_\star\), and every other critical point admits a negative-curvature direction.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) has rank-\(2r\) restricted isometry constant \(\delta<1/5\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every local minimizer obeys \(UU^{\mathsf T}=M_\star\); every nonoptimal critical point has negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noiseless positive-semidefinite matrix sensing with exact-rank factorization and restricted isometry.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem and its strict-saddle conclusion depend on a precise matrix-sensing landscape result. No source is supplied, and the rank order and numerical threshold δ<1/5 require confirmation from a theorem-level locator before the claim can be relied upon.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Factorized Matrix-Sensing Landscape and Restricted Measurement Geometry
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R^p\) be linear, let \(M_\star\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank at most \(r\), and let \(b=\mathcal A(M_\star)+e\) be observed data. Choose a factor width \(q\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers smooth least-squares sensing with arbitrary deterministic measurements. Restricted isometry is recorded as an optional regime descriptor, not assumed automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The asymmetric factorized matrix-sensing landscape is \[\Phi_{\mathcal A,b,q}(U,V):=\frac1{2p}\|\mathcal A(UV^\top)-b\|_2^2+r(U,V),\] for \((U,V)\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\times\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), where \(r\) is an optional smooth balancing regularizer. In the positive-semidefinite symmetric model, \[\Psi_{\mathcal A,b,q}(Y):=\frac1{2p}\|\mathcal A(YY^\top)-b\|_2^2+r(Y).\] The measurement geometry has rank-\(s\) restricted-isometry constant \(\delta_s\) when \(\delta_s\) is the smallest number satisfying \[(1-\delta_s)\|X\|_F^2\leq p^{-1}\|\mathcal A(X)\|_2^2\leq(1+\delta_s)\|X\|_F^2\] for every matrix \(X\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\leq s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-sensing landscape fits a low-rank factor product to linear measurements by squared residual loss, optionally with a smooth balancing regularizer. It has asymmetric and positive-semidefinite symmetric forms. Restricted measurement geometry can be quantified by the smallest constant for which the normalized sensing norm approximately preserves the Frobenius norm of every matrix up to a specified rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Phi_{\mathcal A,b,q}=\frac1{2p}\|\mathcal A\circ\pi_q-b\|_2^2+r,quad \pi_q(U,V)=UV^\top.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(\mathcal A(X)_i=\langle A_i,X\rangle\), the loss is \(\frac1{2p}\sum_{i=1}^p(\langle A_i,UV^\top\rangle-b_i)^2+r(U,V)\).
In the noiseless case \(e=0\), zero residual is equivalent to \(UV^\top-M_\star\in\ker\mathcal A\).
special_cases_latex: Gaussian matrix sensing chooses measurement matrices with independent Gaussian entries under an appropriate normalization.
Symmetric sensing restricts both the target and represented matrices to the positive-semidefinite cone.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the rank-restricted null space of \(\mathcal A\) is trivial at the relevant difference rank, every zero-residual represented matrix equals \(M_\star\).
Measurement injectivity and benign factor-space geometry are separate properties.
boundary_notes: Restricted isometry bounds sufficient for particular landscape theorems are model- and theorem-dependent and are not fixed here.
Matrix completion is not automatically an RIP sensing model under the same uniform low-rank geometry.
No inspected supplied source supports this full definition.

notation.meaning: Rank-s restricted-isometry constant under the stated normalization.

children.title: Matrix-Completion Landscapes

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Completion Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix completion minimizes observed-entry residuals over low-rank factors, usually with incoherence or balancing regularization; its critical-point geometry depends on the sampling operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_\star\in\mathbb R^{n_1\times n_2}\), let \(\Omega\subseteq[n_1]\times[n_2]\), and let \(P_\Omega\) retain entries indexed by \(\Omega\) and set all others to zero. For factor rank \(r\), a matrix-completion landscape is
\[
F_\Omega(U,V)=\frac{1}{2p}\lVert P_\Omega(UV^\top-M_\star)\rVert_F^2+\lambda\mathcal R(U,V),
\]
where \(U\in\mathbb R^{n_1\times r}\), \(V\in\mathbb R^{n_2\times r}\), \(p=|\Omega|/(n_1n_2)\), and \(\mathcal R\) penalizes incoherent factors or imbalance. Its geometry depends on the sampling pattern because unobserved perturbations lie in the nullspace of \(P_\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\Omega\) is a sampling-dependent factorized objective with invariance \(F_\Omega(UQ,VQ^{-\top})=F_\Omega(U,V)\) whenever the regularizer shares that invariance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized factorized least-squares landscape for partially observed low-rank matrices.

notation.meaning: Entry-sampling projection associated with the observed index set.

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses matrix-completion landscape geometry or its regularization conventions.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The objective is a plausible matrix-completion definition, but no cited source supports its normalization, regularization conventions, or landscape claim. The conclusion should also quantify an invertible matrix Q and distinguish general factorization invariance from the typically smaller invariance group preserved by balancing or incoherence regularizers.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(M_\star
after\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(\Omega\subseteq[m]\times[n]\) be a set or multiset of observed indices, and define \((\mathcal P_\Omega X)_{ij}=X_{ij}\) for \((i,j)\in\Omega\) and zero otherwise. Let \(q\geq1\) be the factor width.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition records the empirical sampling geometry and optional smooth incoherence control. It does not assert identifiability or a sample-size threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The basic factorized matrix-completion landscape is \[\Phi_{\Omega,q}(U,V):=\frac1{2p_\Omega}\|\mathcal P_\Omega(UV^\top-M_\star)\|_F^2+r_{\mathrm{inc}}(U,V),\] where \((U,V)\in\mathbb R^{m\times q}\times\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), \(p_\Omega>0\) is a declared normalization, and \(r_{\mathrm{inc}}\) is either zero or a smooth penalty controlling excessive row norms. An incoherence-constrained variant replaces the penalty by the domain \[\mathcal D_\mu:=\{(U,V):\max_i\|U_{i,:}\|_2^2\leq\mu_U,quad \max_j\|V_{j,:}\|_2^2\leq\mu_V\}.\] The landscape depends on \(\Omega\), not only on \(M_\star\) and \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-completion landscape minimizes the squared discrepancy between a factor product and the target only on observed entries. Its geometry is sampling-dependent because unobserved directions lie in the kernel of the sampling projection. Incoherence can be encoded either through smooth row-norm penalties or by restricting the factor domain. The normalization must be stated but does not change minimizers when it is a positive constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Phi_{\Omega,q}=\frac1{2p_\Omega}\|\mathcal P_\Omega\circ(\pi_q-M_\star)\|_F^2+r_{\mathrm{inc}},quad \pi_q(U,V)=UV^\top.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a set of observations, the data-fit term is \(\frac1{2p_\Omega}\sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega}(U_{i,:}V_{j,:}^\top-M_{\star,ij})^2\).
With repeated sampled indices, the same expression uses multiplicities and is an empirical average after selecting \(p_\Omega=|\Omega|\).
special_cases_latex: Uniform entry sampling chooses indices independently or without replacement from \([m]\times[n]\).
Symmetric positive-semidefinite completion uses \(UV^\top=YY^\top\) and observations from a symmetric target.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two represented matrices agreeing on \(\Omega\) have the same unregularized data-fit value.
A zero empirical residual does not alone imply completion of unobserved entries without identifiability assumptions.
boundary_notes: The exact definition of incoherence and its scaling varies across models and must be declared with any theorem.
Nonsmooth clipping or projection mechanisms are outside the smooth penalized form.
No inspected source supports the exact formulation used here.

children.title: Robust Low-Rank Decomposition Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Landscapes coupling low-rank factors with sparse, corrupted, or adversarial components.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Low-Rank Decomposition Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The landscape jointly fits low-rank factors and a sparse corruption, with a balancing penalty controlling factor scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(Y\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), factor rank \(r\), and a sparsity penalty \(\Psi\), a robust low-rank decomposition landscape is
\[
F(U,V,S)=\frac12\lVert UV^\top+S-Y\rVert_F^2+\lambda\Psi(S)+\frac\mu4\lVert U^\top U-V^\top V\rVert_F^2,
\]
with \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\), \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). The first term couples the low-rank and corrupted components, while the balancing term removes scale degeneracy. Taking \(\Psi(S)=\lVert S\rVert_1\) yields the standard sparse-corruption model.
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is a sparsity-promoting penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) represents the decomposition \(Y\approx UV^\top+S\) and explicitly couples low-rank and sparse variables.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint factorized landscape for a low-rank matrix and a sparse corruption.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports robust low-rank decomposition or a specific smoothness convention.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The joint low-rank-plus-sparse objective fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular formulation. The record also permits an extended-valued or nonsmooth penalty and specifically invokes the l1 norm while residing under a smooth-landscape branch; the smooth and nonsmooth variants must be distinguished by a sourced formulation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Y\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be observed, let \(q\geq1\), and represent a low-rank component as \(L=UV^\top\). Let \(S\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) denote a corruption component, let \(\rho:\mathbb R\to	heb R_+\) be a twice continuously differentiable residual loss, and let \(r_S\) and \(r_F\) be declared regularizers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The displayed base class is smooth when all penalties are smooth. Sparse constrained and nonsmooth robust-PCA variants are nearby extensions but are not silently identified with this smooth model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A smooth robust low-rank decomposition landscape is \[\Phi(U,V,S):=\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\rho\bigl(Y_{ij}-(UV^\top+S)_{ij}\bigr)+r_F(U,V)+r_S(S),\] on \(\mathbb R^{m\times q}\times\mathbb R^{n\times q}\times\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). A structured-corruption variant restricts \(S\) to a declared set \(\mathcal S\), such as matrices with at most \(s\) nonzero entries or at most \(s_c\) corrupted columns. The represented decomposition is \(Y\approx L+S\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(L)leq q\). Robustness enters through \(\rho\), the structure of \(\mathcal S\), or the penalty \(r_S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust low-rank decomposition landscape jointly optimizes low-rank factors and an explicit corruption component. The fitted matrix is the sum of the factor product and the corruption. Robustness is specified through a smooth residual loss, a corruption regularizer, or a structural constraint such as entrywise or column sparsity. The factor width bounds the rank of the low-rank component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Phi(U,V,S)=\mathcal L\bigl(Y-UV^\top-S\bigr)+r_F(U,V)+r_S(S),quad \operatorname{rank}(UV^\top)leq q.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating \(S\) by partial minimization gives \(\widetilde\Phi(U,V)=\inf_{S\in\mathcal S}\Phi(U,V,S)\), although the reduced objective need not remain smooth.
A constrained formulation uses \(S\in\mathcal S\) and omits \(r_S\); a penalized formulation uses an unconstrained \(S\) with a structure-promoting penalty.
special_cases_latex: Entrywise sparse corruption takes \(\mathcal S=\{S:\|S\|_0\leq s\}\).
Column-sparse corruption bounds the number of nonzero columns of \(S\).
Dense heavy-tailed noise may be handled by a smooth bounded-influence loss \(\rho\) without an explicit sparse constraint.
immediate_consequences_latex: Without restrictions on \(S\), the decomposition is nonidentifiable because the corruption can absorb arbitrary residuals.
Factor symmetries remain present in the low-rank block even when the corruption is uniquely determined.
boundary_notes: The common \(\ell_1\) corruption penalty is nonsmooth and lies outside the displayed smooth subclass.
Landscape guarantees require separation or incoherence conditions between low-rank and corruption structures.
No inspected source supports this unified definition.

notation.meaning: Explicit corrupted, sparse, or adversarial component.
Declared structural class of admissible corruptions.

children.title: Rank-Misspecification Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Underparameterized, exactly parameterized, and overparameterized factor-rank regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Misspecification Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underparameterization leaves unavoidable approximation error; exact or excessive rank permits zero loss, while overparameterization introduces redundant flat directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_\star\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r_\star\), and define \(F_r(U,V)=\tfrac12\lVert UV^\top-M_\star\rVert_F^2\) on \(\mathbb R^{m\times r}\times\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). If \(r<r_\star\), then
\[
\min F_r=\frac12\sum_{j=r+1}^{r_\star}\sigma_j(M_\star)^2>0.
\]
If \(r\geq r_\star\), the minimum is zero. For \(r>r_\star\), every exact factorization has redundant factor directions, so minimizers are nonisolated and the Hessian has zero-curvature directions generated by factor transformations and unused columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r<r_\star\) gives positive optimal residual, whereas \(r\geq r_\star\) gives zero optimal residual and \(r>r_\star\) creates redundant minimizer directions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainability and degeneracy across under-, exact-, and overparameterized factor ranks.

notation.meaning: Ordered singular values of the target matrix.

review_flags: The supplied spectral-decomposition locator is insufficient for the full rank-misspecification landscape claim.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The optimal-residual formula is mathematically plausible, and property is an appropriate knowledge kind, but the inventory contains no locator supporting the combined underparameterized, exact-rank, and overparameterized Hessian-degeneracy claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Under-, Exact-, and Overparameterized Factor-Rank Regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(M_\star
after\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have intrinsic rank \(r_\star\), let \(q\geq1\) be the factor width used by an optimization model, and let \(\ell:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) be a declared smooth loss. Consider \(\Phi_q(U,V)=\ell(UV^\top)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank misspecification is defined relative to the intrinsic target rank, independently of whether the data identify that target or the loss has a benign landscape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The rank-specification index is \(\kappa=q-r_\star\). The landscape \(\Phi_q\) is underparameterized when \(q<r_\star\), exactly parameterized when \(q=r_\star\), and overparameterized when \(q>r_\star\). The associated family is \[\mathfrak F(M_\star,ell):=\{(\mathbb R^{m\times q}\times\mathbb R^{n\times q},Phi_q,kappa):q
after\in\mathbb N\}.\] In the symmetric positive-semidefinite case, replace \(UV^\top\) by \(YY^\top\) and compare \(q\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(M_\star)\). Overparameterization enlarges the factor domain and introduces rank-deficient representatives; underparameterization excludes exact representation of \(M_\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-misspecification landscape family holds the target and matrix loss fixed while varying the chosen factor width. Width below the target rank is underparameterized, equal width is exactly parameterized, and larger width is overparameterized. This classification concerns representational capacity. It does not by itself determine critical-point geometry or statistical recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[q<r_\star\Rightarrow\text{underparameterized},quad q=r_\star\Rightarrow\text{exactly parameterized},quad q>r_\star\Rightarrow\text{overparameterized}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The three regimes are equivalently identified by the sign of \(\kappa=q-r_\star\).
For exact fitting of \(M_\star\), underparameterization is equivalent to \(M_\star\notin\{UV^\top:U\in\mathbb R^{m\times q},V\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(r_\star=1\), every width \(q>1\) is overparameterized.
In the symmetric model, an overparameterized exact factor may be formed by appending zero columns to a minimal factor.
immediate_consequences_latex: Underparameterized exact squared-loss models have strictly positive minimum residual whenever distance to the rank-at-most-q set is positive.
Overparameterized factors may represent the same target with unused or linearly dependent columns.
boundary_notes: Intrinsic rank can differ from an effective rank selected under noise; that statistical convention must be stated separately.
Overparameterization does not automatically remove or create spurious local minima.
No inspected source supports this precise three-regime landscape definition.

notation.meaning: Intrinsic rank of the target matrix.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Comparing model factor width with target rank is the standard distinction among under-, exact-, and overparameterization.

children.title: Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Quadratic inverse-problem landscapes organized by field, sampling model, and objective construction.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,mathbb C\}\), let \(x_\star
after\in\mathbb K^d\), and let sensing vectors \(a_1,ldots,a_m\in\mathbb K^d\) generate intensity observations \(y_i=|a_i^*x_\star|^2+e_i\). The unavoidable symmetry group is \(G=\{\pm1\}\) over \(\mathbb R\) and \(G=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}\) over \(\mathbb C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition organizes real and complex, noiseless and noisy, empirical and population objectives. It makes no distributional or benign-landscape assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The intensity least-squares phase-retrieval landscape is \[F_m(x):=\frac1{4m}\sum_{i=1}^m\bigl(|a_i^*x|^2-y_i\bigr)^2,quad x\in\mathbb K^d.\] For a sensing distribution \(a\sim\mathcal D\) and noiseless response \(y=|a^*x_\star|^2\), the corresponding population landscape is \[F(x):=\frac14\mathbb E_{a\sim\mathcal D}\bigl(|a^*x|^2-|a^*x_\star|^2\bigr)^2,\] whenever the expectation is finite. Both objectives satisfy \(F_m(gx)=F_m(x)\) and \(F(gx)=F(x)\) for every \(g\in G\). The family consists of these objectives indexed by field, sampling law, noise model, and objective construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A phase-retrieval landscape fits squared magnitudes of linear measurements because the measurement phases are unavailable. The canonical intensity-loss objective is quartic in the candidate signal and can be empirical or population-level. It is invariant under a global sign in the real case and under a unit-modulus global phase in the complex case, so recovery is intrinsically defined only modulo that symmetry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal L_{\mathrm{PR}}=(\mathbb K^d,F_m,G),quad F_m(x)=\frac1{4m}\sum_{i=1}^m(|a_i^*x|^2-y_i)^2,quad F_m(gx)=F_m(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using lifted matrices \(X=xx^*\), each predicted intensity is \(|a_i^*x|^2=\langle a_ia_i^*,X\rangle\), with the nonconvex constraint \(X\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(X)=1\).
The symmetry-adjusted recovery error is \(\operatorname{dist}_G(x,x_\star)=\inf_{g\in G}\|x-gx_\star\|_2\).
special_cases_latex: The real model has sign symmetry and a real quartic polynomial objective.
The complex model uses conjugate transpose and global circular-phase symmetry.
Robust variants replace squared residuals by a declared robust loss.
immediate_consequences_latex: In the noiseless model, every signal in the orbit \(Gx_\star\) has zero empirical residual.
Any uniqueness or recovery claim must be stated modulo \(G\).
boundary_notes: Amplitude losses using \(|a_i^*x|-\sqrt{y_i}\) may be nonsmooth at zero and form a distinct objective family.
Finite-sample landscape properties depend on the sensing ensemble and sample size.
No inspected phase-retrieval source was supplied.

notation.meaning: Real inner product or complex Hermitian inner product.
Unavoidable global sign or phase symmetry group.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Quartic intensity least squares and global sign/phase ambiguity are canonical phase-retrieval formulations.
A directly inspected authoritative phase-retrieval source is absent.

children.title: Real Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Sign-symmetric real-valued landscape models.

knowledge_statements.title: Real Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Real phase retrieval uses a quartic intensity-fitting objective whose unavoidable symmetry makes the target identifiable only up to sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For sensing vectors \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\) and noiseless observations \(y_i=(a_i^\top x_\star)^2\), the real phase-retrieval landscape is
\[
f_m(x)=\frac{1}{4m}\sum_{i=1}^m\big((a_i^\top x)^2-y_i\big)^2,
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
It is an even quartic polynomial: \(f_m(-x)=f_m(x)\). Consequently, the signal is identifiable at best up to sign, and both \(x_\star\) and \(-x_\star\) are global minimizers with objective value zero whenever the observations are consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_m(x)\geq0\), \(f_m(-x)=f_m(x)\), and \(f_m(\pm x_\star)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quartic real-valued least-squares landscape with unavoidable sign symmetry.
review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses real phase retrieval.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The real quartic loss, sign symmetry, and consistent-data minimizers are precise and match the leaf, but the record has no phase-retrieval source or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(x_\star
after\in\mathbb R^d\), let \(a_1,ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^d\), and observe \(y_i=(a_i^\top x_\star)^2+e_i\). The parameter domain is \(\mathbb R^d\), and the intrinsic equivalence relation is \(x\sim z\) when \(z=x\) or \(z=-x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the smooth real intensity-loss model. It excludes complex phase symmetry and nonsmooth amplitude-loss formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The real empirical phase-retrieval landscape is the quartic polynomial \[F_m(x):=\frac1{4m}\sum_{i=1}^m\bigl((a_i^\top x)^2-y_i\bigr)^2,quad x\in\mathbb R^d.\] It is sign invariant: \(F_m(-x)=F_m(x)\). In the noiseless case \(e_i=0\), its exact data-consistency set is \[\mathcal Z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(a_i^\top x)^2=(a_i^\top x_\star)^2\ \text{for every }i\}.\] The intended recovery orbit is \([x_\star]=\{x_\star,-x_\star\}\), and recovery error is measured by \[d_\pm(x,x_\star):=\min\{\|x-x_\star\|_2,\|x+x_\star\|_2\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The real phase-retrieval landscape is a quartic least-squares objective matching squared real linear measurements. It is unchanged when the candidate signal changes sign. In the noiseless case, the zero set consists of all signals reproducing every squared measurement, while the intended identifiable object is the two-point sign orbit of the target. Recovery quality is therefore the smaller distance to the target or its negative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal L_{\mathbb R}=(\mathbb R^d,F_m,\{\pm1\}),quad F_m(-x)=F_m(x),quad F_m(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow x\in\mathcal Z\ \text{when }e=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With the lift \(X=xx^\top\), the predicted measurement is \((a_i^\top x)^2=\langle a_ia_i^\top,X\rangle\) and the signal constraint becomes \(X\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(X)=1\).
The quotient parameter space is \(\mathbb R^d/\{\pm1\}\), with the origin fixed by the sign action.
special_cases_latex: For Gaussian sensing, the vectors \(a_i\) are independent real Gaussian vectors under a declared covariance normalization.
For \(d=1\), the model recovers the magnitude of a scalar and cannot distinguish its sign.
immediate_consequences_latex: Both \(x_\star\) and \(-x_\star\) are zero-loss points in the noiseless model.
Equality \(\mathcal Z=\{\pm x_\star\}\) is an injectivity property of the sensing design, not part of the objective definition.
boundary_notes: Noise can make the minimum value positive and move minimizers away from the exact sign orbit.
The complex model has a continuous unit-modulus symmetry rather than a two-element sign symmetry.
No inspected source was available for this exact real phase-retrieval definition.

notation.meaning: Sign-equivalence orbit of the real target signal.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Real quartic intensity loss, sign symmetry, and distance modulo sign are canonical real phase-retrieval objects.

children.title: Complex Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Phase-symmetric complex-valued landscape models.

knowledge_statements.title: Complex Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complex phase retrieval minimizes intensity residuals and identifies the signal only modulo multiplication by a unit-modulus scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For sensing vectors \(a_i\in\mathbb C^n\) and noiseless observations \(y_i=|a_i^*z_\star|^2\), the complex phase-retrieval landscape is
\[
f_m(z)=\frac{1}{4m}\sum_{i=1}^m\big(|a_i^*z|^2-y_i\big)^2,
\qquad z\in\mathbb C^n.
\]
For every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\), \(f_m(e^{\mathrm i\theta}z)=f_m(z)\). Thus recovery is posed on equivalence classes under global phase, and the orbit \(\{e^{\mathrm i\theta}z_\star:\theta\in\mathbb R\}\) consists of zero-valued global minimizers for consistent measurements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_m(z)\geq0\), \(f_m(e^{\mathrm i\theta}z)=f_m(z)\), and \(f_m(e^{\mathrm i\theta}z_\star)=0\) for every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quartic complex-valued least-squares landscape modulo global phase.
review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses complex phase retrieval.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The complex quartic loss and global-phase symmetry are precise and match the leaf, but no cited source or locator supports the formulation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb C^n\), let \(x_\star\in\mathbb C^n\), and let the noiseless intensity measurements be \(y_r=|a_r^*x_\star|^2\). The parameter space is \(\mathbb C^n\), viewed as a real Euclidean space with inner product \(\operatorname{Re}(z^*w)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, noiseless complex phase retrieval with a smooth quartic least-squares loss and global phase symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The complex phase-retrieval landscape generated by \(\{(a_r,y_r)\}_{r=1}^m\) is the real-valued polynomial
\[F_m(z)=\frac{1}{4m}\sum_{r=1}^m\bigl(|a_r^*z|^2-y_r\bigr)^2,\qquad z\in\mathbb C^n.\]
Its intrinsic parameter domain is the quotient \(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb S^1\), where \(\mathbb S^1=\{\omega\in\mathbb C:|\omega|=1\}\) acts by \(z\mapsto\omega z\). Thus \(F_m(\omega z)=F_m(z)\) for every \(z\) and \(\omega\in\mathbb S^1\), and the target solution class is \([x_\star]=\{\omega x_\star:|\omega|=1\}\). In the noiseless model, \(F_m(z)=0\) exactly when \(|a_r^*z|^2=|a_r^*x_\star|^2\) for every \(r\); uniqueness up to phase additionally requires the measurement map to be injective on the quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given complex sensing vectors and noiseless squared-magnitude observations, the landscape is the average quartic squared residual between predicted and observed intensities. Multiplication of a parameter by any unit-modulus complex scalar leaves every prediction and the objective unchanged, so parameters are naturally identified modulo global phase. The target is the entire phase orbit of the unknown signal. Zero objective means that all measured intensities match; it implies recovery of the target orbit only when the measurement operator is phase-retrieval injective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F_m(z)=\frac{1}{4m}\sum_{r=1}^m(|a_r^*z|^2-y_r)^2,\qquad F_m(\omega z)=F_m(z)\quad(|\omega|=1).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(Z=zz^*\) and \(X_\star=x_\star x_\star^*\), each residual is \(a_r^*(Z-X_\star)a_r=\operatorname{tr}(a_ra_r^*(Z-X_\star))\), subject to \(Z\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}Z=1\).
special_cases_latex: For real sensing vectors and parameters, the symmetry reduces from \(\mathbb S^1\) to the sign group \(\{\pm1\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every nonzero phase orbit is a one-dimensional set of equal objective values, so minimizers and critical points are generally nonisolated in the unquotiented parameter space.
boundary_notes: Additive measurement noise replaces the exact zero-residual characterization by an approximation statement.
Amplitude-based, truncated, and robust losses are different landscapes and are not included in this definition.

notation.meaning: Hermitian inner product between sensing vector and parameter.
Global-phase equivalence class of the target signal.
