children.title: Phase-Retrieval Transfer Pair
children.top_down_role: Transfer from idealized expected geometry to finite-sample objectives.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(a\) be a random sensing vector, let \(x_\star\) be fixed, and define \(\ell(z;a)=\frac14(|a^*z|^2-|a^*x_\star|^2)^2\). For independent samples \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\), all derivatives are taken on the associated real Euclidean parameter space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic definition of the population/finite-sample pair and uniform second-order transfer on a prescribed region; it does not assert that transfer occurs with any particular sample size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The phase-retrieval transfer pair is
\[F(z)=\mathbb E\,\ell(z;a),\qquad F_m(z)=\frac1m\sum_{r=1}^m\ell(z;a_r).\]
For a set \(\mathcal R\) on which both functions are twice differentiable, the empirical landscape is an \((\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\)-uniform \(C^2\) transfer of the population landscape on \(\mathcal R\) when
\[\sup_{z\in\mathcal R}|F_m(z)-F(z)|\le\varepsilon_0,\quad \sup_{z\in\mathcal R}\|\nabla F_m(z)-\nabla F(z)\|\le\varepsilon_1,\]
\[\sup_{z\in\mathcal R}\|\nabla^2F_m(z)-\nabla^2F(z)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\varepsilon_2.\]
The ordered pair \((F,F_m)\), together with these discrepancies, separates idealized expected geometry from its finite-sample realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transfer pair consists of the expected phase-retrieval loss and its sample-average counterpart. On a selected region, uniform second-order transfer means that objective values, gradients, and Hessians differ by at most three stated tolerances. This is a definition of the comparison object; it does not itself guarantee concentration or preservation of critical points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(F,F_m)=\left(\mathbb E\,\ell(\cdot;a),\;m^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^m\ell(\cdot;a_r)\right),\] with transfer errors measured uniformly in value, gradient, and Hessian on \(\mathcal R\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The Hessian condition is equivalent to \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal R,\|u\|=1}|u^*(\nabla^2F_m(z)-\nabla^2F(z))u|\le\varepsilon_2\) when the real Hessians are self-adjoint.
special_cases_latex: Setting \(\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_2=0\) gives exact agreement on \(\mathcal R\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\|\nabla F(z)\|>\varepsilon_1\), then \(z\) cannot be a critical point of \(F_m\).
If \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2F(z))< -\varepsilon_2\), then \(\nabla^2F_m(z)\) retains a negative-curvature direction.
boundary_notes: Uniform transfer over an unbounded parameter domain generally requires additional normalization or tail control.
A value-only uniform law does not constitute \(C^2\) landscape transfer.

notation.meaning: Region on which transfer is measured.

review_flags: The transfer-pair terminology and exact three-tolerance formulation require a dedicated phase-retrieval source.
knowledge_statements.title: Population-to-empirical phase-retrieval transfer pair
Population Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under real Gaussian sensing, the expected quartic phase-retrieval loss has an explicit rotationally invariant formula and exactly two sign-related minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a\sim\mathcal N(0,I_n)\), let \(x_\star\in\mathbb R^n\), and define
\[
F(x)=\frac14\mathbb E\!\left[\big((a^\top x)^2-(a^\top x_\star)^2\big)^2\right].
\]
Gaussian fourth-moment identities give
\[
F(x)=\frac14\left(3\lVert x\rVert^4+3\lVert x_\star\rVert^4-2\lVert x\rVert^2\lVert x_\star\rVert^2-4(x^\top x_\star)^2\right).
\]
Hence \(F\geq0\), and its global minimizers are exactly \(x=x_\star\) and \(x=-x_\star\) when \(x_\star\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}F(x)=\{x_\star,-x_\star\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form population quartic loss for isotropic Gaussian real sensing.
review_flags: No supplied source locator supports the Gaussian fourth-moment representation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The Gaussian population representation and minimizer statement are mathematically consistent, and representation is the correct knowledge kind, but no source locator supports the fourth-moment calculation or exact minimizer characterization.

knowledge_statements.title: Empirical Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The empirical landscape averages finitely many quartic intensity residuals; its critical geometry depends on the realized measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(x_\star\in\mathbb R^n\). The empirical noiseless phase-retrieval landscape is
\[
F_m(x)=\frac{1}{4m}\sum_{i=1}^m\left((a_i^\top x)^2-(a_i^\top x_\star)^2\right)^2.
\]
Its gradient is
\[
\nabla F_m(x)=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\left((a_i^\top x)^2-(a_i^\top x_\star)^2\right)(a_i^\top x)a_i.
\]
Unlike the population loss, its critical points and curvature depend on the realized sensing sample, although \(F_m(\pm x_\star)=0\) always holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_m\) is a nonnegative even quartic polynomial satisfying \(F_m(\pm x_\star)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample quartic landscape generated by independent real sensing vectors.
review_flags: No supplied source locator addresses empirical phase-retrieval landscapes.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The empirical objective and displayed gradient are internally consistent and fit the finite-sample leaf, but no phase-retrieval source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Population-to-Empirical Transfer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform gradient and Hessian concentration transfers population gradient gaps and strict negative curvature to the empirical landscape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) and \(F_m\) be twice continuously differentiable on a compact set \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\). A population-to-empirical transfer condition with tolerances \((\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)\) is
\[
\sup_{x\in K}\lVert\nabla F_m(x)-\nabla F(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon_g,
\qquad
\sup_{x\in K}\lVert\nabla^2F_m(x)-\nabla^2F(x)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\varepsilon_H.
\]
If every population point outside designated minimizer neighborhoods has either \(\lVert\nabla F(x)\rVert>2\varepsilon_g\) or \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2F(x))<-2\varepsilon_H\), then the corresponding empirical point retains a nonzero gradient or a negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Population gradient gaps exceeding \(2\varepsilon_g\) and negative curvature below \(-2\varepsilon_H\) persist for \(F_m\) with halved margins.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform derivative approximation condition transferring strict landscape geometry.

notation.meaning: Region on which transfer is asserted.

review_flags: No supplied source establishes phase-retrieval derivative concentration or sample-size requirements.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic gradient-and-Hessian approximation condition correctly expresses a local geometric transfer mechanism, and condition is the appropriate knowledge kind. A source is still required for this transfer statement and, if phase-retrieval concentration is intended, for its probabilistic and sample-size regime.

children.title: Robust Phase-Retrieval Variant Family
children.top_down_role: Landscape modifications for heavy tails, outliers, and measurement noise.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(a_r\in\mathbb F^n\), \(y_r\in\mathbb R\), and \(\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}\). Let \(w_r:\mathbb F^n\to[0,1]\) be fixed or parameter-dependent weights and let \(\rho_\tau:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\) be an even loss indexed by a robustness scale \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample intensity models allowing bounded-influence penalties, truncation, reweighting, noise, and outliers; smoothness depends on the selected penalty and weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A residual-robustified phase-retrieval landscape is any objective in the parameterized family
\[F_{\rho,w}(z)=\frac1m\sum_{r=1}^m w_r(z)\,\rho_\tau\!\left(|a_r^*z|^2-y_r\right),\qquad z\in\mathbb F^n,\]
where \(\rho_\tau(0)=0\), \(\rho_\tau(t)=\rho_\tau(-t)\), and \(\rho_\tau\) is nondecreasing as a function of \(|t|\). A bounded-influence member additionally satisfies \(\sup_t|\rho_\tau'(t)|<\infty\) wherever the derivative exists. A truncated member has \(w_r(z)=\mathbf1\{|a_r^*z|^2-y_r|\le T_r(z)\}\), or a smooth approximation thereof. For complex parameters the family remains invariant under \(z\mapsto\omega z\) for \(|\omega|=1\), provided each weight depends only on phase-invariant quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family replaces the squared intensity residual by an even robust penalty and may downweight or discard unusually large residuals. Bounded derivative gives bounded residual influence, while indicator or smoothed weights encode truncation. Complex global-phase symmetry is preserved when the weights themselves are phase invariant. The definition accommodates noisy and contaminated observations but makes no recovery guarantee.
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(w_r\equiv1\) and \(\rho_\tau(t)=t^2/4\) recovers the ordinary quartic intensity least-squares landscape.
Choosing \(\rho_\tau(t)=|t|\) yields a nonsmooth absolute-residual landscape.
immediate_consequences_latex: Hard truncation may introduce discontinuities when a residual crosses its threshold.
Smooth bounded-influence penalties can retain differentiability while limiting the effect of arbitrarily large residuals.
boundary_notes: Robustness to heavy-tailed sensing vectors requires control of leverage as well as residual magnitude.
Amplitude residuals \(|a_r^*z|-\sqrt{y_r}\) define a related but distinct family.

notation.meaning: Weight or truncation rule for measurement \(r\).

review_flags: No inspected supplied source supports this exact robust phase-retrieval family or its bounded-influence conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-robustified phase-retrieval landscape family
Robust Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust phase-retrieval landscape replaces squared residuals by a bounded-influence loss, limiting each corrupted observation’s gradient contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given sensing vectors \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\), possibly corrupted intensities \(y_i\in\mathbb R\), and a differentiable robust loss \(\rho:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R_+\), define
\[
F_\rho(x)=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m\rho\!\left((a_i^\top x)^2-y_i\right),
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
The landscape is robust in the bounded-influence sense when \(\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\rho'(t)|<\infty\); then a single observation contributes at most \(2\sup|\rho'|\,|a_i^\top x|\lVert a_i\rVert/m\) to the gradient norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\rho(-x)=F_\rho(x)\), and each summand has bounded residual influence on \(\nabla F_\rho(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intensity-fitting landscape using a bounded-influence loss against corrupted observations.
review_flags: Robust-loss choice and landscape guarantees require a phase-retrieval-specific source.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-derivative calculation is plausible and the definition fits the leaf, but bounded residual influence alone does not establish a phase-retrieval robustness guarantee. No source supports the selected robust-loss class or its intended landscape interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncation removes measurements with excessive amplitude or residual; the resulting objective is smooth only where the accepted index set stays fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For residuals \(r_i(x)=(a_i^\top x)^2-y_i\) and measurable acceptance indicators \(w_i(x)\in\{0,1\}\), a truncated phase-retrieval landscape is
\[
F_{\mathrm{tr}}(x)=\frac{1}{4m}\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(x)r_i(x)^2.
\]
A typical rule accepts indices satisfying simultaneous amplitude and residual bounds, such as \(|a_i^\top x|\leq\tau_a\lVert x\rVert\) and \(|r_i(x)|\leq\tau_r s(x)\), where \(s(x)>0\) is a sample scale. On any region where all indicators are constant, \(F_{\mathrm{tr}}\) is a smooth quartic polynomial; indicator boundaries can make the global objective nonsmooth or discontinuous.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i(x)\in\{0,1\}\) is determined by specified acceptance thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{tr}}\) is piecewise quartic, with smoothness potentially failing where an acceptance indicator changes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample-dependent landscape formed by excluding measurements failing an acceptance rule.
review_flags: No supplied source fixes a canonical truncation rule or its regularity properties.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The generic indicator-weighted objective is piecewise quartic as stated, but no canonical acceptance rule or source locator is supplied. Its global regularity depends on the exact rule and boundary convention, so the claimed truncated landscape remains source-dependent.

knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Phase-Retrieval Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive intensity noise perturbs the noiseless quartic objective by a quadratic term, preserves sign symmetry, and generally shifts stationary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y_i=(a_i^\top x_\star)^2+\eta_i\) and define
\[
F_\eta(x)=\frac{1}{4m}\sum_{i=1}^m\left((a_i^\top x)^2-y_i\right)^2.
\]
Writing \(F_0\) for the noiseless objective gives
\[
F_\eta(x)=F_0(x)-\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{i=1}^m\eta_i\left((a_i^\top x)^2-(a_i^\top x_\star)^2\right)+\frac{1}{4m}\sum_{i=1}^m\eta_i^2.
\]
Thus noise adds a quadratic perturbation plus an irrelevant constant, preserves sign symmetry, and generally displaces stationary points from \(\pm x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\eta(-x)=F_\eta(x)\), while \(\nabla F_\eta(x_\star)=-m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\eta_i(a_i^\top x_\star)a_i\) and \(\nabla F_\eta(-x_\star)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\eta_i(a_i^\top x_\star)a_i\); these gradients need not vanish.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation of the noiseless quartic landscape by additive intensity noise.
review_flags: No supplied source addresses noisy phase-retrieval landscape perturbations.
Corrected the sign of the gradient at \(-x_\star\).

knowledge_statements.title: Robustness Breakdown Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At one-half adversarial contamination, the same observations can support two inequivalent signals, so uniform phase-retrieval identification is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix distinct signals \(x,z\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(z\neq\pm x\), and arbitrary sensing vectors \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\). If an adversary may replace at least \(\lceil m/2\rceil\) intensity observations, construct a dataset whose first \(\lfloor m/2\rfloor\) values equal \((a_i^\top x)^2\) and whose remaining values equal \((a_i^\top z)^2\). This dataset is compatible with truth \(x\) after corrupting the second block and with truth \(z\) after corrupting the first block. Therefore no estimator can uniformly identify the signal up to sign when the allowed adversarial fraction is at least one half.
assumptions_latex: The adversary may replace at least \(\lceil m/2\rceil\) of \(m\) observations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform recovery modulo sign is impossible for adversarial contamination fraction \(\varepsilon\geq1/2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability failure under majority adversarial contamination of intensity measurements.

notation.meaning: Maximum fraction of adversarially replaced observations.
Two signals not equivalent under sign.

review_flags: The supplied inventory contains no source for the adversarial identifiability boundary.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is the correct knowledge kind, and the two-truth contamination construction is coherent, including for odd sample sizes. However, no source locator supports the one-half adversarial identifiability boundary or specifies the replacement-contamination model under which it is asserted.

children.title: Deep Linear Network Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Multilinear parameterizations isolating depth, rank, symmetry, and nonisolated critical geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix depths and widths \(d_0,\ldots,d_L\) with \(L\ge2\). For each layer let \(W_\ell\in\mathbb R^{d_\ell\times d_{\ell-1}}\), and let training data be \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_0\times N}\) and \(Y\in\mathbb R^{d_L\times N}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, fully connected linear networks trained by unregularized squared error; biases, nonlinear activations, and stochastic training are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The deep linear network landscape of depth \(L\) is the polynomial objective
\[\mathcal L(W_1,\ldots,W_L)=\frac{1}{2N}\|W_LW_{L-1}\cdots W_1X-Y\|_F^2\]
on the product space \(\prod_{\ell=1}^L\mathbb R^{d_\ell\times d_{\ell-1}}\). Its end-to-end map is \(P(W)=W_L\cdots W_1\), and the attainable predictor class is
\[\mathcal P=\{W_L\cdots W_1:W_\ell\in\mathbb R^{d_\ell\times d_{\ell-1}}\}.\]
Writing \(r=\min_{0\le\ell\le L}d_\ell\), every attainable end-to-end matrix has rank at most \(r\). The factorized landscape is nonidentifiable: whenever invertible matrices of compatible hidden dimensions are inserted between adjacent factors and canceled in the neighboring factor, the end-to-end product and loss remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deep linear network is a product of at least two trainable matrices, with no nonlinear activation. Its training landscape is squared prediction error after applying the complete matrix product to the data. Widths bound the rank of every realizable predictor. Hidden-coordinate changes that cancel across adjacent layers leave the predictor and objective unchanged, producing nonisolated parameter fibers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal L(W_1,\ldots,W_L)=(2N)^{-1}\|P(W)X-Y\|_F^2,\qquad P(W)=W_L\cdots W_1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The landscape is the pullback \(\mathcal L=\phi\circ P\) of \(\phi(M)=(2N)^{-1}\|MX-Y\|_F^2\) through the matrix-product parameterization.
special_cases_latex: When \(L=2\), the model is a shallow two-factor linear network.
When \(X=I\), training reduces to Frobenius-norm matrix factorization of \(Y\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If a hidden width is smaller than both endpoint dimensions, the architecture imposes an end-to-end rank bottleneck.
Different parameter tuples can represent the same predictor, so parameter-space minimizers need not be isolated.
boundary_notes: Adding weight decay breaks general change-of-basis and scaling invariances.
Affine layers with biases are not represented by this homogeneous matrix product unless coordinates are augmented.

notation.meaning: End-to-end matrix represented by all layers.

review_flags: The supplied source hints cover matrix algebra but not the exact deep-linear-network landscape definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Deep linear least-squares network landscape

children.title: Shallow Linear Network Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Two-factor models linking regression and matrix factorization.

knowledge_statements.title: Shallow Linear Network Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-factor linear network is matrix regression whose predictor rank cannot exceed the hidden width; factorization introduces nonuniqueness without changing attainable predictors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let data matrices satisfy \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{d_0\times n}\) and \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_2\times n}\), and let the hidden width be \(d_1\). A two-layer linear network with weights \(W_1\in\mathbb{R}^{d_1\times d_0}\) and \(W_2\in\mathbb{R}^{d_2\times d_1}\) has squared-loss landscape \[F(W_2,W_1)=\frac12\lVert W_2W_1X-Y\rVert_F^2.\] Writing \(M=W_2W_1\), its attainable predictors are exactly the matrices \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{d_2\times d_0}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{rank}(M)\le d_1\). Thus minimizing \(F\) is equivalent in optimal value to minimizing \(\frac12\lVert MX-Y\rVert_F^2\) over that rank-constrained set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{W_1,W_2}F(W_2,W_1)=\inf_{\operatorname{rank}(M)\le d_1}\frac12\lVert MX-Y\rVert_F^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-factor linear networks represented as rank-constrained matrix regression.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically precise, and the content kind fits the two-factor landscape container. However, no cited source or inspectable locator supports the rank-constrained regression equivalence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R^{d_{\mathrm{out}}\times r}\), \(V\in\mathbb R^{r\times d_{\mathrm{in}}}\), \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_{\mathrm{in}}\times N}\), and \(Y\in\mathbb R^{d_{\mathrm{out}}\times N}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-layer linear network without bias or regularization, linking multivariate regression with rank-constrained matrix factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The shallow linear network landscape of hidden width \(r\) is
\[\mathcal L(U,V)=\frac{1}{2N}\|UVX-Y\|_F^2,
\qquad (U,V)\in\mathbb R^{d_{\mathrm{out}}\times r}\times\mathbb R^{r\times d_{\mathrm{in}}}.\]
The represented regression matrix is \(M=UV\), hence \(\operatorname{rank}M\le r\). For every \(G\in\mathrm{GL}(r)\), the transformation
\[(U,V)\mapsto(UG,G^{-1}V)\]
leaves \(UV\), all predictions, and the objective invariant. The parameter landscape is therefore the pullback of the convex quadratic regression loss \(\phi(M)=(2N)^{-1}\|MX-Y\|_F^2\) through the nonconvex factorization map \((U,V)\mapsto UV\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shallow linear network has one hidden linear layer and represents its predictor as the product of two matrices. Its squared training loss is nonconvex in the factors although the corresponding loss is convex in the end-to-end regression matrix. Any invertible change of hidden coordinates can be applied to one factor and canceled in the other, so equivalent parameters form gauge orbits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal L(U,V)=(2N)^{-1}\|UVX-Y\|_F^2,\qquad \mathcal L(UG,G^{-1}V)=\mathcal L(U,V).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When the factorization can represent every matrix relevant to the regression problem, minimizing over \((U,V)\) is a redundant parameterization of minimizing \(\phi(M)\) over matrices with \(\operatorname{rank}M\le r\).
special_cases_latex: For \(X=I\), the objective is \((2N)^{-1}\|UV-Y\|_F^2\), the standard two-factor matrix approximation landscape.
For \(r=1\), the predictor is an outer product \(uv^T\) and the continuous gauge reduces to reciprocal scalar scaling.
immediate_consequences_latex: The zero factor pair \((0,0)\) always represents the zero predictor.
Unregularized parameter sublevel sets need not be bounded because reciprocal factor scaling preserves the loss.
boundary_notes: A factor-balancing penalty changes the objective even when it leaves the represented predictor class unchanged.
The definition does not claim that all stationary points are globally optimal.
review_flags: No inspected supplied source directly treats two-factor linear-network loss and its gauge symmetry.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-factor linear regression landscape

children.title: Deep Matrix-Product Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Depth-induced critical geometry in multilayer linear parameterizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Deep Matrix-Product Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deep linear network optimizes a loss through a multilayer matrix product. The narrowest layer determines attainable rank, while depth enlarges the nonunique parameter fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix layer dimensions \(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_L\) with \(L\ge2\), weights \(W_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{d_\ell\times d_{\ell-1}}\), and a differentiable terminal loss \(\ell:\mathbb{R}^{d_L\times d_0}\to\mathbb{R}\). The deep linear landscape is \[F(W_L,\ldots,W_1)=\ell(W_LW_{L-1}\cdots W_1).\] Its end-to-end matrices are precisely those \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{d_L\times d_0}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)\le r_*\), where \(r_*=\min_{0\le j\le L}d_j\). Depth changes the fibers of the product map and hence the parameter-space critical geometry, although the attainable end-to-end class depends only on \(r_*\).
assumptions_latex: \(L\ge2\) and every \(d_j\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{W_L\cdots W_1\}=\{M\in\mathbb{R}^{d_L\times d_0}:\operatorname{rank}(M)\le r_*\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth-L linear networks as constrained matrix-product parameterizations.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The matrix-product representation and attainable-rank characterization are coherent, and representation is the correct content kind. An authoritative deep-linear-network source with a specific locator is required, particularly for the claim about depth changing parameter-space critical geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pullback landscape under a deep matrix product
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix \(L\ge2\), widths \(d_0,\ldots,d_L\), a differentiable terminal loss \(\Phi:\mathbb R^{d_L\times d_0}\to\mathbb R\), and factors \(W_\ell\in\mathbb R^{d_\ell\times d_{\ell-1}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general deterministic matrix-product parameterization; unlike the linear-network slot, the terminal loss need not arise from regression data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The deep matrix-product landscape induced by \(\Phi\) is the pullback
\[F(W_1,\ldots,W_L)=\Phi(W_LW_{L-1}\cdots W_1)\]
on \(\prod_{\ell=1}^L\mathbb R^{d_\ell\times d_{\ell-1}}\). For indices \(1\le i\le j\le L\), define the partial product \(P_{j:i}=W_jW_{j-1}\cdots W_i\), with empty products equal to the appropriate identity. The end-to-end map is \(P_{L:1}\). Depth-induced critical geometry means the critical and singular strata of \(F\) are studied relative to ranks of these partial products, because the differential of the product map can lose rank even when the terminal loss has nonzero gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deep matrix-product landscape is obtained by composing any differentiable loss on an end-to-end matrix with a product of two or more matrix factors. Ordered partial products encode the effect of depth. Rank loss in those partial products can make the product parameterization singular and can create parameter-space critical behavior not visible in the unfactorized terminal loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F=\Phi\circ P_{L:1},\qquad P_{j:i}=W_j\cdots W_i.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The landscape is constant on every fiber \(P_{L:1}^{-1}(M)\) of the product map.
special_cases_latex: Taking \(\Phi(M)=\frac12\|M-M_\star\|_F^2\) gives deep matrix factorization.
Taking \(\Phi(M)=(2N)^{-1}\|MX-Y\|_F^2\) gives a deep linear regression network.
immediate_consequences_latex: All parameter tuples with the same end-to-end product have the same objective value.
If an intermediate width equals zero or enforces a strict bottleneck, the attainable end-to-end ranks are correspondingly restricted.
boundary_notes: Nondifferentiable terminal losses require generalized derivatives and are outside this smooth definition.
Skip connections and sums of products are not single deep matrix products.

notation.meaning: Loss defined on the end-to-end matrix.

review_flags: The supplied matrix-algebra sources do not establish this landscape-level definition or depth-induced singular geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Pullback landscape under a deep matrix product

children.title: Network Architecture Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Effects of layer widths and partial-product ranks on the critical set.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a depth-\(L\) matrix product, let the architecture be \(\mathbf d=(d_0,\ldots,d_L)\), let \(W_\ell\in\mathbb R^{d_\ell\times d_{\ell-1}}\), and define partial products \(P_{j:i}=W_j\cdots W_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A stratification of deep linear parameter spaces by layer widths and actual ranks of contiguous partial products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An architecture regime is specified by the width vector \(\mathbf d\) together with a feasible partial-rank profile
\[\mathbf r=(r_{j:i})_{1\le i\le j\le L},\qquad r_{j:i}=\operatorname{rank}(P_{j:i}).\]
Its parameter stratum is
\[\mathcal S_{\mathbf d,\mathbf r}=\{(W_1,\ldots,W_L):\operatorname{rank}(W_j\cdots W_i)=r_{j:i}\text{ for all }1\le i\le j\le L\}.\]
The profile is feasible only if
\[0\le r_{j:i}\le\min_{i-1\le k\le j}d_k\]
and it obeys every rank monotonicity forced by extending a matrix product. An architecture is end-to-end nonbottlenecked for rank \(q\) when \(d_k\ge q\) for every hidden index \(k\); otherwise a width below \(q\) is a rank bottleneck.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regime family records both nominal layer widths and the realized ranks of every contiguous partial product. Parameters with the same feasible rank profile form a rank stratum. A hidden layer narrower than a desired end-to-end rank is a bottleneck, while widths at least that rank are nonbottlenecking at the level of representability. Different strata can have different critical and symmetry geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal S_{\mathbf d,\mathbf r}=\{W:\operatorname{rank}(P_{j:i})=r_{j:i}\ \forall i\le j\}.\]
special_cases_latex: The full-rank layer regime has \(r_{\ell:\ell}=\min(d_{\ell-1},d_\ell)\) for every layer, although longer partial products may still lose rank.
A constant-width square architecture has \(d_0=\cdots=d_L=d\); its invertible stratum satisfies \(r_{j:i}=d\) for all partial products.
immediate_consequences_latex: The end-to-end rank satisfies \(r_{L:1}\le\min_k d_k\).
Rank-deficient profiles identify singular portions of the matrix-product parameterization.
boundary_notes: Width data alone do not determine the realized partial-rank profile.
This definition classifies regimes but does not assert identical landscape behavior throughout a stratum.

notation.meaning: Vector of input, hidden, and output widths.

review_flags: A source is needed for the proposed architecture-regime terminology and full partial-rank stratification.
knowledge_statements.title: Width and partial-rank architecture regimes
Bottleneck Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bottleneck narrower than the target rank makes exact representation impossible; widths at least the target rank permit every target of that rank to factor through the network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a depth-\(L\) linear architecture with dimensions \(d_0,\ldots,d_L\), define the internal bottleneck width by \(b=\min_{1\le j\le L-1}d_j\). The architecture is in the rank-bottleneck regime at target rank \(r\) when \(b<r\le\min\{d_0,d_L\}\). In this regime every end-to-end product \(M=W_L\cdots W_1\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(M)\le b<r\), so no rank-\(r\) target matrix can be represented exactly. If instead \(b\ge r\), every matrix of rank at most \(r\) admits a factorization through all layers of the prescribed dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b<r\Rightarrow \operatorname{rank}(W_L\cdots W_1)<r\) for all weights; \(b\ge r\Rightarrow\{M:\operatorname{rank}(M)\le r\}\) is representable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Architectural bottlenecks classified by the minimum internal width.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The bottleneck condition and factorization claim are mathematically plausible and fit the terminal container, but no inspectable source supports the universal representability assertion through all prescribed layers.

knowledge_statements.title: Width Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to a target rank, minimum hidden width defines underwidth, matched, and overwidth regimes; only underwidth restricts the attainable target class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_{\mathrm{req}}\) be the largest end-to-end rank required by a specified target class, and let \(b=\min_{1\le j\le L-1}d_j\). The architecture is underwidth for that class when \(b<r_{\mathrm{req}}\), exactly width-matched when \(b=r_{\mathrm{req}}\), and overwidth when \(b>r_{\mathrm{req}}\). Underwidth architectures exclude some required predictors by the rank bound. Width-matched and overwidth architectures represent every required matrix, but overwidth introduces additional factorization degrees of freedom because intermediate representations may occupy directions unused by an end-to-end matrix of rank at most \(r_{\mathrm{req}}\).
assumptions_latex: \(L\ge2\) and the target class consists of matrices of rank at most \(r_{\mathrm{req}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b<r_{\mathrm{req}}\) restricts representability, whereas \(b\ge r_{\mathrm{req}}\) does not restrict the specified rank-bounded target class.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Underparameterized and non-bottleneck architectures distinguished by layer widths.

notation.meaning: Largest rank required by the target class.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The proposed width classification fits a condition record, but the underwidth, width-matched, and overwidth terminology is introduced without a source. The assertion about additional inactive-direction degrees of freedom also needs a precise source and qualification.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: End-to-end rank partitions the parameters into strata. Lower-rank products form boundary degeneracies, and matrix rank can fall, but not rise, under limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For weights \(W=(W_L,\ldots,W_1)\), set \(M(W)=W_L\cdots W_1\) and \(r_*=\min_{0\le j\le L}d_j\). The parameter space is partitioned into rank strata \(\mathcal{S}_r=\{W:\operatorname{rank}M(W)=r\}\) for \(0\le r\le r_*\). The full-capacity regime is \(r=r_*\), and the rank-deficient regime is \(r<r_*\). Rank is locally constant on each fixed-rank matrix stratum but may drop on its boundary; consequently, parameter sequences in \(\mathcal{S}_r\) can converge to lower-rank strata, while a rank increase cannot occur in a matrix limit.
assumptions_latex: \(L\ge2\) and all layer dimensions are positive.
Convergence is with respect to the Euclidean topology on the weight matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\mathcal{S}_r}\subseteq\bigcup_{q=0}^{r}\mathcal{S}_q\) after mapping to end-to-end matrices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stratification by end-to-end rank relative to architectural capacity.

notation.meaning: End-to-end product associated with the weights.
Parameter stratum with end-to-end rank exactly r.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The rank-regime condition is locally appropriate and the upper-semicontinuity claim is plausible. A source is required for the parameter-space stratification and its stated closure behavior, especially because the conclusion qualifies the closure only after applying the end-to-end map.

knowledge_statements.title: Architectural Regime Interactions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bottleneck width controls whether a target rank is feasible; excess width and deficient realized rank control how nonunique and degenerate its factorizations can be.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b=\min_{1\le j\le L-1}d_j\), let \(r=\operatorname{rank}(W_L\cdots W_1)\), and let a target matrix have rank \(r_T\). These quantities satisfy \(r\le\min\{b,d_0,d_L\}\). If \(b<r_T\), approximation error cannot vanish solely by changing the factors. If \(b\ge r_T\), representability is unobstructed by width, but whenever some internal width exceeds \(r_T\), the same rank-\(r_T\) end-to-end matrix generally has redundant factorizations, including changes of basis on an active hidden subspace and arbitrary compatible behavior on inactive directions. Thus width governs feasibility, while realized rank governs degeneracy within feasible fibers.
assumptions_latex: \(L\ge2\) and all matrices have compatible dimensions.
The target is an end-to-end matrix of rank \(r_T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b<r_T\) implies infeasibility, whereas \(b\ge r_T\) permits representation and excess internal width creates factorization redundancy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint effect of bottleneck width, realized rank, and factorization redundancy.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property belongs in the architectural-interactions container, but phrases such as “generally,” “active hidden subspace,” and “arbitrary compatible behavior” lack precise hypotheses. A source is needed to determine and state the exact redundancy claim reliably.

children.title: Scaling-Orbit Geometry
children.top_down_role: Layerwise rescaling symmetries and noncompact parameter orbits.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(L\ge2\) and let \(\mathcal W=\prod_{\ell=1}^L\mathbb F^{d_\ell\times d_{\ell-1}}\), where \(\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}\). Let \(P(W)=W_L\cdots W_1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The scalar gauge subgroup of a homogeneous deep matrix product; broader hidden-basis transformations are not part of the defining action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the scaling group
\[\mathcal G=\{c=(c_1,\ldots,c_L)\in(\mathbb F\setminus\{0\})^L:\prod_{\ell=1}^Lc_\ell=1\}.\]
It acts on \(\mathcal W\) by
\[c\cdot(W_1,\ldots,W_L)=(c_1W_1,\ldots,c_LW_L).\]
The scaling orbit of \(W\) is \(\mathcal O(W)=\{c\cdot W:c\in\mathcal G\}\). Since \(P(c\cdot W)=P(W)\), every objective of the form \(F(W)=\Phi(P(W))\) is constant on \(\mathcal O(W)\). If at least two factors are nonzero, an orbit can be noncompact: one factor may be multiplied by \(t\) and an adjacent factor by \(t^{-1}\) as \(|t|\to\infty\), while the represented product remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaling group independently rescales layers by nonzero scalars whose product is one. Its orbit contains all layer tuples obtained by such reciprocal scalings. The end-to-end matrix and every loss depending only on that matrix are invariant along the orbit. These orbits are generally unbounded because one layer can grow while another shrinks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal O(W)=\{(c_1W_1,\ldots,c_LW_L):c_\ell\ne0,\ \prod_{\ell=1}^Lc_\ell=1\},\qquad P(c\cdot W)=P(W).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using coordinates \(c_1,\ldots,c_{L-1}\), one may set \(c_L=(\prod_{\ell=1}^{L-1}c_\ell)^{-1}\), identifying \(\mathcal G\) with \((\mathbb F\setminus\{0\})^{L-1}\).
special_cases_latex: For two factors, \(\mathcal O(U,V)=\{(tU,t^{-1}V):t\ne0\}\).
Restricting real scalings to \(c_\ell>0\) selects the identity component of the real scaling group.
immediate_consequences_latex: Parameter sublevel sets of an invariant loss can be noncompact even when the represented end-to-end matrices remain bounded.
Any isolated-minimizer statement in raw parameter space fails at a nontrivial scaling orbit unless the symmetry is fixed or quotiented.
boundary_notes: Zero factors have larger stabilizers and may yield lower-dimensional orbits.
Weight decay and explicit normalization generally break this scaling invariance.

notation.meaning: Scaling orbit through the parameter tuple \(W\).

review_flags: No inspected source from the supplied hints treats scaling orbits of deep homogeneous models.
knowledge_statements.title: Layerwise reciprocal-scaling orbits
Balancedness Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deep factorization is balanced when adjacent layers have identical interface Gram matrices; approximate balancedness bounds every such mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For compatible real matrices \(W_1,\ldots,W_L\), define the imbalance matrices \(D_\ell=W_{\ell+1}^{\mathsf T}W_{\ell+1}-W_\ell W_\ell^{\mathsf T}\) for \(1\le\ell<L\). The factorization is balanced when \[D_\ell=0\qquad\text{for every }\ell=1,\ldots,L-1.\] Equivalently, the right Gram matrix of each layer equals the left Gram matrix of the preceding layer at every hidden interface. Balancedness fixes relative scale across adjacent factors while retaining compatible orthogonal changes of hidden coordinates. An \(\varepsilon\)-balanced factorization may be defined by \(\max_{1\le\ell<L}\lVert D_\ell\rVert_F\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Balancedness holds exactly when \(W_{\ell+1}^{\mathsf T}W_{\ell+1}=W_\ell W_\ell^{\mathsf T}\) for all \(1\le\ell<L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adjacent-layer Gram equalities selecting balanced deep factorizations.

notation.meaning: Gram imbalance at hidden interface l.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The adjacent-Gram definition is dimensionally consistent, and condition is the correct mathematical role. No authoritative balancedness source or exact locator is supplied for the definition and its geometric interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Orbits
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reciprocal scaling or an invertible hidden-coordinate change applied to adjacent layers preserves the end-to-end product and every product-dependent loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(1\le j<L\). For any scalar \(c>0\), transform adjacent factors by \(W_j\mapsto cW_j\) and \(W_{j+1}\mapsto c^{-1}W_{j+1}\), leaving all other factors unchanged. Then \[(W_L\cdots(c^{-1}W_{j+1})(cW_j)\cdots W_1)=W_L\cdots W_1.\] Hence every objective depending on the weights only through their end-to-end product is constant on this scaling orbit. More generally, for any invertible \(G\in\operatorname{GL}(d_j)\), the transformation \(W_j\mapsto GW_j\), \(W_{j+1}\mapsto W_{j+1}G^{-1}\) preserves the product and generates a hidden-coordinate symmetry orbit.
assumptions_latex: The objective has the form \(F(W)=\ell(W_L\cdots W_1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(W_L,\ldots,W_{j+1}G^{-1},GW_j,\ldots,W_1)=F(W_L,\ldots,W_1)\) for every \(G\in\operatorname{GL}(d_j)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-preserving rescalings of adjacent layers in deep linear networks.

notation.meaning: Group of invertible real matrices of size d_j.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The scalar and general-linear product-preserving actions are correct and fit a representation record. Candidate-review admission still requires an authoritative source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Orbit Noncompactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reciprocal layer scaling creates unbounded parameter sequences with unchanged prediction and loss, so coercivity of the end-to-end problem need not transfer to factor space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two nonzero adjacent factors \(W_j\) and \(W_{j+1}\). Their scaling orbit contains \((cW_j,c^{-1}W_{j+1})\) for every \(c>0\), while the end-to-end product and any product-dependent objective remain constant. As \(c\to\infty\), \(\lVert cW_j\rVert_F\to\infty\), and as \(c\to0\), \(\lVert c^{-1}W_{j+1}\rVert_F\to\infty\). Therefore the orbit is noncompact and the corresponding objective sublevel set need not be bounded. Product-level coercivity alone consequently does not imply coercivity in factor space; normalization, balancing, regularization, or quotienting is needed to remove this obstruction.
assumptions_latex: The objective depends only on \(W_L\cdots W_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The orbit \(\{(cW_j,c^{-1}W_{j+1}):c>0\}\) is noncompact and lies in one objective level set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded parameter sequences generated by product-preserving scaling.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The noncompact scaling orbit is correctly formulated and failure_boundary fits the leaf. A source is required for the factor-space coercivity consequence and the stated remedies.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Reduced Critical Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product-preserving hidden-coordinate transformations carry critical points to equivalent critical points; quotienting their orbits removes this parameterization redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{P}=\prod_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathbb{R}^{d_\ell\times d_{\ell-1}}\), and let the hidden-coordinate group \(\mathcal{G}=\prod_{j=1}^{L-1}\operatorname{GL}(d_j)\) act by consecutive transformations that preserve \(W_L\cdots W_1\). If \(F(W)=\ell(W_L\cdots W_1)\), then \(F(g\cdot W)=F(W)\) for every \(g\in\mathcal{G}\). Consequently, the critical set \(\operatorname{Crit}(F)=\{W:\nabla F(W)=0\}\) is \(\mathcal{G}\)-invariant, and each critical orbit \(\mathcal{G}\cdot W\) represents one symmetry-reduced critical class in the quotient \(\operatorname{Crit}(F)/\mathcal{G}\). This reduction identifies parameter points differing only by invertible hidden-coordinate choices.
assumptions_latex: The group action is restricted to invertible hidden-coordinate transformations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W\in\operatorname{Crit}(F)\Rightarrow g\cdot W\in\operatorname{Crit}(F)\) for every \(g\in\mathcal{G}\), so critical classes are elements of \(\operatorname{Crit}(F)/\mathcal{G}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical points viewed modulo product-preserving group actions.

notation.meaning: Product of hidden-coordinate general linear groups.
Symmetry orbit of a parameter tuple.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The invariance of criticality under the smooth invertible symmetry action is plausible, and the quotient representation matches the container. The group action and quotient-critical-set formulation require an inspectable source and precise locator.

children.title: Multilinear Recovery Landscape Family
children.top_down_role: Canonical structured models sharing factorization, symmetry, and identifiability mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V_1,\ldots,V_K\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real or complex inner-product spaces, let \(\mathcal M:V_1\times\cdots\times V_K\to Y\) be multilinear, let \(\mathcal A:Y\to\mathbb F^m\) be linear, and let \(b\in\mathbb F^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic least-squares recovery through a multilinear factorization, including bilinear and tensor-factor models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The multilinear recovery landscape associated with \((\mathcal A,\mathcal M,b)\) is
\[F(u_1,\ldots,u_K)=\frac12\|\mathcal A(\mathcal M(u_1,\ldots,u_K))-b\|_2^2,
\qquad (u_1,\ldots,u_K)\in\prod_{k=1}^KV_k.\]
Its represented object is \(X=\mathcal M(u_1,\ldots,u_K)\). The canonical scalar ambiguity is
\[(u_1,\ldots,u_K)\sim(c_1u_1,\ldots,c_Ku_K)\quad\text{when}\quad c_k\ne0,\ \prod_{k=1}^Kc_k=1,\]
because multilinearity leaves \(X\) unchanged. Additional permutation, orthogonal, or change-of-basis symmetries may occur for particular parameterizations. Identifiability means that equality of noiseless measurements implies equality of represented objects, and factor identifiability further requires equality only up to the declared symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multilinear recovery landscape fits measurements of an object represented by a multilinear map of several factors. Product-one rescaling of the factors leaves the represented object unchanged, creating a basic gauge symmetry. Measurement identifiability concerns the object itself; factor identifiability is stronger and is always interpreted modulo the model's symmetries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F(u_1,\ldots,u_K)=\tfrac12\|\mathcal A(\mathcal M(u_1,\ldots,u_K))-b\|_2^2.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(\Psi=\mathcal A\circ\mathcal M\), the landscape is the nonlinear least-squares objective \(F(u)=\frac12\|\Psi(u)-b\|_2^2\), with \(\Psi\) multilinear before residual formation.
special_cases_latex: For \(K=2\), the family includes matrix factorization and blind deconvolution.
For \(K\ge3\), canonical polyadic tensor parameterizations give higher-order multilinear instances.
immediate_consequences_latex: Without gauge fixing or regularization, equivalent factor tuples can be arbitrarily unbalanced.
Failure of measurement injectivity produces distinct represented objects with identical noiseless data.
boundary_notes: Models that are polynomial but not multilinear in separate factor blocks are outside this definition.
Noise changes \(b\) but does not remove parameter symmetries of \(\mathcal M\).
review_flags: No inspected source supports this exact umbrella definition and its object-versus-factor identifiability distinction.
knowledge_statements.title: Multilinear inverse-problem landscape family

children.title: Blind-Deconvolution Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Bilinear inverse-problem geometry with scaling ambiguity.

knowledge_statements.title: Blind-Deconvolution Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blind deconvolution becomes rank-one matrix sensing after lifting. Reciprocal rescaling of the two factors leaves both measurements and loss unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\in\mathbb{R}^p\), \(v\in\mathbb{R}^q\), observations \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and a linear measurement operator \(\mathcal{A}:\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\to\mathbb{R}^m\). A standard lifted blind-deconvolution landscape is \[F(u,v)=\frac12\lVert\mathcal{A}(uv^{\mathsf T})-y\rVert_2^2.\] It depends on the factors only through the rank-one matrix \(uv^{\mathsf T}\). For every nonzero scalar \(c\), \((cu,c^{-1}v)\) produces the same lifted matrix and objective value. Thus identifiable solutions are equivalence classes under reciprocal scaling; additional assumptions on \(\mathcal{A}\), noise, and structural subspaces are required for recovery claims.
assumptions_latex: The displayed model uses an unconstrained real bilinear parameterization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(cu,c^{-1}v)=F(u,v)\) for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted bilinear least-squares model with reciprocal-scaling ambiguity.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h\in\mathbb C^{k}\), \(x\in\mathbb C^{n}\), sensing vectors \(b_r\in\mathbb C^k\), \(a_r\in\mathbb C^n\), and measurements \(y_r\in\mathbb C\) for \(r=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional bilinear sensing with squared complex residuals and the intrinsic reciprocal-scaling ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the bilinear measurement map
\[\mathcal B(h,x)_r=(b_r^*h)(a_r^*x)=b_r^*(hx^*)\overline{a_r},\qquad r=1,\ldots,m,\]
with the conjugation convention fixed by the displayed identity. The blind-deconvolution least-squares landscape is
\[F(h,x)=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{r=1}^m|(b_r^*h)(a_r^*x)-y_r|^2.\]
For every nonzero \(c\in\mathbb C\), \(\mathcal B(ch,c^{-1}x)=\mathcal B(h,x)\), so the intrinsic parameter is the equivalence class \([(h,x)]\) under reciprocal scaling. In lifted coordinates \(X=hx^*\), the same model is linear sensing of a rank-one matrix, subject to the nonconvex condition \(\operatorname{rank}X=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blind deconvolution observes products of one linear functional of each of two unknown factors. Its least-squares objective is bilinear before squaring and is invariant when one factor is multiplied by a nonzero scalar and the other is divided by it. Lifting replaces the factor pair by a rank-one matrix, making the measurements linear while retaining a rank constraint.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(X=hx^*\), define \(\mathscr A(X)_r=b_r^*X\overline{a_r}\); then \(F(h,x)=(2m)^{-1}\|\mathscr A(hx^*)-y\|_2^2\).
special_cases_latex: Circular blind deconvolution with known subspaces can be expressed in this form after Fourier transformation and choice of sensing vectors.
immediate_consequences_latex: Unregularized factor sublevel sets may be noncompact along reciprocal-scaling orbits.
Recovery of the factor pair can only be requested modulo the scaling equivalence.
boundary_notes: The exact placement of complex conjugates depends on the chosen Fourier and inner-product conventions.
Blind deconvolution with additive structural constraints or nonsmooth regularizers defines a constrained or composite variant.
review_flags: A dedicated blind-deconvolution source is required to validate the sensing convention and canonical scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted bilinear blind-deconvolution landscape

children.title: Dictionary-Learning Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Sparse latent-factor geometry with permutation and scaling ambiguities.

knowledge_statements.title: Dictionary-Learning Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dictionary learning fits data by a dictionary times sparse codes. Signed permutations preserve the model, while omitting atom normalization also permits reciprocal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given samples \(Y=[y_1,\ldots,y_n]\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times n}\), a dictionary \(D=[d_1,\ldots,d_k]\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times k}\), and codes \(X=[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times n}\), a constrained dictionary-learning landscape is \[F(D,X)=\frac12\lVert DX-Y\rVert_F^2+\lambda\lVert X\rVert_1,\qquad \lVert d_j\rVert_2=1\ \text{for all }j.\] For every signed permutation matrix \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k}\), the transformation \((D,X)\mapsto(DP,P^{\mathsf T}X)\) preserves feasibility and objective value. Without column normalization, reciprocal atom-code scaling supplies an additional noncompact ambiguity.
assumptions_latex: Every dictionary column is constrained to have unit Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(DP,P^{\mathsf T}X)=F(D,X)\) for every signed permutation matrix \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix factorization with sparse codes and signed-permutation symmetries.

notation.meaning: Signed permutation matrix acting on atoms.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The signed-permutation invariance is consistent with the displayed normalized, ℓ1-regularized model, and representation fits the landscape container. A source must be supplied that specifically supports this dictionary-learning objective variant and its ambiguity claims.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let data vectors \(y_1,\ldots,y_N\in\mathbb R^d\), dictionary size \(p\), dictionary \(D=[d_1,\ldots,d_p]\in\mathbb R^{d\times p}\), and codes \(\alpha_i\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional synthesis dictionary learning with unit-norm atoms and an explicit sparsity penalty on latent codes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The normalized sparse dictionary-learning landscape is the constrained composite objective
\[F(D,A)=\frac{1}{2N}\sum_{i=1}^N\|y_i-D\alpha_i\|_2^2+\frac{\lambda}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\|\alpha_i\|_1,\]
where \(A=[\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N]\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and
\[D\in\mathcal D_{d,p}:=\{[d_1,\ldots,d_p]\in\mathbb R^{d\times p}:\|d_j\|_2=1\text{ for every }j\}.\]
For every signed permutation matrix \(P\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\), the transformation \((D,A)\mapsto(DP,P^TA)\) preserves the reconstruction and the \(\ell_1\) penalty. Thus dictionaries are identifiable at best up to atom permutation and sign unless further conventions are imposed. Unit normalization removes continuous atom-code scaling but not these discrete ambiguities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dictionary learning jointly fits a matrix of unit-norm atoms and sparse coefficient vectors to observed data. Squared reconstruction error measures fit, and an entrywise one-norm penalty promotes sparse codes. Simultaneously permuting atoms and code coordinates, or changing corresponding signs, leaves the objective unchanged. Atom normalization removes the otherwise continuous scaling ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{D\in\mathcal D_{d,p},\,A} (2N)^{-1}\sum_i\|y_i-D\alpha_i\|_2^2+(\lambda/N)\sum_i\|\alpha_i\|_1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating the codes defines the dictionary-only value landscape \(\bar F(D)=N^{-1}\sum_i\min_\alpha\{\frac12\|y_i-D\alpha\|_2^2+\lambda\|\alpha\|_1\}\).
special_cases_latex: When \(p=d\) and \(D\) is additionally orthogonal, the model becomes orthogonal dictionary learning.
When \(\lambda=0\), the formulation loses explicit sparsity promotion and reduces to constrained low-rank reconstruction when \(p<d\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every minimizer has a full signed-permutation orbit of equivalent minimizers.
The joint objective is nonsmooth at code entries equal to zero when \(\lambda>0\).
boundary_notes: Overcomplete dictionaries have \(p>d\) and cannot have mutually orthogonal columns.
Alternative formulations impose exact sparsity constraints instead of an \(\ell_1\) penalty.

notation.meaning: Set of dictionaries with unit-norm columns.
Matrix collecting all latent coefficient vectors.

review_flags: No inspected source in the supplied hints covers sparse dictionary-learning objectives and their signed-permutation symmetry.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized sparse dictionary-learning landscape

children.title: Orthogonal Tensor-Decomposition Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Higher-order factor landscapes in identifiable orthogonal regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal Tensor-Decomposition Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonally decomposable symmetric tensor induces a sphere objective whose stationary component directions coincide with its orthogonal factors, with other stationary points expressed as factor mixtures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\in\operatorname{Sym}^3(\mathbb{R}^d)\) admit the orthogonal decomposition \(T=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i a_i^{\otimes 3}\), where \(a_i^{\mathsf T}a_j=\delta_{ij}\) and every \(\lambda_i\neq0\). The sphere-constrained extraction landscape is \[f(u)=-T(u,u,u)=-\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}u)^3,\qquad u\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}.\] Its Riemannian stationary points satisfy \[(I-uu^{\mathsf T})T(u,u,\cdot)=0.\] Thus each signed component direction \(u=\pm a_i\) is stationary, while any additional stationary mixtures are determined explicitly by the orthogonal coordinates \(a_i^{\mathsf T}u\).
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is symmetric and has an orthogonal rank-\(r\) decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(u)=-\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}u)^3\) and \((I-uu^{\mathsf T})T(u,u,\cdot)=0\) characterizes stationarity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric third-order orthogonally decomposable tensors and their single-component extraction landscape.

notation.meaning: Trilinear evaluation of the tensor on three copies of u.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard orthogonally decomposable symmetric-tensor extraction model

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the orthogonal tensor-landscape container and is mathematically coherent, including the projected stationarity condition and the possibility of stationary mixtures. No inspectable citation supports the model or stationary-point characterization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p\ge3\), let \(T\in\operatorname{Sym}^p(\mathbb R^d)\), and fix a component count \(r\le d\). Let \(U=[u_1,\ldots,u_r]\in\operatorname{St}(d,r)=\{U:U^TU=I_r\}\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real symmetric orthogonal tensor decomposition using a constrained Frobenius fitting landscape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The orthogonal tensor-decomposition landscape is
\[F(U,\lambda)=\frac12\left\|T-\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i u_i^{\otimes p}\right\|_F^2,
\qquad (U,\lambda)\in\operatorname{St}(d,r)\times\mathbb R^r.\]
A tensor is orthogonally decomposable of rank \(r\) when there exist orthonormal vectors \(u_1^\star,\ldots,u_r^\star\) and nonzero weights \(\lambda_i^\star\) such that
\[T=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i^\star(u_i^\star)^{\otimes p}.\]
Component permutations preserve the represented tensor. Sign changes satisfy \((-u_i)^{\otimes p}=u_i^{\otimes p}\) for even \(p\), while for odd \(p\) they must be accompanied by \(\lambda_i\mapsto-\lambda_i\). The landscape is therefore interpreted modulo these discrete symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonal tensor-decomposition landscape fits a symmetric tensor by a sum of symmetric rank-one powers whose directions are mutually orthonormal. Exact orthogonal decomposability means such a representation exists with nonzero weights. Permuting components does not change the tensor, and sign ambiguity depends on whether the tensor order is even or odd.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F(U,\lambda)=\tfrac12\|T-\sum_i\lambda_i u_i^{\otimes p}\|_F^2\quad\text{on}\quad \operatorname{St}(d,r)\times\mathbb R^r.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed orthonormal \(U\), minimizing over each weight gives \(\lambda_i=\langle T,u_i^{\otimes p}\rangle\), yielding an equivalent reduced objective on the Stiefel manifold.
special_cases_latex: For \(r=1\), the reduced problem is optimization of the homogeneous polynomial \(u\mapsto\langle T,u^{\otimes p}\rangle\) on the unit sphere.
For \(p=2\), the model reduces to orthogonal spectral decomposition of a symmetric matrix and is outside the higher-order scope.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact decompositions have zero fitting loss.
Identifiability is necessarily stated modulo component permutation and parity-dependent signs.
boundary_notes: Noisy tensors need not admit a zero-loss orthogonal decomposition.
Nonorthogonal component models use a different feasible set and may have additional nonidentifiability.

notation.meaning: Symmetric rank-one tensor formed from \(p\) copies of \(u\).

review_flags: The supplied spectral-decomposition hint concerns matrices, not the exact higher-order orthogonal tensor landscape.
knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonally decomposable symmetric tensor landscape

children.title: Nonorthogonal Tensor-Landscape Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Loss of simple benign geometry outside orthogonal or strongly identifiable regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonorthogonal Tensor-Landscape Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coincident or nearly collinear tensor factors create cancellation directions, destroying uniform identifiability and curvature guarantees available in well-separated orthogonal regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider least-squares fitting of \(T_\star=a^{\otimes3}+a^{\otimes3}\) by \(\Phi(x_1,x_2)=x_1^{\otimes3}+x_2^{\otimes3}\), with objective \(F=\tfrac12\|\Phi-T_\star\|_F^2\). At \((x_1,x_2)=(a,a)\), the perturbation \((h,-h)\) obeys \[D\Phi(a,a)[h,-h]=3\,\operatorname{sym}(a^{\otimes2}\otimes h)-3\,\operatorname{sym}(a^{\otimes2}\otimes h)=0.\] Hence the Hessian of \(F\) has a nonidentifiability null direction not generated merely by permutation. As distinct factors approach collinearity, this cancellation becomes approximate, so uniform curvature and strict-saddle constants cannot persist without a quantitative separation or conditioning assumption.
assumptions_latex: The factorization is parameterized without an identifying separation constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\Phi(a,a)[h,-h]=0\), so \(\nabla^2F(a,a)\) is singular along \((h,-h)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order degeneracy when tensor components coincide or become nearly collinear.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct differential calculation for a coincident-component CP parameterization

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The exact-fit differential cancellation and resulting Hessian null direction are correct. An authoritative source is still required for the broader assertion that near-collinearity precludes uniform curvature or strict-saddle constants without quantitative conditioning assumptions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coherence and degeneracy boundaries for nonorthogonal tensor factors
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p\ge3\), \(T\in\operatorname{Sym}^p(\mathbb R^d)\), unit vectors \(u_1,\ldots,u_r\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\), weights \(\lambda_i\in\mathbb R\), and Gram matrix \(G(U)=U^TU\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A diagnostic family marking departure from orthogonal tensor components and approach to linearly dependent factor configurations; it does not assert a universal bad-landscape threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The nonorthogonal symmetric tensor fitting landscape is
\[F(U,\lambda)=\frac12\left\|T-\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i u_i^{\otimes p}\right\|_F^2,
\qquad u_i\in\mathbb S^{d-1}.\]
Its coherence is
\[\mu(U)=\max_{i\ne j}|u_i^Tu_j|.\]
The orthogonal boundary is departed from when \(\mu(U)>0\), while the factor-degeneracy boundary is the set
\[\partial_{\mathrm{deg}}=\{U:\lambda_{\min}(G(U))=0\},\]
where the columns are linearly dependent. A quantitatively separated nonorthogonal regime may be specified by \(0<\mu(U)\le\bar\mu<1\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(G(U))\ge\gamma>0\). Approaching \(\partial_{\mathrm{deg}}\) means \(\lambda_{\min}(G(U))\downarrow0\), potentially destroying stable factor identifiability even when the represented tensor remains bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonorthogonal landscape fits a tensor using unit but not necessarily orthogonal component directions. Maximum pairwise correlation measures departure from orthogonality, while the smallest Gram eigenvalue detects approach to linear dependence. The degeneracy boundary consists of factor frames with singular Gram matrix. These quantities define geometric regimes but do not by themselves guarantee or preclude benign optimization geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\mu(U)=\max_{i\ne j}|u_i^Tu_j|,
\qquad \partial_{\mathrm{deg}}=\{U:\lambda_{\min}(U^TU)=0\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition \(\lambda_{\min}(U^TU)=0\) is equivalent to \(\operatorname{rank}U<r\).
special_cases_latex: The orthogonal regime has \(G(U)=I_r\) and \(\mu(U)=0\).
For two unit components, degeneracy occurs exactly when \(|u_1^Tu_2|=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Uniform lower bounds on \(\lambda_{\min}(G(U))\) exclude linearly dependent factor frames.
Pairwise coherence below one does not alone ensure good conditioning when many components are present.
boundary_notes: There is no universal coherence value at which spurious critical points must appear; such claims require model-specific hypotheses.
Overcomplete regimes with \(r>d\) necessarily satisfy \(\lambda_{\min}(G(U))=0\).

notation.meaning: Maximum absolute pairwise coherence of component directions.
Gram matrix of the component frame.

review_flags: The node title is not a standard single definition; the coherence/Gram-boundary interpretation needs a source tied to tensor landscapes.
knowledge_statements.title: Coherence and degeneracy boundaries for nonorthogonal tensor factors

children.title: Geometric Estimation Landscape Family
children.top_down_role: Smooth constrained models whose landscape structure is governed by group actions or manifold geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\mathcal M,g)\) be a finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold, let a Lie group \(G\) act smoothly on \(\mathcal M\), and let residual maps \(r_i:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R^{q_i}\) be smooth.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth constrained estimation whose nonidentifiability is represented by a group action and whose intrinsic domain may be a quotient manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A geometric estimation landscape is a smooth objective
\[F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i(r_i(x)),\qquad x\in\mathcal M,\]
where each \(\rho_i:\mathbb R^{q_i}\to\mathbb R\) is smooth, together with a smooth symmetry action satisfying
\[F(g\cdot x)=F(x)\qquad\text{for every }g\in G,\ x\in\mathcal M.\]
The orbit of \(x\) is \(G\cdot x=\{g\cdot x:g\in G\}\), and the stabilizer is \(G_x=\{g:g\cdot x=x\}\). When the action is free and proper, the intrinsic estimation domain is the quotient manifold \(\mathcal M/G\), and \(F\) induces \(\bar F([x])=F(x)\). Criticality on \(\mathcal M\) is defined by \(\operatorname{grad}F(x)=0\); quotient criticality removes directions tangent to symmetry orbits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometric estimation landscape is a smooth residual objective defined on a manifold and invariant under a smooth group action. Equivalent estimates lie on the same group orbit. Stabilizers record symmetries fixing an estimate. For a free and proper action, the objective descends to the quotient manifold, which removes gauge directions from the intrinsic estimation problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F(g\cdot x)=F(x),\qquad \bar F([x])=F(x)\text{ on }\mathcal M/G\text{ when the quotient is regular}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Invariance is equivalent to constancy of \(F\) on every orbit \(G\cdot x\).
special_cases_latex: Synchronization uses a diagonal global group action on a product manifold.
Orthogonal alignment uses a common right or left orthogonal gauge action, depending on the data convention.
immediate_consequences_latex: The directional derivative of an invariant smooth objective vanishes along every tangent direction to a group orbit.
Nontrivial stabilizers can make the quotient stratified rather than a smooth manifold.
boundary_notes: Nonsmooth robust penalties require a generalized criticality notion.
A nonfree action is not covered by the simple quotient-manifold statement.

notation.meaning: Orbit of \(x\) under the symmetry group.

review_flags: No inspected supplied source supports this combined manifold, group-action, and quotient-landscape definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Group-invariant estimation landscapes on manifolds

children.title: Synchronization Landscapes
children.top_down_role: Group-valued estimation models with gauge symmetries.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronization estimates group elements from relative measurements. A common right action leaves the objective unchanged, so the landscape descends to a quotient, while graph or model degeneracies may cause further ambiguity.

atural(g_j^
atural)^{-1})\), every tuple \((g_1^
atural h,\ldots,g_n^
atural h)\) has zero loss. Consequently, the objective descends through the diagonal right-action quotient \(G^n/G\), although disconnected measurement graphs or other model degeneracies may create additional ambiguities.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is compact and \(\rho:G\to O(m)\) is a faithful orthogonal representation.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal G=(V,E)\) be a weighted graph, let \(G\) be a compact matrix group with Frobenius metric, let \(g_i\in G\) be unknown vertex labels, and let \(Y_{ij}\in G\) estimate the relative transform \(g_ig_j^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite graph synchronization over a compact matrix group with squared chordal residuals and a global gauge symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The synchronization landscape is
\[F(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=\frac12\sum_{(i,j)\in E}w_{ij}\|Y_{ij}-g_ig_j^{-1}\|_F^2,
\qquad (g_1,\ldots,g_n)\in G^n,\]
where \(w_{ij}\ge0\). Under the displayed relative-measurement convention, the diagonal right action
\[(g_1,\ldots,g_n)\mapsto(g_1h,\ldots,g_nh),\qquad h\in G,\]
leaves every relative transform and the objective invariant. Hence the intrinsic domain is \(G^n/G\) when the action is regular. In the noiseless consistent case, zero loss means \(Y_{ij}=g_ig_j^{-1}\) on every measured edge. Graph connectivity is required to reduce componentwise gauges to a single global gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronization estimates one group element per graph vertex from noisy relative transformations on edges. The objective sums weighted squared discrepancies between observed and predicted relative transforms. Multiplying all labels on the right by the same group element leaves every prediction unchanged, so estimates are identifiable only up to a global gauge. Disconnected graphs possess one independent gauge per connected component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[F(g)=\tfrac12\sum_{(i,j)\in E}w_{ij}\|Y_{ij}-g_ig_j^{-1}\|_F^2,
\qquad F(g_1h,\ldots,g_nh)=F(g_1,
\ldots,g_n).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For orthogonal groups, expanding the squared norms converts minimization into maximization of a weighted sum of trace correlations \(\operatorname{tr}(Y_{ij}^Tg_ig_j^T)\), up to an additive constant.
special_cases_latex: For \(G=\mathbb S^1\), this is angular or phase synchronization.
For \(G=\mathrm{SO}(d)\), it is rotation synchronization.
immediate_consequences_latex: Fixing one vertex label removes the global gauge on a connected graph.
In a disconnected graph, relative data cannot identify transformations between different connected components.
boundary_notes: Using the opposite relative-transform convention changes whether the global gauge acts on the left or right.
Geodesic-distance losses define related synchronization landscapes but need not equal the chordal formulation.

children.title: Orthogonal Alignment Landscape Family

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb R^{d\times N}\) be point configurations with corresponding columns, let \(Q_i\in\mathrm O(d)\), and let \(w_{ij}\ge0\) be edge weights on a graph \((V,E)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized orthogonal Procrustes alignment with known correspondences, no translations, and a common orthogonal gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The pairwise orthogonal alignment landscape is
\[F(Q_1,\ldots,Q_n)=\frac12\sum_{(i,j)\in E}w_{ij}\|Q_iX_i-Q_jX_j\|_F^2,
\qquad (Q_1,\ldots,Q_n)\in\mathrm O(d)^n.\]
For every common \(R\in\mathrm O(d)\),
\[F(RQ_1,\ldots,RQ_n)=F(Q_1,\ldots,Q_n),\]
so the intrinsic parameter is the quotient of \(\mathrm O(d)^n\) by common left multiplication. Equivalently, one may introduce a template \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d\times N}\) and use
\[F_{\mathrm{temp}}(Q,Z)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^nw_i\|Q_iX_i-Z\|_F^2.\]
Eliminating \(Z\) yields a weighted pairwise alignment objective on a complete graph, with weights determined by the template weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonal alignment assigns an orthogonal transform to each corresponding point configuration and minimizes disagreement between transformed configurations. A common left rotation or reflection changes the coordinate frame but not any pairwise discrepancy, producing a quotient geometry. A template-based generalized Procrustes formulation is an equivalent complete-graph representation after the template is optimized out.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[F(Q)=\tfrac12\sum_{(i,j)\in E}w_{ij}\|Q_iX_i-Q_jX_j\|_F^2,
\qquad F(RQ_1,\ldots,RQ_n)=F(Q_1,\ldots,Q_n).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Expanding the Frobenius norms makes minimization equivalent, up to constants, to maximizing \(\sum_{(i,j)\in E}w_{ij}\operatorname{tr}(Q_iX_iX_j^TQ_j^T)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(n=2\), fixing one gauge gives the classical two-set orthogonal Procrustes problem.
Restricting \(Q_i\in\mathrm{SO}(d)\) excludes reflections and gives rotational alignment.
immediate_consequences_latex: On a connected comparison graph, fixing one \(Q_i\) removes the common orthogonal gauge.
If the graph is disconnected, each connected component has an independent common orthogonal gauge.
boundary_notes: Unknown correspondences, translations, and scale factors require additional variables and define broader registration models.
Rank-deficient configurations can have stabilizers beyond the common global gauge.
review_flags: No inspected source in the supplied hints covers generalized orthogonal Procrustes alignment and its quotient symmetry.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized orthogonal alignment landscape
Alignment Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alignment landscape fits orthogonal transformations to pairwise matched data and is invariant under changing every object to the same global frame.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data matrices \(X_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times p_i}\), correspondence operators \(C_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}^{p_i\times p_j}\), and weights \(w_{ij}\ge0\), the orthogonal alignment landscape is \[F(Q_1,\ldots,Q_n)=\frac12\sum_{(i,j)\in E}w_{ij}\|Q_iX_iC_{ij}-Q_jX_j\|_F^2,\qquad Q_i\in O(d).\] Because left multiplication by a common \(R\in O(d)\) preserves Frobenius norms, \(F(RQ_1,\ldots,RQ_n)=F(Q_1,\ldots,Q_n)\). Thus minimizers are generally identifiable only up to a common orthogonal frame unless one transformation is anchored or an equivalent gauge condition is imposed.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times p_i}\) and all displayed matrix products are dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(RQ_1,\ldots,RQ_n)=F(Q_1,\ldots,Q_n)\) for every \(R\in O(d)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-object orthogonal alignment with pairwise correspondences and gauge invariance.

notation.meaning: Pairwise correspondence operator between objects i and j.
