knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal Procrustes Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonal Procrustes reduces to trace maximization; an SVD supplies a global optimizer, with uniqueness exactly when the cross-covariance is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A,B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}\), consider \[\min_{Q\in O(d)}\frac12\|AQ-B\|_F^2.\] Writing \(C=A^{\mathsf T}B\), this is equivalent to maximizing \(\operatorname{tr}(Q^{\mathsf T}C)\). If \(C=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) is a singular-value decomposition, then \(Q_\star=UV^{\mathsf T}\) is a global minimizer and the optimal trace equals \(\sum_{i=1}^d\sigma_i(C)\). The minimizer is unique when \(C\) is nonsingular; if \(C\) is rank deficient, rotations acting within the unmatched null singular subspaces generate additional global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are real matrices of the same size.
\(Q\) ranges over the full orthogonal group \(O(d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_\star=UV^{\mathsf T}\) minimizes the loss, and \(\max_{Q\in O(d)}\operatorname{tr}(Q^{\mathsf T}C)=\sum_i\sigma_i(C)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form global geometry of the one-sided orthogonal Procrustes problem.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical orthogonal Procrustes SVD characterization

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The SVD solution, optimal trace value, and nonsingularity-based uniqueness statement are correct for optimization over the full orthogonal group. The property fits the Procrustes-landscape container, but no inspectable Procrustes source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Geometry Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge-invariant alignment objective descends to the quotient; quotient critical points and curvature correspond to horizontal criticality and horizontal curvature upstairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=O(d)^n\) carry the product Frobenius metric, and let \(O(d)\) act freely on a region of \(M\) by \(R\cdot(Q_1,\ldots,Q_n)=(RQ_1,\ldots,RQ_n)\). If a smooth function \(F:M\to\mathbb{R}\) is invariant under this action, there is a unique smooth \(\bar F:M/O(d)\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(F=\bar F\circ\pi\). A class \([Q]\) is critical for \(\bar F\) exactly when the horizontal component of \(\operatorname{grad}F(Q)\) vanishes. At a critical representative, the Hessian of \(\bar F\) equals the restriction of the Hessian of \(F\) to horizontal directions; vertical gauge directions contribute structural zero modes.
assumptions_latex: The diagonal action is smooth, free, and proper on the region considered.
\(F\) is smooth and invariant under that action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\bar F\circ\pi\), with quotient gradient and Hessian represented by the horizontal gradient and horizontal Hessian of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-point correspondence for gauge-invariant alignment objectives.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Riemannian quotient correspondence for invariant functions

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Under a free proper isometric action, the invariant function descends to the quotient and the stated horizontal gradient and critical-point Hessian correspondence is standard. The claim nevertheless requires a specific quotient-geometry source, particularly for the Hessian and structural-zero-mode assertions.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonality-Constrained Spectral Landscapes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stiefel trace optimization recovers dominant eigenspaces; stationary points are invariant subspaces, and an eigengap makes the optimal subspace unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_d\), and define \[f(X)=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{\mathsf T}AX),\qquad X\in\operatorname{St}(d,r),\quad X^{\mathsf T}X=I_r.\] A point \(X\) is stationary exactly when \(AX=X\Lambda\) for some symmetric \(\Lambda\), equivalently when \(\operatorname{range}(X)\) is an invariant subspace of \(A\). Global minimizers span a dominant \(r\)-dimensional invariant subspace. If \(\lambda_r>\lambda_{r+1}\), that subspace is unique, although its Stiefel representatives remain equivalent under \(X\mapsto XQ\) for \(Q\in O(r)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{grad}f(X)=0\) iff \(AX=X\Lambda\), and global minimizers span the top-\(r\) invariant subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trace optimization on the Stiefel manifold for invariant-subspace recovery.

notation.meaning: Stiefel manifold of orthonormal r-frames in d-space.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The stationary invariant-subspace characterization, dominant-subspace optimum, and eigengap uniqueness statement are mathematically correct and fit the spectral-landscape container. The cited locator concerns spectral decomposition but does not specifically support the Stiefel stationarity and landscape claims; a more targeted section or theorem is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(1\le r\\le n\), and let \(\mathrm{St}(n,r)=\{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}:X^{\mathsf T}X=I_r\}\). The Grassmann manifold \(\mathrm{Gr}(n,r)\) is the quotient of \(\mathrm{St}(n,r)\) by \(X\sim XQ\) for \(Q\in O(r)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth eigenvector and invariant-subspace models on Stiefel or Grassmann manifolds; nonsmooth spectral penalties and general matrix manifolds are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An orthogonality-constrained spectral landscape is a pair \((\mathcal M,F)\) with \(\mathcal M=\mathrm{St}(n,r)\) or \(\mathrm{Gr}(n,r)\), where \(F\in C^2(\mathcal M)\) is induced by spectral data and, in the Grassmann case, is represented by a right-orthogonally invariant lift \(\widetilde F\in C^2(\mathrm{St}(n,r))\) satisfying \(\widetilde F(XQ)=\widetilde F(X)\) for every \(X\in\mathrm{St}(n,r)\) and \(Q\in O(r)\). The canonical linear spectral instance is \(F([X])=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{\mathsf T}AX)\). Its critical set is \(\operatorname{Crit}F=\{[X]:\operatorname{grad}F([X])=0\}\), equivalently the set of \(r\)-dimensional \(A\)-invariant subspaces in the canonical instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonality-constrained spectral landscape is a twice continuously differentiable objective on a Stiefel or Grassmann manifold whose value is determined by spectral data. A Grassmann objective must have a Stiefel lift invariant under every right orthogonal change of basis. The canonical example minimizes the negative trace of the compression of a symmetric matrix, and its critical points represent invariant subspaces.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(1\le r\le n\).
\(F\) is twice continuously differentiable on the selected manifold.
If \(\mathcal M=\mathrm{Gr}(n,r)\), then the lifted objective is constant on every equivalence class \(\{XQ:Q\in O(r)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mathcal M,F)\) is an orthogonality-constrained spectral landscape precisely when it has the stated orthogonality domain, smoothness, spectral dependence, and quotient invariance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A smooth function on \(\mathrm{Gr}(n,r)\) is equivalently a smooth right-\(O(r)\)-invariant function on \(\mathrm{St}(n,r)\).
For \(F([X])=-\operatorname{tr}(X^{\mathsf T}AX)\), stationarity is equivalent to \((I-XX^{\mathsf T})AX=0\), hence to \(\operatorname{range}(X)\) being \(A\)-invariant.
special_cases_latex: For \(r=1\), the model is the Rayleigh-quotient landscape on the sphere with antipodal points identified.
If an eigengap separates the selected eigenvalue cluster, the corresponding optimal invariant subspace is isolated on \(\mathrm{Gr}(n,r)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Right multiplication by \(Q\in O(r)\) cannot create a distinct Grassmann solution.
Criticality and curvature must be interpreted in tangent spaces of the constraint manifold rather than in the ambient Euclidean space.
boundary_notes: Repeated eigenvalues can produce positive-dimensional critical manifolds, so isolated-critical-point conclusions require an eigengap.
The definition does not assert that every critical point is optimal or that a particular algorithm avoids saddles.

children.title: KL–Landscape–Algorithm Bridge
children.top_down_role: Routes connecting global landscape navigation, entry into a local basin, KL convergence, and computational certification.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(S\subseteq\operatorname{crit}f\) be a target critical set, and let an algorithm generate \((x_k)_{k\ge0}\). Write \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\) for the limiting-slope residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal interface joining global navigation, finite entry into a local region, KL convergence there, and a checkable termination certificate; it is not itself a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KL–landscape–algorithm bridge is a tuple \(\mathfrak B=(f,\mathcal A,S,U,V,\mathcal C)\) such that: \(\mathcal A\) generates iterates \(x_k\); every admissible trajectory reaches \(U\) at a finite index \(\tau\) deterministically or with a stated probability; \(U\) is forward invariant and contained in a KL neighborhood \(V\) of \(S\); on \(V\cap\{f>f(S)\}\) there exist \(\eta>0\) and a concave \(C^1\) function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb R_+\), with \(\varphi(0)=0\) and \(\varphi'>0\), satisfying \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(S))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\); and \(\mathcal C(x)\ge0\) is computable with \(\mathcal C(x)=0\) exactly on the certified target class within \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KL–landscape–algorithm bridge is a specified objective, algorithm, target set, entry region, KL neighborhood, and computable certificate. The algorithm must enter the local region in finite time under its declared deterministic or probabilistic regime; the region must be forward invariant and lie inside a neighborhood where a KL inequality holds; and the certificate must vanish exactly on the locally certified target class.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and \(S\subseteq\operatorname{crit}f\) is nonempty.
The algorithmic regime specifies its admissible initializations and, if randomized, its probability space.
The objective value \(f(S)\) is constant on the target component used by the bridge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak B\) is a bridge exactly when its navigation, entry, KL, invariance, and certification clauses hold simultaneously with consistent domains and quantifiers.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The finite-entry clause can be written \(\tau_U=\inf\{k:x_k\in U\}<\infty\) in the deterministic regime or \(\mathbb P(\tau_U<\infty)\ge1-\delta\) in a probabilistic regime.
For \(\varphi(s)=cs^{1-\theta}\), the KL clause is equivalent to \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge c_0|f(x)-f(S)|^{\theta}\) after rescaling constants.
special_cases_latex: If \(U=V\) and \(x_0\in U\), the global-navigation component is vacuous and the bridge reduces to a local KL interface.
For a smooth objective, \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))=\|\nabla f(x)\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A landscape theorem alone does not instantiate the bridge unless a specified algorithm reaches and remains in the certified KL region.
A KL convergence result alone does not certify global optimality unless \(\mathcal C\) identifies the limiting critical class with the desired targets.
boundary_notes: The definition does not claim that such a tuple exists for every nonconvex problem.
Probability levels, oracle accuracy, and stopping tolerances must be included in a concrete instantiation rather than inferred from this interface.

notation.meaning: First iterate index at which the trajectory enters U.

review_flags: The bridge is a synthesis object whose exact six-component definition is not supported by an inspected supplied source; independent sources are needed for its KL and algorithmic-interface clauses.

children.title: Local Analytic Geometry Bridge
children.top_down_role: Connections between KL behavior and familiar local landscape geometries.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(S\subseteq\operatorname{crit}f\) be a locally closed critical set on which \(f\equiv f_*\), and let \(U\) be a neighborhood of \(S\). Define \(d_S(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\) and \(s_f(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-dimensional geometry near one constant-value critical component; each implication must be declared for the stated smooth or nonsmooth model rather than assumed universally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local analytic geometry bridge at \(S\) is a declared collection \(\mathcal R\\subseteq\{\mathrm{Growth}_q,\mathrm{ErrorBound}_p,\mathrm{KL}_\theta,\mathrm{Morse},\mathrm{MorseBott}\}^2\) of valid local implication arrows. The constituent predicates are \(f(x)-f_*\ge c_gd_S(x)^q\), \(d_S(x)\le c_es_f(x)^p\), and \(s_f(x)\ge c_k(f(x)-f_*)^\theta\) for all \(x\in U\) satisfying the predicate's side conditions, together with the usual Hessian nondegeneracy predicate for Morse points or normal nondegeneracy predicate for Morse–Bott critical manifolds. An arrow \((P,Q)\in\mathcal R\) is part of the bridge only when the function class, neighborhood, exponents, constants, and side conditions under which \(P\Rightarrow Q\) are included in the declaration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local analytic geometry bridge is a model-specific registry of valid implications among local growth, subgradient error bounds, KL gradient domination, Morse nondegeneracy, and Morse–Bott normal nondegeneracy. Each registered arrow includes a neighborhood, constants, exponents, and all regularity conditions. Merely naming two local properties does not declare them equivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and lower semicontinuous and is constant with value \(f_*\) on \(S\).
All predicates are restricted to a common sufficiently small neighborhood \(U\) and to points with \(f_*<f(x)<f_*+\eta\) when required.
Any smooth Hessian predicate is used only where \(f\) is at least \(C^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R\) is a local analytic geometry bridge exactly when every stored arrow is a quantified local implication with compatible domains, constants, exponents, and regularity assumptions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The power-form KL predicate is the desingularized inequality with \(\varphi(t)=ct^{1-\theta}\), up to a positive rescaling constant.
When \(S=\{\bar x\}\), the distance gauge reduces to \(d_S(x)=\|x-\bar x\|\).
special_cases_latex: At an isolated nondegenerate \(C^2\) critical point, the intended bridge contains the Morse-to-\(\mathrm{KL}_{1/2}\) route when separately supported.
At a Morse–Bott critical manifold, distance is measured normally to the whole critical manifold rather than to an arbitrarily selected representative.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition prevents transferring an exponent or rate across models unless the corresponding implication arrow has compatible hypotheses.
Different critical components may require different neighborhoods, constants, or exponents.
boundary_notes: Growth, error bounds, metric subregularity, and KL inequalities are not equivalent without additional structural assumptions.
The bridge records local analytic relations; it does not itself specify an iterative method or a global basin-entry mechanism.

notation.meaning: Distance to the selected critical set.
Registry of supported local implication arrows.

review_flags: No inspected source was supplied for the combined growth–error-bound–KL implication registry; exact implication hypotheses and locators require verification.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Morse Rate Correspondence at an Isolated Critical Point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold, let \(f\in C^2(M)\), and let \(\bar x\in M\) satisfy \(\operatorname{grad}f(\bar x)=0\). Distances and norms are Riemannian and are restricted to a normal neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth finite-dimensional behavior near an isolated nondegenerate critical point; the convergence-rate component concerns descent sequences satisfying explicit sufficient-decrease and relative-error conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Morse rate correspondence at \(\bar x\) is the local data package asserting \(\det\operatorname{Hess}f(\bar x)\ne0\) and recording constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) such that \(c_1d(x,\bar x)^2\le |f(x)-f(\bar x)|\le c_2d(x,\bar x)^2\) on the relevant one-sided level sector and \(c_3d(x,\bar x)\le\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|\le c_4d(x,\bar x)\) for \(x\in U\). Its KL component is the exponent-\(1/2\) inequality \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|\ge\kappa|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^{1/2}\). Its rate component assigns local linear convergence to any sequence remaining in \(U\) that satisfies fixed sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Morse rate correspondence is a local package at an isolated critical point with nonsingular Hessian. It records quadratic objective variation, a gradient norm comparable to distance, a KL inequality with exponent one half, and the associated linear regime for descent sequences that remain nearby and satisfy sufficient decrease and relative error conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^2(M)\), \(\operatorname{grad}f(\bar x)=0\), and \(\operatorname{Hess}f(\bar x)\) is invertible.
The objective-gap comparison is restricted to a one-sided sector where \(f(x)\ne f(\bar x)\); at a saddle, an unsigned lower bound cannot hold on every direction without qualification.
The rate assignment applies only to sequences satisfying \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge a\,d(x_{k+1},x_k)^2\) and \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(x_{k+1})\|\le b\,d(x_{k+1},x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The package identifies Morse nondegeneracy with the local exponent-\(1/2\) KL geometry and labels compatible descent trajectories in that neighborhood as belonging to the linear-rate regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Morse nondegeneracy is equivalently \(\ker\operatorname{Hess}f(\bar x)=\{0\}\).
At a strict local minimum, the one-sided quadratic comparison becomes the ordinary quadratic-growth relation \(c_1d(x,\bar x)^2\le f(x)-f(\bar x)\le c_2d(x,\bar x)^2\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\operatorname{Hess}f(\bar x)\succ0\), then \(\bar x\) is an isolated strict local minimizer.
If the Hessian is invertible but indefinite, \(\bar x\) is a Morse saddle; the KL exponent remains local, but minimization convergence to that saddle requires separate consideration.
immediate_consequences_latex: The critical point is isolated in a sufficiently small neighborhood.
The exponent \(1/2\) is tied to nondegenerate quadratic local geometry, not to global convexity.
boundary_notes: Degenerate isolated critical points can have exponents different from \(1/2\).
Linear convergence is not assigned to arbitrary sequences; descent, relative-error, locality, and convergence-to-component conditions remain essential.

notation.meaning: Riemannian Hessian at the critical point.
Riemannian distance to the critical point.

review_flags: A precise inspected source for the Morse-to-KL exponent one-half correspondence and the stated descent-sequence rate interface was not available.
The objective-gap lower comparison requires careful one-sided qualification at indefinite Morse critical points.
knowledge_statements.title: Morse Rate Correspondence at an Isolated Critical Point
Morse Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Morse critical point has an invertible Hessian, an index counting unstable directions, and an isolated local quadratic normal form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite-dimensional smooth Riemannian manifold and \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable. A critical point \(x_\star\) is Morse, or nondegenerate, when \[\operatorname{grad}f(x_\star)=0\qquad\text{and}\qquad \ker\operatorname{Hess}f(x_\star)=\{0\}.\] Its Morse index is the number of negative eigenvalues of the self-adjoint Hessian, counted with multiplicity. By the local Morse normal form, suitable local coordinates split the objective variation into a negative quadratic form on the unstable directions and a positive quadratic form on the stable directions; in particular, \(x_\star\) is isolated among nearby critical points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\star\) is Morse iff \(\operatorname{grad}f(x_\star)=0\) and \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x_\star)\) is invertible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local geometry of an isolated nondegenerate critical point on a smooth manifold.

notation.meaning: Riemannian Hessian acting on the tangent space at the critical point.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical definition and local normal form of a Morse critical point

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition of a Morse critical point, its index, and isolation are appropriate for the leaf. An authoritative Morse-theory locator is required to support the local normal-form assertion under the stated C2 regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Morse KL Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analytic Morse critical points have KL exponent one-half; standard sufficient-decrease and relative-error iterations therefore converge locally at a geometric rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) be real analytic near a Morse critical point \(x_\star\). Then there are \(c>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x_\star\) such that \[|f(x)-f(x_\star)|^{1/2}\le c\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|\qquad(x\in U).\] Hence the local KL exponent is \(1/2\). Moreover, any sequence remaining in \(U\) that satisfies sufficient decrease \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\) and relative error \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(x_{k+1})\|\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\), with \(a,b>0\), converges locally at a geometric rate whenever it converges to \(x_\star\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is real analytic near the Morse critical point \(x_\star\).
The sequence satisfies the displayed sufficient-decrease and relative-error inequalities.
The iterates remain locally and converge to \(x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|f-f(x_\star)|^{1/2}\le c\|\operatorname{grad}f\|\), and the admissible sequence converges geometrically.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL exponent and descent-rate regime near an analytic Morse critical point.

notation.meaning: Positive constants in the descent and relative-error conditions.
Neighborhood on which the local KL inequality holds.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nondegenerate analytic critical points have KL exponent one-half and yield linear abstract-descent rates

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The one-half gradient inequality near an analytic Morse point is standard, but the abstract geometric-rate conclusion needs an authoritative KL convergence theorem with its complete hypotheses. In addition, x_{k+1}-x_k is not intrinsically defined on a general manifold unless a chart, embedding, retraction displacement, or Riemannian distance is specified.

knowledge_statements.title: Nondegeneracy-to-Rate Transfer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite Hessian geometry supplies quadratic growth and a one-half KL exponent, converting standard descent conditions into local geometric convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(x_\star\) is a nondegenerate local minimizer of a twice continuously differentiable function \(f\), so \(
abla f(x_\star)=0\) and \(
abla^2f(x_\star)\succ0\). Continuity yields constants \(m,L>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) in which \(f\) has quadratic growth and \(
abla f\) is locally Lipschitz. If a sequence in \(U\) satisfies \[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2,\qquad \|
abla f(x_{k+1})\|\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|,\] then the induced KL exponent \(1/2\) transfers these inequalities into geometric decay of objective gaps and iterates.
assumptions_latex: The sequence remains local and satisfies the displayed descent conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(C>0\) and \(q\in(0,1)\) such that \(f(x_k)-f(x_\star)\le Cq^k\) and \(\|x_k-x_\star\|\le Cq^{k/2}\), after adjusting \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from invertible local Hessian to geometric convergence under abstract descent conditions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard KL abstract-descent transfer under nondegenerate local minimality

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Positive-definite Hessian geometry does yield local quadratic growth and a one-half gradient/KL inequality. The claimed objective and iterate rates require a cited abstract-descent result and a precise local-entry or convergence hypothesis ensuring that the sequence is in the applicable basin.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Morse–Bott Rate Correspondence near a Critical Manifold
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold, \(f
e C^2(M)\), and \(C\subseteq M\) a connected embedded submanifold contained in \(\operatorname{crit}f\). Let \(N_xC=(T_xC)^\perp\) and \(d_C(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth behavior around one constant-value Morse–Bott critical manifold; rates concern normal approach to the manifold and do not select a unique point along its tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Morse–Bott rate correspondence along \(C\) is the local data package satisfying \(T_xC=\ker\operatorname{Hess}f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\) and nonsingularity of \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x)|_{N_xC}\). It records a tubular neighborhood \(U\), constants \(c_i>0\), and the comparisons \(c_1d_C(y)^2\le |f(y)-f(C)|\le c_2d_C(y)^2\) on the relevant one-sided sector and \(c_3d_C(y)\le\|\operatorname{grad}f(y)\|\le c_4d_C(y)\). Its KL component is \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(y)\|\ge\kappa|f(y)-f(C)|^{1/2}\), and its rate component assigns local linear decay of objective residual and normal distance to compatible descent sequences remaining in \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Morse–Bott rate correspondence is a package for a smooth critical manifold whose Hessian kernel is exactly the tangent space and whose Hessian is nondegenerate in normal directions. It records quadratic variation and linear gradient growth in distance to the manifold, a KL exponent of one half, and a linear local regime for compatible descent sequences in normal distance and objective residual.

For every \(x\in C\), \(T_xC=\ker\operatorname{Hess}f(x)\), and the Hessian restricted to \(N_xC\) is nonsingular.
The rate assignment is restricted to sequences satisfying sufficient decrease and relative error and remaining inside one common tubular neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The package identifies normal Morse–Bott nondegeneracy with exponent-\(1/2\) KL geometry and the corresponding local linear regime for objective residual and distance to \(C\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The kernel condition is equivalent to Hessian degeneracy occurring only along tangent directions of the critical manifold.
When \(C=\{\bar x\}\), the definition reduces to the isolated Morse rate correspondence.
special_cases_latex: If the normal Hessian is positive definite, \(C\) is a local manifold of minima.
Symmetry-generated solution orbits can form Morse–Bott critical manifolds when all zero-curvature directions are exactly the orbit tangents.

The exponent reflects quadratic normal geometry even though the critical set is not isolated.
boundary_notes: Additional zero Hessian directions transverse to \(C\) violate the Morse–Bott condition.
An indefinite normal Hessian describes a critical manifold containing saddle geometry, so attraction by a minimization method is not automatic.

knowledge_statements.title: Morse–Bott Rate Correspondence near a Critical Manifold
Morse-Bott Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Morse-Bott geometry permits a manifold of critical points but requires the Hessian to be nondegenerate in every direction normal to that manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite-dimensional smooth Riemannian manifold and \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable. The function is Morse-Bott along a connected critical submanifold \(C\subset M\) when every \(x\in C\) satisfies \(\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0\) and \[\ker\operatorname{Hess}f(x)=T_xC.\] Equivalently, the Hessian is nondegenerate on the normal space \(N_xC=(T_xC)^\perp\). The objective is constant on \(C\), has zero second-order variation along tangent directions, and has a nondegenerate quadratic normal form transversely to \(C\). Thus nearby non-isolation arises exactly from the critical manifold rather than additional flat normal directions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset M\) is an embedded connected critical submanifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is Morse-Bott along \(C\) iff \(\ker\operatorname{Hess}f(x)=T_xC\) for every \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegeneracy transverse to a smooth critical manifold.

notation.meaning: Tangent space of the critical manifold at x.
Normal space to the critical manifold at x.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The kernel-equals-tangent-space condition is the correct Morse-Bott definition and fits the geometry leaf. A specific source is required for the equivalence with normal nondegeneracy and for the transverse quadratic normal form under the stated regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Morse-Bott KL Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analytic Morse-Bott critical manifolds retain KL exponent one-half; suitable descent sequences converge to one manifold point with geometric objective and normal-distance decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) be real analytic and Morse-Bott along a compact connected critical submanifold \(C\). For every \(x_\star\in C\), there are \(c>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x_\star\) such that \[|f(x)-f(x_\star)|^{1/2}\le c\|\operatorname{grad}f(x)\|\qquad(x\in U).\] Thus the local KL exponent is \(1/2\), despite tangential zero modes. A bounded descent sequence satisfying sufficient decrease and relative error, remaining in \(U\), has finite length and converges to a single point of \(C\); its objective residual and distance to \(C\) decay geometrically once the sequence enters the local regime.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is real analytic and Morse-Bott along the compact connected submanifold \(C\).
The bounded sequence satisfies sufficient decrease and relative error.
The iterates eventually remain in the stated neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KL exponent is \(1/2\), and admissible local descent sequences have geometric objective-gap and \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,C)\) decay.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL exponent and normal convergence rate near an analytic Morse-Bott critical manifold.

notation.meaning: Riemannian distance from x to C.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: analytic Morse-Bott geometry yields KL exponent one-half through transverse quadratic normal form

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The local one-half KL exponent for analytic Morse-Bott geometry is plausible, but the sequence theorem is not reviewable as written: sufficient decrease and relative error are neither displayed nor parameterized, and the hypotheses ensuring convergence to a single point and geometric normal-distance decay are incomplete. A precise authoritative Morse-Bott/KL rate theorem is required.

Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be \(C^2\) near \( ar x\), and suppose its local critical set is a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\) on which \(f= ar f\). Assume \(\ker

The normal restriction of \(\nabla^2f(\bar x)\) is positive definite.

children.title: Local Regularity Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Model-dependent equivalence and implication routes among neighboring local regularity languages.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(S\subseteq
amespace{crit}f\) be locally closed with \(f|_S=f_*\), and fix a model class \(\mathscr F\), a neighborhood \(U\), and a selected subdifferential \(\partial f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A model-dependent correspondence among neighboring regularity languages; no implication is universal outside its declared function class and side conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local regularity correspondence for \((f,S)\) is a directed labeled graph \(\mathfrak R=(\mathcal P,\mathcal E)\). Its vertices are quantified predicates such as \(q\)-growth \(f(x)-f_*\ge c_gd_S(x)^q\), slope error bound \(d_S(x)\le c_e\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))^p\), metric subregularity of \(\partial f\) relative to \(S\), and KL domination \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge c_k(f(x)-f_*)^\theta\). An edge \(P\xrightarrow{H}Q\) belongs to \(\mathcal E\) only when the auxiliary hypothesis list \(H\), common neighborhood, level-set restriction, exponent transformation, and constants making \(P\Rightarrow Q\) valid for \(f\in\mathscr F\) are part of the edge data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local regularity correspondence is a directed graph whose vertices are fully quantified local properties—growth, error bounds, metric subregularity, or KL domination—and whose edges are valid implications labeled by every additional hypothesis. The graph is relative to a function class, critical set, neighborhood, and chosen subdifferential. Unlabeled equivalence among these properties is not part of the definition.
assumptions_latex:
\(S\subseteq
ame{crit}f\) is locally closed and \(f\equiv f_*\) on the selected component.
Every predicate specifies whether it applies to all nearby points or only to a one-sided level sector \(f_*<f(x)<f_*+\eta\).
Every edge records structural conditions such as convexity, prox-regularity, definability, smoothness, or subdifferential continuity whenever required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak R\) is a valid local regularity correspondence exactly when each edge is a supported implication with explicit hypotheses and no undeclared reversal.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A two-way correspondence between predicates \(P\) and \(Q\) is represented by two separately supported edges \(P\to Q\) and \(Q\to P\), not by one undirected label.
Metric subregularity may be written as a local distance estimate \(d_S(x)\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\) when \(S=(\partial f)^{-1}(0)\) locally.
special_cases_latex: For a smooth strongly convex local model, quadratic growth, a linear gradient error bound, and exponent-\(1/2\) gradient domination can occupy one mutually connected component.
For nonsmooth nonconvex models, only those arrows justified by the selected regularity theory are retained.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing the subdifferential or target component can change the graph.
Exponent transformations are edge data and cannot be inferred solely from property names.
boundary_notes: The definition deliberately distinguishes implication from equivalence.
Global error bounds and global KL inequalities are outside this local correspondence unless separately declared.

notation.meaning: Directed graph of local regularity predicates and supported implications.
Auxiliary hypotheses labeling an implication edge.
Function class on which the correspondence is asserted.

review_flags: The exact model-dependent implication graph lacks an inspected supporting source.
Exponent relations and reversibility must be checked separately for each chosen function class.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Relative Local Regularity Correspondence
Error-Bound Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local gradient error bound is metric subregularity of the gradient mapping; replacing the gradient norm by a locally equivalent residual preserves the property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, let \(S=(
abla f)^{-1}(0)\), and let \( ar x\in S\). The local gradient error bound at \( ar x\) is the existence of \(\kappa,\delta>0\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa\|
abla f(x)\|\) whenever \(\|x- ar x\|<\delta\). This is precisely metric subregularity of the mapping \(
abla f\) at \(( ar x,0)\). If a residual \(r\) satisfies \(c_1\|
abla f(x)\|\le r(x)\le c_2\|
abla f(x)\|\) locally, then the same error-bound property holds with \(r\), with constants changed by the comparison factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa\|\nabla f(x)\|\) is equivalent to metric subregularity of \(\nabla f\) at \((\bar x,0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies a local gradient error bound with metric subregularity relative to the critical set.

notation.meaning: A residual locally equivalent to the gradient norm.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the relations leaf, and the displayed error bound agrees formally with metric subregularity of the single-valued gradient mapping at (bar x,0). No evidence is supplied for the adopted metric-subregularity convention or the residual-equivalence extension.

knowledge_statements.title: Growth Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth lower-bounds the objective gap by squared distance to minimizers; Lipschitz gradient supplies the matching local upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a nonempty local minimizer set of a differentiable function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), with common value \(f_*\). Quadratic growth with modulus \(\mu>0\) means \(f(x)-f_*\ge(\mu/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\) locally. If \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and every nearest point \(x_*\in S\) is stationary, the descent lemma also gives \(f(x)-f_*\le(L/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\). Hence the objective gap and squared distance are locally equivalent whenever quadratic growth and gradient Lipschitz continuity hold together.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a local minimizer set with value \(f_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mu/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\le f(x)-f_*\le(L/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\) locally.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates quadratic growth to distance from the local minimizer set.

notation.meaning: Common objective value on the minimizer set.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the growth-relations leaf. The lower growth bound and Lipschitz-gradient upper bound are standard, but the local set and neighborhood must ensure existence of a nearest stationary point and containment of the relevant segment in the Lipschitz-gradient region. No authoritative source is supplied for this precise local formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: PL Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The PL inequality is exactly the differentiable KL gradient inequality with exponent one-half, although it neither requires convexity nor forces a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable on a neighborhood \(U\), and let \(f_*\) be the relevant minimum value. The Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality with constant \(\mu>0\), \((1/2)\|\nabla f(x)\|^2\ge\mu(f(x)-f_*)\), is equivalent on \(U\cap\{f>f_*\}\) to \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge\sqrt{2\mu}\,(f(x)-f_*)^{1/2}\). Thus PL is the differentiable power-form KL inequality with exponent \(1/2\). It does not by itself assert convexity or uniqueness of minimizers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses the Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality as the KL inequality with exponent one-half.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the PL-relations leaf, and the two displayed inequalities are algebraically equivalent. A source is still required to support identifying this power gradient inequality with the chosen KL exponent convention and to document the stated nonconvex interpretation.

knowledge_statements.title: KL Relations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A power-form subgradient inequality with exponent theta is equivalent to the KL formulation using the corresponding power desingularizing function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\), and set \(\bar f=f(\bar x)\). For \(\theta\in[0,1)\), the power-form inequality \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge c(f(x)-\bar f)^\theta\) on \(0<f(x)-\bar f<\eta\) is equivalent to the KL inequality \(\varphi'(f(x)-\bar f)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\) with \(\varphi(s)=s^{1-\theta}/(c(1-\theta))\). The relation is local and applies only on the specified objective-value slice.
assumptions_latex: The inequalities are restricted to \(0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge c(f(x)-\bar f)^\theta\iff\varphi'(f(x)-\bar f)\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates the power-form KL inequality to its desingularizing-function formulation.

notation.meaning: KL exponent in the power convention.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the KL-relations leaf, and differentiating the stated desingularizing function gives the claimed power inequality. The record identifies the limiting subdifferential but supplies no source for that convention; it also omits the usual spatial-neighborhood restriction from the KL property, stating only an objective-value slice.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Condition Implication Routes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex differentiable objectives, quadratic growth implies a gradient error bound, which implies PL; PL is then KL with exponent one-half.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable near a nonempty minimizer set \(S\), with minimum value \(f_*\). If quadratic growth \(f(x)-f_*\ge(\alpha/2)\operatorname{dist}(x,S)^2\) holds locally, convexity yields \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le(2/\alpha)\|
abla f(x)\|\). More generally, any error bound \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa\|
abla f(x)\|\), combined with convexity, yields \(f(x)-f_*\le\kappa\|
abla f(x)\|^2\), hence PL with constant \(1/(2\kappa)\). PL then gives the KL inequality with exponent \(1/2\).
assumptions_latex: All stated inequalities hold on one common neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{quadratic growth}\Rightarrow\text{gradient error bound}\Rightarrow\text{PL}\Rightarrow\text{KL exponent }1/2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a safe convex implication route among growth, error-bound, PL, and KL conditions.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role is appropriate for an implication-route leaf, and the constants follow formally from the convex first-order inequality. The meaning of convexity only 'near' S and of a minimizer set that is 'nonempty locally' is not precise enough to ensure the required projection segments and convex inequalities share one domain. A source is needed for the exact local theorem and normalizations.

children.title: Saddle Navigation Method Family
children.top_down_role: Method families distinguished by how they avoid, detect, or leave saddle geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f
e C^2(\mathbb R^n)\), let \(g(x)=\nabla f(x)\), \(H(x)=\nabla^2f(x)\), and define the strict-saddle region \(\mathcal S_{\epsilon,\gamma}=\{x:\|g(x)\|\le\epsilon,\lambda_{\min}(H(x))\le-\gamma\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A saddle navigation method family is a collection \(\mathfrak A\) of deterministic maps or Markov transition kernels \(K_f\) equipped with a mechanism label in \(\{\mathrm{generic\ avoidance},\mathrm{perturbation},\mathrm{negative	ext{-}curvature},\mathrm{curvature	ext{-}model},\mathrm{stochastic	ext{-}excitation}\}\). Each member specifies tolerances \((\epsilon,\gamma)\), an escape neighborhood \(U_x\) for every \(x

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A saddle navigation method family is a collection of deterministic or randomized update rules labeled by how they avoid, detect, or leave strict-saddle geometry. Strict saddles are identified through simultaneous small gradient and a Hessian eigenvalue at most \(-\gamma\).
Every randomized member specifies its filtration, initialization law, and probability level; every deterministic member specifies the measure used for genericity.

otin U\}\) and a lower bound on \(\mathbb P(\tau_U
e T)\).

children.title: Generic First-Order Saddle Avoidance
children.top_down_role: Stable-manifold and initialization-based avoidance of strict saddles.

knowledge_statements.title: Generic First-Order Saddle Avoidance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a sufficiently small fixed step, gradient descent converges to any isolated strict saddle only from a measure-zero set, so continuous random initialization avoids countably many such saddles almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(C^2\) with globally \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and choose \(0<\alpha<1/L\). For gradient descent \(x_{k+1}=g(x_k)=x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_k)\), the map \(g\) is a \(C^1\) diffeomorphism. If \(x^s\) is an isolated critical point with \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x^s))<0\), its basin of attraction under \(g\) has Lebesgue measure zero. Therefore an initialization having a density with respect to Lebesgue measure converges to \(x^s\) with probability zero. The same conclusion holds for a countable collection of such strict saddles.
assumptions_latex: The strict saddles under consideration are isolated and at most countable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}(x_k\to x^s)=0\) for every strict saddle \(x^s\) under an absolutely continuous initialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbed First-Order Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the gradient is small, randomly perturb the iterate and test whether a fixed block of gradient steps achieves enough decrease; otherwise return a candidate second-order stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\), step size \(\eta>0\), perturbation radius \(r>0\), gradient threshold \(g_{\mathrm{th}}>0\), horizon \(T\), and decrease threshold \(F_{\mathrm{th}}>0\), perform gradient steps \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta\nabla f(x_k)\). If the resulting point \(y\) satisfies \(f(x_k)-f(y)>F_{\mathrm{th}}\), continue from \(y\); otherwise output \(x_k\) as a candidate approximate second-order stationary point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and its gradient can be evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a post-perturbation iterate achieving decrease greater than \(F_{\mathrm{th}}\) or a candidate approximate second-order stationary point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-based globalization methods—principally trust-region and regularized models—that intrinsically exploit negative curvature through approximate model minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A curvature-model escape family is a collection of algorithms that compute \(s_k\) by approximate minimization of \(m_k\) over a declared model domain \(D_k\), accept or reject the trial point using an actual-to-predicted reduction rule, and satisfy the curvature-exploitation condition: if \(\lambda_{\min}(B_k)<-\epsilon_H\), then \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\ge c_c\Psi(-\lambda_{\min}(B_k),D_k)>0\) for a specified scale function \(\Psi\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curvature-model escape family consists of globalized model-based methods whose approximate subproblem solutions guarantee positive predicted reduction when the model Hessian has sufficiently negative curvature. Each member states its model domain, regularization term, approximation accuracy, actual-to-predicted reduction test, and curvature-dependent decrease scale.

Trust-Region Saddle Escape
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a strict saddle, the trust-region boundary along a most-negative eigenvector guarantees quadratic model decrease proportional to curvature magnitude and the squared radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(s)=f(x)+g^\top s+(1/2)s^\top Hs\) and suppose \(g=0\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(H)=-\gamma<0\). For any trust-region radius \(\Delta>0\), let \(v\) be a unit eigenvector satisfying \(Hv=-\gamma v\). Both \(s=\Delta v\) and \(s=-\Delta v\) are feasible for \(\|s\|\le\Delta\), and each gives \(m(0)-m(s)=\gamma\Delta^2/2\). Hence a global minimizer of the trust-region subproblem achieves model decrease at least \(\gamma\Delta^2/2\), so a strict saddle cannot solve the local quadratic model at the zero step.
assumptions_latex: The trust-region subproblem is minimized over \(\|s\|\le\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(0)-\min_{\|s\|\le\Delta}m(s)\ge\gamma\Delta^2/2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cubic-Regularization Saddle Escape
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cubic regularization automatically selects a finite negative-curvature step whose guaranteed model decrease scales as the curvature magnitude cubed divided by the regularization squared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_\sigma(s)=f(x)+g^\top s+(1/2)s^\top Hs+(\sigma/6)\|s\|^3\), where \(\sigma>0\). Suppose \(g=0\) and \(Hv=-\gamma v\) for a unit vector \(v\) and \(\gamma>0\). Along \(s=tv\), the model change is \(-\gamma t^2/2+\sigma|t|^3/6\). Choosing \(|t|=2\gamma/\sigma\) gives \(m_\sigma(0)-m_\sigma(s)=2\gamma^3/(3\sigma^2)\). Therefore a global minimizer of the cubic model achieves at least this decrease and cannot remain at a strict saddle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_\sigma(0)-\min_s m_\sigma(s)\ge2\gamma^3/(3\sigma^2)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Model Comparison
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust regions cap a negative-curvature step by a radius, while cubic regularization chooses its scale from curvature and penalty; equal step lengths still produce different model decreases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a stationary model point with \(Hv=-\gamma v\), \(\|v\|=1\), and \(\gamma>0\), the trust-region model minimizes the negative quadratic along this direction at the imposed boundary \(|t|=\Delta\), giving decrease \(\gamma\Delta^2/2\). The cubic model with term \((\sigma/6)\|s\|^3\) instead selects the intrinsic scale \(|t|=2\gamma/\sigma\), giving decrease \(2\gamma^3/(3\sigma^2)\). Thus the trust-region radius externally caps the escape step, whereas cubic regularization controls it through a curvature-dependent penalty; setting \(\Delta=2\gamma/\sigma\) equalizes their step lengths but not their predicted decreases.

The cubic term is normalized as \((\sigma/6)\|s\|^3\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{\mathrm{TR}}=\gamma\Delta^2/2\) and \(D_{\mathrm{CR}}=2\gamma^3/(3\sigma^2)\), with respective step scales \(\Delta\) and \(2\gamma/\sigma\).

notation.meaning: Trust-region model decrease along negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic-Noise Saddle Escape
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditionally continuous perturbations almost surely move an iterate off a strict saddle's measure-zero stable manifold, although they do not by themselves provide an exit-time bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(C^2\), let \(x^\star\) be a strict saddle, and suppose the local stable set \(W^s(x^\star)\) of the gradient map \(G(x)=x-\eta\nabla f(x)\) has Lebesgue measure zero. For the perturbed update \(x_{k+1}=G(x_k)+\sigma\xi_k\), where \(\sigma>0\) and each \(\xi_k\) has a density conditional on the past, \[\mathbb{P}\!\left(x_{k+1}\in W^s(x^\star)\mid x_0,\ldots,x_k\right)=0.\] Consequently, additive nondegenerate noise prevents iterates from remaining on the deterministic stable manifold of the saddle almost surely; this property alone does not certify monotone descent or a quantitative exit time.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n)\) and \(x^\star\) is a strict saddle
\(\sigma>0\) and the conditional law of \(\xi_k\) is absolutely continuous
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}(x_{k+1}\in W^s(x^\star)\mid x_0,\ldots,x_k)=0\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure departure from a strict saddle's stable manifold under nondegenerate additive perturbations.

A global benign-landscape method may use the same update rule for \(\mathcal G\) and \(R\), with the basin marking only the point at which local analysis becomes applicable.
immediate_consequences_latex: A local convergence theorem cannot serve as an entry guarantee unless the initialization is already certified to lie in \(U\).
Entry probability and conditional refinement probability must be combined explicitly in a complete end-to-end guarantee.
boundary_notes: Temporary visits to \(U\) are insufficient unless the handoff or forward-invariance condition is satisfied.
The definition does not require the basin to equal the full attraction region.

children.title: Initialization-Refinement Interface
children.top_down_role: Problem-informed initialization followed by locally convergent refinement.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Y\) be a data space, \(X\) a parameter space, \(S(y)\subseteq X\) a target set, and \(U(y)\subseteq X\) a local convergence basin. Let \(\mathcal I:Y\times\Omega	o X\) be an initializer and \(R_y:X	o X\) a refinement map.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage, problem-informed initialization followed by local deterministic or stochastic refinement; the interface explicitly separates entry reliability from local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An initialization–refinement interface is a tuple \((\mathcal I,R,U,S,p,\rho,\varepsilon)\) satisfying \(\mathbb P_\omega(\mathcal I(y,\omega)
e U(y))\ge p\) for every admissible datum \(y\), \(R_y(U(y))\subseteq U(y)\), and \(d_{S(y)}(R_y^k(x))\le\varepsilon(k,d_{S(y)}(x))\) for every \(x
e U(y)\), where \(\varepsilon(k,t)	o0\) as \(k	o\infty\). In a linear refinement regime one may take \(\varepsilon(k,t)=C\rho^kt\) with \(0<\rho<1\). The initializer's output representation and the refinement map's input representation must agree, including any quotient, scaling, or permutation convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An initialization–refinement interface consists of a data-dependent initializer, a local basin, a target set, and a refinement map. The initializer enters the basin with a stated probability uniformly over admissible data, the basin is invariant under refinement, and a declared error envelope tends to zero. The handoff must use compatible representations and symmetries.
assumptions_latex: The initializer is measurable in its random input, and \(U(y)\) and \(S(y)\) are defined for every admissible datum.
The distance \(d_{S(y)}\) respects any equivalence relation used to identify solutions.
The refinement map is well-defined on all initializer outputs counted as successful.
Any data-dependent probability or rate constants are quantified uniformly or their dependence is stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tuple is a valid initialization–refinement interface exactly when it supplies a probabilistic basin-entry guarantee, an invariant handoff, and a vanishing local error envelope.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A deterministic initializer corresponds to \(\Omega\) being a singleton and \(p=1\) on its certified data class.
A contraction formulation \(d_S(R_y(x))\le\rho d_S(x)\) on \(U(y)\) yields the linear error envelope used by the interface.
special_cases_latex: Spectral initialization followed by manifold optimization is an instance when the spectral estimate is certified to enter the manifold method's basin.
A convex relaxation followed by rounding and local refinement requires the rounded point—not merely the relaxed solution—to lie in \(U(y)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The end-to-end success probability cannot exceed the initializer's basin-entry probability unless refinement has an additional recovery mechanism outside \(U(y)\).
Representation mismatch can invalidate an otherwise correct local convergence statement.
boundary_notes: The definition does not claim that the initializer is computationally cheaper than refinement.
Initialization-free navigation is excluded because this interface requires a distinct problem-informed entry map.
review_flags: No inspected source supports this abstract initializer–basin–refinement interface or its uniform quantifiers.
knowledge_statements.title: Initialization–Refinement Interface
Problem-Informed Initialization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A problem-informed initializer maps structured problem data to a starting point and supplies a checkable certificate that the point lies in a local refinement basin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an optimization problem \(\min_{x\in X} f(x)\), a problem-informed initializer is a map \(I:\mathcal D\to X\) from admissible problem data \(d\in\mathcal D\) to \(x_0=I(d)\), together with a verifiable certificate \(C(d,x_0)\). Relative to a target solution set \(X^\star\) and a local-refinement basin \(B\subseteq X\), the initializer is basin-valid on \(\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D\) when \[d\in\mathcal D_0\ \text{and}\ C(d,I(d))\quad\Longrightarrow\quad I(d)\in B.\] The construction may exploit structure in \(d\), but basin validity depends on the displayed implication rather than on the heuristic origin of \(I\).
assumptions_latex: \(I:\mathcal D\to X\) is defined on admissible data
\(B\subseteq X\) is a specified basin for a refinement method
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(d,I(d))\Rightarrow I(d)\in B\) for every \(d\in\mathcal D_0\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization certified by model-specific information to lie in a prescribed refinement region.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the initialization leaf and is internally coherent, but the certificate-based notion is a synthetic interface definition with no cited source or standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Refinement
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting inside an invariant basin, repeatedly accept sufficiently decreasing steps with controlled stationarity residual, stopping when that residual reaches the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in B\), generate \(x_{k+1}=R(x_k)\) while the stopping test fails, where \(R(B)\subseteq B\). Require constants \(a,b>0\) such that every accepted step satisfies \[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge a\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_{k+1}))\le b\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert.\] Stop when \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_k))\le\varepsilon\), and output \(x_k\). If \(f\) has the KL property on \(B\), is bounded below there, and the generated sequence is bounded, these conditions form the standard interface for convergence to a critical point and subsequent KL rate analysis.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, bounded below on \(B\), and KL on \(B\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\) is returned once \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_k))\le\varepsilon\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent refinement governed by sufficient decrease and a relative-error condition inside a certified basin.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is suitable for Local Refinement, but the cited constrained-optimization section does not inspectably support the stated nonsmooth KL framework, limiting-subdifferential relative-error condition, or convergence interface. A direct KL convergence source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Basin-Entry Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basin-entry predicate is a checkable threshold whose satisfaction guarantees invariance under local refinement and convergence toward the target solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:X\to X\) be a local-refinement map, let \(X^\star\subseteq X\) be its target solution set, and let \(V:X\to[0,\infty]\) be a certificate function. A basin-entry interface is the predicate \[E(x):=\bigl[V(x)\le\rho\bigr],\] with \(\rho>0\), satisfying \[E(x)\Longrightarrow x\in B,\qquad R(B)\subseteq B,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(R^k(x),X^\star)\to0.\] A navigation method may hand an iterate \(x_\tau\) to the local solver only after verifying \(E(x_\tau)\); thus the interface separates probabilistic or global entry guarantees from deterministic post-entry convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(x)\Rightarrow x\in B\), \(R(B)\subseteq B\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(R^k(x),X^\star)\to0\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate connecting a global navigation phase to a certified local-refinement phase.

notation.meaning: Invariant basin of the local method.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the basin-entry interface. However, the threshold predicate and its combined invariance and convergence requirements constitute a synthetic interface with no source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Initialization-Free Landscape Navigation
children.top_down_role: Global navigation based on certified benign landscape regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Initialization-Free Landscape Navigation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every second-order stationary point is globally optimal, an arbitrary-start method converging to such points achieves global recovery without a special initializer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be bounded below, and suppose every second-order stationary point is globally minimizing. Consider an algorithm that may start from any \(x_0\) in a prescribed sublevel set and whose accumulation points almost surely satisfy \(\nabla f(x)=0\) and \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq0\). If its iterates are almost surely bounded and their objective values converge, then every accumulation point is a global minimizer almost surely. If, additionally, the whole sequence has a unique accumulation point—for example through an applicable KL convergence theorem—then the iterates converge almost surely to a global minimizer without a basin-specific initialization.
assumptions_latex: Every second-order stationary point of \(f\) is globally minimizing
The arbitrary-start algorithm is almost surely bounded and has only second-order stationary accumulation points
The objective values converge almost surely
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}(\text{every accumulation point is globally minimizing})=1\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global recovery from arbitrary starts by combining second-order stationarity with benign landscape geometry.

notation.meaning: Arbitrary initial point in the prescribed sublevel set.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits the initialization-free navigation container, and the accumulation-point implication is logically plausible under the stated assumptions. No source supports the benign-landscape premise, almost-sure stationarity interface, or KL-based whole-sequence qualification.

children.title: Deformation Path Family
children.top_down_role: Progressive deformation toward a difficult nonconvex landscape.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional space or manifold and let \(F:X\times[0,1]	o\mathbb R\) define objectives \(f_t(x)=F(x,t)\). The initial problem \(f_0\) is tractable and \(f_1\) is the target nonconvex objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuation or homotopy routes that track a selected critical or minimizing branch through progressively deformed objectives and use local correction at each stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A deformation path is a tuple \((F,z,U,\Pi,\mathcal T)\), where \(z:[0,1]	o X\) is a continuous selected solution branch satisfying \(\operatorname{grad}f_t(z(t))=0\), \(U_t\) is a local basin containing \(z(t)\), and \(\Pi_{s	o t}:U_s	o X\) is a predictor between parameters. For a grid \(\mathcal T=\{0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=1\}\), the path is admissible when the predictor-corrector handoff satisfies \(\Pi_{t_j	o t_{j+1}}(x_j)
e U_{t_{j+1}}\) for every certified \(x_j
e U_{t_j}\), and the corrector for \(f_{t_{j+1}}\) remains in \(U_{t_{j+1}}\) and converges to the selected component containing \(z(t_{j+1})\). A deformation path family collects such tuples with explicit regularity, branch-selection, and grid conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deformation path family progressively changes a tractable objective into the target objective while tracking a selected stationary or minimizing branch. Each member specifies the objective homotopy, branch, local basins, predictor, correction method, and parameter grid. Every predictor must place the current approximation inside the next correction basin, and every corrector must remain there and converge to the selected component.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is sufficiently smooth in \(x\) and continuous in \(t\) for the selected branch and local correctors to be defined.
The branch \(z(t)\) exists on the full interval and the intended component is specified at bifurcations or symmetry changes.
The initial state lies in \(U_0\), typically because the \(t=0\) problem is solved directly.
Grid spacing is chosen so that every predictor satisfies the next-basin handoff condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tuple is an admissible deformation path exactly when the selected branch exists from \(0\) to \(1\) and all finite predictor-corrector handoffs preserve basin membership through the target problem.
equivalent_formulations_latex:
With the identity predictor, the handoff condition becomes \(x_j
e U_{t_{j+1}}\), requiring consecutive basins to overlap along the tracked branch.
A differential predictor may use a branch tangent \(\dot z(t)\) when that tangent is well-defined.
special_cases_latex: Regularization continuation varies a penalty parameter while warm-starting each subproblem.
Smoothing continuation begins with a smooth surrogate and decreases the smoothing parameter toward the target model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Local convergence at each fixed parameter does not guarantee successful continuation unless the inter-stage basin condition holds.
A singularity or unhandled bifurcation can terminate the selected path before the target parameter.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that every stationary branch ends at a global minimizer of \(f_1\).
Infinite or adaptive parameter sequences require an additional limiting formulation beyond the finite-grid interface stated here.

notation.meaning: Predictor mapping between neighboring parameter values.

review_flags: No inspected continuation or homotopy source supports the exact predictor–basin–corrector interface and full-branch assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Deformation Path Family
Continuation Routes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuation alternates tangent prediction and local correction while changing a parameter, reducing the parameter step whenever correction or residual tests fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable and suppose \(F(x_0,t_0)=0\). Choose a mesh \(0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=1\). At stage \(j\), compute the tangent \(v_j\) from \[D_xF(x_j,t_j)v_j+D_tF(x_j,t_j)=0,\] predict \(\widehat x_{j+1}=x_j+(t_{j+1}-t_j)v_j\), and apply a local corrector to solve \(F(x,t_{j+1})=0\) from \(\widehat x_{j+1}\). Accept \(x_{j+1}\) only when the residual and corrector tests pass; otherwise reduce the step. Output \(x_N\) when \(t_N=1\). Regular tracking requires \(D_xF\) to remain nonsingular along the followed branch.
assumptions_latex: \(D_xF\) is nonsingular along the tracked branch
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_N,1)=0\) up to the prescribed correction tolerance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictor-corrector tracking of a regular stationary branch as a parameter changes incrementally.

notation.meaning: Branch tangent used by the predictor.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Continuation Routes. A source is required because nonsingularity along a branch alone does not document the step-control and corrector conditions needed for successful tracking to t=1, and no predictor-corrector locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Homotopy Routes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homotopy continuously deforms a solved equation into the target equation; a regular solution route follows zeros of the deformation across the parameter interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an easily solved equation \(F_0(x)=0\) and a target equation \(F_1(x)=0\), a homotopy route is a continuous map \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \[H(x,0)=F_0(x),\qquad H(x,1)=F_1(x).\] A solution route is a continuous curve \(x:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \(H(x(t),t)=0\) for all \(t\). If \(H\) is continuously differentiable and \(D_xH(x(t),t)\) is nonsingular along the curve, then the route is locally unique and is eligible for regular continuation from the known solution \(x(0)\) to the target solution \(x(1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deformation from an easily solved problem to the target problem through a parameterized equation family.

notation.meaning: Homotopy connecting the easy and target equations.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits Homotopy Routes, and the endpoint and regular-branch statements are mathematically coherent when the asserted solution curve exists. No authoritative source or locator supports the definition and implicit-function continuation qualification.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Tracking Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the fold equation x²=t, the branch derivative diverges at zero and the Jacobian becomes singular, defeating regular parameter continuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the scalar homotopy \(H(x,t)=x^2-t\) for \(t\in[0,1]\). Its real solution branches are \(x_\pm(t)=\pm\sqrt t\) for \(t>0\), while \(D_xH(x,t)=2x\). Along either branch, \[\left|\frac{dx_\pm}{dt}\right|=\frac{1}{2\sqrt t}\longrightarrow\infty\quad\text{as}\quad t\downarrow0,\] and \(D_xH(0,0)=0\). Thus parameterizing the route by \(t\) loses regularity at the fold: the tangent predictor becomes unbounded and the implicit-function continuation guarantee fails. Step reduction alone cannot restore a uniformly conditioned \(t\)-parameterization; reparameterization, such as pseudo-arclength continuation, is required to cross the boundary robustly.
assumptions_latex: The branch is parameterized directly by \(t\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_xH(0,0)=0\) and \(\lvert dx_\pm/dt\rvert\to\infty\) as \(t\downarrow0\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of regularity at a fold makes parameter continuation singular and arbitrarily ill-conditioned.

notation.meaning: The two real solution branches of the fold homotopy.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role exactly fits the leaf, and the fold calculation is internally correct. A source is still required for the stronger methodological claim concerning uniformly conditioned parameter tracking and pseudo-arclength reparameterization.

children.title: Computational Certificate Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Certificate families connecting landscape geometry to computational guarantees; quantitative bounds remain in the complexity chapters.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be an objective, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the region under examination, and let \(\mathcal C:X\to 2^{\mathcal Y}\) assign the exact mathematical certificates valid at each point. Let an algorithm have access to an oracle \(\mathcal O\) returning numerical observations in a space \(\mathcal Z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic interface definition. It separates the semantic validity of a landscape certificate from the computational procedure used to report it; it does not impose an iteration-complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A computational certificate interface for \((f,X,\mathcal C)\) is a tuple \(\mathfrak I=(\mathcal O,\widehat C,V,\eta,\delta)\), where \(\widehat C:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Y\cup\{\bot\}\) is a reporting map, \(V:X\times\mathcal Y\to\{0,1\}\) is a validity predicate, \(\eta\ge0\) is a numerical tolerance, and \(\delta\in[0,1]\) is a failure level. It is sound on \(X\) when, for every \(x\in X\), \(\mathbb P(V(x,\widehat C(\mathcal O(x)))=1\mid \widehat C(\mathcal O(x))\ne\bot)\ge1-\delta\), and \(V(x,y)=1\) implies that \(y\) is an \(\eta\)-accurate relaxation of some member of \(\mathcal C(x)\). It is complete for a subfamily \(\mathcal C_0\) when every \(x\) possessing a certificate in \(\mathcal C_0(x)\) is reported with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computational certificate interface consists of an observation oracle, a reporting map that may abstain, a validity predicate, an accuracy tolerance, and a failure probability. Soundness means that every non-abstaining report is, with the stated probability, a valid tolerance-relaxed version of an exact landscape certificate. Completeness for a chosen certificate family means that such a certificate is reported with at least the stated probability whenever it exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in X:\quad \mathbb P\!\left(V(x,\widehat C(\mathcal O(x)))=1\mid \widehat C(\mathcal O(x))\ne\bot\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a deterministic oracle, soundness reduces to \(\widehat C(\mathcal O(x))\ne\bot\Rightarrow V(x,\widehat C(\mathcal O(x)))=1\) for every \(x\in X\).
special_cases_latex: A first-order interface can use \(\mathcal Y=\mathbb R_+\) and report an upper bound for \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\).
A curvature interface can report \(v\in\mathbb S^{n-1}\) satisfying \(v^T\nabla^2f(x)v\le-\gamma\), or report a lower bound on \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Soundness alone permits abstention at every point; a useful detection guarantee therefore additionally requires completeness or a nontrivial coverage condition.
boundary_notes: The definition does not identify a universally canonical certificate family or cost model.
A source establishing this synthesized interface definition, rather than only particular stationarity tests, was not located in the supplied material.

notation.meaning: Permitted numerical relaxation of the exact certificate.
Maximum probability of an invalid report or missed detection, according to the stated property.

Terminology appears blueprint-specific and requires an authoritative locator.
