knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a class of differentiable functions \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\). For each \(f\in\mathcal F\), an algorithm \(A\) generates iterates \((x_k)_{k\ge0}\), possibly randomly, and \(M_1(x;f):=\|\nabla f(x)\|\) is the first-order stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth finite-dimensional optimization. Complexity is measured by a worst-case hitting time; oracle-call complexity requires an additional per-iteration cost specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), define the first-order hitting time \(T_\varepsilon(A,f,x_0):=\inf\{k\in\mathbb N_0:M_1(x_k;f)\le\varepsilon\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). The worst-case first-order stationarity complexity of \(A\) over \(\mathcal F\) is \(N_A^{(1)}(\varepsilon):=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\sup_{x_0\in X_0(f)}T_\varepsilon(A,f,x_0)\). For a randomized method and confidence \(1-\delta\), replace the hitting time by \(T_{\varepsilon,\delta}:=\inf\{k:\mathbb P(\min_{0\le j\le k}M_1(x_j;f)\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\}\). A bound \(N_A^{(1)}(\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{-p}\) defines an \(O(\varepsilon^{-p})\) first-order stationarity guarantee on the declared problem class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-order stationarity complexity is the worst-case number of iterations needed to produce an iterate whose gradient norm is at most the requested tolerance. The worst case ranges over the stated function class and admissible initial points. For randomized methods the definition includes a confidence level, and oracle complexity additionally counts the oracle work performed through the stopping iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_A^{(1)}(\varepsilon)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\sup_{x_0\in X_0(f)}\inf\{k\ge0:\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If each iteration uses at most \(q\) first-order oracle calls, then the corresponding oracle bound is at most \(qN_A^{(1)}(\varepsilon)\).
special_cases_latex: At \(\varepsilon=0\), finite hitting time requires exact stationarity and is substantially stronger than approximate-stationarity complexity.
immediate_consequences_latex: A complexity rate has meaning only after fixing \(\mathcal F\), admissible initial data, the stationarity measure, and the counted computational unit.
boundary_notes: For constrained or nonsmooth problems, \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\) must be replaced by an appropriate projected-gradient, gradient-mapping, or subdifferential residual.
The inspected sources define stationarity but do not support this complete worst-case complexity definition.

notation.meaning: First iteration at which the stationarity tolerance is attained.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\subset C^2(\mathbb R^n)\), and let an algorithm \(A\) generate \((x_k)_{k\ge0}\). Fix tolerances \(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H\ge0\) and define \(M_g(x):=\|\nabla f(x)\|\) and \(M_H(x):=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice-differentiable unconstrained finite-dimensional optimization. The two tolerances are independent unless a particular complexity theorem couples them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(x\) is an \((\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)\)-second-order stationary point when \(M_g(x)\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(M_H(x)\le\varepsilon_H\), equivalently \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\ge-\varepsilon_H\). Its hitting time is \(T_{\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H}:=\inf\{k\ge0:M_g(x_k)\le\varepsilon_g,\ M_H(x_k)\le\varepsilon_H\}\). The worst-case second-order stationarity complexity is \(N_A^{(2)}(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H):=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\sup_{x_0\in X_0(f)}T_{\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H}(A,f,x_0)\). A reported rate must specify whether iterations, gradients, Hessian-vector products, eigenvalue-oracle calls, or factorizations are counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order stationarity complexity is the worst-case work needed to find a point having both a small gradient and no Hessian eigenvalue below the permitted negative-curvature tolerance. The complexity is a function of two tolerances and of an explicitly declared computational cost model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_A^{(2)}(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)=\sup_{f,x_0}\inf\{k:\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon_g,\ \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x_k))\ge-\varepsilon_H\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The curvature condition is equivalent to \(v^T\nabla^2f(x)v\ge-\varepsilon_H\) for every unit vector \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
special_cases_latex: With \((\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)=(0,0)\), the point satisfies the exact first- and second-order necessary conditions.
Setting \(\varepsilon_H=+\infty\) formally leaves only the first-order requirement.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small gradient alone does not constitute a second-order certificate because strict saddles may have zero gradient and negative curvature.
boundary_notes: Positive-semidefinite Hessian is necessary but not sufficient for local minimality without stronger assumptions.
The supplied trust-region source supports exact second-order criticality, but not this full approximate complexity object.

notation.meaning: Magnitude of the Hessian's detectable negative curvature.

children.title: Landscape-to-Global Complexity Transfer
children.top_down_role: Conversion of stationarity guarantees into global conclusions under benign geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Landscape-to-Global Complexity Transfer
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quantitative landscape error bound converts approximate second-order stationarity complexity directly into global objective-gap complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be an invariant sublevel set, let \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\), and assume a nondecreasing modulus \(\Psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) with \(\Psi(0)=0\) satisfies \[f(x)-f^\star\le\Psi\!\left(\max\left\{\lVert\nabla f(x)\rVert,\,[-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))]_+\right\}\right)\quad\text{for all }x\in S.\] If an algorithm produces within \(T(\varepsilon)\) iterations a point with both residuals at most \(\varepsilon\), then that point is \(\Psi(\varepsilon)\)-globally optimal. Therefore an objective accuracy \(\delta\) is attained in \(T(\Psi^{\leftarrow}(\delta))\) iterations for any generalized inverse satisfying \(\Psi(\Psi^{\leftarrow}(\delta))\le\delta\).
assumptions_latex: The displayed landscape error bound holds on \(S\)
The algorithm reaches both stationarity residuals at most \(\varepsilon\) within \(T(\varepsilon)\) iterations
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f^\star\le\Psi(\varepsilon)\), hence global accuracy \(\delta\) costs at most \(T(\Psi^{\leftarrow}(\delta))\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of approximate stationarity complexity through a quantitative benign-landscape error bound.

notation.meaning: Landscape modulus converting stationarity residual to objective gap.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits landscape-to-global transfer, and the direct substitution at a common residual tolerance is coherent. No source supports the quantitative landscape modulus or the stated generalized-inverse convention used to translate objective accuracy into iteration complexity.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) have global value \(f_*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), let \(S:X\to\mathbb R_+\) be a computable stationarity measure, and let \(Q:X\to\mathbb R_+\) measure global error, such as \(Q(x)=f(x)-f_*\) or \(Q(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,X_*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic transfer definition. It applies only on the declared region and does not by itself prove that an algorithm reaches that region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A landscape-to-global transfer modulus on \(R\subseteq X\) is a nondecreasing function \(\Psi:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R_+\) with \(\Psi(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that \(Q(x)\le\Psi(S(x))\) for every \(x\in R\). If an algorithm guarantees an iterate \(x_k\in R\) with \(S(x_k)\le\varepsilon\) within \(N_S(\varepsilon)\) units of work, the induced global-accuracy complexity is the composed bound \(N_Q(\tau)\le N_S(\Psi^{\leftarrow}(\tau))\), where \(\Psi^{\leftarrow}(\tau):=\sup\{t\ge0:\Psi(t)\le\tau\}\), provided the selected inverse tolerance is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A landscape-to-global transfer is an error bound that converts a computable stationarity residual into a global objective or solution error on a specified region. Composing this modulus with a stationarity-complexity bound yields a global-accuracy bound, but only when the algorithm's certified iterate lies in the region where the transfer inequality holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall x\in R,\quad Q(x)\le\Psi(S(x)),\qquad N_Q(\tau)\le N_S(\Psi^{\leftarrow}(\tau)).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\Psi(t)=Ct^\alpha\), a stationarity tolerance \(\varepsilon=(\tau/C)^{1/\alpha}\) suffices for global error at most \(\tau\).
special_cases_latex: For differentiable convex \(f\), every exact stationary point is globally minimizing, giving the zero-tolerance qualitative transfer.
Under a gradient-dominance inequality \(f(x)-f_*\le C\|\nabla f(x)\|^p\), take \(S(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|\) and \(\Psi(t)=Ct^p\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A transfer that is only local cannot turn a global stationarity bound into a global recovery guarantee unless basin entry is also certified.
boundary_notes: Benign absence of spurious local minima alone need not provide a quantitative modulus.
No inspected source supports the complete abstract transfer-and-composition definition.

notation.meaning: Modulus converting stationarity error to global error.

children.title: KL Post-Entry Rate Certification
children.top_down_role: Local rate classification after an algorithm enters a KL neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.title: KL Post-Entry Rate Certification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After basin entry, the KL exponent yields finite, linear, or polynomial objective-gap decay under the standard descent recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_k=f(x_k)-f^\star\ge0\) after a finite entry index \(k_0\), and suppose \(e_k\downarrow0\). If the KL exponent is \(\theta\in[0,1)\) and the algorithmic decrease and relative-error conditions yield \[e_k-e_{k+1}\ge a e_{k+1}^{2\theta}\qquad(k\ge k_0)\] for some \(a>0\), then the post-entry objective gaps have the following certified regimes: finite termination when \(\theta=0\); geometric decay \(e_k\le Cq^{k-k_0}\) for some \(C>0\), \(q\in(0,1)\), when \(0<\theta\le\tfrac12\); and \(e_k=O\!\left((k-k_0)^{-1/(2\theta-1)}\right)\) when \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta=0\) gives finite termination; \(0<\theta\le1/2\) gives geometric decay; \(1/2<\theta<1\) gives \(e_k=O(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)})\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate classification from a KL exponent after entry into a neighborhood satisfying descent-compatible recurrence.

notation.meaning: Objective gap after entry into the KL neighborhood.
KL exponent under the convention dist(0,∂f) bounded below by a power θ of the gap.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial F\), and let \((x_k)\) be an algorithmic sequence. Write \(r_k:=F(x_k)-F(\bar x)\) and \(d_k:=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x_k))\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KL post-entry rate certificate at \(\bar x\) is a tuple \((K,U,\eta,c,\theta,a,b)\) with \(K\in\mathbb N_0\), neighborhood \(U\), \(\eta,c,a,b>0\), and \(\theta\in[0,1)\), such that for all \(k\ge K\), \(x_k\in U\), \(0<r_k<\eta\) implies \(d_k\ge c^{-1}r_k^\theta\), while the algorithm satisfies \(F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\) and \(d_{k+1}\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\). The certified rate class is the rate conclusion associated with these declared constants and exponent, measured from the entry index \(K\), rather than from initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KL post-entry rate certificate records an entry index, a KL neighborhood and value window, a power-type KL exponent and constant, and the descent and residual constants of the algorithm. Every condition must hold for all later iterates. Rates certified from these data are local rates counted from the entry index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[k\ge K,\ 0<r_k<\eta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d_k\ge c^{-1}r_k^\theta,\quad F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2,\quad d_{k+1}\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\varphi(s)=\frac{c}{1-\theta}s^{1-\theta}\), the power inequality is \(\varphi'(r_k)d_k\ge1\).
special_cases_latex: The exponent \(\theta=0\) corresponds to the sharpest power-type regime.
The entry index \(K=0\) gives a rate certificate valid from initialization.
immediate_consequences_latex: A post-entry certificate does not bound the work required to reach \(U\).
boundary_notes: Different KL exponent conventions reverse or shift the displayed rate classification; the convention must be retained with the certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Complexity-to-Stopping Translation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A best-iterate bound of order inverse iteration-count to power p guarantees that threshold stopping occurs by the corresponding inverted complexity horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\geq0\) be a computable stopping measure inspected after every iteration. Assume constants \(C>0\) and \(p>0\) satisfy \[\min_{0\leq k\leq N}m_k\leq\frac{C}{(N+1)^p}\qquad\text{for every integer }N\geq0.\] For any \(\varepsilon>0\), define \(N_\varepsilon=\max\{0,\lceil(C/\varepsilon)^{1/p}\rceil-1\}\). Then some \(k\leq N_\varepsilon\) satisfies \(m_k\leq\varepsilon\); consequently, the rule that stops at the first such iterate terminates after at most \(N_\varepsilon+1\) measure evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is evaluated reliably at every completed iteration.
The best-iterate bound holds uniformly for every nonnegative integer horizon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{k:m_k\leq\varepsilon\}\leq N_\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a family of mutually declared landscape properties of \((f,x)\), such as approximate stationarity, negative curvature, or membership in a certified basin. Let \(\mathcal O(f,x)\) denote available exact or noisy numerical observations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-dimensional decision interface. It formalizes detection reliability and abstention without prescribing a derivative technology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A landscape detection interface is a map \(D:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal P\cup\{\mathrm{unknown}\}\) together with tolerances \(\eta\), a validity relation \(\models_\eta\), and error levels \((\alpha,\beta)\in[0,1]^2\). For each target property \(P\in\mathcal P\), it is \((\alpha,\beta)\)-reliable on \(X\) when \(\sup_{(f,x):\,(f,x)\not\models_\eta P}\mathbb P(D(\mathcal O(f,x))=P)\le\alpha\) and \(\sup_{(f,x):\,(f,x)\models P}\mathbb P(D(\mathcal O(f,x))\ne P)\le\beta\). The first inequality controls false certificates; the second controls missed detections, including abstention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A landscape detection interface maps numerical observations to a declared landscape property or to an unknown outcome. Its tolerance-relaxed validity relation specifies what counts as a correct numerical certificate. Reliability separately bounds false positive and missed-detection probabilities uniformly over the stated problem class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sup_{(f,x)\not\models_\eta P}\mathbb P(D=P)\le\alpha,\qquad \sup_{(f,x)\models P}\mathbb P(D\ne P)\le\beta.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For deterministic observations and \(\alpha=\beta=0\), detection is sound and complete on the separated property classes.
special_cases_latex: A negative-curvature detector can take \(P=\{\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\le-\gamma\}\).
A stationarity detector can take \(P=\{\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\varepsilon\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If tolerance-relaxed positive and negative property classes overlap, zero-error detection is not defined without a tie or abstention convention.
boundary_notes: This definition concerns pointwise detection, not the complexity of reaching a detectable point.

children.title: Matrix-Free Curvature Interfaces

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable at \(x\), and put \(H:=\nabla^2f(x)\). An algorithm may submit vectors \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) but does not form or factorize the matrix \(H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional matrix-free computation. The interface may be exact or approximate and is intended for Krylov or truncated-subspace methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free curvature interface at \(x\) is an oracle \(\mathcal H_x:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\|\mathcal H_x(v)-Hv\|\le\eta_H\|v\|\) for every queried vector \(v\), for a declared error \(\eta_H\ge0\). A returned unit vector \(q\) is a \((\gamma,\eta_H)\)-negative-curvature certificate when \(q^T\mathcal H_x(q)\le-\gamma\); it then certifies \(q^THq\le-\gamma+\eta_H\). A truncated subspace interface with orthonormal basis \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) exposes only \(Q^THQ\) or its approximation, and its Ritz value \(\lambda_{\min}(Q^THQ)\) is an upper bound on \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free curvature interface returns Hessian-vector products, possibly with a uniform operator error, without constructing the Hessian. Negative curvature is certified by a unit vector with a sufficiently negative computed Rayleigh quotient. A truncated Krylov subspace reports Ritz curvature restricted to its generated subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|\mathcal H_x(v)-\nabla^2f(x)v\|\le\eta_H\|v\|,\quad q^T\mathcal H_x(q)\le-\gamma\Longrightarrow q^T\nabla^2f(x)q\le-\gamma+\eta_H.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\eta_H=0\), the interface is the linear operator \(v\mapsto\nabla^2f(x)v\).
special_cases_latex: A finite-difference product is \(\mathcal H_x(v)=[\nabla f(x+hv)-\nabla f(x)]/h\), with first-order truncation error under a locally Lipschitz Hessian.
Newton-CG is Hessian-free when its inner iterations access curvature only through Hessian-vector products.
immediate_consequences_latex: A computed threshold \(\gamma>\eta_H\) yields a rigorous direction of strictly negative true curvature.
boundary_notes: A nonnegative smallest Ritz value does not certify global positive semidefiniteness unless the explored subspace or approximation guarantee is sufficient.
Finite-difference products also contain evaluation and roundoff errors not represented by truncation error alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Subspace Curvature Detection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lanczos searches the available Krylov subspace for a Ritz vector whose Rayleigh quotient certifies negative curvature; early subspace closure is handled explicitly, and failure to detect negative curvature is not by itself a global absence certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric operator \(H:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), a unit vector \(q_1\), an integer \(m\) with \(1\leq m\leq n\), and \(\varepsilon_H\geq0\), form \(\mathcal K_m(H,q_1)=\operatorname{span}\{q_1,Hq_1,\ldots,H^{m-1}q_1\}\). Let \(d=\dim\mathcal K_m(H,q_1)\), and use Lanczos, stopping at an invariant-subspace breakdown if it occurs, to construct an orthonormal basis \(Q_d\) of this subspace. Form \(T_d=Q_d^\top H Q_d\), compute a unit eigenvector \(y\) associated with \(\theta_d=\lambda_{\min}(T_d)\), and set \(v=Q_dy\). If \(\theta_d< -\varepsilon_H\), return \(v\), which satisfies \(\|v\|=1\) and \(v^\top Hv=\theta_d< -\varepsilon_H\). Otherwise return “undetected”; this is not an absence certificate without an independent Ritz-error bound or completion of an invariant subspace sufficient for the desired global conclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is symmetric and available through exact matrix-vector products.
\(q_1\in\mathbb{R}^n\) has unit norm and \(1\leq m\leq n\).
Lanczos arithmetic is exact, or loss of orthogonality and residual error are separately controlled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned \(v\) is a verifiable negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lanczos–Ritz detection of negative curvature using only symmetric matrix-vector products.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Subspace Solves
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated Krylov solve returns an accurate interior model stationary point or a boundary step generated by nonpositive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a symmetric operator \(H\), radius \(\Delta>0\), and tolerance \(\eta\geq0\), choose nested subspaces \(\mathcal K_1\subseteq\mathcal K_2\subseteq\cdots\) generated by \(g\) and products with \(H\). At stage \(m\), compute \[s_m\in\arg\min_{s\in\mathcal K_m,\ \|s\|\leq\Delta}\left(g^\top s+\tfrac12s^\top Hs\right),\qquad r_m=g+Hs_m.\] Stop and return \(s_m\) when \(\|r_m\|\leq\eta\) and \(\|s_m\|<\Delta\), or when the projected solve reaches the boundary along detected nonpositive curvature. Otherwise enlarge the subspace; terminate no later than dimension \(n\) in exact arithmetic.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is symmetric and matrix-vector products are available.
The projected trust-region subproblem is solved exactly at each stage.
Arithmetic is exact for the finite-termination assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either an \(\eta\)-stationary interior model step or a curvature-driven boundary step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact trust-region model minimization over an expanding matrix-free Krylov subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Accuracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hessian-vector error creates an equally large Rayleigh-quotient uncertainty; curvature below that scale cannot be reliably distinguished in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be symmetric and let a matrix-free oracle \(B\) satisfy \(\|Bv-Hv\|\leq\eta\|v\|\) for every \(v\). For every unit \(v\), \[|v^\top Bv-v^\top Hv|\leq\eta.\] Hence \(v^\top Bv<-(\varepsilon_H+\eta)\) certifies \(v^\top Hv< -\varepsilon_H\), whereas values within \(\eta\) of the threshold are inconclusive. This margin is unavoidable: for a unit \(u\), the same oracle \(B=-\tfrac{\eta}{2}uu^\top\) is within error \(\eta/2\) of both \(H_0=0\) and \(H_1=-\eta uu^\top\), although only \(H_1\) has curvature \(-\eta\).
assumptions_latex: The oracle error bound holds uniformly for every vector.
Curvature is assessed with unit vectors in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reliable negative-curvature certification requires a threshold margin exceeding the oracle error \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature resolution limits imposed by uniformly inaccurate Hessian-vector products.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative Approximation Interfaces

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First- and second-order numerical certificate measures
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable and let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). Fix gradient and curvature tolerances \(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth finite-dimensional pointwise certification. The measures describe stationarity and negative curvature, not algorithmic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the first-order numerical certificate measure by \(m_1(x):=\|\nabla f(x)\|\), and the second-order violation measure by \(m_2(x):=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\}\). The combined normalized certificate is \(M_{\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H}(x):=\max\{m_1(x)/\varepsilon_g,m_2(x)/\varepsilon_H\}\) when both tolerances are positive. A point is first-order certified when \(m_1(x)\le\varepsilon_g\), and second-order certified when both \(m_1(x)\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(m_2(x)\le\varepsilon_H\). Exact second-order criticality is \(m_1(x)=m_2(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first-order measure is the gradient norm. The second-order violation is the magnitude of the Hessian's negative part, given by zero when the Hessian is positive semidefinite and otherwise by the absolute value of its smallest eigenvalue. Comparing both measures with declared tolerances yields a numerical second-order stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[m_1(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|,\qquad m_2(x)=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\},\qquad M_{\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H}(x)\le1\iff m_1(x)\le\varepsilon_g,\ m_2(x)\le\varepsilon_H.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inequality \(m_2(x)\le\varepsilon_H\) is equivalent to \(v^T\nabla^2f(x)v\ge-\varepsilon_H\) for all unit vectors \(v\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\varepsilon_g=\varepsilon_H=0\), certification means \(\nabla f(x)=0\) and \(\nabla^2f(x)\succeq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A direction \(v\) with \(\|v\|=1\) and \(v^T\nabla^2f(x)v<0\) disproves exact second-order criticality.
boundary_notes: These measures are coordinate- and scaling-dependent unless norms and variable scaling are fixed.
Second-order criticality is a necessary condition for a smooth local minimum, not a sufficient global-optimality certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Stopping Measures
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stopping test is reliable when the computed measure plus its certified error is below tolerance; multiple requested conditions must all pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)\geq0\) be a target criticality measure, and suppose the computed value \(\widetilde m(x)\) has a certified absolute error \(|\widetilde m(x)-m(x)|\leq\delta(x)\). For a requested tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), define the reliable stopping predicate \[\operatorname{Stop}_\varepsilon(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \widetilde m(x)+\delta(x)\leq\varepsilon.\] Whenever this predicate holds, \(m(x)\leq\varepsilon\). If several conditions \(m_j(x)\leq\varepsilon_j\) are required, termination occurs only when \(\widetilde m_j(x)+\delta_j(x)\leq\varepsilon_j\) holds for every reported condition.
assumptions_latex: The absolute-error certificate is valid at the tested point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Stop}_\varepsilon(x)\Rightarrow m(x)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error-aware stopping predicate derived from a nonnegative criticality measure.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Reporting Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A report must identify the measure, point, tolerances, computed values, and validated errors so an independent checker can reproduce the acceptance decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A first-order termination report is a tuple \(\mathcal R=(x,\varepsilon,\widetilde m,\delta,\mathsf{id})\), where \(x\) is the reported point, \(\mathsf{id}\) identifies the exact criticality measure \(m\), and the attached validation data certify \(|\widetilde m-m(x)|\leq\delta\). The report is accepted precisely when \(\widetilde m+\delta\leq\varepsilon\). A second-order report additionally contains \((\widehat\lambda,\eta_\lambda,\varepsilon_H)\), validation data for \(|\widehat\lambda-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))|\leq\eta_\lambda\), and the check \(\widehat\lambda-\eta_\lambda\geq-\varepsilon_H\). Passing these checks certifies the claims named by \(\mathsf{id}\).
assumptions_latex: The reported measure identifier uniquely fixes its mathematical definition and norm.
All attached error bounds are independently validatable.
The reported point and numerical values use a specified precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted report certifies \(m(x)\leq\varepsilon\), and, when included, \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\geq-\varepsilon_H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A self-contained numerical record enabling independent verification of termination claims.

notation.meaning: identifier of the reported criticality measure

knowledge_statements.title: Measure-Reliability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measurement uncertainty creates sharp acceptance, rejection, and indeterminate regions; in the indeterminate region both an acceptable exact value and a rejecting exact value are compatible with the observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\geq0\), let \(\widetilde m\geq0\) be observed, and assume only \(|\widetilde m-m|\leq\delta\) with \(\delta\geq0\). Relative to a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the observation certifies acceptance when \(\widetilde m+\delta\leq\varepsilon\), certifies rejection when \(\widetilde m-\delta>\varepsilon\), and is indeterminate otherwise. These regions are sharp: whenever \(\widetilde m-\delta\leq\varepsilon<\widetilde m+\delta\), the admissible interval \([\max\{0,\widetilde m-\delta\},\widetilde m+\delta]\) contains at least one value satisfying \(m\leq\varepsilon\) and at least one value satisfying \(m>\varepsilon\). Without a valid finite \(\delta\), no conclusion about \(m\leq\varepsilon\) follows from \(\widetilde m\) alone.
assumptions_latex: The only relation between the exact and observed measures is the stated absolute-error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is certified by \(\widetilde m+\delta\leq\varepsilon\), rejection by \(\widetilde m-\delta>\varepsilon\), and neither decision is certified otherwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp accept, reject, and indeterminate regions for an error-contaminated stopping measure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical detectability margin and cost tradeoff
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a scalar landscape feature be represented by an exact quantity \(s(f,x)\), a threshold \(\tau\), and a numerical estimator \(\widehat s_{h,m}(f,x)\) depending on resolution \(h>0\) and computational budget \(m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic or high-probability numerical detection. The definition exposes the separation needed to distinguish a feature from estimation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(|\widehat s_{h,m}(f,x)-s(f,x)|\le E(h,m)\) on a stated class. The signed detection margin is \(\Delta(f,x):=|s(f,x)-\tau|\). The threshold feature is numerically detectable at \((h,m)\) when \(E(h,m)<\Delta(f,x)\); then the sign of \(\widehat s_{h,m}(f,x)-\tau\) equals the sign of \(s(f,x)-\tau\). A numerical detectability tradeoff is the feasible set \(\mathcal D:=\{(h,m):E(h,m)<\Delta\}\) together with its cost map \(C(h,m)\). For finite differences, a typical error decomposition is \(E(h,m)=E_{\mathrm{trunc}}(h)+E_{\mathrm{eval}}(m)/h\), so decreasing \(h\) reduces truncation error but amplifies evaluation or roundoff error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A landscape feature is numerically detectable when its separation from the decision threshold exceeds the estimator's certified error. The detectability tradeoff records which resolutions and computational budgets achieve that separation and what they cost. In finite differences, smaller steps improve truncation error only until evaluation and roundoff amplification dominate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[E(h,m)<|s(f,x)-\tau|\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{sign}(\widehat s_{h,m}(f,x)-\tau)=\operatorname{sign}(s(f,x)-\tau).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Robust detection holds whenever the uncertainty interval \([\widehat s-E,\widehat s+E]\) lies wholly on one side of \(\tau\).
special_cases_latex: For forward finite differences, the inspected source gives a model of the form \((L/2)h+2\mathbf uL_f/h\).
For curvature detection, \(s=\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\) and \(\tau=-\gamma\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(E(h,m)\ge\Delta\), the error contract alone cannot determine the correct side of the threshold.
boundary_notes: The condition is sufficient and worst-case; a particular noisy realization may be classified correctly with a larger error bound.
Conditioning of eigenvalue or subspace computations may add error terms beyond derivative approximation.

notation.meaning: Exact separation of the feature from its decision threshold.
Computational cost at the selected resolution and budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioning Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly conditioned variable metric preserves KL-compatible descent and residual bounds, while modifying their constants according to its spectral bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and suppose \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) for constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\). If \(\Phi(x_k)-\Phi(x_{k+1})\geq a\lVert s_k\rVert_{H_k}^2\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi(x_{k+1}))\leq b\lVert s_k\rVert_{H_k}\), then \(\Phi(x_k)-\Phi(x_{k+1})\geq am\lVert s_k\rVert^2\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi(x_{k+1}))\leq b\sqrt{M}\lVert s_k\rVert\). Thus a uniformly conditioned preconditioner changes the KL-interface constants but not the qualitative descent–residual structure.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is proper and lower semicontinuous on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
The displayed metric descent and residual inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Phi(x_k)-\Phi(x_{k+1})\geq am\lVert s_k\rVert^2,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi(x_{k+1}))\leq b\sqrt{M}\lVert s_k\rVert.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly positive-definite variable metrics preserve the descent and residual estimates used by KL convergence arguments.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Accuracy Control
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Control function-value errors by a summable budget and residual errors by a vanishing tolerance; then steps vanish and cluster points are critical.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be bounded below along \((x_k)\), and set \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\). A dynamic-accuracy schedule is KL-compatible at the basic stationarity level if, for some \(a,b>0\), \(\Phi(x_{k+1})\leq\Phi(x_k)-a\lVert s_k\rVert^2+\varepsilon_k\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi(x_{k+1}))\leq b\lVert s_k\rVert+\delta_k\), where \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), and \(\delta_k\to0\). Then \(\sum_k\lVert s_k\rVert^2<\infty\), and every cluster point at which the limiting subdifferential is closed is critical.
assumptions_latex: The displayed inexact descent and residual bounds hold with \(a,b>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2<\infty,\qquad 0\in\partial\Phi(\bar x)\ \text{for every admissible cluster point }\bar x.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable descent errors and vanishing residual errors retain the basic stationarity consequences of inexact descent.

notation.meaning: The allowed error in the descent estimate.
The allowed error in the stationarity residual.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Summable descent errors do imply square-summable steps, but criticality of a cluster point requires a precisely stated closed-graph argument, normally including convergence of the associated function values to the value at that cluster point. The phrase 'at which the limiting subdifferential is closed' is not a sufficient formal hypothesis, and no authoritative source is supplied to resolve the intended version.

knowledge_statements.title: Landscape Detectability Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preconditioned residual can amplify or suppress Euclidean stationarity evidence; the ambiguity factor is the square root of the metric condition number.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be symmetric positive definite with \(mI\preceq H\preceq MI\), and measure a stationarity vector \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) by \(r_H(g)=\lVert g\rVert_{H^{-1}}\). Then \(M^{-1/2}\lVert g\rVert\leq r_H(g)\leq m^{-1/2}\lVert g\rVert\). Consequently, the test \(r_H(g)\leq\tau\) guarantees only \(\lVert g\rVert\leq\sqrt{M}\tau\), whereas \(\lVert g\rVert\leq\sqrt{m}\tau\) guarantees the metric test. The uncertainty between the sufficient and necessary Euclidean thresholds has factor \(\sqrt{M/m}\), exposing the detectability cost of poor conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[M^{-1/2}\lVert g\rVert\leq\lVert g\rVert_{H^{-1}}\leq m^{-1/2}\lVert g\rVert.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioning changes residual visibility through norm equivalence, with sensitivity governed by the metric condition number.

notation.meaning: The stationarity residual measured in the inverse metric.
Uniform lower and upper eigenvalue bounds for the metric.

children.title: KL-Framework Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdowns in the analytic, compactness, or sequential mechanisms required by KL convergence arguments.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous and let \((x_k)\subset\operatorname{dom}F\). Consider a KL convergence framework requiring sufficient decrease, a relative-error estimate, continuity along convergent subsequences, a cluster point, and a KL inequality near the cluster set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional abstract KL framework. Failure means that at least one declared framework hypothesis cannot be established; it does not assert that the sequence diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define predicates \(H_D:\exists a>0,\ F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\ge a\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\); \(H_R:\exists b>0,\ \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x_{k+1}))\le b\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\); \(H_C:\omega(x_0)\ne\varnothing\) and objective values are compatible with cluster limits; and \(H_K\): a uniform KL inequality holds on a neighborhood of the relevant cluster set and value level. A KL-framework failure occurs when \(\neg(H_D\wedge H_R\wedge H_C\wedge H_K)\). Its failure signature is \(\Sigma:=\{D:H_D\text{ fails}\}\cup\{R:H_R\text{ fails}\}\cup\{C:H_C\text{ fails}\}\cup\{K:H_K\text{ fails}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KL-framework failure is the failure of at least one explicitly required analytic or sequential hypothesis: sufficient decrease, a subgradient-to-step residual bound, existence and compatibility of cluster points, or a uniform KL inequality around the relevant limit set. The failure signature records exactly which hypotheses are missing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Sigma\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \neg(H_D\wedge H_R\wedge H_C\wedge H_K).\]
special_cases_latex: An unbounded trajectory has \(H_C\) unverified even if objective values decrease.
Persistent errors can invalidate \(H_R\) while exact descent remains valid.
immediate_consequences_latex: The signature can contain several failures simultaneously and need not identify a unique cause.
boundary_notes: Some KL theorems use summable errors, inertial terms, or alternative descent metrics; their predicates differ from those displayed here.
No KL source was available to support this exact canonical failure signature.
review_flags: The precise KL framework and limiting-subdifferential convention require an authoritative source.
knowledge_statements.title: KL-framework admissibility failure

children.title: Trajectory Compactness Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure to reach or remain in a neighborhood where KL geometry is useful.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_k)\) be a sequence in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let \(\omega(x_0)\) be its cluster set, and let \(U\) be a neighborhood on which a KL inequality relevant to the target value is valid.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential failure definition. It distinguishes absence of cluster points from failure to enter or remain in a particular KL neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The trajectory has a compactness failure when its tail is not relatively compact, equivalently in finite dimensions when \((x_k)\) is unbounded. Relative to a KL neighborhood \(U\), it has an entry failure when no \(K\) satisfies \(x_k\in U\) for every \(k\ge K\), that is, \(\forall K\ \exists k\ge K\) with \(x_k\notin U\). It has a value-window failure for \((F_*,F_*+\eta)\) when infinitely many tail iterates lie outside that window. Any of these conditions blocks direct application of a local KL inequality to the complete tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trajectory compactness failure means that the sequence has no relatively compact tail; in finite dimensions this is unboundedness. Even a bounded trajectory has a KL-entry failure if it leaves the relevant KL neighborhood infinitely often, or a value-window failure if its tail does not remain in the value range where the KL inequality applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{entry failure relative to }U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall K\in\mathbb N\ \exists k\ge K:\ x_k\notin U.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In \(\mathbb R^n\), relative compactness of \(\{x_k:k\ge0\}\) is equivalent to boundedness.
special_cases_latex: A coercive objective with a decreasing bounded-value trajectory excludes unboundedness, provided all iterates remain in the relevant sublevel set.
immediate_consequences_latex: Pointwise KL geometry at a candidate cluster point cannot control iterates that do not eventually remain in its KL neighborhood.
boundary_notes: Having several cluster points is not itself compactness failure.
Local entry failure does not exclude entry into a different critical neighborhood.

notation.meaning: Set of subsequential limits of the trajectory.
Neighborhood where the selected local KL inequality applies.

review_flags: No inspected KL source supports the exact entry and value-window failure definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Trajectory compactness and KL-entry failure
Escaping Trajectories
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient descent on the analytic function exp(−x) escapes to infinity while objective values and gradient norms approach zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f(x)=e^{-x}\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), choose any \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}\), and apply unit-step gradient descent: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-f'(x_k)=x_k+e^{-x_k}\). The sequence is strictly increasing and satisfies \(x_k\to+\infty\); otherwise a finite limit would contradict the positive limiting increment. Moreover, \(f(x_k)\downarrow0\) and \(\lvert f'(x_k)\rvert=e^{-x_k}\to0\), but \((x_k)\) has no finite cluster point. Hence descent and vanishing gradients do not supply the compactness needed to enter a KL neighborhood of a finite critical point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_k\to+\infty,\qquad f(x_k)\downarrow0,\qquad \lvert f'(x_k)\rvert\to0,\qquad \operatorname{cluster}(x_k)=\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An analytic objective can generate decreasing, asymptotically stationary iterates that escape every bounded set.

notation.meaning: The set of finite cluster points of the iterate sequence.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically coherent and fits Escaping Trajectories, but it has no cited source or inspectable locator. Self-contained computation alone does not satisfy the evidence requirement.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Compactness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Descent confines iterates only when the relevant sublevel set is compact; otherwise a decreasing sequence may escape to infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and suppose only that \(\Phi(x_{k+1})\leq\Phi(x_k)\). If the initial sublevel set \(L_0=\{x:\Phi(x)\leq\Phi(x_0)\}\) is compact, then \((x_k)\subset L_0\) has a cluster point. If compactness of \(L_0\), boundedness of the iterates, or an equivalent coercivity condition is removed, monotonicity alone gives no cluster point: for \(\Phi(x)=e^{-x}\) and \(x_k=k\), one has \(\Phi(x_k)\downarrow0\) while \(\lVert x_k\rVert\to\infty\). Thus trajectory compactness is an independent KL-entry requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[L_0\ \text{compact}\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{cluster}(x_k)\neq\varnothing,\qquad \text{but descent alone does not imply this conclusion}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL convergence cannot be localized without a cluster point or another mechanism confining the trajectory.

notation.meaning: The objective sublevel set determined by the initial iterate.
The set of finite cluster points of the trajectory.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional compactness implication and the escaping-sequence example correctly describe the failure boundary, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: KL-Neighborhood Entry Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KL inequality near a point gives no trajectory conclusion when the iterates never remain inside both its spatial and value windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\Phi\) has the KL property at \(\bar x\): there exist a neighborhood \(U\), \(\eta>0\), and a desingularizing function \(\varphi\) such that \(\varphi'(\Phi(x)-\Phi(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Phi(x))\geq1\) whenever \(x\in U\) and \(0<\Phi(x)-\Phi(\bar x)<\eta\). The KL convergence step requires an index \(K\) for which every \(k\geq K\) satisfies both restrictions. If no such \(K\) exists, the local inequality cannot be applied along the tail and yields no finite-length or convergence conclusion for that trajectory.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) satisfies the displayed local KL inequality at \(\bar x\).
No tail of \((x_k)\) remains in the associated spatial and value window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\neg\exists K\ \forall k\geq K:\ x_k\in U,\ 0<\Phi(x_k)-\Phi(\bar x)<\eta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{the local KL step is unavailable}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local KL inequality is unusable unless the tail enters and remains in its prescribed position-value neighborhood.

notation.meaning: The spatial neighborhood on which the KL inequality is valid.
The upper width of the KL value window.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly identifies failure of eventual entry into the spatial and value window as preventing direct use of the displayed local KL inequality. A canonical KL definition or convergence theorem with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Descent-Residual Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure of the decrease or residual mechanisms linking an algorithm to KL geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \((x_k)\subset\operatorname{dom}F\), set \(s_k:=\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\), and let \(r_{k+1}:=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x_{k+1}))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract KL-compatible algorithmic sequence. The failure boundary is defined relative to quadratic sufficient decrease and a linear relative-error condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A descent failure occurs when no uniform \(a>0\) and index \(K\) satisfy \(F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\ge a s_k^2\) for all \(k\ge K\). A residual-link failure occurs when no uniform \(b>0\) and index \(K\) satisfy \(r_{k+1}\le b s_k\) for all \(k\ge K\). The descent–residual failure boundary is present when at least one failure occurs, equivalently when \(\sup_{k\ge K}s_k^2/[F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})]=+\infty\) under positive denominators for every \(K\), or \(\sup_{k\ge K}r_{k+1}/s_k=+\infty\) under positive steps for every \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The descent–residual boundary is crossed when the trajectory admits neither an eventual uniform amount of objective decrease per squared step nor an eventual uniform bound linking the stationarity residual to the step length. These are distinct failures: an algorithm may decrease the objective but still have residuals unrelated to its steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\neg\exists a,b>0,\ K\ \forall k\ge K:\quad F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\ge a s_k^2\ \text{ and }\ r_{k+1}\le b s_k.\]
special_cases_latex: For an inexact method, a residual condition of the form \(r_{k+1}\le bs_k+e_k\) belongs to a different error-tolerant framework unless \(e_k\) is absorbed or controlled.
immediate_consequences_latex: Objective monotonicity alone does not imply sufficient decrease.
Vanishing steps alone do not imply stationarity without a residual link.
boundary_notes: The displayed quadratic and linear forms are not universal; Bregman, variable-metric, and inertial KL analyses use modified inequalities.
No inspected source supports this KL-specific failure definition.

notation.meaning: Subdifferential stationarity residual at the new iterate.

review_flags: Requires a source for the exact descent and relative-error framework and its admitted variants.
knowledge_statements.title: Descent–residual compatibility failure
Non-Descent Behavior
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The iteration x↦−x cycles between two noncritical points of a quadratic, showing that boundedness without descent does not ensure convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), take \(x_0=1\), and define \(x_{k+1}=-x_k\). Then \(x_k=(-1)^k\), so \(f(x_{k+1})=f(x_k)=\tfrac12\), \(\lvert x_{k+1}-x_k\rvert=2\), and \(\lvert f'(x_k)\rvert=1\) for every \(k\). The trajectory is bounded but has two noncritical cluster points and infinite length. Therefore a residual formula or boundedness assumption cannot replace a genuine decrease mechanism in a KL convergence argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f(x_k)=\tfrac12,\qquad \lvert f'(x_k)\rvert=1,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lvert x_{k+1}-x_k\rvert=+\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Without sufficient decrease, even a bounded exact-gradient trajectory may cycle away from stationarity.

notation.meaning: The scalar stationarity residual at the kth iterate.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Descent Functions p. 71

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - 3.5 Descent Functions p. 71

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Error
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persistent, nonvanishing gradient error can cause an inexact method to cycle on a coercive analytic quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the inexact gradient iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k-(f'(x_k)+e_k)\) for \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\). Set \(x_0=1\) and \(e_k=(-1)^k\). Inductively, \(x_k=(-1)^k\), because \(f'(x_k)+e_k=2(-1)^k\). Hence the iterates cycle, \(f(x_k)=\tfrac12\), and \(\lvert f'(x_k)\rvert=1\). The errors satisfy neither \(e_k\to0\) nor \(\sum_k\lvert e_k\rvert<\infty\). Thus an uncontrolled oracle error can destroy descent and stationarity even for a coercive analytic quadratic.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) and the step size is one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_k=(-1)^k,\qquad f(x_k)=\tfrac12,\qquad \lvert f'(x_k)\rvert=1,\qquad \lvert e_k\rvert=1.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent inexactness can reinforce the true gradient and produce a nonstationary cycle.

notation.meaning: The additive gradient-oracle error at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Link Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decreasing quadratic trajectory can have vanishing steps yet converge to a noncritical point when no residual-to-step bound is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) and define \(x_k=1+(k+1)^{-1}\). Then \(x_k\to1\), \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\to0\), and \(f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)\). Indeed, the decrease dominates \(\lvert s_k\rvert^2\) for every \(k\), while \(\lvert f'(x_{k+1})\rvert=x_{k+1}\to1\). Consequently, no constant \(b<\infty\) can satisfy \(\lvert f'(x_{k+1})\rvert\leq b\lvert s_k\rvert\) on the tail. The sequence converges to a noncritical point despite descent and vanishing steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_k\to1,\qquad s_k\to0,\qquad f'(x_k)\to1,\qquad \frac{\lvert f'(x_{k+1})\rvert}{\lvert s_k\rvert}\to+\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing steps and sufficient decrease do not imply stationarity without a residual-to-step estimate.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The sequence has sufficient decrease relative to its squared steps, converges to the noncritical point 1, and violates every uniform residual-to-step bound on its tail. It is an appropriate counterexample, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: KL Recognition Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Models outside established analytic or tame recognition routes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of a KL recognition route
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(S\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\partial F\) be the relevant critical set, and let \(\mathfrak R\) be a declared collection of sufficient recognition classes such as real-analytic, semialgebraic, or definable functions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epistemic recognition boundary. It distinguishes failure to verify a standard sufficient class from mathematical failure of the KL property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The model \(F\) lies beyond the KL recognition boundary of \(\mathfrak R\) on \(S\) when no available certificate establishes \(F\in R\) locally at every \(\bar x\in S\) for any \(R\in\mathfrak R\), and no direct desingularizing function \(\varphi_{\bar x}\) with \(\varphi'_{\bar x}(F(x)-F(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\ge1\) has been established on the required punctured neighborhoods. This is denoted \(\operatorname{Recognized}_{\mathfrak R}(F,S)=0\). It is a failure of certification, not the assertion \(\exists\bar x\in S\) at which \(F\) is non-KL.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KL recognition failure means that the objective cannot currently be placed in any declared sufficient KL class and no direct KL inequality has been certified near every relevant critical point. It is an absence-of-certificate statement, not a mathematical claim that the objective lacks the KL property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{Recognized}_{\mathfrak R}(F,S)=0\ \not\Longrightarrow\ \exists\bar x\in S:\ F\text{ is non-KL at }\bar x.\]
special_cases_latex: A model containing an externally computed black-box term may fall outside a chosen definability recognition route even if it happens to satisfy a local KL inequality.
immediate_consequences_latex: KL-based convergence claims remain unsupported until either a recognition theorem or a direct local inequality is supplied.
boundary_notes: The boundary depends on the available recognition library \(\mathfrak R\) and can change when new closure or definability results are established.
No authoritative KL-recognition source was supplied or located.

notation.meaning: Declared library of sufficient KL recognition classes.
Indicator that a recognition or direct KL certificate is available on the relevant set.

review_flags: Recognition classes and closure properties require exact authoritative citations.
The definition intentionally treats recognition failure as epistemic rather than as non-KL geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of a KL recognition route
Non-KL Objectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective is non-KL at a point when every admissible local desingularizer fails the KL slope inequality somewhere arbitrarily near that point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\). The objective is non-KL at \(\bar x\) if, for every neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), every \(\eta>0\), and every continuous concave \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb{R}_+\) with \(\varphi(0)=0\), \(\varphi\in C^1(0,\eta)\), and \(\varphi'>0\), there exists \(x\in U\) satisfying \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\) and \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))<1\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and lower semicontinuous on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall(U,\eta,\varphi)\ \exists x:\ f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta,\quad \varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))<1.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negation of the local nonsmooth KL property at a subdifferential-domain point.

notation.meaning: Points where the limiting subdifferential is nonempty.
An arbitrary neighborhood of the reference point.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The quantified statement is a plausible negation of the local KL property, including the nonempty value-window requirement implicit in that negation. Because KL definitions vary in their desingularizer class and endpoint conventions, a canonical source with a precise definition locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Objectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to a specified family of sufficient recognition tests, an objective is uncertified when none of those tests has been established; this does not show that the objective is non-KL.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix sound KL-recognition predicates \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) on a class of proper lower-semicontinuous objectives, meaning \(R_j(f)\Rightarrow\operatorname{KL}(f)\) for every \(j\). Relative to this certificate family, \(f\) is uncertified when no predicate \(R_j(f)\) has been established. This status yields no implication about \(\operatorname{KL}(f)\): the converse \(\operatorname{KL}(f)\Rightarrow\bigvee_{j=1}^mR_j(f)\) need not hold. An uncertified objective must therefore remain distinct from an objective proved non-KL by failure of the defining inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
eg igvee_{j=1}^{m}R_j(f)\ 
ot\Rightarrow\ 
eg\operatorname{KL}(f).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of available recognition tests is epistemic and must not be identified with failure of the KL property.

notation.meaning: A sound but potentially incomplete KL-recognition predicate.
The assertion that the objective has the required KL property.

knowledge_statements.title: Recognition-Route Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recognition route certifies only objectives inside its proven closure rules; route failure is not evidence that the KL property fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be a function class for which membership implies the KL property, and let \(T\) be an operation used to construct a new objective from \(f_1,\ldots,f_q\in\mathcal{C}\). Certification through this route is valid only when a closure result establishes \(T(f_1,\ldots,f_q)\in\mathcal{C}\). Without that closure result, componentwise certificates do not certify the composite objective. Likewise, failure to represent an objective in \(\mathcal{C}\) implies only failure of this recognition route, not failure of the KL property itself.
assumptions_latex: The objective is constructed as \(T(f_1,\ldots,f_q)\) from certified components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[ igl(f_i\in\mathcal{C}\  orall i igr)\ \wedge\  igl(T(\mathcal{C}^q)\subseteq\mathcal{C} igr)\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{KL}(T(f_1,\ldots,f_q));\quad 
eg(f\in\mathcal{C})\ 
ot\Rightarrow\ 
eg\operatorname{KL}(f).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Every KL-recognition route is only sufficient and remains valid under operations preserving its certified function class.

notation.meaning: A function class furnishing a sufficient KL certificate.
An objective-forming operation such as composition, addition, or marginalization.
The required KL property for the objective.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The principle correctly separates class-membership and closure certificates from the KL property itself and fits the recognition-route boundary leaf. Its operation-specific closure premise and KL-certification interpretation require an authoritative source with a precise locator.

children.title: Nonuniform KL Parameters on Critical Sets
children.top_down_role: Failure of pointwise KL information to provide uniform setwise rate control.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform KL Parameters on Critical Sets
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KL inequalities can hold at every critical point while their constants degenerate along a noncompact critical set, preventing a uniform convergence-rate estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(u,v)=e^{-u^2}v^2\), and let \(C=\mathbb{R}\times\{0\}\). Every \((u,0)\in C\) has a neighborhood on which a KL gradient inequality with exponent \(1/2\) holds. However, along \(v\to0\), \[\frac{\|\nabla f(u,v)\|}{\sqrt{f(u,v)}}\longrightarrow 2e^{-u^2/2}.\] Consequently, no constants \(c>0\) and \(\eta>0\) give \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge c\sqrt{f(x)}\) simultaneously near every point of \(C\) with \(0<f(x)<\eta\). Pointwise KL information therefore does not yield uniform setwise rate constants without compactness or an explicit uniformization hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) has pointwise exponent-\(1/2\) KL inequalities on \(C\), but no positive KL constant is uniform over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A smooth noncompact critical set whose pointwise KL constants admit no positive uniform lower bound.

notation.meaning: The noncompact critical set of f.
A proposed uniform KL gradient constant.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The example and limiting ratio are mathematically consistent and fit the failure-boundary container, but no citation supports the pointwise KL assertion or the setwise uniformization conclusion. Source uncertainty therefore remains material to the KL formulation.

knowledge_statements.source_title: Nonuniform KL Parameters on Critical Sets
knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonuniformity of KL data on a critical set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(\Omega\subseteq\operatorname{crit}F:=\{x:0\in\partial F(x)\}\) be a set on which \(F\) is constant with value \(F_*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Setwise local KL geometry. Pointwise KL inequalities may hold throughout \(\Omega\) while uniform parameters fail on a noncompact or otherwise uncontrolled set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Pointwise power-type KL data on \(\Omega\) consist, for every \(\bar x\in\Omega\), of constants \(c_{\bar x}>0\), \(\eta_{\bar x}>0\), a neighborhood \(U_{\bar x}\), and an exponent \(\theta_{\bar x}\in[0,1)\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\ge c_{\bar x}^{-1}(F(x)-F_*)^{\theta_{\bar x}}\) whenever \(x\in U_{\bar x}\) and \(0<F(x)-F_*<\eta_{\bar x}\). The parameters are nonuniform on \(\Omega\) when there do not exist a neighborhood \(U\supseteq\Omega\), \(c,\eta>0\), and \(\theta\in[0,1)\) for which the same inequality holds for every eligible \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KL parameters are nonuniform on a critical set when each critical point may have its own neighborhood, value window, constant, and exponent, but no single collection of these data controls a neighborhood of the entire set. Pointwise KL information then does not by itself yield a uniform setwise rate certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall\bar x\in\Omega\ \exists(c_{\bar x},\eta_{\bar x},U_{\bar x},\theta_{\bar x})\quad\text{but}\quad \nexists(c,\eta,U,\theta)\ \text{valid uniformly on }\Omega.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Uniformity fails if every proposed common tuple \((c,\eta,U,\theta)\) is violated by some admissible point arbitrarily near \(\Omega\).
special_cases_latex: On a compact critical set with constant objective value, an appropriate uniformization theorem may convert pointwise KL data into a common desingularizing function; that is an additional sourced result, not part of this definition.
immediate_consequences_latex: A rate derived from parameters at one cluster point cannot automatically be applied to trajectories visiting neighborhoods of other critical points.
boundary_notes: Variation of pointwise exponents does not alone prove nonuniformity if a weaker common exponent and constants remain valid.
If \(F\) is not constant on \(\Omega\), uniformization requires a formulation accommodating multiple critical values.

notation.meaning: Relevant set of critical points at a common objective value.
Pointwise power-type KL exponent at a critical point.

review_flags: A precise KL uniformization source is required to validate the parameter convention and compact-set boundary note.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniformity of KL data on a critical set

children.title: KL Convergence without Optimality
children.top_down_role: Convergence to a critical point without a local- or global-optimality conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: KL Convergence without Optimality
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient descent on an analytic objective may converge along a stable subspace to a saddle, so KL convergence alone does not imply optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x,y)=x^2-y^2\) and gradient descent \(z_{k+1}=z_k-\alpha\nabla f(z_k)\) with \(0<\alpha<1\). If \(z_0=(x_0,0)\), then \(z_k=((1-2\alpha)^kx_0,0)\to(0,0)\). The polynomial \(f\) is analytic and hence has the KL property at the limit. Nevertheless, \((0,0)\) is not a local minimizer, since \(f(0,y)=-y^2<0=f(0,0)\) for every \(y\ne0\). Thus a KL convergence theorem can establish convergence to a critical point without establishing local or global optimality of that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k\to(0,0)\), although \((0,0)\) is a saddle and not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Analytic gradient descent converges to a strict saddle from its stable subspace.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The gradient-descent calculation and nonoptimal saddle conclusion are correct and fit the container. The cited optimization section supports saddle terminology but does not support the essential assertion that analyticity implies the KL property or the invoked KL-convergence interpretation.

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5.1 Global and local minima; saddle points p. 25

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - 1.5.1 Global and local minima; saddle points p. 25

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(\partial f\) be the limiting subdifferential, and let \((x_k)_{k\ge0}\subset\operatorname{dom}f\) be an algorithmic trajectory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, possibly nonsmooth and nonconvex setting. The definition concerns what a KL-based convergence certificate concludes; it does not assert that every listed trajectory satisfies the hypotheses of a KL convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The trajectory has \emph{KL convergence without optimality} if there exists \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) such that \[x_k\to\bar x,\qquad f(x_k)\to f(\bar x),\qquad 0\in\partial f(\bar x),\] and the resulting certificate contains no implication that \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer or belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}f\). Equivalently, its certified terminal set is the critical set \(\operatorname{crit}f:=\{x:0\in\partial f(x)\}\), rather than a designated optimal-solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KL convergence without optimality means that the entire trajectory converges, its values converge to the value at the limit, and the limit is critical, while the certificate does not classify that critical point as locally or globally minimizing.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and lower semicontinuous and \(x_k\in\operatorname{dom}f\) for every \(k\).
The phrase “KL” refers to a convergence argument using a Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz inequality near the trajectory’s cluster set; the inequality itself is not an optimality condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x_k,f(x_k))\to(\bar x,f(\bar x)),\qquad \bar x\in\operatorname{crit}f,\] with no certified inclusion \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\) and no certified local-minimum property.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(S\) is the intended solution set, the certificate is optimality-free precisely when its formal conclusion establishes only \(\bar x\in\operatorname{crit}f\), not \(\bar x\in S\).
special_cases_latex: For differentiable \(f\), criticality reduces to \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\).
A convergent trajectory ending at a strict saddle still satisfies this definition whenever value convergence and criticality hold.
immediate_consequences_latex: Additional landscape information—such as convexity, invexity, absence of spurious critical points, or a strict-saddle classification—is required to convert this certificate into an optimality conclusion.
boundary_notes: The definition does not mean that \(\bar x\) must be nonoptimal; it means optimality is not established by the KL convergence conclusion alone.
Convergence merely to the critical set, without convergence of the whole trajectory to one point, is not included.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of the Benign Local-to-Global Landscape Property
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of a region \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), and write \(f_*:=\inf_{x\in U}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonconvex optimization. The definition fixes one explicit benign-landscape benchmark; other application-specific benchmarks require separate treatment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The landscape of \(f\) on \(U\) is \emph{benign in the local-to-global sense} when every local minimizer in \(U\) attains \(f_*\), and every stationary point \(x\in U\) with \(f(x)>f_*\) has a direction of strict negative curvature: \[\nabla f(x)=0\ \wedge\ f(x)>f_*\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))<0.\] A \emph{landscape failure} is the negation of this property. Thus either a nonglobal local minimizer exists, or a nonglobal stationary point exists whose Hessian is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A landscape failure occurs when local geometry no longer supports the benign conclusion that every local minimum is global and every other stationary point is exposed by negative curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the region on which local minima, stationary points, and the reference infimum are evaluated.
The Hessian criterion is used only in the stated \(C^2\) regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists x\in U:\ \bigl[x\text{ is a local minimizer and }f(x)>f_*\bigr]\ \vee\ \bigl[\nabla f(x)=0,\ f(x)>f_*,\ \nabla^2f(x)\succeq0\bigr].\]
equivalent_formulations_latex:
The failure set is \(\mathcal F_U(f):=(\operatorname{locmin}_U f\setminus\operatorname*{argmin}_U f)\cup\{x\in U:
abla f(x)=0,\ f(x)>f_*,\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2f(x))\ge0\}\); failure means \(\mathcal F_U(f)
e\varnothing\).
special_cases_latex: A spurious local minimum realizes the first disjunct.
A degenerate nonglobal saddle with positive-semidefinite Hessian realizes the second disjunct.
immediate_consequences_latex: First- and second-order stationarity alone cannot provide a global-optimality certificate at every critical point when this failure set is nonempty.
boundary_notes: Poor numerical conditioning without either disjunct is not, by itself, a landscape failure under this definition.
For nonsmooth objectives, Hessian-based strict saddles must be replaced by a specified generalized geometric certificate.

notation.meaning: The infimum of the objective over the region.
The local minimizers of the restriction of the objective to the region.

knowledge_statements.title: Spurious Local Minima
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tilted double well contains a strict local minimum whose value exceeds that of the other well, demonstrating a spurious locally stable solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2+x/10\). The equation \(f'(x)=4x(x^2-1)+1/10=0\) has local-minimum solutions \(x_-\in(-2,-1/2)\) and \(x_+\in(1/2,2)\), characterized by \(f''(x_\pm)=12x_\pm^2-4>0\). The positive-well solution \(x_+\) is an isolated strict local minimizer, but it is not global: the positive linear tilt makes the negative well lower, so \(f(x_-)<f(x_+)\). Hence an algorithm that is locally attracted to \(x_+\) may return a locally stable but globally spurious solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_+\) is a strict local minimizer but \(x_+\notin\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A tilted double-well objective has an isolated local minimizer that is not globally minimizing.

notation.meaning: The local minimizer in the negative well.
The local minimizer in the positive well.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a topological space, let \(C\subseteq X\) be the feasible set with its relative topology, and let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be an extended-real objective with finite infimum \(f_*:=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition applies to constrained or unconstrained optimization and does not require differentiability. Locality is always relative to the feasible set \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(\bar x\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) is a \emph{spurious local minimum} if there exists a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\) in \(X\) such that \[f(\bar x)\le f(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in C\cap V,\] but \[f(\bar x)>f_*.\] It is a strict spurious local minimum if \(V\) can be chosen so that \(f(\bar x)<f(x)\) for every \(x\in(C\cap V)\setminus\{\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spurious local minimum is feasible and minimizes the objective in some feasible neighborhood, yet its value is strictly worse than the globally best feasible value.
assumptions_latex: The comparison defining local minimality is taken only over feasible points in \(C\).
The strict inequality \(f(\bar x)>f_*\) excludes every global minimizer, including unattained-infimum edge cases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bar x\in\operatorname{locmin}_C f\setminus\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When the global infimum is attained, spuriousness is equivalent to the existence of \(x_*\in C\) with \(f(x_*)<f(\bar x)\), despite local minimality of \(\bar x\).
special_cases_latex: For \(C=\mathbb{R}^d\) and differentiable \(f\), a spurious local minimum necessarily satisfies \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\).
For smooth equality- or inequality-constrained problems, a spurious local minimum may satisfy all applicable first- and second-order necessary conditions while remaining nonglobal.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any claim that every local minimizer is globally minimizing fails whenever a spurious local minimum exists.
boundary_notes: A nonglobal stationary point that is not locally minimizing is not a spurious local minimum.
A global minimizer is not spurious merely because the optimizer is nonunique or statistically unidentifiable.

notation.meaning: The set of feasible local minimizers.

A precise source locator supporting both local minimality and strict global suboptimality is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A smooth constraint can introduce infinitely many local minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An explicit smooth inequality-constrained example showing that constraints may complicate rather than simplify the local landscape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x_1,x_2)=(x_2+100)^2+0.01x_1^2\), the unconstrained problem has the unique solution \((0,-100)^T\). After imposing the smooth constraint \(x_2-\cos x_1\ge0\), the constrained problem has local solutions near \(x^{(k)}=(k\pi,-1)^T\) for every \(k\in\{\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\ldots\}\), and hence has infinitely many local solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The given strongly convex quadratic objective has the unique unconstrained minimizer (0,-100). Adding the smooth inequality x2 at least cos(x1) produces local constrained solutions near (k pi,-1) for every nonzero odd integer k, yielding infinitely many local solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^2}f(x)=\{(0,-100)^T\},\qquad \forall k\in2\mathbb Z+1\ \exists\text{ a constrained local solution near }(k\pi,-1)^T.
